stories.title: Afzal Ansari says daughter’s wedding jewellery stolen:Almirah locks found broken; occupants found at sealed house in Lucknow
stories.summary: In Lucknow, the sealed bungalow of Ghazipur MP Afzal Ansari was opened on Wednesday (2 Sept) afternoon following a court order. The bungalow, located in Dalibagh, is registered in the name of his wife, Farhat Ansari, and was sealed by the Ghazipur administration four years ago. The municipal corporation team removed the seal and handed over the keys to Afzal and his family. Afzal Ansari alleged that the locks of the cupboards inside the bungalow were found broken. He said that valuable jewellery and items worth lakhs of rupees had been kept there for his daughter's wedding. He said, “A theft had taken place there a few days after the bungalow was sealed. Despite a complaint, police and administrative officials did not pay attention to the matter.” See 3 pictures... Afzal Arrives to Take Possession Following Court Order Ghazipur MP Afzal Ansari arrived at the Dalibagh bungalow on Wednesday with both his daughters to take possession. After the court ruled in Farhat Ansari's favour, the process of handing over the bungalow was initiated in the presence of the municipal corporation and police. A large number of people also gathered at the spot following Afzal's arrival. Bungalow Built on 6,700 Square Feet The bungalow, built on approximately 6,700 square feet in Dalibagh, is registered in Farhat Ansari's name. On the orders of the Ghazipur district magistrate, a team from the Ghazipur police arrived in Lucknow and sealed the bungalow on October 28, 2022. Subsequently, responsibility for its maintenance and monitoring was entrusted to the Lucknow municipal commissioner. The Ghazipur court, granting relief to Farhat Ansari, had ordered that the mansion registered in her name be returned to her. Following this, the Ghazipur district administration sent a letter to the Lucknow Municipal Commissioner, asking for the seal to be removed from the mansion and for it to be handed back. After the DM's order, a municipal corporation team arrived on Wednesday to hand over the keys. Naib Tehsildar Rajendra Kumar and a lekhpal were also part of the team. The mansion is linked to Mukhtar Ansari's family This mansion is linked to the family of mafia don Mukhtar Ansari and his elder brother, Member of Parliament Afzal Ansari. For this reason, it remained under the administration's surveillance for a long time. A large amount of garbage was lying in front of the mansion's gate. The municipal corporation's team had it removed, after which the process of handing over the mansion was taken forward. Earlier, the mansion's gate faced the main road in Dalibagh. Now, the gate has been closed due to the construction of the boundary wall of the LDA's Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Housing Scheme. This housing scheme has been built on land freed from Mukhtar Ansari's encroachment. The mansion can now be accessed from the Bandha Road toward 1090.

stories.title: Special TET for 62,000 UP teachers:Exam date to be announced soon; 150 questions to be answered in 2.5 hours, no negative marking
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has ordered the conduct of a Special Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) for around 62,000 in-service teachers of the Basic Education Council. Following the Supreme Court's order, the jobs of 186,000 teachers in the state had come under threat. Now, teachers who have not passed the UPTET will also be able to save their jobs by passing this special examination. Anil Yadav, state president of the Uttar Pradesh BTC Teachers' Association, said that this would provide major relief to teachers appointed before 2011. However, the date of the examination has not yet been announced. It is being said that the examination will be held soon. The Special TET will carry 150 marks and will consist of multiple-choice (objective) questions. The examination will be two and a half hours long. Each question will carry one mark, and there will be no negative marking. How many marks are required to pass? Teachers from the general category will have to score at least 90 marks, or 60%, in the examination. Meanwhile, candidates belonging to the SC, ST, OBC, dependents of freedom fighters, ex-servicemen, and persons with disabilities categories will be considered to have passed if they score 82 marks, or 55%. For general-category candidates from the Economically Weaker Section (EWS), 82 marks will also be required to pass. Basic Education Department Additional Chief Secretary Parth Sarathi Sen Sharma has issued the action plan for conducting a Special Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) in Uttar Pradesh. The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission has been directed to issue the examination notification soon and conduct the test. Special TET for serving government school teachers The regular TET is conducted for candidates seeking eligibility to become teachers. The Special TET, however, will be held for teachers already working in government schools who have not yet cleared the TET. Around 62,000 serving teachers will be eligible to apply for the Special TET. Following a Supreme Court order, around 1,42,818 teachers in the state were affected by the requirement to qualify for the TET. Of these, around 86,000 teachers have cleared the TET examination held recently. Teachers must clear TET by 2028 In its order dated September 1 last year, the Supreme Court made it mandatory for all serving teachers to qualify for the TET by August 31, 2028. Teacher organisations subsequently launched protests seeking special relief. The state government then announced that a separate Special TET would be conducted for serving teachers. The action plan for the examination has now been approved. Two papers, similar to regular TET The Special TET will have two papers, similar to the regular Uttar Pradesh TET. Paper 1: For teachers of Classes 1 to 5 Paper 1 will be for teachers teaching Classes 1 to 5. It will include questions on: Paper 2: For teachers of Classes 6 to 8 Paper 2 will be for teachers teaching Classes 6 to 8. It will include: The first three subjects will carry 30 marks each, while the final subject will carry 60 marks. Special TET being held exclusively for teachers after 15 years The first TET in the country was conducted on November 13, 2011. At that time, all eligible candidates were allowed to appear for the examination. TET was not mandatory for teachers appointed in 2010 or earlier, so many of them did not take the examination. Following the Supreme Court's order, TET qualification has now become mandatory for serving teachers as well. This has led to the Special TET being organised exclusively for serving teachers for the first time in around 15 years.

stories.title: Mainpuri CO says, ‘Send video to Akhilesh':Twirls moustache, shows nameplate, says ‘Ashok Singh, from Azamgarh’
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party workers created a ruckus at the post-mortem house over the murder of a truck cleaner in Mainpuri. They began recording a video of Circle Officer (CO) City Ashok Singh and threatened to complain to Akhilesh Yadav. At this, CO Ashok Singh lost his temper. While twirling his moustache, Ashok Singh said- "What are you recording? Go ahead, record it...." Pointing to his nameplate, he said, "Look at the name-Ashok Kumar Singh... Father's name-Balbir Singh... I am a resident of Azamgarh. Record the video, make it viral... Give it to Akhilesh Yadav...." Actually, on the evening of August 30, a truck cleaner was shot dead by some strongmen after an electricity wire snapped. The driver was also injured in the firing. The next day, Monday, when the body was brought to the post-mortem house, the cleaner's family members began protesting and demanding the arrest of the accused. CO Ashok Singh was trying to reason with the family when he got into an argument with SP leaders. The CO's video has gone viral on social media. He issued a clarification, saying that some people were presenting the video in a misleading manner. See 2 pictures related to the incident... Now, see the full story... Chased the truck for 1 km before shooting Uproar over demand for the arrest of accused Kanhaiya Yadav Subhash's family members accused Kanhaiya Yadav, the former village head's son, of carrying out the firing along with his associates. On August 31, Subhash's family members created a commotion at the postmortem house, demanding Kanhaiya Yadav's arrest. The family members also demanded that the arrested accused be released, claiming that he was innocent. Upon receiving information about the protest, City CO Ashok Kumar Singh reached the spot and tried to reason with the family members. Some people present there began recording a video. They started saying that they would send the video to SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. Hearing this, CO Ashok Kumar Singh became angry. He had an argument with the protesters. CO said, ‘I was described as an officer belonging to a particular caste’ CO Ashok Singh said, "Some people present at the spot described me as a police officer belonging to a particular caste and as a political person. They said that the video would be sent to political figures. At that time, I said that instead of sending the video to the concerned person, it should be sent to someone senior to him." The CO said that one part of the conversation was taken out of context and posted on social media. CO said, ‘Action was taken on the basis of evidence’ CO Ashok Kumar Singh said, “The police had taken completely impartial action in the case. The police reached the spot as soon as they received information about the incident.” Footage from CCTV cameras installed at the scene and in the surrounding areas was examined. Mohit Yadav was identified as the main accused. An FIR was registered based on the statement of the injured truck driver. The driver identified Mohit Yadav before the police as the main shooter. He was arrested on this basis. Claim of an old rivalry over Kanhaiya The CO said that an old feud has been ongoing between two groups in the village. According to him, one son of the incumbent village head, Sugriv Yadav, is already in jail in a case registered under Section 307. Pressure was also being exerted to name his other son, Kanhaiya Yadav, as an accused in the murder case. The CO claims that the police investigated Kanhaiya's location and the entire sequence of events. According to him, at the time of the incident, Kanhaiya was in Mainpuri, about 30 kilometres from the crime scene. His location was found in Mainpuri at 6:52 p.m. that same day. Despite this, pressure was exerted to name him as an accused in the murder case.

stories.title: Doctors stage massive protest in Lucknow:Demand equal pay; Dy CM arrives in rain, says govt order will be issued tomorrow
stories.summary: Bonded doctors staged a protest in Lucknow's Hazratganj for about an hour on Wednesday evening. The doctors raised slogans over pay disparity. The police tried to persuade them, but they insisted on meeting Deputy Chief Minister and Health Minister Brajesh Pathak. Following this, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak reached the Gandhi statue, drenched in the rain, and met the doctors. The Deputy CM spoke with the doctors for around 20 minutes. He said that the file related to their demands had been completed. By 2 p.m. tomorrow, a government order fulfilling all the doctors' demands, including equal pay, would be issued. The doctors then ended their protest. See 2 pictures... Receiving a salary of ₹50,000-55,000 Doctors say that despite having the same MBBS degree, the same bond, and the same service conditions, they are being paid different salaries. Doctors serving at CHCs, PHCs, and other government health institutions in rural areas are receiving an honorarium of around ₹50,000 to ₹55,000 per month. Meanwhile, doctors completing bond service at government medical colleges are being paid up to around ₹1.10 lakh per month. Under the bond service, doctors are required to complete two years of mandatory government service or fulfil the condition of a ₹10 lakh bond. The doctors also demanded the implementation of equal pay and the payment of pending arrears. Brajesh Pathak said equal pay should be provided After meeting the doctors, Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak said that all doctors should receive equal pay. "As soon as we received the information yesterday, we instructed the ACS at 6 a.m. today. The file is being processed. The doctors will receive the government order by 2 p.m. tomorrow." Brajesh Pathak said that as soon as he learned about the protest today, he reached the doctors amid the rain. He said, "These are the children of our own homes. It is our duty to fulfil their demands." Doctors have come here from different districts and have no place to stay. We have arranged accommodation and food for them. The Deputy Chief Minister said that the state government is working to fulfil everyone's demands. Whether they are candidates or victims, we stand shoulder to shoulder with all of them.

stories.summary: Doctors at Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences in Lucknow have provided significant relief to a 32-year-old man who had suffered nearly 40 shoulder dislocations over four years. Led by Dr Pankaj Agrawal of the Department of Orthopaedics, the team successfully operated on the patient using the advanced arthroscopic bone block cerclage technique (keyhole surgery). After his health improved, the patient was discharged from the hospital. The doctor advised him to protect his shoulder and undergo physiotherapy and rehabilitation. According to orthopaedic specialist Dr Pankaj Agrawal, the patient, a resident of Gorakhpur, had been troubled for nearly four years by recurrent shoulder dislocations. He was unable to carry out daily activities. Tests revealed that the bone had worn away due to severe instability in the shoulder joint. Therefore, instead of conventional treatment, this specialised surgery was required to stabilise the shoulder again. Surgery performed through a small incision Dr Pankaj Agrawal stated that the orthopaedics team performed the surgery using arthroscopic bone block circlage. Instead of making a large incision, the bone block was positioned correctly with the help of a camera through a small 5 mm hole and secured using the circlage technique. This will strengthen the shoulder and reduce the likelihood of it dislocating again. This technique is used to treat complex cases Dr Deepak Kumar, Head of the Department of Orthopaedics, said that bone block circlage treatment is a good option for patients suffering from recurrent shoulder dislocations. The institute is treating complex cases with the help of modern arthroscopic and sports injury surgery facilities. Dr Nidhi and Dr P. K. Das from the Department of Anaesthesiology participated in the operation. According to the doctors, such shoulder dislocation problems generally occur due to sports injuries.

stories.title: Hybrid Asiatic lion to arrive from Tirupati at Gorakhpur Zoo:Big cat to arrive from Tirupati, will be ‘Gauri’ lioness’s mate; zoo administration steps up preparations
stories.summary: A special guest will soon be entering the Ashfaq Ullah Khan Zoological Park in Gorakhpur. The zoo administration is fully engaged in preparations to bring a hybrid Asiatic lion here. The lion will be brought to Gorakhpur from Tirupati. Permission has already been received from the Tirupati Zoo Authority, while a proposal has now been sent to the Central Zoo Authority in Delhi for final approval. As soon as approval is granted, the process of bringing the lion will begin. In fact, the lioness 'Gauri', already housed at the zoo, will become the companion of this new lion. There are plans to keep the two together so that they may produce cubs in the future. This will increase the number of lions at the zoo, and in the coming days, the arrival of tiny cubs will become a major attraction for visitors, especially children. What is a hybrid Asiatic lion? A hybrid Asiatic lion is developed by crossbreeding Asiatic and African lions. It is stronger than ordinary lions and adapts more quickly to different conditions. This is why the zoo administration hopes that the lion will easily adapt to Gorakhpur's climate. Gorakhpur's weather is often humid, but a hybrid lion is capable of living in such an environment. The zoo's veterinarians will conduct regular checkups, and special attention will be paid to every aspect, from its diet to its health, to ensure that it remains completely fit. Modern Enclosure and Robust Security Arrangements Before the lion arrives, an enclosure equipped with modern facilities is being prepared for it. No shortcomings are being left in arrangements for its safety, comfort, and diet. The zoo administration says that the lion will be cared for according to international standards. The arrival of the hybrid lion is expected to bring a definite increase in the number of tourists visiting Gorakhpur Zoo. Children, families, and visitors coming from far-off places will be excited to see this special lion. This will not only increase the zoo's popularity but also further strengthen the identity of Gorakhpur city.

stories.title: Why Jeetendra Mishra became Ram Mandir CEO:39 years in Air Force, led Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor; know all about him
stories.summary: Former Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra, who led the Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor-2025, has been appointed as the first CEO (Chief Executive Officer) of the Ayodhya Ram Temple. The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust announced his appointment on Wednesday. He has also been awarded the Yudh Seva Medal (SYSM). With more than 3,000 hours of flying experience over 39 years of service, Jeetendra Mishra has flown more than 18 types of fighter aircraft, transport aircraft and helicopters. Jeetendra Mishra is a native of Bhopatpura village in Bankata block of Deoria, Uttar Pradesh. He was commissioned into the fighter stream of the Indian Air Force from the Air Force Academy on December 6, 1986. He retired on April 30 this year. A devout follower of Lord Ram, Jeetendra Mishra has been given his new responsibility as the Ram Temple CEO just 125 days after his retirement. His entire family lives in Delhi. His family includes his wife, Sarita Singh, a son and a daughter. Sarita Singh has served as president of the Air Force Wives Welfare Association (AFWWA). His father, Nathuni Mishra, was a professor of commerce at Delhi University. Jeetendra Mishra's younger brother, Dr Devendra Mishra, holds an administrative position at a medical college in Delhi, while his sister, Dr Vandana Mishra, is a professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU). Why was Jeetendra Mishra appointed as Ram Temple CEO? 1. He was involved in Operation Sindoor: Jeetendra Mishra was the head of the Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor. He was also awarded the Yudh Seva Medal (SYSM) for his role. 2. Uttar Pradesh connection: He is from Deoria, Uttar Pradesh. His UP connection is also being seen as a factor in his appointment as CEO of the Ram Temple Trust. Brahmins account for around 13% of Uttar Pradesh's population, and Jeetendra Mishra belongs to this community. 3. Air Force experience: He spent nearly 40 years in the Air Force and held several important command positions. His military administrative experience could be considered important for managing the temple's expanding administration, security, crowd management and large-scale operations. How much salary will Jeetendra Mishra receive? The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust had clarified the position regarding the CEO's salary while inviting applications for the post. The notification stated that the salary and allowances of the selected officer would be decided by mutual agreement. The monthly salary would be determined based on the officer's extensive administrative experience and qualifications. The officer will be appointed on a three-year contract. During this period, accommodation, an official vehicle, security arrangements and other VIP facilities will be provided directly from the Ram Temple Trust fund. Three stories of Jeetendra Mishra's bravery In a recent podcast with ANI, Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra spoke about how the Indian Air Force targeted Pakistan's radar and command centres during Operation Sindoor and managed to evade its air defence system. 1. Officer told him, ‘Turn off the lights, the enemy could target you’ During Operation Sindoor, Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra was at the Western Air Command headquarters. Amid the tense wartime situation, a staff officer approached him anxiously and said, "Sir, please turn off the lights in your office. The enemy could track the location of your office and target you directly." Jeetendra Mishra responded fearlessly, "I openly challenge them; whoever has the courage can come and target me." He believed that the Indian Air Force was so well prepared that he could lead the entire operation from his office rather than hiding in a bunker. 2. Only one word for a target 314 km away: ‘Shoot’ During the operation, Indian Air Force radar and missile defence units were on full alert. At one point, air defence crews detected a major enemy target at a very long range. As soon as Air Marshal Mishra was informed, he gave the control room a brief and firm command in just one word: "Shoot". The S-400 missile system was fired immediately after his command. Pakistan's airborne early warning and control (AEWC) system and several major ground-based radar systems located around 314 km inside Pakistan from the Indian border were destroyed. It was described as one of the longest-range surface-to-air missile strikes in military history. 3. Pakistan's air defence system was weakened According to Mishra, the objective of the Indian Air Force during Operation Sindoor was not merely to target Pakistani aircraft but also to weaken its surveillance and air defence systems. This left Pakistan "blind and paralysed". According to Mishra, Indian fighter aircraft destroyed Pakistan's airborne early warning and control (AEWC) system and six major ground-based radar systems within just 15 to 17 minutes. This meant that Pakistan's air chief and commanders were unaware that Indian jets had struck their military installations and returned safely. Became a fighter pilot officer on December 6, 1986 Jeetendra had been interested in flying aircraft since childhood. He studied at the National Defence Academy in Pune, the Air Command and Staff College, Air University and the Royal College of Defence Studies. Jeetendra Mishra was appointed as a fighter pilot officer in the Air Force at Tezpur, Assam, on December 6, 1986. He has been awarded the Ati Vishisht Seva Medal and Vishisht Seva Medal. At the beginning of the Kargil War, he played an important role in a team operating laser-guided bombs on Mirage 2000 aircraft. Led Indian team for Garuda air exercise in France In June 2010, he led the Indian Air Force team for the Garuda air exercise in France. He also served as the Chief Operating Officer of a Sukhoi-30 MKI operating base in Pune. He has flown more than 18 types of fighter and transport aircraft and helicopters. In an interview given in August 2026, he revealed that during Operation Sindoor, Pakistani jets did not venture within 200 km of Indian territory due to the threat posed by the Russian S-400 air defence system. He also said that Pakistan had activated sleeper cells in India to find its location. More than 3,000 hours of flying experience He has served as a fighter combat leader and test pilot and has more than 3,000 hours of flying experience. During his career spanning more than 39 years, he served as the commanding officer of a MiG-21 squadron, an instructor at the Air Force Test Pilots School, and commanded forward air bases such as Pathankot and Bareilly. He also served in several other positions, including Deputy Chief of Operations at Integrated Defence Staff (IDS).

stories.title: Two Kanpur ARTOs suspended, RTO issued notice:Illegal collection at transport office; FIR filed against 15 people
stories.summary: The Transport Department has taken major action in the case of irregularities and illegal extortion at the Regional Transport Office in Kanpur Nagar. On the instructions of Transport Minister of State (Independent Charge) Dayashankar Singh, two ARTOs in Kanpur Nagar have been suspended with immediate effect. Meanwhile, a show-cause notice has been issued to the RTO (Administration), directing them to submit an explanation within 15 days. Irregularities Revealed During Surprise Inspection Following complaints in the matter, the District Magistrate of Kanpur ordered a surprise inspection of the Regional and Assistant Transport Offices under the leadership of the Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police and the Joint Magistrate/Sub-Divisional Magistrate. The team questioned around 50 people present at the office. During the inspection, 11 suspicious individuals were identified who were illegally collecting money from applicants in the name of vehicle registration and obtaining driving licences. During the investigation, cash amounting to ₹43,485 was recovered from these individuals. The investigation also revealed the involvement of two clerks of the Transport Office, Madhur Mishra and Vipin Kumar. FIR Registered Against 15 People In the case, the district administration filed an FIR against a total of 15 people at Kakadeo Police Station in Kanpur Nagar. Two clerks from the Transport Office are also among them. Following the administration's action, an investigation into the role of the responsible officials has also been initiated at the departmental level. Accused of Taking ₹26,750 and Issuing a Receipt for ₹21,750 During the inspection, a truck driver told the officials that an employee at the office had taken ₹26,750 from him but had given him a deposit receipt for only ₹21,750. On reconciling the cash, the investigation team also found indications of similar irregularities. The District Magistrate had sent the complete inspection report to the office of the Transport Commissioner. Two ARTOs Suspended, RTO Asked to Explain ARTO Enforcement Third Squad Somlata Yadav and ARTO Administration Alok Kumar have been suspended on charges of prima facie involvement in irregularities, negligence in supervising the office, failure to exercise effective control over subordinate employees, and disregard for government orders. Meanwhile, a show-cause notice has been issued to RTO Administration Officer Rakendra Singh. He has been directed to submit his explanation to the government within 15 days. Minister says corruption and fraud will not be tolerated Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh said, “The government and the headquarters have been issuing continuous instructions to prevent unauthorised persons from working in transport offices.” Despite this, the involvement of unauthorised persons in the Kanpur office, allegedly in collusion with officers and employees, is a serious matter. He made it clear that negligence, illegal collection of money, and fraud against people at any level in the Transport Department will not be tolerated. Strict action will continue to be taken against the officers and employees responsible in such cases. They Will Remain Attached to Headquarters During the Suspension Period During the suspension period, Somlata Yadav and Alok Kumar have been attached to the headquarters of the Transport Department. They will be paid subsistence allowance as per the rules. The Deputy Transport Commissioner (Region), Varanasi, has been appointed as the investigating officer to conduct a departmental inquiry into the entire matter.

stories.title: New syllabus released for UP teacher recruitment:120 questions and negative marking introduced in Super TET, commission forms committee to resolve TET result objections
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission (UPESSC) has taken a major step to address the objections and representations raised by candidates regarding the UPTET 2026 examination results. The Commission has constituted a five-member special committee, which will examine the candidates' complaints and submit its report. Along with this, the Commission has also released the new syllabus and examination pattern for the recruitment of assistant teachers in primary schools (Super TET 2026). Five-Member Committee Formed for Candidates Rejected in UPTET 2026 Following the UPTET examination results announced by the Commission on August 26, 2026, several candidates submitted their objections at the Commission's office. In their complaints, some candidates argued that, under the rules, candidates who obtained scores between 81.50 and 81.99 and between 89.50 and 89.99 in the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET)-2026 are entitled to the benefit of rounding up to the next whole mark. However, the Selection Commission did not follow this provision while declaring the UPTET results. According to the commission's criteria, general category candidates were required to score 90 marks, and candidates from other reserved categories were required to score 82 marks to pass the UPTET. If they are awarded the benefit of full marks, these candidates who have already been rejected will have a chance to be selected. Meanwhile, there are approximately 60,000 candidates who mistakenly entered their roll number, centre code, subject code, and booklet number incorrectly on the UPTET OMR sheet. All such candidates have been declared "rejected". When their answers are matched with the answer key released by the commission, all these rejected candidates are found to have passed. Therefore, this error should be rectified, and they should also be given an opportunity to appear for the Super TET examination. BJP leaders also wrote to the commission regarding this matter BJP MLC Ashutosh Sinha and MLC Devendra Pratap Singh have written to the commission regarding cases involving roll numbers and other details mistakenly entered incorrectly in the OMR sheets and answer sheets. They have appealed for human errors to be rectified with consideration for the candidates. In response to these complaints and objections, the commission issued a notice on September 1 and constituted a five-member committee. This committee will decide on the candidates' applications. If any candidate wishes to correspond with the commission, they may also send their representation to the commission's official email ID, upessc.prayagraj@gmail.com. New Super TET syllabus released: 120 questions, negative marking too The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission has announced the framework for the 2026 recruitment examination for primary school assistant teachers (Classes 1 to 5). This time, some major changes have been made to the examination pattern. Content from Class 12 to the D.El. Ed. Curriculum Included The level of the questions asked in the examination has been divided into two categories. The first covers up to Class 12. It will include questions related to languages (Hindi, Sanskrit, and English), mathematics, science, environmental studies, and social studies. The second category will include questions related to teaching skills, child psychology, information technology, life skills management, and aptitude from the D.El.Ed. curriculum. stories.title: Hearing in ‘Tejomahalaya’ case deferred:Next hearing on Oct 8; plea seeks permission for Jalabhishek and prayers
stories.summary: The hearing in the case seeking permission to perform water consecration and offer prayers during Sawan at the Taj Mahal, claiming it to be Tejo Mahalaya, could not be held in court on Wednesday, September 2, due to rain. Neither the plaintiff nor the defendants appeared, and the next hearing has now been scheduled for October 8; the case has also been transferred for the first time to the court of Additional Civil Judge (Senior Division)-VII, Rajat Shukla. The case has been transferred for the first time to the court of the Additional Civil Judge (Senior Division)-VII, Rajat Shukla. In the previous hearing, advocate Raisuddin, representing Syed Ibrahim Hussain Zaidi, who had filed an application to become a party to the case, had also not appeared in court. Kunwar Ajay Tomar, state president of the Yogi Youth Brigade, filed the suit on July 23, 2024, through his advocates Shiv Aadhar Singh Tomar and Jhamman Singh Raghuvanshi. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) Superintending Archaeologist and the Union of India have been named as defendants. The suit seeks permission to perform water consecration and milk consecration and offer prayers at the Taj Mahal during the month of Sawan and on Hindu festivals. Plaintiff says the fight will continue until permission is granted Plaintiff Kunwar Ajay Tomar says that the Taj Mahal is actually Tejo Mahalaya and a temple of Lord Shiva. He says that his legal fight will continue until permission is granted to perform Jalabhishek, Dugdhabhishek and prayers at the Taj Mahal in accordance with all religious rituals. He claims to have solid evidence in the case and says he will present his arguments strongly in court. Case was earlier being heard in the Small Causes Court The case was earlier being heard in the Small Causes Court. The previous hearing could not proceed because the court was changed. Earlier, during the hearing on May 5, Syed Ibrahim Hussain Zaidi's lawyer had sought time due to an operation. After this, the court had set the next date. Meanwhile, during the hearing on February 23, 2026, the court imposed a fine of Rs 300 on Syed Ibrahim Hussain Zaidi for repeatedly asking for a copy of the case. Claim that the Taj Mahal was Tejomahalaya Kunwar Ajay Tomar claims that the Taj Mahal was originally the Tejomahalaya Shiva temple built by King Paramardidev. He says that later, King Man Singh and King Jai Singh used it as their palace. Shah Jahan seized it from King Jai Singh, and it was later presented as a tomb. However, the claim that the Taj Mahal was Tejomahalaya or a Shiva temple has not been accepted in established historical records or in the official position of the ASI. The matter is currently pending before the court, and no judicial decision has been issued in this regard so far.

stories.title: Retd. Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra appointed Ram Mandir CEO:Led Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor
stories.summary: Former Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra will be the first CEO of the Ayodhya Ram Temple Trust. The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust announced his appointment on Wednesday. Mishra led the Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor and served in the Air Force for 39 years. The Trust has also appointed Ram Temple treasurer Govind Dev Giri as its new secretary. In addition, three new members have been appointed to the Trust: Delhi-based Mahesh Bhagchandka, Ayodhya-based advocate Madan Mohan Pandey and Nirmala Yadav of Shikohabad, who is associated with the RSS. Nirmala Yadav will be the Trust's first woman trustee. The changes come three months after a case involving the alleged theft of offerings at the temple came to light. Eight accused are currently in jail in connection with the case. Subsequently, on July 2, Trust general secretary Champat Rai and trustee Anil Mishra resigned. Following their resignations, retired IFS officer Krishna Mohan was appointed acting general secretary. He held the post for 58 days. Why was Jeetendra Mishra chosen as CEO? Hero image from Operation Sindoor: Jeetendra Mishra was the head of the Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor. He was also awarded the prestigious Yudh Seva Medal (SYSM) for his role. Uttar Pradesh connection: He is from Deoria, Uttar Pradesh. His UP connection is also being seen as a factor in his appointment as CEO of the Ram Temple Trust. Military experience: He spent nearly 40 years in the Air Force and held several important command positions. His military administrative experience could be considered important for managing the temple's expanding administration, security, crowd management and large-scale operations. Brahmin face: Brahmins account for around 13% of Uttar Pradesh's population. Jeetendra Mishra belongs to this community. Brahmin voters are considered to play an important role in determining governments in the state. Now, know about the three new trustees Advocate Madan Mohan Pandey: He was part of the legal team representing Ramlalla in the Ram Janmabhoomi-Babri Masjid dispute. He played an important role in presenting the Ram Janmabhoomi side's arguments before the Allahabad High Court and the Supreme Court. In an interview in January 2024, he said the Supreme Court verdict was the biggest achievement of his 51-year legal career. Mahesh Bhagchandka: A Delhi-based businessman and relative of former Vishwa Hindu Parishad president Ashok Singhal, he runs the Ashok Singhal Foundation. He has authored books including Ashok Singhal: Hindutva Ke Puródha, Bolti Anubhutiyan and Shri Ram Mandir Kavya Yatra. He was the main yajman during the Ram Temple bhoomi pujan ceremony in 2020 and the pran pratishtha ceremony on January 22, 2024. Nirmala Yadav: She is from Shikohabad and has been associated with the RSS. She is the Trust's first woman member, increasing women's representation in the Trust. Understand the Ram Temple CEO's appointment and responsibilities through questions and answers Q: Why was there a need to appoint a CEO? A: With the number of devotees and the temple's operations increasing, the need was felt for a full-time officer to oversee daily arrangements, security and monitoring. The need became more pressing after the case involving the alleged theft of offerings. Q: Why was an existing IAS officer not chosen as CEO? A: The Trust wants the temple's administration to remain directly under its control rather than the government's. Therefore, a retired IAS officer or someone with equivalent experience was preferred over a serving government official. Q: How was the CEO selected? A: A three-member committee was formed. The committee shortlisted candidates and presented three names to the Trust. Jeetendra Mishra was selected from among them as the first CEO. Q: Why did the Trust need such an officer? A: Most of the trustees live in other cities and are not regularly present in Ayodhya. Therefore, the Trust needed an officer who could be present at the temple every day and manage the entire system. Q: What will the structure under the CEO look like? A: A professional team comprising engineers, financial experts and around 1,500-2,000 employees will work under the CEO. The CEO will oversee security, offerings, AI cameras, crowd management, employees and construction work. In other words, the chairman will be at the top of the Trust, followed by the CEO, with the entire professional team working under the CEO to manage the temple's day-to-day operations. Now, know about the Ram Temple's assets Temple has 32 kg of gold and 1,518 kg of silver From the construction of the Shri Ram Temple until now, 32 kg of gold and 1,518 kg of silver have been received as offerings. The silver items are sent by the Trust to the Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India for melting. They are then returned to the Trust in the form of 99.99% pure silver bars. The Trust has kept them secure in a bank locker. Ram Temple Trust has ₹1,876 crore in cash At the Trust's meeting on July 6, details were presented on how much the temple had received in offerings and where the money had been spent. The Shri Ram Temple Trust has accounts with SBI, Bank of Baroda and Punjab National Bank, with ₹1,876 crore deposited in them. During the temple's construction, ₹3,264 crore was received through the Samarpan Nidhi. The temple received ₹582 crore in offerings. Of this, ₹2,370 crore was spent on temple construction and ₹391 crore on management.

On Wednesday (2 Sept), the court quashed the detention order issued against her under the National Security Act (NSA). A violent protest by workers took place in Noida on April 13, 2026. Lucknow-based journalist Satyam Verma and Noida activist Aakriti Chaudhary were booked under the NSA in connection with the case. Both were accused of instigating workers through social media and receiving foreign funding. Aakriti was arrested from a metro station on April 11. According to Live Law, a bench of Justice Atul Shridharan and Justice Achal Sachdeva, which heard the case, quashed Aakriti's detention order and said: Aakriti's detention was based on a "fabricated story" presented by the state. If her arrest is not required in any other case, she should be released immediately. The court also ordered compensation of ₹5 lakh for Aakriti. It directed that the amount be paid from the salary of Noida DM Medha Rupam. A day earlier, on Tuesday, the High Court had sought a response from the Uttar Pradesh government on whether Aakriti had been served a notice for breach of peace before the FIR was registered. The court had also sought details of the videos and WhatsApp chats allegedly used to instigate the workers. Bhaskar's report had raised the same questions three months ago After the protest in Noida, Dainik Bhaskar conducted a ground report. The report, published around three months ago, had also raised questions similar to some of those the High Court has now put to the government. The Bhaskar report questioned: If Aakriti was arrested from a metro station on April 11, how could she have played a role in instigating the violence that took place on April 13? The report also raised these questions: Police took Satyam Verma from Lucknow on April 17, but his arrest was shown as having taken place on April 19. Satyam was not in Noida at the time. He was in contact with police and had removed an article at the police's request. In a press note, police claimed that Satyam had received ₹1 crore in funding from abroad. Why did police not present evidence related to this claim before the court? Why was there a delay in registering the FIR? Why were multiple FIRs registered in the same case? Court says it appears notice proceedings were conducted after arrest The Uttar Pradesh government told the court that Aakriti Chaudhary had been arrested at 10.56 am on April 12. Police had also served her a notice under Section 130 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). She was accused of instigating a crowd of workers to engage in arson and stone-pelting. Justice Atul Shridharan then asked whether Aakriti had previously been served a notice under Section 126 of the BNSS. The government denied this. Section 126 relates to maintaining peace and public order. The judge said that the procedure under Section 126 must be completed before action can be taken under Section 130. The court also examined information recorded in the police general diary. It then questioned the government's claim that the notice had been issued before Aakriti was arrested. The court said, “It appeared that Aakriti had been arrested first, and the notice proceedings were carried out later. The court also questioned the allegation that she had instigated workers to engage in violence.” The government said, “People had started gathering for the protest from April 11. Justice Shridharan then asked, if no violence had taken place on April 11, what violence had Aakriti allegedly instigated on that day?” In other words, the court's question was based on the sequence of events: Aakriti's arrest took place first, while the violence for which she was accused occurred later. Court had asked government to show videos, but refused more time During Tuesday's hearing, the court asked the state government to produce videos that could establish that Aakriti had instigated protesters to engage in stone-pelting or set vehicles on fire. The government sought more time, but the court refused, noting that Aakriti had been in jail for around five months. The court also asked where in the record it was stated that Aakriti had called people to engage in stone-pelting and whether there was any video evidence of this. The government referred to the chargesheet and witness statements. Justice Shridharan then asked on what basis the witnesses had named Aakriti and what the video showed that could establish the allegation that she had instigated violence. Know about Aakriti Chaudhary Aakriti Chaudhary has a postgraduate degree in history from Delhi University. In connection with the Noida workers' protest case, the Uttar Pradesh Police invoked the National Security Act (NSA) against her on May 13. Activist and journalist Satyam Verma also faced action under the NSA in the same case. At the time, Noida Police Commissioner Laxmi Singh had claimed that there was strong electronic and video evidence against Aakriti and the other accused. After she was denied bail by the lower court, Aakriti approached the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court first directed her to approach the High Court, following which she challenged her arrest and detention before the High Court.

stories.title: Sardar Sena creates ruckus in Lucknow, clashes with cops:Tried to march to Assembly against reservation; police carried protesters away
stories.summary: Around 500 Sardar Sena workers and candidates from 22 government recruitment examinations staged a protest in Lucknow on Wednesday (2 Sept), raising slogans in support of reservation and marching towards the Legislative Assembly from Charbagh railway station. Police stopped the protesters near Harbilas Hospital with barricades, leading to a scuffle that continued for about an hour before the police detained organisation president RS Patel and several other protesters. See 5 pictures of the protest... The march began in Prayagraj on August 26 Dr R.S. Patel, founder of Sardar Sena, said that the Save Reservation March began on August 26 at Allahabad University in Prayagraj. The march reached Lucknow on Wednesday via Kaushambi, Fatehpur, and Rae Bareli. Thousands of Sardar Sena members and supporters of reservation participated in the march. The organisation alleges irregularities in the implementation of the reservation system in several government recruitments in the state. Sardar Sena has alleged reservation-related irregularities in 22 recruitments, including UPSSSC, the recruitment of 68,500 and 69,000 teachers, the Animal Husbandry Department, the Medical Department, and the recruitment of lekhpals. The organisation says that eligible candidates from the SC, ST, and OBC categories are not receiving the full benefits of reservation. Claim that SC, ST, and OBC candidates are not receiving their rightful benefits The organisation says that despite the constitutionally mandated reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes, eligible candidates are not receiving the expected benefits. Sardar Sena has called for the reservation system in government recruitments to be implemented transparently and for an investigation into the alleged irregularities. Sardar Sena's Main Demands

stories.title: BJP MLA Anil Sharma dies:Four-time MLA and former minister breathed his last in Delhi after battling cancer
stories.summary: BJP MLA Anil Sharma from Shikarpur in Bulandshahr has passed away. He breathed his last at a private hospital in Delhi at 12 noon on Wednesday. 63-year-old Anil Sharma had been battling cancer since 2023. He was a four-time MLA and served as a Minister of State (Forest and Environment) during the first term of the Yogi government. Political journey started with village head election, became a 4-time MLA Anil Sharma, a resident of Surjawali village in Bulandshahr, began his political career by contesting the village head (pradhan) election. He was elected pradhan unopposed. In 2002, he was elected as an MLA for the first time from the Khurja assembly seat on a BSP ticket. Following this, in 2007, he won the election from the Khurja seat on a BSP ticket for a second consecutive term. In 2012, he lost the election from the Shikarpur seat on a BSP ticket. Thereafter, he joined the BJP. In 2017, he was elected as an MLA from the Shikarpur assembly constituency on a BJP ticket and became the Minister of State for Environment in the Yogi government. In 2022, he secured victory from Shikarpur on a BJP ticket for the second consecutive time. 6 Assembly seats now vacant following the demise of MLAs Following the death of Anil Sharma, six assembly seats have now fallen vacant in the state. Of these, three seats belong to the SP, two to the BJP, and one to the BSP. Prior to this, on 5 August, the sole BSP MLA, Umashankar Singh, passed away. Meanwhile, on 23 July, SP MLA Alam Badi Azmi from Azamgarh's Nizamabad seat passed away. Earlier this year in January, SP MLA Vijay Singh Gond from Sonbhadra's Duddhi seat and BJP MLA Prof. Shyam Bihari Lal from Bareilly's Faridpur seat had passed away. Last year, SP MLA Sudhakar Singh from Mau's Ghosi seat passed away. However, by-elections will not be held for these seats now, as less than a year remains for the assembly's term to conclude.

stories.title: CO hugs and cries with father who lost 4 children:‘I’m with you, please listen to me’; father refused to perform last rites
stories.summary: The CO embraced and wept with the father who had lost four children in the explosion at an illegal firecracker factory on the Prayagraj-Kaushambi border. He continued to hug him, console him and offer words of support. Then he seated him on the cot lying nearby, placed his hands on his cheeks and said, "We are with you. Please listen to me for now and perform your children's last rites." Gaya Prasad Sahu had insisted that he would not perform the children's last rites until several demands, including an increase in the compensation amount, were met. When the bodies of all four children reached home after the post-mortem on Tuesday evening amid rain, he became distraught and began sobbing uncontrollably. With a choked voice, he said, "I have lost everything. What is the point of living now? The administration is not providing adequate compensation." After this, Gaya Prasad took to the road with the villagers and blocked traffic. Seeing the protest intensify, Sirathu CO Satyendra Tiwari reached the spot and consoled the father. Later that evening, the last rites of all four children were performed. It may be recalled that after the blast caused the house to collapse, Gaya Prasad's daughter Jhanvi (15) and sons Aditya (10), Ravi (7), and Amit (2) lost their lives. Gaya Prasad demands that he be given land for farming at the very spot in Manauri town where his house collapsed in the blast. On August 31, an explosion occurred at a firecracker factory, claiming 14 lives Girl traumatized by the accident unable to speak Meanwhile, the girl who was rescued alive from the debris is traumatized by the accident. When she was discharged and reached home on Tuesday, a Bhaskar reporter tried to speak with her, but the girl was so terrified that she could not respond. The accused's house was demolished using a bulldozer

stories.title: Salaries of 3.5 lakh UP employees rise by ₹7,000:Insurance cover up to ₹50 lakh; Yogi launches Outsource Service Corporation
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Outsource Service Corporation website was launched by CM Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday. Along with unveiling the corporation's logo, he also distributed cheques to outsourced workers. With the launch of the corporation, the salaries of 3,50,000 outsourced employees across the state have been increased by ₹7,000. Addressing the event, CM Yogi said: Every outsourced employee will receive remuneration commensurate with their hard work. Earlier, they did not even know how much remuneration they were receiving. We would go and ask an employee how much remuneration they were getting. They would say that the amount mentioned on paper was ₹9,000, but they were receiving only ₹6,000. Where was the remaining money going? He said: "No outsourced company can dismiss you. If it wants to dismiss you, it will have to report the matter to the government. We will investigate, and only after that can any action be taken." See the pictures... Key points from CM Yogi's speech... 1- ‘Our system was earlier divided into three camps’ CM Yogi said: “Earlier our system was divided into three groups. On one side were the personnel and employees, on the other was the agency, and on the third was the government. Often, our employees had to visit different offices with their problems. But there was no resolution. There was no guarantee of service, and their grievances were not heard. No one listened to their pain. The relationship between the government and its employees cannot be limited to salaries. It is also a relationship of trust and responsibility. To ensure that an employee's life is not spent dealing with paperwork and visiting offices, we have implemented a new system.” 2- ‘Now employees are not alone; the government stands with them’ The CM said that an employee should feel that their good work is being recorded and that care is being taken to secure their future. “The employee is not alone. They should receive their salary on time, and their provident fund should remain secure. We believe that economic discrimination must be eliminated to remove social discrimination. When a person is working, they should also receive respect commensurate with their work. They should be guaranteed social security. In the event of an accident, they should not be left alone; rather, they should also have a safety cover,” he said. 3- ‘₹5 lakh for emergency medicines, ₹10 lakh for air ambulance services’ CM Yogi said that provident fund contributions would also be deposited into the accounts of outsourced workers. “When you retire after reaching a certain age, you will have capital for the future. No agency can dismiss you arbitrarily. If you are unable to receive cashless treatment under ESI, we will link you to the Ayushman scheme,” he said, adding, “On the other hand, we have signed an MoU with the State Bank. Under this, employees receiving different salaries will be provided accident insurance coverage of ₹20 lakh to ₹50 lakh for their families in the event of an accident or disaster. If someone becomes a victim of a fire, assistance of ₹10 lakh will be provided. Assistance of ₹5 lakh will be available for emergency medication and ₹10 lakh for an air ambulance.” "If a major misfortune occurs in life, the government stands with the family. ₹500,000 will be provided for a son's education and ₹800,000 for a daughter's education. Assistance will also be provided for a daughter's marriage. We are going to organise the outsourced workforce," he said. 4- The entire family, not just one person, will benefit CM Yogi said: “This benefit will not be limited to just one person; the entire family will benefit from it. Families will have the assurance that their hard work will not go to waste. Through this corporation, we want to provide security cover to 20 lakh people.” Now, government departments, outsourcing agencies, and employees will all be connected through a transparent, technology-based system. Manpower requirements will be assessed, and the supply of human resources will be planned accordingly. Appointments will be made in accordance with the government's reservation policy. Digital management and digital monitoring will also be implemented. 5- Before 2017, there was despair all around CM Yogi said that before 2017, people everywhere were disheartened. The businesses that people had been managing for generations had been ruined due to the inefficiency of previous governments. “People had skills in their hands, but the market was out of their reach.” The double-engine government implemented the ODOP scheme and connected artisans with technology and markets. The results are visible. Once artisans gained access to markets, their skills became a source of employment in the state and they became part of Uttar Pradesh's economy. Our small entrepreneurs used to run from pillar to post to set up enterprises. We said, "Find out which NOCs are required for a small enterprise later; set up the enterprise first and keep obtaining the NOCs." Today, there are 96 lakh MSMEs, providing employment to 3 crore people. “We have created a single-window system. If an NOC is not received within the stipulated period after applying, a deemed NOC will be granted. Along with providing security, we have worked to make people economically prosperous,” Yogi said. This change has been witnessed in Uttar Pradesh. As many as 2,25,000 recruitments have taken place in the police force. Once an atmosphere of security was established, investment proposals worth ₹50 lakh crore were received. Through this, young people have found employment in their own villages and cities. We are connecting the youth with skills, innovation, and technology. Young people are being trained in AI and robotics. The government that follows the wishes of the people is the people's government: Brajesh Pathak Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak said, "You had been demanding this for a very long time. I felt deeply distressed. You thought that you might lose your job today or tomorrow and remained afraid. Sometimes you wondered why this was happening. The Chief Minister has resolved this issue. All governments function, but the government that runs according to the wishes of the people is truly the people's government." "We studied and were born right here. Earlier, the government used to be run from home. Brother would wake up at 12 noon, then play badminton in the evening, and at night there would be a national program. Do you know what the national program was?" Now tell me, is Uttar Pradesh doing well or not? When you learned that a recruitment corporation was being established, you should understand that God has granted wisdom. The Chief Minister worships. The temples where he goes to seek blessings are where the Chief Minister has spent his entire life. Pathak said: “You are human resources. You are working for the country and society. Work with dedication. Earlier, you used to receive ₹7,000 to ₹8,000. Previously, the person who hired you would keep interfering here and there. Now that hassle is over. No one will take even a penny now. No one will be able to dismiss you from your job either.” “You will receive an honorarium of at least ₹20,000. Those working in senior positions will receive an honorarium of up to ₹40,000. If something happens, an accident occurs, or you suffer a disability, you will receive insurance coverage of ₹50 lakh. Did you ever think you would get insurance for free? The Chief Minister has arranged all this,” he said. “When the Chief Minister is with you, you also have a duty. The opportunity has now arrived. People will try to provoke you. The video that was released for them is accurate. Earlier, it was one district, one mafia. During their rule, whenever the Legislative Assembly was in session, their people would arrive carrying ten guns each. When there was trouble in the west, the matter was settled there. The matter will be settled here,” he said. Everyone, gather together. There are more than 3,50,000 of you. All of you come together and rebuild it. You do your work, and we will do ours. If you sit at a crossroads, say that the BJP and lotus government must be formed, and Yogi must be made Chief Minister again. The roads have been built beautifully, electricity is available, and medical colleges have been established in every district. Shoes, notebooks, and uniforms are being provided in schools. Uttar Pradesh is moving toward becoming number one in the entire country. The corporation was formed last year, but work has not yet begun In the budget for the financial year 2025-26, Chief Minister Yogi had announced the creation of a corporation to recruit outsourced employees in the state. Subsequently, the government formed the Uttar Pradesh Outsource Services Corporation last September and appointed IAS officer Amrita Soni as the corporation's managing director. The Secretariat Administration Department has been designated as the corporation's nodal department. An office for the corporation is also being prepared in the PICUP Building. Budget increased by ₹426 crore; ₹20 crore approved to run the corporation Chief Minister Yogi had announced in the Assembly that employees' salaries would be increased. The government had increased the budget by ₹426 crore, and ₹2,223.84 crore had been released. The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet had also approved providing ₹20 crore at zero interest to operate the Uttar Pradesh Outsource Services Corporation. These benefits will be available to outsourced employees Honorarium to Be Paid by the 5th of Every Month - Under the new system, outsourced employees will receive their honorarium in their bank accounts by the 5th of every month. If any vendor company fails to pay the honorarium on time, it will be fined. If more than three complaints against a company are found to be valid consecutively, it may be blacklisted. 26 Working Days a Month, Weekly Holiday - There is a provision for outsourced employees to work 26 days a month. Training will also be provided from time to time to enhance employees' efficiency. Female employees will be granted maternity leave. PF, ESI, and Mediclaim Benefits - Along with the honorarium, 13% EPF (Employees' Provident Fund) and 3.25% ESI (Employees' State Insurance) contributions must also be deposited on time. The corporation will also ensure that the EPF and ESI contributions are being deposited on time along with the employees' honorarium. In addition, Mediclaim and accidental insurance benefits will be provided. Funeral assistance of ₹15,000 in the event of death - If an employee dies during the period of service, a provision has also been made to provide the employee's family with ₹15,000 in funeral assistance. Selection will be conducted through a written test and interview Employees will be selected on the basis of a written examination and interview. In the new appointments, 21% reservation will be provided for Scheduled Castes (SC), 2% for Scheduled Tribes (ST), 27% for Other Backward Classes (OBC), and 10% for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS). This will bring transparency to the recruitment process. At the same time, outsourced employees already working in government departments will not be removed. Their services will continue in accordance with the terms of the tender. These 10 departments have the highest number of outsourced employees Urban Local Bodies Medical and Health Medical Education Energy Transport Women and Child Welfare Agriculture Industrial Development MSME Labour Department What was wrong earlier - Previously, employees were being appointed on contract by different agencies. There were allegations that the employees were being exploited. They were neither paid on time nor given the fixed remuneration. Employees have been making such complaints for a long time: Taking money before joining: Some vendors take one to two months' remuneration in advance from employees before offering them a job. Deduction from remuneration: In many places, complaints have emerged that 10 to 20% of employees' remuneration is taken back in cash. Arbitrary recruitment: There are also complaints that vendors and officials collude to give jobs to people of their choice, leaving qualified youth without opportunities. Dismissal without notice: Many employees allege that vendors and officials remove them from their jobs whenever they wish, without giving any notice. Transfer elsewhere as punishment for mistakes: If an outsourced employee commits an irregularity, they are often sent from one office to another instead of being dismissed. This does not improve the system.

stories.title: Rajbhar clashes with department officials, writes to Yogi:Alleges funds for scheme publicity were siphoned off; seeks removal of principal secretary, director
stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar has written a letter to CM Yogi Aditynath against officials of his own department. He has accused Principal Secretary Anil Kumar and Director Amit Kumar Singh of negligence. He said that the officials do not listen to anyone. "They are allegedly siphoning off the money allocated for promoting schemes in collusion with others. They should be removed immediately," Rajbhar wrote. According to sources, work is underway on a digital library scheme in the Panchayati Raj Department. The minister and officials could not reach an agreement on the tender for its second phase. The officials then sent the file upward through the Chief Secretary and got a decision taken. The minister did not approve of this and he then complained about the matter to CM Yogi. Whatever is decided at the top is not being implemented Rajbhar told a media house that whatever is decided at the higher level is not being implemented in the department. Negligence is being shown in the work on the fecal sludge treatment (waste management) project in rural areas. On the one hand, a report was submitted stating that the work on the first phase of the digital libraries had been completed. On the other hand, a request was made to take action against 16 DPROs in the same matter. Along with submitting an incorrect report, negligence was also observed in the digital libraries in Sambhal and Unnao. Funds meant for promoting and publicising Panchayati Raj schemes were spent arbitrarily. Asked the CM to remove the Principal Secretary and Director Rajbhar said that the elections are approaching and the work on the first phase of the digital libraries has still not been completed. Therefore, instructions had been given to complete the work as soon as possible. As for the tender, no discussion took place regarding the selection of any particular agency in this matter. He also verbally asked the CM to remove the Principal Secretary and the Director.

stories.title: Ganga rises 2cm per hour in Varanasi:Varuna floodwater enters 11 localities, 1,388 leave homes; boats ply in streets
stories.summary: Clouds covered the sky in Varanasi on Wednesday. The Meteorological Department has issued an alert for heavy rain today. According to the data, 61 mm of rain was recorded in Varanasi from 5 pm on Monday to 5 pm on Tuesday. Around 25 mm of rain fell between Tuesday morning and evening alone. Amid the incessant rain, the water level of the Ganga is also rising rapidly. At 8 am on Wednesday, the water level of the Ganga was recorded at 70.28 meters. The river is rising at a rate of about 2 centimeters per hour. After crossing the warning level, the water level is now moving toward the danger mark. Meanwhile, flooding in the Varuna River has led to water entering around 11 neighborhoods. A total of 1,388 people from 328 families have been affected. Of these, 935 people from 219 families are staying in 13 relief camps. Water reached the paved ghats and lanes Rising water levels in the Ganga have increased the concern among people living in areas along the river. Several permanent ghats, lanes connected to the ghats, and roads have been submerged. Movement has been affected in many places. The rising water in the Ganga is now causing backflow into the Varuna River. This has also increased the risk of flooding in dozens of settlements and residential areas along the Varuna. Water reaches homes and roads in Konia Ghat The Konia Ghat area has been affected by the rising water level of the Ganga and the backflow from the Varuna. Here, floodwater has reached the areas around homes and the roads. Despite this, many people are still staying in their homes. People are also worried about the safety of their belongings kept at home and the risk of theft as the water level rises. In some places, they are having to rely on boats, while many people are being forced to wade through the water to travel. In some areas, the situation has reached the point where people have to cross roads through waist-deep water. 1,388 people from 11 neighbourhoods affected Approximately 11 neighbourhoods have been affected by the Varuna flood. A total of 1,388 people from 328 families have been affected. Of these, 935 people from 219 families are staying in 13 relief camps. Food, clean drinking water, bedding, lighting, sanitation, and medical facilities are being provided at the relief camps. Milk, fruit, and ration kits are also being distributed to those in need. 32 boats deployed, several departments on alert Thirty-two boats have been deployed for relief and rescue operations. Teams from the administration, police, health department, municipal corporation, water police and National Disaster Response Force are engaged in relief and rescue work in coordination with one another. stories.title: Story of absconding shooters in singer Ankit’s murder:Satyam’s family worth billions, owns 150 acres; Aryan is Class 10 pass; both under 20
stories.summary: The investigation into the murder of Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan has now reached Karnal. The names of Satyam Kadyan and Aryan Sandhu have emerged in the UP Police investigation. Both accused are said to be absconding along with their families. Locks are hanging on the houses of both in Karnal. The police are continuously conducting raids in search of them. Their social media accounts are being scrutinized. According to sources, the police have also questioned several close associates. Shooter Satyam Kadyan is around 18-19 years old. Satyam comes from a business family, and the family owns more than 150 acres of agricultural land. He is the only son in the family. Meanwhile, the second shooter involved in this murder, Aryan Sandhu (20), is the youngest of five siblings. His father passed away several years ago. He had also dropped out of school after completing 10th grade. First, know the story of Satyam from the billionaire family Aryan's father is deceased, family has left the house The family of the second accused involved in this murder case, Aryan Sandhu (20), lives in the Kalandari Gate area. Aryan has an elder brother and three sisters. One sister is married. His father, Narendra, passed away several years ago. Aryan studied up to the 10th grade at a private school in the Subhash Gate area. He dropped out of school 2-3 years ago. Since dropping out, Aryan often used to hang out with Satyam. After his name appeared in the Ankit murder case, his house has been locked. Encounter of Sumit and Mohit from Sonipat In the Ankit murder case, the UP Police gunned down Sumit (22) and Mohit (24) from Sonipat in an encounter on Monday morning. The two had met about three months ago and started living together. On August 25, both came to Sumit's house with new clothes. While leaving, Sumit told his father, "Papa, I am helpless." The next day, when the video of the Ankit Baliyan murder case surfaced, the family identified Sumit by his clothes. On Tuesday, both were cremated under police protection.

stories.title: Army officer’s family allegedly misbehaved with while visiting Kashi:Family of 10 staged protest on road while going to watch film
stories.summary: A case has reportedly emerged in which police personnel allegedly misbehaved with and pushed the family of an Indian Army officer who had come to visit Kashi. Following the incident, the angry family members sat on the road in protest and demanded action against the police personnel responsible. Speaking to the media, the Army officer said that he was going to watch the film "Hanuman Ansh," based on Neem Karoli Baba, with around 10 members of his family. According to him, the film show was scheduled for 6:30 p.m., and they had the tickets with them. The cinema was about 500 meters from the spot where the incident occurred, and the family was traveling by rickshaw. Two police officers forcefully pushed their rickshaw The officer alleges that during this incident, two police officers in plain clothes forcefully pushed their rickshaw. A woman around 70 years old was also sitting in the rickshaw and reportedly sustained injuries. When the family asked the police officers why they had pushed the rickshaw, the two officers allegedly began hurling abuses and behaved rudely with the family members, even grabbing them by the collar. According to the officer, when the family objected, another person arrived at the scene. After the incident, the family complained to administrative officials. They said that some people from the administration arrived at the scene and spoke with them for about 10 to 15 minutes, but they did not receive any immediate satisfactory solution. After this, the family decided to sit on the road and protest. Multiple pieces of evidence, including video, available The Army officer said they have multiple pieces of evidence related to the incident, including video footage. They demanded that the administration ensure that the police personnel who allegedly behaved improperly and pushed them admit their mistake and that action be taken against them in accordance with the rules. They said their main demands are action against the guilty police personnel and that the administration acknowledge the matter and provide appropriate justice. The family said they would continue their protest until proper action is taken on their complaint.

stories.title: Case filed against SP leader Dakku, city president:Encroachment, assault case in Gorakhpur; Dakku says he went to clear debris from his land
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Zafar Amin Dakku, who had contested the Assembly election from Gorakhpur Rural, has been accused of land grabbing, assault, and issuing death threats. A named complaint was registered against him at Rajghat police station late on Tuesday night. Samajwadi Party city president Shabbir Qureshi and several others have also been named as accused in the case. On Tuesday, a dispute broke out between Dakku and some women in Khokhar Tola over the removal of debris from a plot of land. A video of the incident also went viral on social media. The commotion continued at the spot for about 15 minutes. Police reached the scene and pacified both sides. Later that night, a case was registered on the complaint of Shahana Khatoon, a resident of Khokhar Tola. Woman claims: Occupying the house for 70 years In the written complaint submitted to the police, Shahana Khatun stated that she has been living in a house located in Khokhar Tola for nearly 70 years. She claims that the house was built on land bearing plot number 91 in Deeh. According to her, the land belonged to former zamindar Vallabhdas, who had given her ancestors the land to build a house and live there. Shahana alleges that in 2023, Zafar Amin Dakku occupied half of the house. On Tuesday, Dakku, Shabbir Qureshi and their supporters again arrived at the spot and tried to occupy the remaining portion. According to Shahana, she opposed this and stated that the matter concerning the land is pending before the court. It is alleged that she was subsequently verbally abused and assaulted. She was also threatened with death. She was rescued after people nearby intervened. The woman has requested the police to take action and provide security. Dakku says he bought the land and had gone to remove the debris Jafar Amin Dakku has rejected the women's allegations. He said that he bought the land in 2017. He occupies half of the property, while tenants live in the other half. According to Dakku, no one had been living in his portion for around 35 years. Residents of the locality had complained to the municipal corporation that the house was in a dilapidated condition. Following this, the municipal corporation issued a notice in 2020 to demolish the house. Another notice was issued in 2023, warning that if the house was not demolished, the municipal corporation would demolish it and recover the expenses from him. Dakku said that after the municipal corporation's action, that part of the house had been demolished. Debris had been lying there ever since. On Tuesday, he arrived with his supporters to remove the debris and carry out construction. During this, the female tenants began protesting. Dakku said the court did not grant a stay Dakku said that the tenants had approached the court, but they were not granted a stay. They were asked to produce documents related to the land, but they could not show them. The matter had also been brought before the police. He said that the inspector had also reached the spot three days earlier. In his presence, the tenants had said that they would get the land registered. Later, during the conversation, they had said that construction could be carried out without disturbing them. Dakku claims that this conversation took place in front of the police. He said that when he arrived to carry out construction three days later, the same women began protesting. Dakku accused the women of behaving indecently. He said that the CO has summoned him, and he will present all the documents related to his land there. Police install two CCTV cameras at disputed land Following the dispute, the police have increased surveillance at the site. Rajghat police have installed two CCTV cameras at the disputed location. Activities taking place on the land are being monitored through them so that action can be taken in the event of another dispute or an attempt to occupy. The Revenue Department has been instructed to examine the land records and the claims of both parties. SP City Nimesh Patil said that a case has been registered based on the woman's complaint. The matter is being investigated. The actual ownership and status of the land will be determined after examining the revenue records and relevant documents. The police have been instructed to maintain law and order at the site.
