stories.title: Akhilesh meets CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka behind closed doors:90-minute meeting in Lucknow; refuses to speak upon exiting
stories.summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) national co-convener Ashutosh Ranka met Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav in Lucknow on Thursday. The meeting took place at 4pm at the Janeshwar Mishra Trust office, located near the SP headquarters. The two held a closed-door meeting for around an hour and a half. After the meeting, Ashutosh Ranka left the trust office without speaking to the media. The SP has also not disclosed the reason for the meeting. However, it is being speculated that Akhilesh Yadav discussed issues concerning students, Gen-Z and Gen-Alpha with Ranka. Both are also said to have agreed to raise issues related to education. When Ranka was attacked during the ‘Fix the Schools’ campaign in Rajasthan last month, Akhilesh Yadav had also raised the issue publicly. Warning to UP government over examination paper leaks Following Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation on July 25, Ranka had warned the Uttar Pradesh government from Jantar Mantar. After the protest concluded, he said, “If paper leak incidents do not stop in Uttar Pradesh, there will be an even bigger movement there.” Why is the meeting considered important? Political analysts believe the meeting between the two leaders is significant for three reasons. 1. Developments after the Bagru violence A CJP delegation was attacked in the Bagru area of Jaipur, Rajasthan, on August 21. Akhilesh Yadav reacted strongly to the incident, condemning the attack and targeting the Rajasthan government. 2. Support from Dimple Yadav The SP has provided direct support during recent CJP movements. During the protest held on July 20, Mainpuri MP Dimple Yadav not only participated but was also seen at the forefront during the police lathi-charge. 3. Alliance and shared issues Amid emerging political equations, the closed-door meeting is being viewed as a possible attempt to create a joint opposition front on youth issues, irregularities in competitive examinations and matters of public interest. The sudden one-and-a-half-hour meeting has fuelled speculation in political circles over whether the CJP and SP are preparing to launch a major joint movement on a significant issue, or whether it signals the beginning of a new political equation. What happened during the Bagru violence in Jaipur? Ashutosh Ranka and his associates were attacked in Jaipur on August 21. Ranka had arrived at 10am to inspect the Government Primary School in Rampura Kanwarpura, Sitapura. Villagers allegedly beat them and chased them away, while their vehicles were also pelted with stones. Village women reportedly threw soil at the female supporters accompanying Ranka. Ranka accused BJP workers of carrying out the assault. He said the attack resulted in vehicle windows and mobile phones being damaged, a woman being assaulted and her shirt being torn, while one member of the team suffered a fractured hand. Who is Ashutosh Ranka? Ashutosh Ranka is a young socio-political activist and the national co-convener of the CJP. Originally from Jaipur, Rajasthan, he holds a B.Tech degree from IIT Kanpur and a master’s degree in Public Administration from the London School of Economics (LSE). Before entering active politics, Ranka worked at the consulting firm McKinsey Company. He later left his corporate career to work on issues related to education system reform. Before joining the CJP, he was also associated with the intellectual wing of the Aam Aadmi Party. In June 2026, he was appointed the CJP’s chief national co-convener. He has been the main face of the 36-day protest at Jantar Mantar against irregularities in the NEET examination and the ‘Fix Schools’ campaign in Rajasthan. CJP formed following CJI Suryakant’s remark The CJP was formed following a statement by Chief Justice Suryakant regarding the country’s youth. During a hearing on May 15, CJI Suryakant reportedly referred to unemployed youth as ‘cockroaches’. He said some unemployed young people were like cockroaches who later became media personnel, social media users or RTI activists and began attacking the system. The bench comprising the CJI and Justice Joymalya Bagchi was hearing a petition filed by a lawyer seeking Senior Advocate status. While reprimanding the lawyer, the bench reportedly said that society already had parasites who attacked the system. Following the remarks, Abhijit Dipke launched the Cockroach Janta Party in the US on May 16. Accounts were created on X and Instagram. On May 22, an online petition was filed on the party’s website demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. More than 8 lakh people signed the petition. Violent protests took place during the Parliament march on July 20. Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 25. Following this, the CJP launched the ‘Fix Schools’ campaign, which is currently being conducted across the country.

stories.title: Sub-inspector shoots himself in forehead, dies in Mathura:Body found in uniform along Yamuna; service pistol lying nearby; wife is constable
stories.summary: A sub-inspector posted in Mathura died by suicide after allegedly shooting himself on Thursday afternoon. His body was found lying in uniform near Gokul Barrage on the banks of the Yamuna. His service pistol was found nearby. Soon after the incident was reported, police and a forensic team reached the spot and collected necessary evidence. The deceased was identified as Pankaj Kumar Yadav, 31. He was posted as the reader to the SP (Traffic). He joined the police force on 30 June 2019. The bullet hit him in the middle of his forehead. Pankaj’s wife, Deepti, is also a constable and is currently posted at Sadar police station in Mathura. SSP Shlok Kumar said Pankaj Kumar had his service pistol issued to him earlier on Thursday. He allegedly used the same pistol to kill himself. The reason for his suicide is being investigated. Pankaj was a resident of the Pilua police station area in Etah district. His father’s name is Rajveer Singh. He was having a house constructed in the Damodarpura area of Sadar in Mathura. On Thursday afternoon, he went home from duty. After staying there for some time, he left home in uniform and allegedly shot himself on the way. See 2 pictures... The initial investigation has indicated a possible family dispute. Police have sent the body for post-mortem. Further legal action will be taken on the basis of questioning and scientific evidence. After receiving information about the incident, Pankaj’s wife, Constable Deepti, also reached the spot.

stories.title: Girl goes to school on one leg, Yogi ensures treatment:Girl had asked Ballia DM for a bicycle, saying, 'I want to study a lot'
stories.summary: Ragini's plea to the DM in Ballia for a bicycle has reached Yogi. Efforts have begun to treat the leg of the girl who hops to school on one leg. The CM has said that the Uttar Pradesh government will bear the entire cost of the girl's treatment. The Health Department is now active. Alakh Pandey, CEO of Physics Wallah coaching, has sent ₹10 lakh to help Ragini. A day earlier, the DM had also given the girl a bicycle. After her medical examination at the district hospital on Thursday, it was decided to send her to BHU Hospital in Varanasi. Ragini innocently said to the DM, "Thank you, uncle." See 2 pictures... Ragini sits down several times on her way to school Devendra Rajbhar's family lives in Ranipur village. He works as a labourer in Hyderabad. His father, Narad; mother, wife, Babita Devi; and only daughter, Ragini (7), live in the village. Ragini lost one of her legs when she was six months old. Ragini studies in Class 1 at the primary school in Dighera village. The distance between Ragini's school and home is only 400 metres. But for Ragini, this journey is very long. While covering the 400-metre distance, she often gets tired, sits down on the ground, and begins to cry in pain. She had told the DM, ‘Get me a bicycle.’ Upset by this, Ragini made an emotional appeal to the DM on Monday (August 31). She said, "DM uncle, one of my legs is disabled. Please get me a bicycle. I will study very hard." Hearing her appeal, Mangla Prasad Singh reached the village on Wednesday. Instead of one, he gave Ragini two tricycles. After this, Ragini said, "I have received a bicycle; I don't need anything else now." Ragini reached the DM's office with her mother On Thursday, the DM said that the child was undergoing a medical examination. The CM has directed that the state government will bear the entire cost of the child's treatment. At the district hospital, orthopaedic specialist Dr Karan Singh Chauhan thoroughly examined Ragini's leg in the presence of CMO Dr Abhay Narayan Rai. After this, with the family's consent, it was decided to take her to BHU for further tests. After this, Ragini reached the DM's office with her mother, Babita Devi. It was decided there that Ragini would be taken to Varanasi for an examination on Saturday. Ragini said, "DM uncle has said that my leg will become completely fine. I am very happy. Thank you, uncle." DM Mangla Prasad Singh said that a team of doctors has examined her. They have recommended two tests that cannot be conducted here. Therefore, the girl is being sent to BHU. Our effort is to treat her leg through surgery or by any other possible means. The team of doctors will decide what needs to be done. Our aim is for the girl to be able to stand on her own feet. The state government will bear all the expenses incurred in this process. Fractured in childhood, the knee could not be joined CMO Dr Abhay Narayan Rai said, “The girl fractured her leg during childhood, but it could not be joined at the knee. Her muscles continued to weaken, causing her foot to bend.” Some essential tests required for treatment cannot be conducted in Ballia. Only after these tests will we be able to determine how the girl can be treated. There is every hope that the girl will be able to stand on her own. Alakh Pandey sent ₹10 lakh Ragini's appeal has now begun to resonate everywhere. The DM gave the girl two tricycles and essential supplies. He also promised to have a road and a house built. Aam Aadmi Party Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh immediately sent ₹26,000 in assistance. Alakh Pandey, co-founder and CEO of Physics Wallah, has sent ₹10 lakh for the girl's treatment. In a video message, Alakh Pandey said that since morning, many people had sent him the girl's video and tagged him in it. He said he was deeply saddened after watching the video. "This is a very young girl who wants to go to school." Ragini's mother, Babita Devi, told Dainik Bhaskar over the phone that Alakh ji had spoken to them on the phone. He said, "We have sent ₹10 lakh to your account. Please ensure that the child receives proper treatment." Ragini met with an accident while her mother was on her way to get medicine for her Mother Babita said, "Ragini was six months old. She was ill at the time. I was carrying her in my arms and going to get medicine when we met with an accident on the way. In that accident, one of Ragini's legs was badly fractured. She received treatment, but her leg could not fully recover. We sought treatment at several places, but nothing helped." Ragini does all her work with the support of one leg Her mother said that Ragini is now 7 years old. She does all her work using only one leg. Her video has gone viral, which is why everyone is coming to see her. When children from the neighbourhood passed in front of our house carrying school bags, Ragini would start crying. She would say, “I also want to study.”

stories.title: Friends kill 27-year-old photographer:Break his limbs, stuff body in bag and dump it on hill in MP, 62 km away
stories.summary: In Prayagraj, three friends murdered a 27-year-old reel maker and photographer (digital creator). They first shot him, hitting his shoulder, and then strangled him with their hands. After that, they broke his hands and legs and stuffed him into a bag. The accused took the bag approximately 62 kilometres away to Rewa in Madhya Pradesh and dumped it on Sohagi Hill. The police uncovered the case after examining CCTV footage from the apartment complex. The footage showed three young men leaving photographer Alok Gupta's flat carrying a large bag. The police arrested all three on Friday. The accused have confessed to the crime. The police have also called the photographer's girlfriend for questioning. According to the police, the accused murdered him to loot his expensive cameras and other gadgets. The incident took place in the Dhoomanganj area. His phone was switched off on the 11th; a report was filed on the 22nd Alok Gupta was a resident of Kunda in Pratapgarh. For the past few years, he had been living in a rented flat in Amber Apartment in Dhoomanganj, Prayagraj. He was a digital creator who worked on photoshoots for weddings and other ceremonies. He also made reels. Alok suddenly went missing somewhere on August 10. On the morning of August 11, his family members called his mobile phone several times, but there was no response. The phone was switched off. After that, when his family reached his flat, they found it locked. Despite searching extensively, they could not find any trace of Alok. The family then filed a missing-person report at Dhoomanganj police station on August 22. CCTV showed 3 youths carrying a large bag While searching for Alok, the police examined CCTV footage from Amber Apartments. The footage showed three youths leaving Alok's flat on the night of August 10, carrying a large bag. After that, the three youths got into a silver-coloured Swift car and left the scene. After the CCTV footage surfaced, the police began identifying the three youths. They also examined the call details of Alok's mobile phone. During the investigation, a girl's number appeared in the CDR of Alok's mobile phone. The police called her for questioning. She said, "I know one of the boys seen in the video. His name is Shubham Tiwari. He is a resident of Nawabganj." After this, the police apprehended him on Wednesday (September 1). When questioned about Alok, he denied knowing him. Confessed after seeing himself on CCTV When the police showed Shubham Tiwari the apartment's CCTV footage, he became nervous and confessed the truth. He said, "Both of the boys seen in the video are my friends. Their names are Shubham Yadav and Ankush Yadav." "My two friends and I went to Alok's flat at around 10 p.m. on August 10. There, I fired at Alok with a country-made pistol. He ducked, so the bullet hit his shoulder. After that, all three of us restrained him and strangled him." "We then put the body in a bag. We took it from Prayagraj to Sohagi Hill in Madhya Pradesh's Rewa district in a silver-coloured Swift car. We dumped the body there and returned." He said, ‘There was a debt of ₹50,000; he used to humiliate me’ The main accused, Shubham Tiwari, said, "I had borrowed ₹50,000 from Alok Gupta. Alok repeatedly demanded that I return his money. He would repeatedly humiliate me over the money. He would also say, 'You won't be able to do anything.' He flaunted his wealth and money." After Shubham's confession, Dhoomanganj police contacted Rewa police. They learned that on August 14, the body of a young man had been found in a bag on Sohagi Hill. The body could not be immediately identified. Therefore, after conducting a post-mortem on the unidentified body, it was buried. Family identified Alok by his clothes After learning the full details from Rewa police, Alok's family members were called to identify the body. The family identified the body as Alok's based on the clothes. Following this, police also arrested both of Shubham's friends on Friday. The police are now looking for a connection between Alok's girlfriend and Shubham Tiwari. They are also investigating the conversations and contacts between the two. DCP City Sagar Jain said that the body found on Sohagi Hill in Rewa district has been identified. The entire case will be disclosed soon.

stories.title: Jayant Chaudhary attends rally with wife and daughter:Elderly man dances with joy after standing up from seat; says Yogi is soft on farmers in Saharanpur
stories.summary: RLD leader Jayant Chaudhary arrived at the party’s Swabhiman Rally in Saharanpur on Thursday with his wife Charu Chaudhary and daughter Saira, marking the first time the three attended the rally together. Their arrival boosted enthusiasm among party workers, who welcomed the family with slogans and songs, while an elderly supporter was seen dancing joyfully in the pandal. While addressing the rally, Jayant Chaudhary launched a fierce attack on the Samajwadi Party and the opposition. Referring to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, he said that Yogi is extremely strict with those who stand against the government and the system. However, his heart is very soft for farmers. When MLAs meet the Chief Minister over sugarcane prices and issues related to farmers, he says, "I am also a farmer." A large pandal was set up for the rally held at the Gochar Krishi Inter College ground. Between 7,000 and 8,000 people are present at the rally venue. Supporters from nearby districts are still arriving. See 4 pictures... Read Jayant's Key Statements Samajwadis have now begun opposing Chaudhary Ajit Singh Jayant said, "While continuously opposing farmers and farming, the Samajwadi leaders have now begun opposing Chaudhary Ajit Singh as well. Farmers need to recognise who their well-wisher and advocate is." Farmers are in the majority. Governments are formed and brought down on their strength. However, the harsh reality of the country is that the farmers' lobby is weak in political corridors. This is why farmers must choose a strong representative to speak for them. The Opposition sees a rasgulla in sugarcane Jayant cornered the opposition over the sugarcane issue. He said that while in opposition, people make statements that can get them four extra votes. However, they are not ready to discuss the sugarcane issue. The reason may be that they can still see the rasgulla. He said that he would also write a letter to the opposition on this issue. If they agree, he would send a good packet of rasgullas to Lucknow as well. Meanwhile, former MLA Malook Nagar also targeted SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. He said, "Forget talking about a quarter, half, or one rupee. The SP state president is a two-bit president. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, there was not a single seat that the SP could have won without the RLD's support." He claimed that the opposition alliance benefited on several seats only because of the RLD.

stories.title: Interest fully waived under Municipal Corporation’s OTS scheme:₹36.43 lakh collected; big defaulters also under watch
stories.summary: Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation has implemented a one-time settlement (OTS) scheme for property tax from August 15 to December 15 to help citizens settle old dues and get relief on interest. Mayor Dr Manglesh Srivastava and Municipal Commissioner Ajay Jain announced the scheme at a press conference on Thursday (3 Sept). Full waiver of interest on old outstanding dues Eligible defaulters under the OTS scheme will receive a full waiver on the interest and surcharge levied on old property tax. Defaulters may pay the entire amount at once at their convenience or deposit the outstanding amount in a maximum of three instalments. Installment payments must be made within the prescribed time. One-third of the total outstanding amount must be deposited within 30 days of the implementation of the scheme. The remaining two-thirds may be deposited in monthly instalments. Discount on current tax also available until September 15 The Municipal Corporation has also extended the period for the discount available on depositing current property tax. Previously, the discount was available until August 31; it has now been extended to September 15. A 12 per cent discount will be available for depositing current property tax online, and an 8 per cent discount for offline payments. Applications for OTS can be submitted until November 14 The last date to apply for the OTS scheme is November 14, 2026. Citizens can apply both online and offline. However, the outstanding amount must be paid in full within a maximum period of three months. If the instalment or the entire amount is not deposited within the prescribed period, the OTS application will be cancelled. After this, action will be taken as per the rules after December 15. Payment can be made both online and offline Citizens can also make payments through the QR code provided on the demand bill, the chatbot, and BBPS, apart from the online portal of the Municipal Corporation. Additionally, payment facilities are available at the counters of all zonal offices and the Municipal Corporation headquarters. Payments can also be made through door-to-door collectors. The amount can be deposited through cash, online payment, net banking, cheque, demand draft, and other prescribed modes. So far, 802 people have applied According to the Municipal Corporation, 802 applications have been received so far under the OTS scheme. Of these, 625 citizens have opted to make full payment, while 177 have opted to pay in instalments. So far, 87 citizens have made full payment, while two citizens have deposited the first instalment. The Municipal Corporation has recovered ₹36.43 lakh so far and granted citizens a concession of ₹10.32 lakh. Large defaulters are also being contacted The municipal corporation has launched a special campaign for major defaulters. Personal contact is being made with defaulters owing between one lakh and five lakh rupees, between five lakh and ten lakh rupees, and more than ten lakh rupees. Officials and recovery personnel are sending letters to these defaulters providing information about the OTS scheme and encouraging them to deposit their outstanding dues. OTS Camps Being Organised in Wards To reach as many people as possible, municipal corporation teams are contacting residents door to door. OTS camps are being organised in various wards. Special counters have also been set up at zonal offices and the municipal corporation headquarters. In addition, the scheme is being publicised through newspapers, hoardings, digital screens, garbage collection vehicles, FM radio, and the municipal corporation's digital platforms. Councillors have also been informed about the scheme so that they can tell the people in their wards about it.

stories.title: Yogi says, ‘No more need to raise 'Farukkhabadi chuse ganna’:Crowd chants, ‘Expressway le gaye Khanna…’; takes dig at minister Suresh Khanna
stories.summary: CM Yogi Adityanath targeted the Samajwadi Party (SP) in Farrukhabad on Thursday over the outsourcing service corporation. He said, “Most of the outsourcing companies were part of the Saifai Syndicate. They had years of experience in looting and plundering. We put an end to that just yesterday.” Taking a dig at his minister Suresh Khanna over the proposed link expressway in the district, he said: A link expressway is coming that will connect you with the Ganga Expressway and the Bundelkhand Expressway. Farrukhabad is becoming a junction. Now you will not have to raise the slogan, ‘Farrukhabadi chuse ganna, expressway le gaye… As the CM left the sentence unfinished, people in the gathering shouted, “Expressway le gaye Khanna.” The CM smiled at the response. At around 12 noon on Thursday, the CM’s helicopter landed at the police lines at the district headquarters. At a large pandal set up there, he distributed relief kits containing 26 types of items to 1,000 flood-affected people. He also distributed leases for residential land to people who had been rendered homeless by the floods, along with financial assistance to build houses. He then addressed a public meeting. During the programme, he also took a selfie with Karan Kashyap, a Class 10 student affected by the floods. See the pictures... Read the key points from CM Yogi’s speech… 1. Teachers to teach in flood relief camps for the first time CM Yogi began his speech by paying tribute to Baba Neem Karoli. He said, “I pay my respects to the sacred land of Maa Ganga and the holy land of Baba Neem Karoli. I have inspected Sadar, Kaimganj and Amritpur. Our leaders have been serving you for the past 15 days. “We are active 24 hours a day. Relief material is being provided to houses where floodwater has entered. People who are staying in their homes are also being given relief kits. These contain 26 items, including two kilograms of gram, wheat and oil. Teachers are going to relief camps to teach children affected by the floods. They are being taught separately. This has never happened before.” 2. Money to be given for potatoes stored in cold storage Yogi said the government had sought proposals to improve connectivity in villages. Some proposals had also been submitted by the elected representatives. Farrukhabad is an agricultural belt with a large number of potato farmers. He said the issue of providing money per sack for potatoes stored in cold storage had been raised at a meeting in Lucknow. “Our NDA government stands with the farmers,” he said. He said the government had increased the price of sugarcane to ₹400 per quintal, from around ₹350 earlier. “We have used technology. People here also cultivate maize. The government has made arrangements for its procurement,” he said. He said an international centre was being established in Agra with assistance from Peru for potato farmers. “Potatoes will be produced according to the kind of potatoes demanded in the market. Farmers will be provided potatoes accordingly,” he said. A survey is being conducted to assess the losses suffered by potato farmers, he added, saying the compensation would be transferred directly into their bank accounts. 3. Scooters for 50,000 final-year undergraduate women students Yogi said, “We are now going to provide scooters to 50,000 final-year undergraduate women students. They will receive scooters under the Rani Lakshmibai Scooter Scheme. “We launched the Outsourcing Services Corporation just yesterday. A total of 352,000 personnel have been brought under a structured system. Earlier, ₹12,000 used to be released by the government, but the worker received ₹10,000. We said this kind of loot would not be allowed.” 4. Earlier, the poor were given ₹4,000 and sent back Yogi said teachers had been provided with cashless medical facilities. “Now teachers will be able to secure their children’s future without fear,” he said. “Earlier, if a poor person’s house was burnt down, they were given ₹4,000 and sent back. But today the government stands with you. We have told the leaders that as soon as the floodwater recedes, the roads that have been damaged should be rebuilt immediately with the help of the PWD,” he said. 5. No one can play with the future of the youth Yogi said young people were receiving jobs without discrimination for the first time. “The youth of Farrukhabad are also getting jobs. Now no one can commit injustice or discrimination. There are many opportunities for young people in the MSME sector. The state has received investment proposals worth ₹50 lakh crore. Uttar Pradesh has attracted the highest investment in the country. This will create employment opportunities for young people. No one can play with the jobs of the youth,” he said. 6. Before 2017, the Saifai Syndicate used to emerge Yogi said, “Before 2017, this Saifai Syndicate used to emerge to grab jobs. Now, if anyone does this, they will be sent to jail.” He said good arrangements were being made for girls’ education. Kasturba Gandhi schools had been established in every block. “If a girl is educated, she will make society self-reliant,” he said. stories.title: Jeetendra Mishra takes charge as Ram Mandir’s first CEO:Former Air Marshal says, ‘Time to leave old issues behind and move forward’
stories.summary: Former Air Marshal Jitendra Mishra has taken charge as the first CEO of the Ram Temple. He arrived in Ayodhya from Delhi by flight on Thursday morning and went straight to the Ram Temple from the airport. He offered prayers and had darshan of Ram Lalla before taking charge of his new responsibility. Speaking to the media at the airport, the former Air Marshal said, “It is time to leave the past behind and move forward. I am wholeheartedly grateful to the selection committee and Lord Shri Ram, who chose me for this great and sacred task.” However, he appeared upset after seeing the media at the gate of the Teerth Kshetra office at the Ram Temple Trust. When asked questions, he said: “Look, I recognise all of you. I will not allow you to come again if you do this to me.” Besides Mishra, Govind Devgiri took charge as general secretary, while Mohan Bhagchandka assumed the post of treasurer. The Ram Temple’s new trustees, Mohan Pandey and Nirmala Yadav, also took charge. These responsibilities were assigned to them at the trust’s meeting on Wednesday (2 Sept). The changes came three months after a case involving the alleged theft of offerings at the temple came to light. New dress code for priests from Janmashtami A new dress code is being prepared for the priests serving Ram Lalla, which is expected to be implemented from Janmashtami. Eighty sets of clothing have been ordered from Varanasi for the 36 priests, of which 40 have already reached Ayodhya. The dress is yellow in colour. The lower garment will be an achala, worn like a lungi, while the upper garment will be an uttariya. Neither garment will be stitched, and neither will have pockets. Each dress set is reportedly priced at ₹7,000. Get to Know the New CEO Jeetendra Mishra is a resident of Bhopatpura village in the Bankata block of Deoria. He was commissioned into the fighter stream of the Indian Air Force from the Air Force Academy on December 6, 1986. He retired on April 30 this year. A deeply devoted follower of Lord Ram, Jeetendra Mishra was given the new responsibility of becoming the CEO of the Ram Mandir within just 125 days. His entire family lives in Delhi. His family includes his wife, Sarita Singh, and a son and a daughter. Sarita Singh has served as the president of the Air Force Wives Welfare Association (AFWWA). His father, Nathuni Mishra, was a commerce professor at Delhi University. Jeetendra Mishra's younger brother, Dr Devendra Mishra, holds an administrative position at a medical college in Delhi, while his sister, Dr Vandana Mishra, is a professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU). Jeetendra Mishra has flown more than 18 types of fighter aircraft, transport aircraft, and helicopters. Why did Jeetendra Mishra become the CEO of the Ram Mandir? 1. Participated in Operation Sindoor: Jeetendra Mishra was the head of the Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor. He was also awarded the highest war service medal (SYSM) for this role. 2. Connection with Uttar Pradesh: He hails from Deoria, Uttar Pradesh. This means that his Uttar Pradesh connection also played a role in his appointment as the CEO of the Ram Mandir Trust. Brahmins make up around 13% of Uttar Pradesh's population. Jeetendra Mishra belongs to this community. 3. Use of Air Force experience: He served in the Air Force for around 40 years and held several important commands. Therefore, his military administrative experience may be considered valuable for the temple's expanding administration, security, crowd management, and large-scale operational activities. Changes to Ram Lalla's Aarti and Bhog Arrangements A major change is also being made to the arrangements for Ram Lalla's aarti and bhog. From Ram Lalla's awakening at dawn until he retires for the night at 10 p.m., traditional devotional verses will now be sung before him during the aarti and bhog rituals. Traditional verse singers have been selected for this purpose. The new arrangement is likely to be implemented this week. It is believed that singing traditional devotional verses will make the atmosphere during Ram Lalla's aarti even more spiritually uplifting. This is expected to give devotees a distinct experience of devotion and spirituality at the temple. New dress code for priests from Janmashtami A new dress code is also being introduced for the priests of Ramlala. Preparations are underway to implement it from Janmashtami. For this purpose, 80 outfits have been ordered from Varanasi for all 36 priests. Around 40 of these outfits have already reached Ayodhya. Preparations are being made to distribute them today or tomorrow. Each priest will be given two outfits. The garments will be yellow silk, with no stitching The new dress code will consist of yellow silk garments. The lower garment will be an achala, worn like a dhoti. The upper garment will be an uttariya, which will be draped over the shoulders. These garments will have no pockets and will not be stitched. Each dress set is reportedly priced at around ₹7,000. The priests will also be provided with a second set by the end of this week. After that, all the priests will serve and worship Ramlalla only in the prescribed new dress code. Now, learn about the assets of the Ram Mandir Temple has 32 kg of gold and 1,518 kg of silver From the construction of the Shri Ram Mandir until now, 32 kg of gold and 1,518 kg of silver have been received as offerings. The silver items are sent to the Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India for melting. They are then returned to the trust in the form of 99.99% pure silver bars. The trust has kept them safe in a bank locker. Temple trust has ₹1,876 crore in cash At the trust's meeting on July 6, details were recorded regarding how much donation the temple received and where it was spent. The Shri Ram Mandir Trust has accounts with SBI, Bank of Baroda, and Punjab National Bank. A total of ₹1,876 crore is deposited in these accounts. At the time of the temple's construction, ₹3,264 crore was received as contribution funds. The temple received ₹582 crore in donations. Of this, ₹2,370 crore was spent on temple construction and ₹391 crore on management.

stories.title: Mayawati lashes out at Akash Anand, says ‘not mature yet’:Not invited to meeting; younger brother Ishan attends in his place
stories.summary: BSP supremo Mayawati has taken major action against her nephew Akash Anand, removing him from the post of national coordinator. He was also not invited to the national executive meeting held in Lucknow on Thursday. Mayawati said Akash still needs to become more mature. She said, “It would not be appropriate to give him a major responsibility in the party until then, especially as little time is now left before the elections.” She added, “Akash is not yet prepared to deal with tactics such as saam, daam, dand, bhed that opponents may use against the party.” She said: Kanshi Ram also allowed family members and relatives to assist in the party’s work, but he was not in favour of making them contest elections or giving them any position if the government was formed. I too remain committed to this view. The BSP’s objective is to ensure the participation of oppressed people in power. In this work, there is no one who is my own or an outsider. Anyone who works in the interest of the BSP and the Bahujan Samaj is welcome. Mayawati held the BSP’s national executive meeting at the party office in Lucknow. The meeting discussed preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections in five states, including Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Punjab. For the first time, her nephew Akash Anand’s younger brother, Ishan, attended the meeting. Ishan arrived wearing a BSP stole and accompanied Mayawati and his father, Anand Kumar. He remained standing with them until Mayawati took her seat. Ishan had earlier visited the party office with his brother Akash on Mayawati’s birthday in 2024. Besides Ishan, Yukesh Singh, son of late BSP MLA Umashankar Singh, also attended the meeting. Mayawati had launched both of them three days ago. See 3 pictures – More than 30 assembly in-charges announced, 50 names shortlisted The BSP has stepped up preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections. The party has so far announced in-charges for more than 30 Assembly seats, while more than 50 names are reportedly on the shortlist. The announced in-charges have also started public outreach and election-related activities in their respective Assembly constituencies.

stories.title: Son-in-law attacks sleeping in-laws with sword, 5 critically injured:Mob beats him to death with sticks in Fatehpur; was angry with wife for refusing to live with him
stories.summary: In Fatehpur, a son-in-law attacked his brother-in-law, sister-in-law, and three nephews with a sword at his in-laws' home. He first struck the three sons of his sleeping brother-in-law one after another with the sword. Hearing their screams, the brother-in-law and his wife rushed to the scene, and he attacked them on the head and neck as well. Hearing the commotion, villagers arrived at the spot. They surrounded the accused and snatched the sword from him. They then beat him to death with sticks. The incident took place in Beekampur village, under the jurisdiction of Aung police station, around 60 kilometers from the district headquarters. The accused son-in-law has been identified as Pawan Vishwakarma, a resident of Asapur. His wife had been living separately from him for about nine years. He had been involved in a dispute with his in-laws over this matter. He had gone to his in-laws' home on Wednesday. According to the family members, one of the brothers-in-law who had accompanied the son-in-law is also missing. The son-in-law had taken him along to arrange a marriage, but returned alone at night. When asked, he said that the man had stayed with relatives. The police are now searching for the missing brother-in-law. See the pictures... Know the Full Story... Mahavir's family lives in Beekampur village under the jurisdiction of Aung police station. The family consists of his two sons, Raju and Rajesh, and his daughter, Phoolkumari, also known as Seema. All of them are married. Raju has three sons and a daughter. His sons are Khatu, also known as Rajkaran (25), Pradeep (23), and Gore (20), while his daughter is Gudiya (18). Rajesh's wife's name is Buddha (37). About 26 years ago, Mahavir married his daughter Phoolkumari to Pawan, a resident of Asapur. Pawan was a carpenter. They have four children-daughters Sheetal, also known as Mansi (22), Komal (18), Radha (15), and a son, Satyam (12). Gudiya Described What She Witnessed Raju's daughter Gudiya said that her aunt Phoolkumari had been having disputes with her husband, Pawan. About nine years ago, she left her husband and began living at her parental home. Later, she went to Gujarat to stay with a relative. Pawan suspected that his in-laws were preventing the dispute between the husband and wife from being resolved. This was the reason for his anger. According to Gudiya, Pawan came to their house on Wednesday evening. He took her father, Raju (55), with him on the pretext of showing a girl for his son's marriage. Pawan returned alone at around 9 p.m. When asked about Raju, he said that Raju had stayed in the girl's village and that everyone would go to see the girl in the morning. When the family members asked him to let them speak to Raju over the phone, Pawan said that he had not brought the girl's family's mobile number. He then ate dinner and went to sleep. Attacked all three brothers Gudiya said that she was in her room, while her three brothers, Gore, Pradeep and Khatu, were sleeping outside in the veranda. At around 2 a.m., Pawan suddenly woke up and attacked all three of them with a sword. All three were injured in the attack. Hearing the screams, Rajesh and his wife Budha came outside, at which point Pawan also attacked them with a sword. When Gudiya tried to intervene, the sword struck her hand as well. She somehow managed to hide in a room and save her life. Villagers surrounded Pawan Hearing the screams and commotion, villagers reached the spot. They surrounded Pawan and snatched the sword from his hand. After this, the family members and villagers began beating him with sticks. Pawan died due to serious injuries. SP reached the spot Upon receiving information about the incident, police from several stations reached the spot. According to the police, the initial investigation revealed that Pawan's wife had been living separately for a long time. He was angry with his in-laws over this issue. The police suspect that he first took Raju with him and then returned to his in-laws' house with the intention of attacking them. Dr Rajesh Maurya, principal of the medical college, said that the condition of all four injured people is critical. All of them have deep wounds on their bodies. They have been referred to Kanpur for treatment. SP Abhimanyu Manglik said- The injured are undergoing treatment. Efforts are being made to locate Raju. Pawan's body has been sent for post-mortem.

stories.title: Air India flight makes emergency landing in Lucknow:Took off from Varanasi; smoke alarm went off in cargo compartment
stories.summary: An Air India Express flight travelling from Varanasi to Delhi had to make an emergency landing at Lucknow airport on Thursday morning (3 Sept). According to sources, a smoke alarm went off in the aircraft’s cargo compartment. The pilot immediately contacted Lucknow. As soon as clearance was received from Air Traffic Control (ATC), the aircraft was landed. Once the aircraft touched down, the response team took charge. Fire brigade personnel and technical experts also reached the spot, and the aircraft was inspected. The aircraft (IX 1253) took off from Varanasi airport at around 8 am on Thursday . Shortly afterwards, the smoke detection alarm in the cargo compartment began sounding. The pilot then landed the aircraft at Lucknow airport at 8:52 am. At 9:02 am, 155 passengers and crew members were deplaned. After the inspection, the aircraft was parked at the airport stand. Following the initial checks, it was reported that there were no signs of smoke inside the aircraft. An investigation is underway to determine why the alarm was triggered. Passengers to be sent to Delhi on another aircraft Air India has parked the aircraft at the Lucknow airport. An expert team will inspect the entire aircraft. Meanwhile, the passengers will now be sent to Delhi on another aircraft. For the time being, all passengers have been accommodated at a hotel near the airport. They will be sent to Delhi once another aircraft is arranged. Major aviation-related incidents in Uttar Pradesh in the past one-and-a-half years 19 August 2026: The tail of an IndiGo aircraft struck the ground while landing at Gorakhpur airport. The pilot then took the aircraft back into the air. After receiving clearance from ATC, the aircraft was landed again. 21 January 2026: A small Air Force aircraft had to be landed in a pond in Prayagraj due to a technical problem. Both pilots on board safely escaped using parachutes. 12 November 2025: An Air India flight arriving from Mumbai made an emergency landing in Varanasi after receiving a bomb threat. All passengers were safe. 25 May 2025: An IndiGo flight arriving from Delhi had to make an emergency landing in Varanasi due to security reasons. All passengers were safe. 14 September 2025: An IndiGo flight bound for Delhi returned and landed at Lucknow airport shortly after take-off due to a technical fault. There were 151 passengers on board, all of whom were safe. 6 May 2025: An IndiGo flight travelling from Mumbai to Gorakhpur developed a technical problem after take-off. The aircraft had to make an emergency landing at Mumbai airport. All 190 passengers on board were safe. They were later sent to Gorakhpur on another flight.

stories.title: CM Yogi to visit Gorakhpur tomorrow:Will participate in Shri Krishna Janmotsav celebrations; to felicitate teachers
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will arrive in Gorakhpur on Friday evening (4 Sept). He will attend the Shri Ram Janmotsav programme organised at the Gorakhnath Temple. On Saturday morning (5 Sept), he will listen to the problems of people attending the public grievance hearing. After that, from 10 a.m., he will attend the Teacher Felicitation Ceremony organised at the Yogiraj Baba Gambhir Nath Auditorium on the occasion of Teachers' Day. Teachers who have performed outstanding work across the state will be honoured at this programme. As every year, the Chief Minister will be present in Gorakhpur this year too on the occasion of Janmashtami. After the Shri Krishna Janmotsav celebration in the sanctum sanctorum of the Gorakhnath Temple, the CM will bring out the child form of Lord Krishna and rock him in a swing. A costume competition will also be organised at the temple during this event. The CM will present gifts to children dressed as Lord Krishna. A bhajan programme will continue at the Gorakhnath Temple until late at night. 81 teachers to be honoured with the State Teacher Award On the occasion of Teachers' Day, 81 teachers from across the state will be honoured with the State Teachers' Award in Gorakhpur on September 5. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will attend the programme as the chief guest. At the event, organised at the Yogiraj Baba Gambhirnath Auditorium, the Chief Minister will honour selected teachers from the Basic and Secondary Education departments. Among those who will be honoured are 61 teachers from the Basic Education Department and 20 teachers from Secondary Education. Each awardee will receive a cheque for ₹25,000, a memento, and a shawl. The honoured teachers will also be granted a two-year extension of service during their teaching tenure, along with free transportation facilities. This is a state-level ceremony. Selected teachers from different districts across the state will attend. The Education Department is finalising the preparations. Arrangements are being made for teachers arriving from across the state. Senior officials from the Education Department will also come from Lucknow.

stories.title: Gorakhpur, Izzatnagar Express engine’s pantograph breaks:Sparks fly from overhead wire; passengers panic
stories.summary: A major rail accident was averted at Gorakhpur Junction on Wednesday night. The 15009 Izzatnagar Express, departing from Gorakhpur, was moving from the old washing pit to enter the platform. During this time, at around 9:15 PM, the engine's pantograph suddenly broke. With the breaking of the pantograph, the engine's power connection was severed, and sparks began to fly from the overhead electric wires. Seeing the sparks between the wire and the pantograph, panic ensued among the passengers present nearby. People on the spot shouted to stop the train. A video of the incident is also going viral on social media, in which the sound of people shouting and calling to stop the train can be heard. Train stopped before reaching the platform The 15009 Izzatnagar Express was coming from the old washing pit to be placed on platform number-9 of Gorakhpur Junction. During this, sparks suddenly erupted from the engine's pantograph, and shortly after, the pantograph broke. After the pantograph broke, the engine's contact with the overhead power line was severed. The train was stopped in time, averting a major accident. Lines on the eastern side of Gorakhpur Junction affected Due to the breaking of the pantograph, all rail lines on the eastern side of Gorakhpur Junction remained affected for about an hour and a half. The railway administration was informed about the incident. Following this, the Traction Distribution department team reached the spot and began the technical process. Railway employees first lowered the engine's pantograph. After this, alternative arrangements were made to move the engine forward. Pantograph lowered at 10:20 AM According to the railway administration, the Traction Distribution Department lowered the engine's pantograph at around 10:20 PM. After this, the front pantograph of the engine was connected to the overhead equipment. Once the technical arrangements were completed, the train was given permission to proceed. Train reached the platform at 10:37 PM After the technical work was completed, the Izzatnagar Express was dispatched at 10:37 PM to be placed on the platform at Gorakhpur Junction. With this, operations on the affected rail lines on the eastern side were gradually normalised. Passengers panicked after seeing sparks At the time of the incident, when people present on the platform and nearby saw sparks flying from the overhead wire and pantograph, a situation of chaos prevailed for some time. Many people started recording videos of the incident. In no time, the video of the incident started going viral on social media.

stories.title: Manikarnika Ghat submerged in Varanasi:Cremations shift to rooftops as floodwater enters residential areas; over 10,000 homes at risk
stories.summary: The Ganga’s water level in Varanasi has crossed the warning mark, submerging 84 ghats. The rising water has also increased concern among nearly 10,000 families living in the Varuna area, who may have to leave their homes and move to safer locations if the situation worsens. Meanwhile, shopkeepers near Assi Ghat have started building temporary walls at the entrances of their shops to prevent rainwater from entering and damaging their goods. Read Dainik Bhaskar’s special report… Varuna River rises, nearly 30,000 homes at risk Flood-like conditions have emerged in the Varuna River alongside the rising Ganga, triggering concern among families living along its banks. Floodwater has reached close to nearly 30,000 homes in the vulnerable areas of Saraiya, Nakkhi Ghat, Shailputri, Shalarpur and the Varuna area. Residents begin preparing for evacuation With the water level continuing to rise, people living in these areas have started preparing to leave their homes and move to safer locations if the situation worsens. Savitri Devi said, “Water has entered our house, and we are facing a lot of difficulty. There are around 500 people in our Nakkhi Ghat area. We are staying near a well under plastic sheets so that our belongings do not get stolen from our homes. The administration has not made adequate arrangements. We travel by boat to collect our belongings from our house.” Another resident Vijay Kumar Chaubey said, “Business has declined because the water level has risen. The water has entered the lanes of Assi Ghat. We have a sari shop, but customers are no longer coming. So now we have to close it. This problem occurs every year. Who can stop Mother Ganga? Who has that much power?” Flood puts boat operators out of work Golu said, “We operate boats, but services have been suspended due to the flood. We are unable to earn even a single rupee. We also have to stay awake at night to keep watch over the boats, as they could be swept away if the water level rises suddenly.” Manikarnika Ghat submerged, floodwater enters lanes Floodwater has entered the lanes around Manikarnika and Harishchandra Ghats, while the Water Police station has also been inundated. Connectivity between the ghats has been disrupted due to the rising Ganga water level. If the water continues to rise, roads near Assi Ghat could also be affected. Water nears Ratneshwar Mahadev Temple The rising water has reached close to the spire of the Ratneshwar Mahadev Temple at Scindia Ghat. Boat operations have been completely suspended due to the rising Ganga level, leaving boatmen waiting for the water to recede. 5,000 shops across 84 ghats shut due to flooding Around 80 to 100 shops operate at each of Varanasi’s ghats, selling items such as flower garlands, tea and snacks. Although the Municipal Corporation regularly removes these temporary shops, they remain the main source of daily income for many vendors along the Ganga. Daily-wage vendors struggle as shops remain closed With the Ganga’s water level rising, all these shops have been forced to shut, leaving daily-wage vendors worried about their livelihoods. Vendors said those with ration cards are receiving food supplies, while those without them are facing significant difficulties. However, some shops in the lanes around the ghats continue to operate. We met Tinku at Assi Ghat. He told us that he has been running his shop for nearly 12 years. However, when floods occur, he has to shut down his shop. There are many such shops across the 84 ghats that have been forced to close. Some people sell flower garlands, but their livelihoods have also been affected. 1,388 families affected as Ganga and Varuna rise With the water levels of the Ganga and Varuna rivers rising in Varanasi, the district administration is continuously monitoring flood-affected areas. The Ganga water level was recorded at 70.54 metres, above the warning mark of 70.26 metres. 11 localities affected by flooding Around 11 localities and wards have been affected. A total of 1,388 people from 328 families have been impacted, while 935 people from 219 families are currently staying in 13 relief camps. Relief camps equipped with essential facilities The relief camps have arrangements for food, drinking water, bedding, lighting, sanitation and medical care. Thirty-two boats have been deployed for relief operations. Multiple agencies involved in rescue operations The police, Health Department, Municipal Corporation, Water Police and NDRF are jointly carrying out relief and rescue operations in the affected areas.

stories.title: Fake drug network from Lucknow reaches Saharanpur:Packaging setup found in Nagaal basement; 32.555 kg of medicine strips seized
stories.summary: The investigation into the supply of fake medicines in Lucknow has now reached Saharanpur. Following the questioning of Ejaz, a Saharanpur resident arrested in a case registered in Aminabad on Wednesday night, the Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) team carried out a raid in the Nangal area of Saharanpur. The team found a complete medicine-packing setup in the basement of a house. It seized a strip-packing machine, batch stereo, die punches, printed aluminium foil, 32.555kg of medicine strips and a large quantity of printed cartons. Ejaz's questioning leads investigators to Saharanpur Ejaz, a resident of Saharanpur, has been named in the FIR registered at Aminabad police station. He is accused of being involved in the supply of cheap and fake medicines. After his arrest during a joint operation by the Lucknow SOG and police, he was questioned by investigators. Information obtained during the interrogation led the FSDA team to the suspected location in Saharanpur. At a house in Kotha village under Nangal police station, the team found 41 corrugated boxes belonging to Lupin and two belonging to Macleods. A basement beneath the boxes contained a strip-packing machine, printed aluminium foil for Defcort-6, a batch stereo and different die punches. During questioning, a man identified as Vinod reportedly told the team that medicines were packed in the basement. Medicine samples from Lucknow also fail tests The operation led to the seizure of around 32.555kg of Defcort-6 strips, 973 printed cartons and 472 printed cartons of Rosuvas-F 10. The team also recovered around 6.950kg of yellow tablets and 4.900kg of white tablets. Samples of four medicines have been collected and sent for testing. All the recovered material has been sealed. In a separate investigation in Lucknow's Aminabad area, samples from two batches of Levera-500 had been sent to a government laboratory. Laboratory testing found the samples to be ‘not genuine in nature’. Records showed that around 76,790 strips had been purchased, while sales and stock together accounted for 85,832 strips. Investigators are also examining the discrepancy of 9,042 strips. Investigation reaches firms in Roorkee During questioning, investigators also came across references to several firms and locations in Roorkee, including Prizark Healthcare, Radiant Printo Pack and V-Bros Lifesciences. The FSDA is investigating their alleged roles in the network. FIRs have been registered in both the Lucknow and Saharanpur cases, and the investigation is continuing.

stories.title: Kaushambi blast: Wife of firecracker factory owner arrested:Son shot in leg and arrested in encounter; death toll reaches 14
stories.summary: Police on Thursday arrested Kahkasha Bano, wife of Naushad, the owner of the illegal firecracker factory in Kaushambi. A reward of ₹25,000 had been announced for information leading to her arrest. Earlier, at around 2 am on Wednesday, police arrested Naushad’s 18-year-old son, Adil, in an encounter. He sustained gunshot wounds to both legs and has been admitted to the district hospital. Adil injured in exchange of fire According to police, officers surrounded Adil and attempted to stop him. He turned his bike around and tried to flee, but the motorcycle skidded. He then opened fire at the police, firing two rounds. Police retaliated, and Adil was shot. 14 killed in factory explosion The death toll in the firecracker factory explosion has risen to 14, including nine children. On Tuesday morning, police arrested Adil’s father and factory owner, 50-year-old Naushad, following an encounter. He was allegedly trying to flee the city. Later that Tuesday night, a bulldozer was used to demolish Adil’s house. Accused's house demolished after 11 hours of bulldozer operation On Tuesday evening, the 3-story house belonging to Adil, the son of the main accused and firecracker factory owner Naushal, was demolished after 11 hours of bulldozer operation. This 72-square-yard house consisted of a basement and three floors. The house plan had not been approved by the Prayagraj Development Authority. This demolition action was carried out by a joint team of PDA officials and Kaushambi police. The bulldozer action began at 6 PM on Tuesday. By 5 AM on Wednesday, the entire house was razed to the ground. PDA Zonal Officer Gangesh Kumar Singh stated that commercial activities were being conducted in the basement and ground floor, while people were residing on the top two floors. On August 31, an explosion occurred in a firecracker factory, claiming 14 lives.

stories.title: Bodies of both jawans who drowned at Hathinikund Barrage found:One swept 200 km to canal in Jind; other found in UP
stories.summary: The bodies of both army personnel who went missing after drowning at the Hathnikund Barrage in Haryana’s Yamunanagar have been recovered. The first body was recovered from the Yamuna near Bartha Korsi village in Uttar Pradesh, around 15 kilometres from the barrage, on Wednesday night. The deceased has reportedly been identified as Ajay, a resident of Akhnoor in Jammu and Kashmir. The second body was carried around 200 kilometres downstream and reached the Hansi Branch canal in Jind. It was found near Amreheri village on Thursday morning. He has been identified as Aryan Patil, a resident of Maharashtra. However, the Army has not yet officially confirmed the identities of either body. The incident took place on Tuesday evening when five Army personnel jumped from a Chinook helicopter onto a boat positioned in the Yamuna during a training exercise. The boat suddenly sank. Three personnel managed to swim to safety, while two went missing. Following the incident, teams from the Army, NDRF, SDRF, police and the administration launched a search operation across Yamunanagar and the surrounding canals. Here is a step-by-step account of what happened over the two days… 1 September: Five personnel drowned at around 5 pm At around 5 pm on Tuesday, five personnel from the Van Para Special Forces jumped from a Chinook helicopter onto a motorboat positioned in the Yamuna near Hathnikund Barrage as part of a training exercise. After the personnel reached the boat, it failed to start and suddenly began sinking. The five personnel then jumped into the river wearing diving kits and life jackets. Three of them managed to swim out through the gates of the Western Yamuna Canal, while Maharashtra resident Aryan Patil and Ajay, a resident of Akhnoor in Jammu and Kashmir, went missing. The Army and local divers began the search operation that night. 2 September: Body of one personnel recovered at night On Wednesday, teams from the Haryana and Uttar Pradesh SDRF joined the Army in the search operation. Surveillance was also carried out using helicopters. As the search continued, routes between Haryana and Uttar Pradesh near the barrage were closed. Ten Army teams conducted a search across a 15-kilometre area. Water in the Western Yamuna Canal was stopped for an hour to lower the water level and facilitate the search. Army personnel entered the canal and formed a human chain while searching for the missing personnel. In the evening, two life jackets and a diving kit were found at Dadupur Head, around 15 kilometres from the barrage. However, the Army did not disclose whether the items belonged to the missing personnel. At night, the body of one Army personnel was found near Bartha Korsi village in Uttar Pradesh’s Saharanpur district. The Irrigation Department informed the Army about the recovery.

stories.title: SP leader close to Azam Khan sent to jail:Spends night in high-security ward over land-grab, assault case in Gorakhpur; city chief absconding
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Zafar Amin Dakku, considered close to senior party leader Azam Khan, was sent to jail by police on Wednesday night in connection with a land dispute and assault case in Gorakhpur. Dakku was kept in a high-security cell in jail, where he reportedly spent the night in distress. Police have launched raids to arrest other accused, including SP city president Shabbir Qureshi. Dakku has been a prominent SP leader in Gorakhpur and was reportedly close to Azam Khan during the previous SP government. According to local accounts, Khan would often visit Dakku's house whenever he came to Gorakhpur and mention him at public events. Dakku remains at police stations for 18 hours Police detained Dakku late on Tuesday night after a complaint alleged an attempt to take over land and assault women. From Wednesday morning, senior SP leaders began gathering at Kotwali and Rajghat police stations. SP leaders alleged that police kept moving Dakku between different police stations throughout the day and mentally harassed him. They claimed police repeatedly told them that Dakku would be released after being booked for disturbing public order. However, police later completed the paperwork and sent him to jail. SP leaders also alleged that Dakku was detained around 2.30 am but remained at the police station for nearly 18 hours before being sent to jail. Four teams formed to arrest absconding accused Based on a complaint by Shahna Khatun, Rajghat police registered a case on Tuesday against 10 people, including Zafar Amin Dakku and SP city president Shabbir Qureshi, under serious sections related to the land dispute and alleged assault. Kotwali Circle Officer Omkar Dutt said law and order remained under control and four teams had been formed to trace the absconding accused. Police search Qureshi's house, check cupboards and coolers Police carried out a series of raids from midnight on Tuesday until around 4 am on Wednesday. One of the teams reached Shabbir Qureshi's house late at night. Police searched different rooms and reportedly checked cupboards, a refrigerator and coolers while looking for the SP leader. Around 1 am, Rajghat and Kotwali police teams reached Qureshi's house in Ismailpur. Female police personnel were also part of the team. The search continued for around an hour and covered the rooms and terrace. Qureshi's family alleged that police also checked the water tank, cupboards, refrigerator and coolers. A video of the raid has also gone viral on social media. According to the family, police repeatedly asked them to call Qureshi on his mobile phone, but the phone was switched off. Dakku has contested Assembly elections twice Zafar Amin Dakku, a resident of Khokhar Tola under Rajghat police station, is considered close to Azam Khan. Dakku contested an Assembly election from the urban seat for the first time in 1991. He later contested the 2012 Assembly election from Gorakhpur Rural on an SP ticket. He secured 41,864 votes in the 2012 election but lost by 16,985 votes to BJP candidate Vijay Bahadur Yadav. What is the dispute about? The dispute began on Tuesday over a plot of Deeh land in Khokhar Tola under Rajghat police station. According to the complaint, Zafar Amin Dakku allegedly reached the site with his supporters and SP city president Shabbir Qureshi and began removing a tin shed and pipes installed on the land. When women objected, an argument reportedly broke out between the two sides. Rajghat police later registered a case based on Shahna Khatun's complaint against Dakku, Qureshi and others over alleged attempts to take possession of the land, assault and threats to kill. Woman claims family has occupied house for 70 years In her complaint, Shahna Khatun said her family had been occupying a house in Khokhar Tola for around 70 years. She claimed the house stood on Deeh land recorded as Araji No. 91. According to her complaint, the land belonged to former landlord Vallabhdas, who had given it to her ancestors to build a house and live there. Khatun alleged that Dakku took possession of half of the house in 2023. She claimed that on Tuesday, Dakku, Qureshi and their supporters returned and attempted to take possession of the remaining portion. She said she objected and told them that the land dispute was already pending before a court. Khatun alleged that she was then abused and assaulted and threatened with death. She was reportedly rescued after local residents intervened. She has told police that she fears for her life and sought action against those involved. Police install CCTV cameras at disputed site Following the dispute, police and administrative officials took note of the situation. Rajghat police installed two CCTV cameras at the disputed site to monitor activity and prevent further attempts at encroachment or fresh clashes. The revenue department has also been directed to examine the land records and verify the claims made by both sides. Police say social media video led to case City SP Nimish Patil said a video circulating on social media showed some people allegedly assaulting and behaving indecently with women during a dispute over possession of land. Based on the complaint, a case was registered at Rajghat police station and the main accused, Zafar Amin Dakku, was taken into police custody, he said. Patil added that four teams had been formed to arrest the remaining accused and further action was underway.

stories.title: Ram Mandir CEO’s uncle says, ‘He will now serve God’:Jai Shri Ram’ slogans raised in Deoria village; locals call it reward for honesty
stories.summary: Former Air Marshal Jitendra Mishra has become the first CEO of the Ayodhya Ram Mandir Trust. The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust announced this on Wednesday, September 2. He led the Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor and served in the Air Force for 39 years. Jitendra Mishra is originally from Bhopatpura village in Bankata, located 60 km from the Deoria district headquarters. There is a celebratory atmosphere in the village since his appointment as CEO. Sweets were distributed, and chants of 'Jai Shri Ram' were raised. Jitendra Mishra's uncle said, "My nephew served the country earlier, and now he will serve Lord Ram." The Dainik Bhaskar team reached his village and spoke to his family members. Read the full report... Jitendra's uncle, Rampyare Mishra, who lives in Bhopatpura village, has been a head clerk at Malviya Inter College. He says - There was an atmosphere of education and discipline in the family from the very beginning. My elder brother and Jitendra's father, Nathuni Mishra, was a professor at JNU. One son is pursuing a PhD in London, the other is doing B.Tech Rampyare Mishra says - My brother's family has been living in Delhi for a long time. Jitendra's younger brother, Devendra Mishra, is also a Managing Director at Maulana Azad Hospital in Delhi. My sister-in-law and Jitendra's mother, Saraswati Devi, live with them in Delhi. Jitendra's wife, Vatsala Devi, is a homemaker. They have two sons, Saranya and Shantanu. Saranya is pursuing a PhD from London, while Shantanu is pursuing a B.Tech. Uncle said - Nephew got the opportunity to serve Lord Ram Rampyare Mishra has been a head clerk at Malviya Inter College. He expressed happiness over Jitendra Mishra's appointment. He said that his nephew has served the country for a long time while being in the Indian Air Force. Now he has received the responsibility of work related to Lord Shri Ram. This is a matter of pride for both the family and the village. Jitendra Mishra had come to the village after his father's death The uncle mentioned that Jitendra Mishra's father, Nathuni Mishra, passed away in 2022. Following this, a ceremony was held in their ancestral village, Bhopatpura, which Jitendra Mishra attended. Since then, the family has maintained a constant connection with the village over the phone. However, due to Jitendra's education and subsequent military service, he spent most of his time in Delhi. Villagers said - It is a matter of pride for us As soon as the news of Jitendra Mishra being appointed as the CEO of the Ram Mandir Trust reached the village on Wednesday, an atmosphere of joy spread among his family members and villagers. Chants of 'Jai Shri Ram' began to echo. The villagers say that for someone from Bhopatpura to have become an Air Marshal in the Air Force and now to receive such a major responsibility in the Ram Mandir Trust is a matter of pride for the entire region. Neighbors say - Received a reward for honesty Jagdish Mishra, an elder and relative living in the village, says - Jitendra has served in the armed forces. It feels very good that he has been entrusted with such a big responsibility now. Another relative, Daya Shankar Mishra, said that this is a matter of great honor and prestige. Jitendra is a very honest person. He has received this as a reward for his honesty. Prime Minister Narendra Modi himself had shaken his hand and patted him on the back. BJP leader said - A moment of pride for our region BJP leader Rajkumar Shahi stated - Jitendra Mishra is a resident of our assembly constituency. He had also done very courageous and historic work in the army. It was a coincidence that the members of the Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra committee selected him for the post of CEO. This is a moment of great pride for Bankata block, Bhatpar Rani assembly constituency, Deoria district, and UP. In this regard, we are very happy. It feels as if someone from our own home and courtyard has become the CEO. For this, I also thank God that Jitendra will get the opportunity to serve Shri Ram. As long as he was in service, he protected the country. Today, he will again be engaged in protecting our culture. Appointment made after theft of offerings in Ram Mandir The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust announced the appointment of former Air Marshal Jitendra Mishra as the first CEO of the Ayodhya Ram Mandir Trust. His appointment comes 3 months after the case of theft of offerings in the Ram Mandir came to light. Why was Jitendra Mishra made the CEO? Hero image in Operation Sindoor: Jitendra Mishra was the head of the Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor. He also received the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal (SYSM) for this role. Connection to UP: He hails from Deoria, Uttar Pradesh. This means his UP connection is also a factor in the appointment of the Ram Mandir Trust CEO. Use of military experience: He served in the Air Force for nearly 40 years and held several important commands. In this context, his military administrative experience can be considered significant for the temple's growing administration, security, crowd management, and large-scale operational tasks. Brahmin face: Brahmins make up about 13% of the population in UP. Jitendra Mishra comes from this community. Brahmin votes play a decisive role in forming the government in the state.

stories.title: Krishna Janmashtami on September 4:Know puja vidhi; Grihastha, Vaishnava devotees to observe fast same day, Kashi astrologer shares auspicious muhurat
stories.summary: Shri Krishna Janmashtami will be celebrated on Friday, September 4. Both householders and followers of the Vaishnava tradition will observe the Janmashtami fast and celebrate Lord Krishna’s birth on the same day, ending the confusion over whether the festival would fall on September 4 or 5. Ashtami must prevail at midnight to determine date According to a Kashi-based astrologer, the date of Janmashtami is not determined simply by checking when the Ashtami tithi begins. The key factor is whether Ashtami prevails during the midnight period traditionally considered the time of Lord Krishna’s birth. Ashtami continues through midnight on September 4 According to Panchang calculations, the Ashtami tithi of Krishna Paksha in the month of Bhadrapada will begin at 2:25 am on September 4 and continue until 12:13 am on September 5. As Ashtami will be in effect at midnight on September 4, the Janmashtami fast and celebration of Lord Krishna’s appearance will be observed that day. Harshan Yoga will prevail until 3:44 pm on Janmashtami September 4 will begin with Harshan Yoga, which will continue until 3:44 pm. Vajra Yoga will then begin and remain in effect until 12:47 pm on September 5. Mrigashira Nakshatra to coincide with Vajra Yoga at midnight Rohini Nakshatra will remain in effect until 11:04 pm on September 4, after which Mrigashira Nakshatra will begin. Therefore, at the prescribed midnight time for Lord Shri Krishna’s birth worship, Mrigashira Nakshatra and Vajra Yoga will coincide. Janmashtami worship begins with Gauri-Ganesha puja and Kalash sthapana According to Kashi-based astrologer and Professor Vinay Pandey, “Janmashtami is not only about rituals; devotion is equally important. Devotees celebrate Lord Shri Krishna’s birth by worshipping him in his child form, accepting him as a member of their family and as their own son.” Gauri-Ganesha worship performed before waiting for Krishna’s birth The rituals begin with the worship of Gauri-Ganesha and the installation of the sacred Kalash. Lord Ganesha is worshipped to ensure that the rituals are completed without obstacles, while Lord Varuna is invoked in the Kalash. Devotees then wait for the midnight birth of Lord Shri Krishna. Some traditions depict Krishna’s birth through a cucumber or lamps Professor Vinay Pandey explained that different parts of the country follow different folk traditions to celebrate Krishna Janmashtami. In some regions, the sentiment of Krishna’s birth is expressed by making him appear from a cucumber. In others, a dark room is suddenly illuminated with lamps at midnight to symbolise the Lord’s manifestation. Krishna’s child form is bathed with milk or Panchamrit In many places, devotees celebrate the birth by bathing the child form of Lord Krishna with milk or Panchamrit. These traditions reflect the devotion of devotees who accept Krishna as their own child. Krishna’s birth is seen as divine manifestation, not ordinary birth From a religious perspective, Lord Shri Krishna is considered unborn. Therefore, his birth is not viewed as that of an ordinary living being, but as the divine manifestation of his incarnation and a sacred act of divine play. Observe the Janmashtami fast while chanting Krishna’s name According to Subhash, associated with the BHU Department of Astrology, “Devotees should observe a fast as far as possible and spend Janmashtami in kirtan and devotion to Lord Shri Krishna. Chanting the Lord’s name and singing devotional songs are considered important parts of the festival’s devotional tradition.” Chant Krishna’s names and offer seasonal fruits and sattvic food Devotees can chant names of the Lord such as “Shri Krishna Govinda Hare Murari, He Nath Narayana Vasudeva” and “Govinda Damodara Madhave”. Seasonal fruits, sattvic dishes and other offerings can also be presented to the Lord. Arghya and Madhuparka offered to mark Krishna’s birth There is also a tradition of celebrating Lord Krishna’s birth by offering arghya and Madhuparka. These rituals are performed as part of the devotional observance of Janmashtami. Janmashtami celebrations will light up temples and homes On Janmashtami, Krishna temples across the country are specially decorated for the festival. Many temples create tableaux depicting a prison to represent the place where Lord Krishna was born. At midnight, when the Lord’s birth is commemorated, conch shells and bells are sounded, while devotees raise celebratory slogans. Homes are decorated like temples for Bal Gopal Householders also decorate their home shrines like temples and adorn idols of Bal Gopal or Laddu Gopal. Women sing auspicious songs and sohar, while family members come together to celebrate Lord Krishna’s birth. Devotees also pray for children and marriage Janmashtami worship is also associated with prayers for wishes related to children and marriage. Devotees seek the Lord’s blessings while celebrating his birth with their families. Why and when do householders and followers of the Vaishnava sect celebrate Janmashtami on different days?
