stories.title: How strong is Amarmani’s claim to contest from Pharenda:Has he found a way around 6-year election ban after completing sentence?
stories.summary: After completing his life imprisonment sentence for the murder of young poet Madhumita Shukla from Lakhimpur Kheri, Amarmani Tripathi wants to be active in politics once again. He announced this at a programme in the Pharenda assembly constituency of Maharajganj district on August 30. He claimed that he would contest the 2027 assembly elections from Pharenda himself, while his son Amanmani Tripathi would contest from Nautanwa. The question is, can 70-year-old Amarmani Tripathi, who has been released after serving a life sentence, contest elections? His area of operation has been Nautanwa, from where he was elected MLA four times. In such a situation, why was Pharenda chosen? If Amarmani does not get legal permission to contest the election himself, what could be his Plan-B? Read this report... Amarmani increasing political activity Since completing his sentence, Amarmani Tripathi has increased his political activity. He is participating in various programmes held in the Nautanwa and Pharenda regions. On August 30, he attended a dialogue program at Krishna Marriage Hall in Anandnagar. His uncle and former minister Shyam Narayan Tripathi was also present with him. While addressing this program, Amarmani announced that he would contest the next assembly election from Pharenda. Later, his son and former Nautanwa MLA Amanmani Tripathi also supported his statement and appealed to the people to ensure his victory. Can a person who has served a sentence contest an election? BJP leader and lawyer Ashwini Upadhyay had filed a petition in the Supreme Court demanding a lifetime ban on convicted politicians from contesting elections. The Supreme Court had sought a response from the Central Government on this in February 2025. At that time, the Central Government, while filing an affidavit, clarified that the Parliament has already determined the conditions for electoral disqualification under the Representation of the People Act. Under Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act (RP Act, 1951), if a person is sentenced to 2 years or more, they become disqualified from contesting elections while in jail and for 6 years after their release. The Central Government also clarified in court that a lifetime ban cannot be imposed on convicted politicians. They can contest elections 6 years after completing their sentence. Will Amarmani get legal exemption? Amarmani was released in August 2023 on the grounds of 'good conduct' following a Supreme Court order. Now, the legal debate has centered on whether he will be considered eligible to file nominations in 2027 immediately after his release, or if a 6-year cooling-off period will apply. Regarding this, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to his son, Amanmani Tripathi. He stated, “My father, Amarmani Tripathi, has not made any claim out of thin air. We have taken legal advice on this. There are sufficient documents and grounds to contest the election.” Why did Amarmani choose Pharenda instead of Nautanwa? Amarmani Tripathi himself has already given the answer to this at a program in Anand Nagar. He had said from the stage that my family has been involved in politics while living among the public for a long time. Our relationship is not limited only to elections. We always stand with our people in their joys and sorrows. My family has been serving the public for three generations. Amarmani Tripathi's uncle and former minister Shyam Narayan Tripathi has been an MLA from Pharenda 5 times. Shyam Narayan Tripathi was also convicted in a murder case, which was pardoned by the President. After this, Shyam Narayan Tripathi was elected MLA from Pharenda. This means Pharenda is the seat that can facilitate this family's political comeback. Shyam Narayan Tripathi has now grown old. Amanmani Tripathi himself is active in Nautanwa. He has also been an MLA from there once from 2017 to 2022. In such a situation, Amarmani Tripathi has chosen the Pharenda seat himself. Does Amarmani also have a Plan B ready? What will happen if, for any reason, Amarmani is not granted permission to contest the election, or if his nomination is rejected based on the provisions of the Representation of the People Act? His son, Amanmani Tripathi, provided the answer to this as well. He said, "I have a joint family. There are many people in the family who are eligible to contest the election. Although such a situation will not arise, if it does happen for any reason, someone else from the family will step in." This means the Tripathi family also has a 'Plan B' ready for Pharenda. Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh says, "Amarmani Tripathi's statement could also be a part of pressure politics. He holds influence in districts like Maharajganj, Gorakhpur, and the surrounding areas. Amarmani Tripathi himself has been associated with the BSP, Congress, SP, and the Communist Party. He has also served as a minister in the BJP government." However, at present, this family is not in any party. Often, such statements are also made to demonstrate one's political weight. It is also possible that by making these statements, he wants to prepare a safe pitch for his son, Amanmani Tripathi, in Nautanwa. Political Equation of Pharenda Assembly Constituency The Pharenda assembly constituency has always been a center of Brahmin and Kshatriya (Thakur) politics. Amarmani's uncle, Shyam Narayan Tripathi, had a strong hold in the Pharenda region. Amarmani is now trying to regain his political ground through the same old family influence and emotional card. The number of Brahmin, Nishad, Muslim, and other OBC voters is decisive in Pharenda. Apart from this, there is also a large number of Maurya, Sainthwar, and Dalit voters. Amarmani's focus is on creating a new equation by connecting his traditional Brahmin cadre and the non-Yadav Other Backward Classes (OBC). Virendra Chaudhary of the Congress is currently the MLA for the Pharenda assembly seat. Last time, he defeated BJP candidate and former MLA Bajrang Bahadur Singh in a close contest. Bajrang Bahadur Singh has been an MLA from this seat three times. Before him, Shyam Narayan Tripathi used to be elected as the MLA from this seat. How much impact will this have on Purvanchal politics? The 2027 assembly election will be a battle for survival for the 'Tripathi family'. After coming out of jail, Amarmani would want to re-establish the political existence of his family in Purvanchal by winning the Pharenda and Nautanwa seats. Amarmani becoming active could prove to be a major factor in consolidating the Brahmin vote bank in Purvanchal politics. Amarmani started his political career with the Communist Party of India. He became an MLA for the first time in 1989. He then became an MLA again in 1996, 2002, and 2007. During this period, he was associated with the Congress, BSP, and SP. In 2002-03, he was a minister in the Mayawati government. Prior to this, he had also served as a minister in the BJP governments led by Kalyan Singh (1997), Ram Prakash Gupta (1999), and Rajnath Singh (2000). He was in the SP at the time of his arrest in the Madhumita murder case. the Madhumita murder case Madhumita was a poet. On May 9, 2003, she was shot dead in her 2-room apartment in Lucknow's Paper Mill Colony. At that time, she was 24 years old and 7 months pregnant. Madhumita's post-mortem report revealed that there was a foetus in her womb, which matched the DNA of Amarmani Tripathi. Meanwhile, Amarmani Tripathi was born on February 14, 1956. His father had also been an MLA from the Nautanwa assembly constituency. His son, Amanmani, contested the election from Nautanwa on a Samajwadi Party ticket in 2012 but lost by a narrow margin. In 2017, Amanmani Tripathi succeeded in winning from Nautanwa but lost again in 2022.

stories.title: IAS Divya brought water to this village:People once needed ration cards for tankers, queued at waterfall 5 km away | Part -1
stories.summary: “Since we were born, we have depended on springs and water tankers. We would sit near the spring from 8 pm to collect water the next morning. Divya Mittal came to us like a god. She brought water to our village.” These are the words of Rakesh Yadav, a resident of Lahuriyadah village in Mirzapur. Like Rakesh, nearly 90% of the villagers credit former IAS officer Divya Mittal with changing the fate of their village. Villagers once walked 5 km for drinking water Divya Mittal took charge as the District Magistrate of Mirzapur in September 2022. During a visit to Lahuriyadah, villagers told her they had to walk nearly 5 km to fetch clean drinking water. Moved by their plight, Mittal told them, “I will not drink the water here until water reaches this village.” A year later, water finally reached Lahuriyadah After nearly a year of efforts, the villagers’ long-standing wait finally ended as drinking water was supplied to the village. Mittal was transferred from Mirzapur a few months later, in September 2023. Divya Mittal’s resignation brings village story back into focus On August 30, 2026, Mittal resigned from government service. Her work in Lahuriyadah, where access to drinking water transformed daily life, has now brought the village back into the spotlight. Read the full report... Water was provided upon showing a ration card Located on the UP-MP border, about 65 km from the Mirzapur district headquarters, this village received water four years ago based on ration cards. The villagers said that each person was given only 15 liters of water. This village is situated atop Hanumana Hill. Many times, even water tankers could not reach it. In such situations, the villagers had to walk 5 km through the forest. They would collect water seeping from the mountain in containers and bring it back. Until 2022, there was no tap-water facility for drinking water in the village. Women Were Insulted While Loading Water onto Trucks In the village, we met Kamla Devi Kesarwani, who runs a roadside shop. She said, "We used to travel 5 km to Bhainsor to fetch water. We would load water onto the trucks returning from there. The truck drivers would make lewd and abusive remarks. But we had no choice, so we had to tolerate everything." Kamla further said, "In 2022, Divya Mittal visited our village. The village is situated on a mountain at a considerable height. Water could not be brought here through pipes. So, she finalized a project to build a water tank. She did exactly what she had promised. She did not invite any MP or MLA to the inauguration. Because of this, MP Anupriya Patel had her transferred." We were forced to drink rainwater Vikas Kumar, who runs a shop in Lahuriyadah, was filling containers at his home with water during heavy rain. When asked why he said, “We use it to wash the dirty utensils from the shop. Divya Mittal brought water to our homes through taps and pipes. Before her, we had told several officials about our problem, but no one listened to us.” She left after building stairways to heaven for the village Dainik Bhaskar’s team travelled deeper into the village through the rain and met Rakesh Yadav, who was sitting with his family. Recalling the days before drinking water reached the village, He said, “Earlier, we would constantly travel between Bhainsor and Drummondganj to arrange water. Every member of the family, including my wife and children, was involved in fetching it.” ‘Fetching water was our only job’ Rakesh added, “Collecting water throughout the day and carrying it back home was our only routine. Just as people carry a kanwar on their shoulders, my wife and children would carry two containers of water on their shoulders. When this officer came, water finally reached our village. By bringing water to the village, she has earned a place in heaven.” Water was available only after paying ₹1,500–2,000 for weddings Hirawati lives at one end of the village. Her husband has passed away. Recalling the severe water shortage, she says, “Whenever there was a wedding in the village, a water tanker would arrive only after paying ₹1,500–2,000. The shortage was so severe that we would go and sleep near the spring. We would get our turn after three to four days, and only then could we collect water.” Tap installed, but no water supply for six days Reeta Adivasi, another villager said, “The installation of a tap outside her house has not fully resolved the problem.” She added, “It has been six days since the tap was installed, but no water has come through it. We are collecting rainwater and using it for drinking as well as other household needs.” After 32 years, I have finally seen a water tap in the village Gaurishankar Adivasi from the village says, “I am 32 years old. I have finally seen a water tap in the village. The biggest change after the water supply began is that now one member of the household does not have to sit near the spring.” He added, “That person can attend to other household chores, and the children can also go to school. Earlier, they too were sent to the spring to fetch water.” When asked are the children able to go to school? he said, “The school currently available is 4 km away. There is a forest along the way. Therefore, we are afraid to send the children there.” People said-if Divya contests the election, they will support her. There is speculation in political circles that Divya Mittal may contest the election from Mirzapur. BJP spokesperson Prashant Umrao has claimed that Divya will contest the election on a Congress ticket. People on social media are also making similar predictions. Residents of Lahuriyadah village say, “If Divya Mittal enters the electoral fray, we will fully support her.” But what do the people of Mirzapur city think about Divya Mittal? We visited Mirzapur city to find out. We will share the full story in the next part.

stories.title: Farmer hacked to death with sword in Ghaziabad:He did not get up after falling to the ground, row began over refusing to call accused ‘brother’
stories.summary: In Ghaziabad, a farmer was hacked to death with a sword during a quarrel over not addressing someone as "brother." When the farmer's family members rushed to save him, the neighbours also attacked them. During the confrontation, members of both families came face to face. Sticks, clubs, swords, and knives were used by both sides. Police reached the spot after receiving information from local residents. The injured were admitted to a hospital for treatment, where doctors declared the farmer dead. Two boys injured in the clash are undergoing treatment. The accused have been absconding since the incident. The incident took place at 4 p.m. on Sunday in Kannauja village of Muradnagar. 3 pictures related to the incident ... A neighbour said, “You call me by my name? Wait, I'll teach you a lesson now” Ajay Sharma, a resident of Kanoja village, was leaving his house at around 4 p.m. on Sunday evening. On the way, he met Sonu Sharma, who lived in the neighborhood. Ajay said, "Sonu, are you fine?" Sonu became angry over this. He angrily said to Ajay, "How dare you call me by my name? Call me Sonu Bhai." After this, an argument broke out between the two. Soon, the two began fighting. Meanwhile, Sonu called his family members. Ajay also called his family and friends during the fight and asked them to come. People from both sides arrived at the spot carrying sticks, swords, and knives. They then attacked each other with swords and knives. During the incident, Ajay's uncle Devendra suffered deep wounds to his abdomen and shoulder from a sword. He died in the hospital during treatment. ACP says police are conducting raids to arrest the accused Injured Ankit said that the attackers included Mohit Sharma, Sonu Sharma, Mohit, Prince, Vikas and Deepu Sharma. They came carrying swords in their hands. Following information about the incident, ACP Masuri Sunil Bhardwaj and DCP Rural Surendranath Tiwari also reached the spot. ACP Masuri Sunil Bhardwaj said that at around 4 p.m. in Kannauja, an argument broke out between two groups over an exchange of words. Devendra Sharma died during treatment. Based on a complaint from the victim's family, a murder case has been registered against one of the attackers.

stories.title: Madhumita murder convict Amar Mani to contest elections:Announces bid at rally in Maharajganj, says ‘if anyone can compete, tell me’
stories.summary: Amarmani Tripathi, the killer of poetess Madhumita Shukla, has announced that he will contest the 2027 Assembly elections from Maharajganj. Amarmani appeared in public after nearly 20 years. He said, "I will contest the election from Pharenda in 2027. My son Amanmani will contest from Nautanwa. If there is anyone who can take him on, let me know." A public interaction programme was organized at 4 p.m. on Sunday at Krishna Marriage Hall in Anandnagar. Amarmani met people at the event. Amarmani said, "The youth have changed governments in Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, and Nepal. In India, Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan had to resign under pressure from the youth." He said, ‘My family has been among the people for three generations’ Amarmani Tripathi said, "Our family has been involved in politics while remaining among the people for a long time. Our relationship with the public is not limited to elections. We will continue to remain among the people and stand by them in their joys and sorrows." He also mentioned his long-standing association with the Farenda Assembly constituency. Supporters showed enthusiasm while Amarmani was present on the stage. Former Minister of State for Persons with Disabilities Shyam Narayan Tiwari, along with a large number of party workers and supporters, was present at the event. Amanmani says, ‘Make my father win from Pharenda’ Former Nautanwa MLA Amanmani Tripathi also sought support for his father. He appealed to people to ensure Amarmani's victory from Pharenda. Amanmani took a dig at Congress's incumbent MLA Virendra Chaudhary, saying that after contesting elections several times, he won this time due to the public's sympathy. He levelled serious allegations against former BJP MLA Bajrang Bahadur Singh. He said that the former MLA had amassed assets worth thousands of crores through gravel theft and contracting. He said that there was a need to rein in such people. In the political battle, the public should support his family. However, Amar Mani Tripathi has not announced that he will contest the election on a ticket from any party. But since Amar Mani's return, political activity has begun in Maharajganj. Recently, during the inauguration of a private hospital in Nautanwa, his supporters raised slogans of "Long live Amar Mani Tripathi." Since then, there has been speculation about him contesting the election. Amarmani lost his legislative seat after being sentenced to life imprisonment Assembly elections were held in Uttar Pradesh in 2007. The BSP had expelled Amarmani from the party. However, the SP fielded him from the Nautanwa seat in Maharajganj. Amarmani won the election while he was in jail. But just a few months later, on October 24, 2007, a Dehradun special court sentenced him to life imprisonment in the Madhumita murder case, and he consequently lost his legislative seat as well. It may be noted that Amar Mani Tripathi and his wife Madhumani were sentenced to life imprisonment in the Madhumita Shukla murder case. After spending nearly 20 years in jail, both were released in 2023. Amarmani spent 10 years of his sentence in the hospital by pretending to be "ill" Amarmani was initially lodged in Roshanabad Jail in Haridwar, where his wife Madhumani was also imprisoned. Later, by 2012, both were transferred to Gorakhpur Jail. But exactly a year after arriving at the jail, on February 13, 2013, Amarmani reached Gorakhpur's Baba Raghav Das (BRD) Medical College on the pretext of receiving treatment. He then stayed there for the next 10 years. The couple made Room No. 16 of the hospital's psychiatry department their permanent residence. Police guards were stationed outside. Although Amarmani remained in the hospital as a VIP prisoner, he was fully active in his ancestral constituency of Nautanwa, around 80 kilometers away. From the hospital itself, he strengthened the political career of his son, Amanmani Tripathi. In 2017, he got him elected as an independent MLA.

stories.title: Hindu Yuva Vahini’s Lucknow division in-charge murdered:Driver allegedly abducted him, shot him and dumped his body in canal
stories.summary: Hindu activist leader Dhirendra Pratap Singh, who was kidnapped from Lucknow's Sushant Golf City area, was murdered. His body was recovered around 5 p.m. on Sunday from a small canal in Sarai Premraj Nagar, Dubagga. Dhirendra lived in the PGI area and was originally from Unnao. He was in charge of the Lucknow division of the Hindu Yuva Vahini. Initial investigations suggest that the murder was linked to a dispute over land in Unnao. His wife had accused Dhirendra's driver of carrying out the murder in collusion with his rivals. Police have detained two suspects, including the driver, and are questioning them. Body found lying face down in canal At around 5 p.m. on Sunday, passersby spotted a man's body lying face down in a small canal located in Sarai Premraj Nagar. Police reached the spot, pulled the body out of the canal, and began efforts to identify it. The police shared a photograph of the body on social media and in police groups. Meanwhile, the photograph was matched with the report filed by Dhirendra at the Sushant Golf City police station. The body was subsequently identified as that of Dhirendra Pratap Singh. Kidnapping case had been registered on his wife's complaint According to DCP South M. Mushtaq, Dhirendra was reported missing on Saturday, 29 August. On Sunday, 30 August, the case was amended to include charges of kidnapping and murder based on a complaint filed by his wife, Mamta Singh. She had alleged that Dhirendra's driver had kidnapped him with the help of his accomplices. Six police teams were formed to investigate the case. The teams were searching for Dhirendra and working to solve the case through surveillance and CCTV footage. During the investigation, it emerged that the driver had murdered Dhirendra with the help of his accomplices. Body and vehicle recovered, two suspects detained According to DCP South, Dhirendra's body and the vehicle in which the murder is suspected to have taken place have been recovered. Two key suspects, including the driver, have been detained and are being questioned. The body is being sent for a post-mortem examination after the inquest proceedings. The police officer said that the preliminary investigation revealed a dispute over land in Unnao. The role of other people in the case is also being investigated. Strict action will be taken against all the accused involved in the incident.

Will IAS officer Divya Mittal contest from Mirzapur?:MP Anupriya Patel sought her transfer; speculation grows after her resignation
stories.summary: Political discussions have intensified over whether UP IAS officer Divya Mittal, who has resigned from the civil service, will contest an election. Divya served as Mirzapur District Magistrate for the longest period of her career. During her tenure, she had confrontations with MP Anupriya Patel and Uttar Pradesh government minister Ashish Patel. Both are alleged to have used their influence to get her transferred out of Mirzapur. Divya was transferred to Basti but did not join there. Later, when she became the District Magistrate of Deoria, she had a dispute with MLA Shalabh Mani Tripathi. Following this, she was sent to the Revenue Board. She has now decided to resign from her post. Since then, social media has been abuzz with speculation about her entering politics and possibly contesting from Mirzapur. First reason: The language of her resignation message In an emotional message shared on social media, Divya Mittal made a special mention of Mirzapur. She wrote: “Deoria taught me that standing with what is right is not an option, but a duty. Mirzapur taught me that ‘impossible’ is not a fact, just an opinion.” She also wrote that, while sitting at the feet of Maa Vindhyavasini, she learnt that true power does not come from any position, but from the goddess’s grace and the trust of the people. Divya described the blessing of an elderly woman living on the hill in Lahuriadah village as a moment she would never forget. When tap water reached the village for the first time, the woman silently blessed her by placing her trembling hands on Divya’s head. Second reason: She remains connected with Mirzapur’s villages and village heads During her tenure as District Magistrate, Divya Mittal visited hundreds of villages. According to local sources, she remains in contact with around 200 village heads (Gram Pradhans). The relationships built during her tenure through development projects, drinking water schemes, road construction and public hearings have continued even after she left the post. It is being said that she remains in regular communication with village heads and continues to discuss various local issues with them. Third reason: The Rakshabandhan connection Recently, on the occasion of Rakshabandhan, many people from Mirzapur approached Divya Mittal to have rakhis tied by her. The tradition of celebrating the sacred brother-sister bond strengthened the emotional connection between her and the people of the district. Although she is no longer in office, many people continue to regard her as their daughter and sister. Fourth reason: Her recent visit to Mirzapur Divya Mittal visited Mirzapur for three days in July in connection with a review of Revenue Department work. During the visit, she first paid her respects at the court of Maa Vindhyavasini and then visited Sarnath Mahadev Temple. She also reviewed the new Collectorate building and visited areas including Kachhwa, where she had undertaken development work during her tenure. People welcomed her with garlands at several places. Becoming emotional, Divya Mittal said that she could never forget the love she had received from Mirzapur. Earlier, a photograph of her enjoying a swing during Sawan had also gone viral, with the image reflecting her connection with the local culture. One-year tenure in Mirzapur Divya Mittal served as Mirzapur District Magistrate from September 17, 2022, to September 1, 2023. Her biggest achievement during this period was bringing piped water to Lahuriadah village. Around 75–76 years after Independence, tap water reached 125 households in the hilly village. Divya inaugurated the project herself. This reportedly displeased Anupriya Patel, Union Minister and Mirzapur MP. She was transferred just two days after the ‘Jal Pujan’ (water worship) ceremony. When she was transferred, people and traders in Mirzapur showered flowers on the streets to bid her farewell. Local people used to affectionately call her ‘DM Beti’ (DM Daughter). Now see what people are discussing on social media...

stories.title: 'Haryana's wrestlers made me hero', remarks Brij Bhushan Singh:Says, 'Got recognition across the country' after Vinesh Phogat's allegations
stories.summary: BJP leader Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh said that he gained nationwide recognition due to the allegations made by some female wrestlers from Haryana, so he is not angry with them. Citing the example of the Ramayana, he said that just as King Ram gained recognition as Lord Ram because of Kaikeyi, similarly, the wrestlers' allegations brought him recognition across the entire country. They took him out of Uttar Pradesh and made him a hero in Haryana as well. Former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) president Brij Bhushan Singh had arrived at a welcome ceremony in Patheda village of Mahendragarh district on Sunday, held for international kabaddi player Sachin Tanwar on his promotion to the post of DSP in the Rajasthan Police. It is worth noting that Brij Bhushan Singh was acquitted by Delhi's Rouse Avenue Court on the 3rd of this month in the sexual harassment case involving female wrestlers. Now know what Brij Bhushan Singh said.... Earlier they used to get lakhs of rupees, now they are struggling for pennies Addressing from the stage, Brij Bhushan Singh said, "The situation of the female wrestlers who were earlier felicitated at various events has now changed. Earlier they used to get lakhs of rupees, now they are struggling even for pennies. Now no one even invites them. They made me famous, so there is no need to be angry." Lit the funeral pyres of 5 brothers and a young son Brij Bhushan Singh said that he has faced many difficult situations in his life, but never gave up. He said, "I have performed the last rites of my five brothers and a young son. I have seen my house being demolished in front of me. The first case filed against me was for the demolition of my own house." Accused of having links with Dawood He said that during the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, the CBI was the first to arrest him. He mentioned that in 1996, there was a Congress government, and he was accused of helping Dawood Ibrahim. He said, "Sitting in jail, I was thinking that I have no connection with Dawood, yet Narasimha Rao sent me to jail. Later I realized that I was sent to jail because my wife had become an MP." Sachin Tanwar, who has captained in the Junior Asian Championship Sachin Tanwar from Mahendragarh is an international kabaddi player. He has played for teams like Gujarat Giants, Patna Pirates, and Tamil Thalaivas in the Pro Kabaddi League (PKL). He has also been among the expensive players of the league. Sachin Tanwar has won a gold medal while captaining the Indian team in the Junior Asian Championship. He has been promoted/appointed to the post of DSP in Rajasthan Police under the sports quota.

stories.title: Ravi Kishan says Gorakhpur is like Spain, calls opponents blind:Yogi breaks into laughter; SP MP retorts, ‘Look for the blind in BJP’
stories.summary: BJP MP Ravi Kishan has compared Gorakhpur to Spain. Praising the development in Gorakhpur and the changing face of the city, he said, "Gorakhpur looks like Spain to me. What can I do if someone is blind?" Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, minister Swatantra Dev, and Sanjay Nishad were seen laughing at his remark. Ravi Kishan made the statement on Saturday while inaugurating the newly constructed Kalyan Mandapam in Basharatpur. After the video went viral on Sunday, social media users began trolling Ravi Kishan. Samajwadi Party MP Dharmendra Yadav also hit back. He said, "Now I don't know who all are blind; they should look for them in their own party. Some people thought Varanasi looked like Kyoto, and he thinks Gorakhpur looks like Spain-there is no cure for that. The public knows everything, and the people of Gorakhpur know as well. There are potholes on the roads, canals have been formed, and boating is taking place. Boating is even happening on the roads; the people of Gorakhpur can see it too." Now read the details... Ravi Kishan said in Bhojpuri-Gorakhpur feels like Spain to me Ravi Kishan was speaking in Bhojpuri. Without naming anyone, he launched a fierce attack on the opposition. He said, 'I am proud of Gorakhpur. I feel Gorakhpur is Spain. I feel Gorakhpur is an amazing place. I feel Gorakhpur is a smart city. I have visited many places. If someone is blind, what can I do? The one who cannot see anything.' After hearing Ravi Kishan's speech, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Fisheries Minister Sanjay Nishad, who were seated on the stage, were seen laughing. The people present also appeared to burst into laughter. The female anchor hosting the event could not contain her laughter either after seeing the MP's style. 'Before 2017, Gorakhpur was a hub of murders' In his address, Ravi Kishan attacked the opposition while referring to Gorakhpur before 2017. He said that at that time, Gorakhpur used to be a hub of murders. Sisters and daughters were not safe. The double-engine government is continuously carrying out development work. He also led the people present at the event in chanting slogans of 'Victory to Mother India' and 'Har Har Mahadev.' What was wrong with describing Gorakhpur as Spain? Later, Ravi Kishan said that they had visited many places and had felt the changes that had taken place in Gorakhpur. If someone cannot see the development, what can they do about it? He said that his statements are constantly criticized, but if he described Gorakhpur as being like Spain, what was wrong with that? People posted sarcastic VIDEOS on social media... Social media users are trolling MP Ravi Kishan. An X user named Raj posted the video and wrote, “Gorakhpur remains waterlogged during the rains, but Ravi Kishan is busy describing Spain.”

stories.title: Women wrestle in veils during Hamirpur’s Kajli festival:Daughters and daughters-in-law face off in an arena tradition dating back to British rule
stories.summary: An unusual wrestling competition for women was held in Nivada village of Hamirpur, Uttar Pradesh, on the occasion of the Kajli festival, the day after Raksha Bandhan. On Saturday, daughters-in-law and young women demonstrated wrestling moves in the traditional competition while keeping their faces covered with veils. Hundreds of women and young girls arrived to watch the event. They encouraged the wrestlers by beating drums and clapping to the rhythm. In the competition, Malti Shukla of the village defeated Maya Gupta. Kaushilya brought Muliya down, while Ramsakhi pinned Shakuntala. Sampat Savita defeated Shyama Pal. Vidya emerged victorious in the bout against Mohini. Meanwhile, Rani Bhurji registered a win by defeating Meera Savita. According to the villagers, in this old wrestling tradition dating back to the era of British rule, the village daughters-in-law and young women enter the arena wearing saris and covering their faces with veils. Matches are then held between the female wrestlers. The entry of men into the arena and its surrounding area is completely prohibited. Village elders say that during British rule, when the men of the village would leave and go elsewhere to escape oppression, the women learned wrestling techniques for their protection. In Nivada village, located about 70 km from the district headquarters, this wrestling competition has been held for hundreds of years. Now Read the History of This Unique Wrestling Competition Village head representative and retired manager Nathuram explained that they had heard from the village elders about the centuries-old tradition of the wrestling competition. Although no written evidence of its history is available, the story remains associated with the competition as a folk tale passed down from generation to generation. Circumstances have changed over time, but women have continued to enter the wrestling arena. At the conclusion of the competition, village head Girija Devi honoured the winning and runner-up women by presenting them with cash prizes and gifts. Abhilasha Gupta and Pooja Gupta served as referees. At this wrestling competition held in Lodhipur Niwada village in the Muskra development block, no man is allowed to enter the arena or its surrounding area. The men of the village either stay in their homes or leave the village during the competition. From watching the competition to participating in the bouts, the women handle all the responsibilities. Why is the wrestling event held only during the Kajli festival? In Bundelkhand, the Kajli festival has long been deeply connected with folk life and traditional celebrations. Events held after Raksha Bandhan also feature songs, music, fairs, and traditional games. This women's wrestling event in Lodhipur Nivada is considered a part of the same tradition. This event held during the Kajli festival is not merely a wrestling competition. It also gives the village women an opportunity to come together, demonstrate their physical strength, and carry forward a tradition passed down through generations. Keeping the tradition alive is more important than winning the wrestling competition According to the villagers, the most special thing about this event is that wrestling here is not limited to winning or losing. For elderly women, it is an opportunity to keep an old tradition alive, while for young women from the new generation, it is becoming a platform to showcase their strength, confidence, and sporting talent. Women who enter the wrestling arena wearing veils reflect the traditional social culture of Bundelkhand on the one hand, while also demonstrating women's empowerment through wrestling on the other. This is why the annual wrestling competition held in the village has now become a part of the local cultural identity. A confluence of Bundelkhand's folk tradition and women's power Although the format of this wrestling event may have changed over time, its essence remains intact. Women entering the wrestling arena, elders boosting morale with the beat of drums, and men staying away from the event make this competition different from ordinary wrestling tournaments. This women's wrestling competition held in Lodhipur Nivada on the occasion of the Kajli festival is a unique confluence of Bundelkhand's folk culture, community participation, and women's power. This tradition is what makes it special every year for the villagers and women from the surrounding areas.

stories.title: Shooters travelled from Karnal to Shamli to kill Ankit Baliyan:Four in custody, police in 4 states hunt mastermind; 80 CCTV cameras checked
stories.summary: Police have detained four suspected attackers in the murder case of Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan. During the investigation, police examined around 80 CCTV recordings and checked the gym's entry register. The SOG team identified all four shooters through CCTV footage; they had reached Shamli from Karnal in Haryana via Bidouli. Police are now piecing together footage from CCTV cameras installed along the entire route from Shamli to Karnal to trace their movements. The call details, criminal histories, and movements on the day of the murder of all four detained attackers are being investigated. Based on their interrogation, the search is underway for the mastermind behind the conspiracy. Teams from the police forces of four states-Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi, and Punjab-are investigating this high-profile murder case. It may be recalled that on 6 August 2026, at 4:30 p.m., Ankit Baliyan was shot dead in a barrage of gunfire outside his gym. Four assailants riding two motorcycles fired 18 rounds as he sat in his car, five of which hit Ankit. On the day of the incident, Haryana's Gogi Gang claimed responsibility for the murder through a Facebook post, while singer-actor Bhupendra Dhingra released a video making the same claim. However, Bhupendra later retracted his statement. Watch how Ankit Baliyan was murdered in 5 CCTV footage clips- They stayed around the gym for more than an hour and had been conducting reconnaissance in advance The SOG investigation has revealed that after reaching Shamli, the attackers stayed around Ankit's gym for more than an hour. They monitored Ankit's movements and waited for him to leave the gym. Before that, the shooters had been roaming around the same market for nearly two hours. At around 6:42 p.m., as soon as Ankit came out of the gym, the attackers surrounded him and opened fire. After the incident, the accused fled the scene. Police are now linking the recordings from CCTV cameras installed along the route from Karnal to Bidouli and from Bidouli to Shamli. The investigation is focused on identifying the attackers' vehicle, the people traveling in it, and their activities along the way. After suspicious activities emerged at several locations, police began matching the footage. Police hope that connecting recordings from different locations will help establish the attackers' complete movements and identify the vehicle they used. SOG examined the gym register and questioned several people On Friday, a team from the SOG once again reached Shamli from Saharanpur and inspected the crime scene. The team went to the gym and checked the entry register. It questioned several people present at the gym and in the surrounding area to gather information. The SOG team also took the CCTV footage with them. A technical analysis of the footage is being conducted to match the attackers' routes of arrival and departure with their activities. Several teams, including the STF, engaged in the search Given the seriousness of the matter, the police have formed several special teams. Teams from the ADG Meerut Zone, DIG Saharanpur, STF, and Shamli Police are continuously searching for the accused. Raids are also being conducted at suspected hideouts in other districts and states. The investigation is being advanced based on CCTV footage, gym registers, technical evidence, and questioning of the suspects taken into custody. Here is the complete case explained step by step- He posted a new song an hour before the murder Ankit posted a song on his Instagram at 6 p.m. on Wednesday evening, exactly one hour before the murder. In it, he was seen sitting in a car and singing, "Murder someone on the road." His song "We'll Shoot in the Packed Courtroom" was released on February 15, 2023. The song was banned. After this, he became well-known in the world of Haryanvi music. Married six years ago; wife is a government teacher Ankit was a resident of Bantīkheda village in Shamli. He lived in Sonipat, Haryana. However, for the past several months, he had been living with his family in his village. His father, Satbir, is a retired soldier, while his mother, Amaresh, is a homemaker. Ankit was the youngest of four siblings. His elder brother Rajeev is not married yet. He is pursuing an MBBS degree in Kota. His two elder sisters, Reena and Ritu, are married. Ankit got married to Seema six years ago. Seema is a government teacher in Delhi. However, Ankit and Seema do not have any children yet.

stories.title: JE made to swear on Hanuman Chalisa over power cuts:Gonda residents protest for 2.5 hours; FIR filed
stories.summary: In Gonda, Uttar Pradesh, troubled by power cuts, villagers reached the electricity substation carrying the Hanuman Chalisa. They surrounded the junior engineer (JE). Placing the JE's hand on the Hanuman Chalisa, they asked him, "Swear and tell us, how many hours of electricity do you provide out of 24 hours?" A video related to the incident has surfaced on social media. In the video, people can be seen making the JE swear with his hand on the Hanuman Chalisa, hurling abuses. About 15 villagers created a ruckus at the electricity substation for nearly two and a half hours. The JE has filed a case against the villagers for abusing, assaulting, and threatening him, as well as damaging government property. The incident reportedly took place at 8:30 p.m. on Friday at the electricity substation in the Katra Bazar area, about 30 kilometers from the district headquarters. Take a look at the pictures- Details of the matter Villagers allege that despite electricity being available at the power house in the Katra Bazar area, the supply to their feeder was being disconnected. Pawan Kumar Dubey, who participated in the protest, said that for nearly six months, their area has not been receiving even two hours of regular electricity. The Ranjitpur feeder supplies electricity to around 10 villages, including Chandvatpur. However, due to unannounced power cuts, an electricity crisis persists in several villages, including Ranjitpur, Sisai Joga, Tilka, Raipur, Pure Bahori, Ashokpur, Pure Maholi, Sarvangpur, Bhairampur and Bamdera. More than 10,000 people have been affected. Argument with retired lineman over the phone; reached the power house at 8:30 p.m. Pawan alleges that at around 8 pm on August 28, he called the retired lineman present at the power house. He was told over the phone, "You're acting like a big leader; come here and we'll supply you with electricity." After this, he reached the power house at around 8:30 pm along with other villagers. According to Pawan, electricity was available there, but the feeder's supply was not being provided. During this, a young man who had accompanied him took out the Hanuman Chalisa and asked the employees to swear and say how many hours of electricity they supplied in a 24-hour period. The police then arrived at the spot and calmed the situation. Pawan denied any kind of assault, abusive language, or tearing up of government documents. JE files complaint against three named individuals and 10 unidentified people Adarsh Kumar Ojha, JE at the Katra Rural Electricity Substation, submitted a complaint at around 11 p.m. on Saturday night at Katra Bazar police station. He stated that at around 8:44 p.m. on 28 August, SSO Sudhanshu Mishra, Rahul Gautam, and lineman Arjun Gupta were present on duty at the substation. According to the written complaint, at around 8:49 p.m., Pawan Kumar Dubey, Raj Kumar alias Kallu, and Rajan Kumar arrived at the substation along with approximately 8 to 10 unidentified people. The junior engineer (JE) alleged that they verbally abused, assaulted, threatened, and misbehaved with the duty staff. They were also accused of damaging the official logbook, CUG mobile phone, and other government documents, as well as obstructing government work. In the complaint, the JE stated that the incident disrupted the substation's electricity supply for a considerable period, causing inconvenience to approximately 17,000 electricity consumers. He demanded that a case be registered against the accused. Power supply affected due to the failure to install a 5 MVA transformer Delay in installing a transformer with a capacity of 5 MVA is being cited as a major reason for the power supply problem in the area. Over this issue, BJP MLA from Katra Bazar, Bawan Singh, held a meeting with officials of the Electricity Department at the residence of District Magistrate Priyanka Niranjan late Saturday night. Instructions to commission the transformer by September 10 During the meeting, the issue of low power supply in villages connected to the Ranjitpur, Ramapur, Devapasia and Parsiyarani feeders in the Katra Bazar area, as well as the delay in installing the 5 MVA transformer, was raised. The Superintending Engineer, Electricity Department, and the Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division, Colonelganj, were instructed to complete the work on the 5 MVA transformer to be installed in Katra Bazar town and commission it before September 10. According to officials, this is expected to provide relief from the problem of unscheduled power cuts in the area. Station House Officer said complaint received, action will be taken Katra Bazar Station House Officer Manoj Pathak said: “A video has surfaced showing villagers reaching the power house and making inquiries regarding the electricity problem. A complaint has also been received from the Electricity Department. Further action will be taken based on the facts that emerge during the investigation. The complaint reportedly describes Pawan Kumar Dubey as close to BJP MLA Bawan Singh. However, these allegations are being investigated.”

stories.title: Akhilesh demands attempted murder FIR against IPS Avinash:‘Who is emboldening him?’ Asks when bulldozer will roll in singer murder case
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav called Samajwadi Party leaders Mohit Jatav and Digvijay Bhati to Lucknow after they accused former Meerut SSP Avinash Pandey of assaulting them. He held a press conference with the two leaders on Sunday and demanded that an FIR under Section 307 of the IPC for attempted murder be registered against the IPS officer. “What kind of behaviour is this from a police superintendent? Who is emboldening him? What happened to Digvijay Bhati? If the rule of law existed, an FIR under Section 307 would have been registered against the IPS officer,” Yadav said. He added, There is no rule of law, which is why they are having to wander around seeking justice. An IPS officer like this should not be allowed to continue in service. A case should be registered against him. The police are following just one formula—grease their palms and they become lenient. During the press conference, Mohit Jatav and Digvijay Bhati also recounted their allegations against the former SSP. They claimed that after assaulting them, the officer told them, “We will carry out your encounter.” They alleged that the police then drove them around for two to three kilometres before MLA Atul Pradhan arrived and intervened. According to the two leaders, Pradhan’s intervention saved their lives. They reiterated their demand that a case be registered against the officer. First, read what the Samajwadi Party leaders from Meerut said... Digvijay’s account Digvijay Bhati said that on 19 August, Avinash Pandey called Mohit Jatav and invited them to meet, saying, “Come, let’s sit and have tea.” When they arrived, Pandey allegedly asked Mohit, “Are you a Jatav?” He then asked Digvijay, “Are you a Gurjar?” He allegedly went on to accuse them of being criminals and stealing. “We folded our hands and pleaded with him, saying, ‘Sir, please don’t humiliate us.’ He then said, ‘I’ll make you a leader right now.’ They took both of us inside the cabin and allegedly beat us with their elbows, hands and feet. When I tried to hold his feet, he kicked me. Whenever we asked for water, they would only put the cap of a bottle in our mouths,” Digvijay alleged. Mohit Jatav’s account Mohit Jatav said that he and Digvijay had travelled to Lucknow to meet Akhilesh Yadav and had spoken to media personnel during the visit. “When I returned to Meerut, Avinash Pandey called me. He said, ‘You are going to Lucknow and giving sound bites; I’ll make you a leader.’ They then took us to the SOG office, where both of us were severely beaten,” Mohit alleged. Read Akhilesh Yadav’s 7 major statements 1. On Ankit Baliyan Murder Case, He Asked: Where Is the Bulldozer? Speaking about the murder of Shamli-based Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan, Akhilesh Yadav said that criminals from other states were entering Uttar Pradesh and carrying out attacks. “Mafias from other states are coming to Uttar Pradesh and firing 18 rounds each. Even the names are similar—what is the name... the Gogi gang? So, what is the connection? It seems there is no partnership. If there is no partnership, then why the cover-up? Where is the bulldozer, and when will it be deployed? His father, wife and brother are seeking justice, but the government does not care at all,” he said. 2. Kannauj’s cow milk plant sold, ‘Who are the Bandits and Looters?’ Akhilesh Yadav alleged that Kannauj’s cow milk plant, where products made exclusively from cow’s milk were manufactured, had been sold. He also claimed that Chhatar Manzil, located next to the Clark Hotel in Lucknow, had been sold, while Plasio Mall was allegedly sold in exchange for a commission. “More buildings are also being prepared for sale. Valuable land has been handed over to people of their own caste. To fill their pockets, they handed over the Agra-Lucknow Expressway toll to their own people,” he alleged. Yadav said he recently noticed potholes at several places on the expressway while travelling and questioned the expenditure on its maintenance. “₹1,500 crore was spent on maintenance. The minister in charge, Nand Gopal Nandi, was removed because instead of filling the potholes, he filled his own pockets. Who are the bandits? Who are the looters?” he said. 3. 'These adulterated people turn away when questioned” Yadav alleged that the BJP avoids answering questions and accused the party of being “unrighteous”. “The entire country knows that the person who abducted Mother Sita also came in disguise. Even a beggar does not steal from a temple. The BJP is an unrighteous gang. You must have seen the video in which a distressed mother is being threatened. Neither God nor we will forgive these people,” he said. Calling them “narrow-minded”, Yadav alleged that they refused to answer questions and turned away when questioned. “These are adulterated people. As soon as the festival arrived, they made sugar more expensive. Everything is expensive. Our mothers and sisters kept waiting for buses, but no bus arrived anywhere. They have ruined the ambulance services. These people have decided to shut down the schools,” he said. 4. 'If we form the government, we will reopen 26,000 schools” Akhilesh Yadav said the Samajwadi Party would reopen 26,000 schools if it formed the government in Uttar Pradesh. “We assure you that 26,000 schools will be reopened. They are saying they will provide 100,000 jobs. The way looting is taking place makes it seem as though the election is approaching,” he said. Yadav said the SP would conduct a PWD audit after coming to power and alleged corruption in the Irrigation Department. “Just fill the tank with water and it will collapse. Villages have been dug up to lay pipelines,” he said. He alleged that corruption had demoralised honest officers, who were neither willing to work nor receiving any respect. “Several officers have submitted applications for retirement. Commission-taking is rampant. There is pressure on officers to help several BJP members seize properties. What can the officers do? Even in the temple theft case, honest officers are not being given an opportunity to work,” Yadav alleged. 5. “If SP Government is formed, we will conduct caste census within 3 months” Yadav said that if the SP formed the government in Uttar Pradesh, it would conduct a caste census within three months. “If the SP government is formed, a caste census will be conducted in Uttar Pradesh within three months. Support us, and we will respect you,” he said. He accused the BJP of being a party of wealthy businessmen and questioned who would benefit from ethanol production and rising sugar prices. “Ethanol is being produced because of sugarcane. Whom do they want to benefit from this? Whom do they want to benefit by making sugar expensive?” he asked. Yadav also blamed profiteering for contributing to inflation and promised financial support for girls’ education. “We will ensure that your daughters study, progress and receive educational grants. They ask us where we will get ₹40,000 from. We will give ₹50,000. They are keeping ₹30,000 as a loan. We will save the money being looted and embezzled under the BJP government and use it to help the poor,” he said. 6. ‘Bundelkhand Expressway broke down on its very first occasion’ Akhilesh Yadav criticised the condition of several expressways in Uttar Pradesh, alleging that the Bundelkhand Expressway developed problems on its very first occasion and that the Purvanchal Expressway was causing “backbreaking trouble”. “The Lucknow and Kanpur expressways are collapsing every day. Today, it became known that the design itself was faulty. Surely, the person who designed it isn’t colour-blind,” he said. Referring to the redevelopment of Akbarnagar, Yadav said the government had promised to build a riverfront there. “Tell me, does a riverfront ever get built on a drain? Their models are designed to line their pockets. The BJP sold JPNIC. Before selling it, they cleared the contractors’ payments. This will be the first government to survive by repeatedly paying contractors,” he alleged. Yadav also alleged that an architect who was under investigation was later awarded a ₹3,000-crore project for a railway station being built in Delhi. “Every one of their actions is aimed at lining their pockets,” he said.

stories.title: Law student attacked with axe, iron rod in Bulandshahr:Beaten for 20 minutes, accused flee firing shots; dies 10 days later
stories.summary: Law student Ankur Chaudhary, 22, died at around 10 pm on Saturday while undergoing treatment at Fortis Hospital, 10 days after he was brutally assaulted by fellow college students in Bulandshahr’s Khurja. The 20-minute attack, carried out with sticks, iron rods, axes and stones, left him with severe head and facial injuries. The assault took place on the night of 20 August in Bagrai village, around 38 km from the Bulandshahr district headquarters. CCTV footage of the incident has now emerged, showing the accused repeatedly attacking Ankur before fleeing the spot while allegedly firing shots. See 3 photos... Read the Full Case... Ashok Chaudhary is a practising lawyer in Bagrai village, while his wife, Babli, is the principal of a primary school. Ankur was their only son. Their elder daughter, Arpita, 28, is married. Ankur was a final-year LLB student and was unmarried. Ankur’s father, Ashok, said that on the night of August 20, Ankur was sitting with his friends near Electricity House No. 4 in Murari Nagar when around 11-12 men arrived in a Santro car and two or three motorcycles and surrounded him. The attackers allegedly assaulted Ankur for around 20 minutes using sticks, iron rods, axes and stones. When his friends tried to intervene, the attackers allegedly brandished country-made pistols and other firearms, threatening them. They then fled the scene while allegedly firing shots. Ankur’s friend Anil said that he and others tried to rescue him, but the attackers pulled out their weapons. Panic spread after the firing. Ankur suffered severe injuries to his head and collapsed on the ground, covered in blood. Police reached the scene, gathered information and began examining CCTV footage from cameras installed nearby. Parts of the assault were captured on camera, which helped investigators identify the accused. Ankur’s grandfather, R.K. Chaudhary, told the SSP, “We had no enmity with anyone. Those who killed our child should be killed in an encounter.” He also levelled serious allegations against the local village head, claiming that the village had been in turmoil for the past five years. He alleged that the village head had hired goons and supplied them with alcohol. ₹25,000 rewardee Lakhan arrested in police encounter, 3 others also sent to jail After Ankur’s death, pressure mounted on the police to arrest the accused who were still absconding. At around 8.30 pm on Monday, a Khurja police team was conducting checks near Chandralok Bambe, behind RK Farm House, when a motorcyclist allegedly tried to flee towards an unpaved road after spotting the police. According to Khurja CO Shobhit Kumar, the motorcycle skidded after the rider had travelled some distance. The police claimed that, after realising he was surrounded, the man opened fire at the police team with the intention of killing them. The police retaliated, and a bullet struck him in the leg. The injured man was identified as Lakhan. Police arrested him and admitted him to Surajmal Jatia Hospital for treatment. An unnumbered Splendor motorcycle, an illegal country-made pistol and cartridges were allegedly recovered from his possession. During interrogation, Lakhan allegedly admitted to his involvement in the attack on Ankur. Police records show that more than six cases, including attempted murder, are registered against him. He had been absconding since the attack, following which the SSP announced a ₹25,000 reward for information leading to his arrest. Police said four accused, including Lakhan, have so far been arrested and sent to jail in connection with the case. Several teams are conducting raids at suspected hideouts to arrest the remaining five accused. Ankur’s body brought home on sunday morning After the post-mortem, Ankur’s body was brought to his village on Sunday morning. SSP Dinesh Kumar Singh and SP Rural Antariksh Kumar Jain met his family and assured them that strict action would be taken against those responsible. As a precautionary measure, a large police force was deployed in the area. Ankur’s last rites were later performed in the village amid tight security. Police Face Challenge of Arresting Remaining Accused The case, which began as an assault on 20 August, has now turned into a murder case following Ankur’s death. CCTV footage, eyewitness accounts and the police investigation are key elements of the case. Police said efforts were underway to arrest the remaining accused and produce them before the court. Khurja CO Shobhit Kumar said: CCTV footage is being examined. Police teams have been formed to ensure the swift arrest of the accused. A thorough investigation into the matter is underway.

stories.title: Ankit Baliyan murder case:Shooters came from Karnal; CCTV captures them in Shamli, 4 suspects detained, Bhupendra Dhingra says, 'I didn’t kill him'
stories.summary: Murder case of Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan in Shamli, police have detained four suspects. During the investigation, they examined around 80 CCTV recordings and checked the gym’s entry register. CCTV footage reviewed by the SOG team showed that the four suspected shooters had travelled to Shamli from Karnal in Haryana via Bidoli. Police are now piecing together CCTV footage from the entire route from Karnal to Bidoli and then to Shamli to track the suspects’ movements. Investigators are focusing on identifying the vehicles used, the people travelling in them and their activities along the route. After suspicious movements were noticed at several locations, police are matching footage from different points to establish the suspects’ complete route and identify the vehicle used in the crime. The police are also checking the call details, criminal records and activities of all four detained suspects on the day of the murder. Teams from the Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi and Punjab police are involved in the investigation. At around 6:42 pm on 6 August, 2026, 32 year old YouTuber and Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan was shot dead while leaving a gym in Shamli. He was a resident of Bantikheda village in Shamli. After the murder, Bhupendra Dhingra had claimed responsibility for killing Ankit. He has now retracted the claim. In a video released on Saturday evening, he said: It is being widely reported on social media and in the media that I killed Ankit Baliyan, but I did not kill him. I was out of town when Ankit was murdered. My location can be verified. Watch 5 CCTV clips showing how Ankit Baliyan was murdered… First, know what the investigation has revealed… The SOG investigation has found that after reaching Shamli, the attackers loitered around Ankit’s gym for nearly an hour. Before that, they spent around two hours in the same market, apparently assessing the entry and exit routes. They also kept track of Ankit’s movements and waited for him to leave the gym. At around 6:42 pm, as soon as Ankit stepped out, the attackers surrounded him and opened fire. Riding two motorcycles, the four assailants fired 18 rounds after Ankit got into his car. Five bullets hit him. The attackers then fled the scene. SOG examined gym register and questioned several people On Friday, a Saharanpur SOG team again visited Shamli and inspected the crime scene. The team examined the gym’s entry register and questioned several people present at and around the gym. It also collected CCTV footage from the area. The footage is now being analysed to trace and match the attackers’ route and movements. Several teams, including STF, deployed to track attackers Several special police teams have been formed to track down the attackers. Teams from the ADG Meerut Zone, DIG Saharanpur, STF and Shamli Police are conducting searches. Raids are also being carried out at suspected locations in other districts and states. The investigation is being based on CCTV footage, gym records, technical evidence and questioning of the detained suspects. Bhupendra Dhingra denies killing Ankit On the day of the incident, Haryana-based Gogi gang claimed responsibility for Ankit’s murder through a Facebook post. Later, singer-actor Bhupendra Dhingra also released a video claiming responsibility for the killing. He has now retracted his statement. In a new video released on Saturday evening, Bhupendra said, “It is being reported on social media and in the mainstream media that I killed Ankit Baliyan, but I did not kill him. I was away when Ankit was murdered. My location can be checked.” Bhupendra also expressed condolences to Ankit’s family. He said, “Ankit’s parents, wife and family are mourning after his murder. I am also a Haryanvi artist and do not have my own parents. I request Ankit’s family to consider me their son and brother. I regard Ankit’s sister as my own sister.” Let’s understand the entire case chronologically… Posted a new song an hour before the murder Ankit posted a song on Instagram at 6 pm on Wednesday, exactly an hour before his murder. In the video, he was seen sitting in a car and singing about killing someone on the road. His song We’ll Shoot in the Full Court was released on February 15, 2023. The song was later banned, bringing him recognition in the Haryanvi music industry. Married 6 years ago, wife is a government teacher Ankit was a resident of Bantīkheda village in Shamli and had been living in Sonipat, Haryana. However, for the past few months, he had been staying with his family in his native village. His father, Satbir, is a retired soldier, while his mother, Amresh, is a homemaker. Ankit was the youngest of four siblings. His elder brother, Rajiv, is unmarried and studying MBBS in Kota. His two elder sisters, Reena and Ritu, are married. Ankit married Seema six years ago. She works as a government teacher in Delhi. The couple did not have any children.

stories.title: Lucknow Cantt to become model cantonment board:Rajnath Singh lays foundation for 12 projects worth ₹101 crore
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh is set to develop Lucknow Cantonment as a model cantonment board. On Sunday, he laid the foundation stones for 12 development projects in the cantonment, with the works to be completed at a cost of ₹101 crore. Rajnath Singh arrived at Dilkusha Lawn with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath at around 10.50 am. At 11 am, they listened to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Mann Ki Baat programme. All BJP MLAs from Lucknow, several Uttar Pradesh ministers, Mayor Sushma Kharkwal and Cantonment Board officials were present during the programme. At around 12.30 pm, Rajnath Singh is scheduled to reach the Prerna Sthal near the Dubagga-Sitapur Road bypass, where he will unveil a statue of Rani Avantibai Lodhi. stories.title: Ganga floods Prayagraj’s Lete Hanuman temple:50 stranded in Chitrakoot rescued; SDRF carries children to safety
stories.summary: Heavy rains continue to lash Uttar Pradesh, pushing several rivers into spate. In Chitrakoot, the Mandakini River has swollen, with water levels rising nearly 30 feet. A 300-foot-long bridge near Hanuman Dhara was washed away in the floods, while around 400 shops have been inundated. Water has also entered the railway tracks, leaving people stranded inside hotels and homes. Two helicopters and SDRF teams have been deployed for rescue operations. So far, around 50 people have been rescued. SDRF personnel carried children trapped inside homes in their arms and brought them to safety. The situation in Chitrakoot has worsened due to continuous rainfall and the release of water from Madhya Pradesh’s Bargi Dam. Meanwhile, the water levels of the Ganga and Yamuna are rising rapidly in Prayagraj. At around 3:45 am on Sunday, the Ganga reached the sanctum of the Lete Hanuman temple, bathing the idol. As the water entered the sanctum, devotees began performing prayers and rituals. A special aarti was also performed amid the beating of drums and other traditional instruments to welcome the Ganga. In Varanasi, the Ganga has risen close to the danger mark. Last rites are being performed on rooftops and in lanes, while all 84 ghats remain submerged. In Sitapur, a rain-weakened mud wall collapsed, trapping a couple and their two-year-old daughter under the debris. Police reached the spot after receiving information, rescued all three and rushed them to hospital. Rain alert has been issued for 27 districts across Uttar Pradesh today, with a warning of heavy rain in Sonbhadra. Lucknow and 10 surrounding districts remained cloudy in the morning, although sunshine emerged as the day progressed. Photos of the rain and floods… Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said, The monsoon system over Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and southern Uttar Pradesh has moved ahead. As a result, rainfall activity is expected to decrease until August 31. After that, a fresh weather disturbance is likely to trigger another spell of rain in the first week of September.

stories.title: Husband-wife found dead in room in Jhansi:Husband half-naked, bodies infested with insects; son suspects murder
stories.summary: Bodies of an elderly couple were found inside their locked house in Jhansi on Saturday night. The bodies were lying on the floor of a room occupied by their tenant. The husband was found partially undressed, while his wife’s body was lying nearby. The bodies are believed to be around five to six days old. Eight days ago, the couple had prepared meat with their son and the tenant. They also drank alcohol during the gathering. The son later left his parents and the tenant and returned to his home. On Saturday evening, the tenant called the son and told him that the couple were not answering their phones. The son tried calling his parents nearly 10 times, but received no response. He reached their house at night and, after finding the gate locked, climbed over it to enter the premises. He then found his parents’ bodies lying on the floor. The son alleged that his parents had been murdered and that the house had also been looted. He said a cupboard was found open and cash and jewellery were missing. The tenant has reportedly switched off his mobile phone. Police are examining CCTV footage as part of the investigation. The incident was reported from the Sipri Bazaar police station area. Now read the entire case in detail Son lived 2 kilometres away The deceased were identified as Vishwanath Pal (70) and his wife, Bhuvan Devi (65). Both were residents of Purabag Rouni village in the Todi Fatehpur police station area. Around 25 years ago, the couple moved to Mahisaganj in Sipri Bazaar. They had one son, Jagpal, and two daughters, Phoola and Geeta. All three children are married. Their son Jagpal said, “In 2014, my father sold around 15 bighas of agricultural land in the village. He then purchased a plot in Govindpuri Colony. In 2019, he built a house there, and my parents moved into it.” “I live with my wife, Kanti Devi, and our two children in our old house, around 2 kilometres away. I used to visit my parents from time to time.” Bus conductor had rented one room The son further said, “The new house had three rooms on the ground floor and two on the first floor. A young man named Satendra had rented one of the rooms downstairs. He worked as a bus conductor. He added, '"He would come to his room every two to four days and usually had his meals at my parents’ house. I had visited my parents eight days ago. At the time, I had an argument with my mother over money. I asked her for ₹500 for expenses, but she offered me ₹100. She later gave me ₹150, after which I returned to my own house.” Son lives 2 km away The deceased were identified as Vishwanath Pal (70) and his wife, Bhuvan Devi (65). They were residents of Purabagaroni village in the Todi Fatehpur police station area. The couple had three children — a son, Jagpal, and two daughters, Phoola and Geeta. All three are married. Jagpal said his father sold 15 bighas of ancestral land in the village in 2014 and used the money to purchase a plot in Govindpuri Colony. The house was constructed in 2019, after which his parents moved there. Jagpal lives with his wife, Kanti Devi, and their two children in their old house, around 2 km away. He said he would visit his parents occasionally. The new house has three rooms on the ground floor and two on the first floor. One of the rooms on the ground floor had been rented to a man named Satendra, a bus conductor who would return to the room every two to four days. He would also eat with the elderly couple. Jagpal said he had visited his parents eight days ago and had an argument with his mother over money. He had asked her for ₹500 for expenses, but she initially offered him ₹100. She later gave him ₹150. He then returned to his home. The tenant switched off his mobile phone The son further said, “At around 6:30 p.m. on Saturday, I received a call from the tenant, Satendra." He said that when he went to the house. “I reached the house at night. I called out and knocked on the gate, but there was no response. I then climbed over the gate and entered. Inside the tenant’s room, I found my parents’ bodies lying on the floor. The cupboard was open, and the jewellery and cash were missing." “I have an 18-year-old daughter whom I wanted to get married. My mother had told me that she had kept ₹2 lakh and jewellery for her granddaughter’s wedding. She said she would deposit the money in the bank. That money is also missing.” Mystery surrounding the lock The son said the main gate was locked from the inside, but the lock did not belong to the house. It appears that the assailants may have put their own lock on the gate after the incident before leaving. A dog and a goat were also inside the house. Maggots had begun to appear on the bodies, indicating that the couple had been dead for several days. The son alleged that his parents had been murdered and that the house was also looted. Bodies found in tenant’s room Rahul Pal said, “My sister’s father-in-law and mother-in-law have died. A tenant lived in the room where the bodies were found. When we arrived, both bodies were lying on the floor inside the room. My sister’s father-in-law was partially undressed, while her mother-in-law was fully clothed.” It is alleged that the elderly couple were murdered after being robbed. Their belongings were scattered throughout the house, and the cupboard was found open. Cash was also missing. Two bloodstained towels were recovered from the scene. IG says, ‘SOG deployed to crack the case’ IG Akash Kulhari said the couple’s bodies were five to six days old and had decomposed significantly, making it difficult to determine the cause of death at this stage. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem, which will be conducted by a panel of doctors. The exact cause of death is expected to be established after the examination. He said the couple’s son, Jagpal, has raised suspicion on the tenant, Satendra. Eight days ago, the family had prepared meat and consumed alcohol together. Jagpal then returned to his home, while the other three remained at the house. On Saturday, Satendra was the one who called Jagpal and told him that his parents were not answering their phones. He has been missing since then, and police are trying to trace him. A case is being registered based on Jagpal’s complaint. The Special Operations Group (SOG), along with local police, has been assigned to investigate the case. The SP (City) has been appointed as the nodal officer, and multiple police teams are working to establish what happened.
