stories.title: Brij Bhushan’s daughter Shalini ready to contest polls:‘Will definitely fight if I get the ticket’; says family ties are her strength
stories.summary: Shalini Singh, daughter of Uttar Pradesh strongman leader and former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Singh, has decided to enter politics. On Sunday, Shalini said in Bulandshahr that she has been active in the social sector in Noida for nearly 15 years. She believes in raising her voice on the right issues, rather than taking sides based on whether someone is in the ruling party or the opposition. Shalini Singh said that a leader is identified not by any position or party ticket, but by their leadership. If the party's top leadership asks her to contest an election, she will certainly enter the electoral arena. Shalini said that she is a third-year-trained member of the Rashtra Sevika Samiti (RSS) and recently completed her third-year training in Nagpur. She said that she does not want to distance herself from this ideology. On dynastic politics-family is not a weakness, but a strength Responding to criticism of nepotism because she comes from a political family, Shalini Singh said that children from political families face greater pressure to prove themselves. She said that if a family has done good work, being part of that family is not a weakness but a strength. She said that people also have higher expectations regarding the advantages that come with belonging to a political family, which is why such individuals have to work even harder to prove their capabilities. She said that from childhood, she had learned to sit among people, understand their needs, and work on their problems. Shalini said on Swatantra Bhardwaj's arrest-Let the law take its course Regarding the attack on the father of CJP worker Nishu Azad at Jantar Mantar and the arrest of the accused, Swatantra Bhardwaj, Shalini Singh said that the law is doing its work, and it is also listening to those who are raising their voices. She said that both sides should be heard in every case, and the appropriate action taken thereafter should be respected. A connection with Bihar, and love for Purvanchal too Speaking about her political future, Shalini Singh said that the place of work does not matter. If a person has the passion and ability to work, they can work anywhere. She said that she also has ties to Bihar and is Bihar's daughter-in-law. She also receives considerable affection from Purvanchal. However, she said that finding a political foothold in any particular area is not her objective. "We have come here to work. I believe we are in the role of the young leadership that the party needs." She said that the party is experiencing a generational gap, and she belongs to the generation that understands both young people and the elderly. On the Gen-Z movement: The party has brought about change, and that should be respected Speaking about the Gen-Z movement, Shalini Singh said that it could significantly narrow the gap between young people and political parties. She said that Gen-Z has put forward its voice effectively. He said that if a political party changes its policies, it should be respected. According to him, if there had been a dictatorship, the party would have stuck to its decision, but it changed its decision and tried to understand the people. He said that the narrative surrounding the issue has also changed on social media, and people are now listening to the youth. In-laws are former Bihar MPs Former MP Brij Bhushan Singh married Shalini Singh to Vishal Singh, the only son of late former MP Ajit Singh from Ara and former MP Meena Singh. Vishal Singh is a resident of Ara, Bihar, but currently lives in Noida. He is also a BJP leader. He is also the chairman of the National Cooperative Consumers' Federation (NCCF). Besides this, he is the president of the Bihar State Cooperative Marketing Union (BISCOMAUN). Shalini and Vishal have a 13-year-old son named Atharva. He has authored a book titled I Am Fearless, Not Rude.

stories.title: Well found beneath demolished mosque in UP’s Saharanpur:ASI called to examine age; Rajbhar asks Akhilesh, ‘Will you offer Fatiha there?’
stories.summary: A well was found beneath the site of a mosque after it was demolished in the Saharanpur Collectorate premises. The well is around 20 feet deep and 1.5 metres wide. It was covered with a stone slab. When the administration had the stone cut with a cutter, the well became visible. Police have covered it with an iron sheet to prevent debris from falling inside. The administration has called the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) to determine how old the well is. Heavy police forces have been deployed at the spot. The area has been barricaded and no one is being allowed to enter. Vikas Tyagi, who had complained about the mosque, claimed that there might have been a temple at the site earlier and that the mosque was built after it was demolished. He demanded an investigation. Political controversy has also begun over the mosque. MP Chandrashekhar said, "We will fight this battle in the House, in court and on the streets. Why was there such a hurry to demolish the mosque?" Meanwhile, Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar wrote on X, "Akhilesh ji, will you go to Saharanpur and offer Fatiha in front of the debris of the illegal building? Uttar Pradesh is asking, Please tell us?" The mosque was demolished on Saturday after bulldozers operated for 16 hours. The debris was cleared by Sunday morning. The administration said the mosque was demolished following a court order. The mosque's side, however, alleged that it was not given an opportunity to appeal in the High Court. Advocate Babar Wasim said, “We will approach the High Court against the action.” See 3 pictures from today… Muslim clerics and representatives of the mosque claim that it was around 100 years old. They said it was mentioned in Waqf documents dating back 70 years.

stories.title: Woman returns home alive in Lucknow after 27 months:Fled in-laws' home, family had cremated unclaimed body mistaking it for missing daughter
stories.summary: In Lucknow, a family performed the last rites of a woman they believed was dead, but she returned home alive 27 months later. Twenty-eight-year-old Shivani reached her maternal home in Navikot Nandana village of BKT tehsil on September 5. Her family members were shocked to see her. About a year and a half ago, the body of an unidentified woman was found in a drain behind IIM Road. Her maternal family members identified it as Shivani. The last rites were subsequently performed at Bhainsakund. A case of dowry death was also filed against her in-laws. Now that Shivani has returned alive, the case has become complicated. The question is, whose body was found in the drain? The police have taken Shivani to the police station and are questioning her. Now, know the full story According to her maternal family, Shivani was married on April 22, 2020, to Anand Singh, a resident of Saktapur in Sitapur, at the Bhuiyan Devi Temple in BKT. After the wedding, Anand's family had a house built in Bhikhapur village of BKT. Shivani then began living there. It is alleged that after some time, Shivani's in-laws began demanding a plot of land from her. Her family refused to fulfil the demand. Meanwhile, Shivani's grandmother passed away. She came to her maternal home and told her mother about her in-laws' demand. After this, the family refused to send her back to her in-laws' home. Shivani had gone out to get her Aadhaar card, then suddenly went missing At around 9 a.m. on May 2, 2024, Shivani told her mother that she was going to the new house of her in-laws in Bhikhapur to get her Aadhaar card. She then said she would go to the Indora Bagh CHC for treatment for stomach pain. However, she did not return home until late evening. Her father, Sarvesh Singh, also known as Heegu, said, "I asked Shivani's in-laws about her. Her mother-in-law, Sheela Devi, said that Shivani had probably gone to the rented room of Anand's maternal uncle, Sushil Singh, in Bharat Nagar, Madiyaon. The family also searched for Shivani there, but she could not be found." Woman's body found in a drain after one and a half months On May 4, 2024, the family filed a missing person report for Shivani at the BKT police station. On July 16, 2024, a woman's body was found in a drain behind IIM. The body could not be identified. The police informed Shivani's family. The family went to the medical college. They identified the body as Shivani's based on the sacred thread tied around her hand and the ring on her finger. The body was cremated at Bhainsakund in the presence of the police. After this, the family filed a dowry death case against her in-laws. On September 5, Shivani suddenly arrived at her parents' home in Navikot Nandana. The family was shocked to see her. She said that she had been living in the Para area all this time. Her family informed the police. The police took Shivani to the station, where she is being questioned. Shivani had been living with Javed According to the police, Shivani had been living with a young man named Javed in Para. Javed looks after a municipal corporation toilet. Shivani said that she had met Javed in Para itself. Javed had repeatedly asked her to return home, but she did not go back. The police are now trying to contact Javed. They are also investigating where Shivani had been staying all this time. At the same time, they are trying to determine whose body was found in the drain. The BKT police station in-charge said- The family members themselves had identified the woman's body as that of Shivani. The body was subsequently cremated. Now that Shivani has appeared, the entire case is being reinvestigated.

stories.title: SP leader protests by standing in pothole:Says Hindu-Muslim politics ruined the city, fills pothole himself
stories.summary: Akhlas Ahmed alias Sonu, president of the Jajmau Traders' Association, staged an unusual protest against the poor condition of roads in Kanpur and the negligence of the departments concerned. He climbed into a nearly six-foot-deep pothole on Jajmau's VIP Road and protested for 30 minutes. Even after the protest, officials took no notice of the issue. Taking a dig at the government, he said that the city had been turned into hell by focusing on Hindu-Muslim issues. Responsible officials from all departments, including the Municipal Corporation and the Jal Nigam, have maintained silence. When no action was taken even after the protest, he spent ₹12,000 from his own pocket to get the pothole repaired. Pothole had appeared on VIP Road leading to Circuit House The six-foot-deep pothole near Purani Chungi on the VIP Road from Jajmau to Circuit House had existed for the past four months. Local residents had complained several times to officials of the Municipal Corporation and the Jal Nigam, but no permanent solution was found. Two-wheelers and e-rickshaws were frequently overturning because of the pothole. Several pedestrians had also been injured as a result. Because of this problem, Akhlas Ahmed climbed into the pothole on Saturday and protested for about 30 minutes. He claims that his health deteriorated due to the gas emanating from the pothole during the protest. His colleagues immediately took him to a nearby private hospital, where he received treatment. Despite this, instead of backing down, he decided to have the pothole filled himself. According to Akhlas, he spent around ₹12,000 from Saturday night until 7 a.m. Sunday. He had two tractor-trolleys of soil dumped into the pothole and then had the road paved with cement and sand. He says this will provide relief to pedestrians and reduce the risk of accidents.

stories.title: CM Yogi reprimands leaders on stage in Chitrakoot:Video surfaces as local politicians jostle for photos during flood relief check distribution
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath strongly reprimanded leaders on stage during a programme in Chitrakoot on Sunday, September 6, after they began competing to get their photographs taken with him while he was distributing relief cheques to the poor. Seeing this, the Chief Minister gestured to the leaders to move back so that the poor would not face difficulty moving around. The CM said – "The people of Chitrakoot will not be left alone. The government stands with you in this hour of crisis. Families whose homes have been completely washed away will be provided houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana or the Chief Minister Housing Scheme. Needy families who do not have land will be given residential leases." Earlier, CM Yogi conducted an aerial survey of the flood-affected areas of Chitrakoot and assessed the rising water level of the Mandakini River. He then met flood victims staying in relief shelters. He distributed relief kits weighing 50 kg each to 800 affected families. The kits contained lentils, rice, flour, potatoes, buckets, and umbrellas. He listened to the problems of the affected families and gave chocolates to the children. He told the officials that there must be no negligence of any kind in delivering relief. See 3 pictures – 2 major things said by CM Yogi- 1- The flood was devastating, but by the blessings of Kamta Nath, no one lost their life The CM said, "This time, the water level of the Mandakini River had reached a dangerous level. The severity of the flood can be gauged from the fact that a bridge built over the river in the neighbouring state of Madhya Pradesh was also washed away. Despite this, no one lost their life in Chitrakoot. This is due to the blessings of Kamta Nath. The government and administration began relief and rescue efforts in time and provided assistance to the affected people." 2- Before 2017, people received very little relief during floods No person affected by the floods will be left without assistance. Before 2017, people received very little relief during floods. Now the government has expanded relief arrangements. Our aim is not only to provide immediate assistance but also to rehabilitate affected families. Floods in Chitrakoot affect 14,000 people in 36 villages

stories.title: Ghat dome collapses in Gorakhpur, killing a lawyer:Advocates stage 2-hour protest at district hospital, vandalise ambulance; another victim critical
stories.summary: A dome-shaped canopy on the banks of the Rapti River in Gorakhpur collapsed at around 11:30 am on Sunday, killing a lawyer and seriously injuring another. People nearby removed the debris and pulled both men out, but it is alleged that an ambulance called after the incident did not reach the spot for nearly half an hour, following which they were placed on a sheet and taken to the district hospital in an e-rickshaw. Doctors later referred Alok Asthana to the medical college after finding his condition critical. Alok Asthana died on the way. After his body was brought to the district hospital in an ambulance, a large number of lawyers arrived and began protesting. Angry lawyers also vandalised the ambulance. The protest has continued for around two hours. The city SP, CO, and police personnel from several police stations are present at the scene. The accident occurred at Gorakhnath Ghat, built along the Rapti River, about 4 kilometres from the district headquarters. More than eight platforms have been constructed here for people attending funeral ceremonies to sit. These platforms also have dome-shaped shelters. On Sunday, one of the shelters suddenly collapsed. The deceased lawyer has been identified as 45-year-old Alok Asthana. His wife filed a complaint at the police station, accusing the doctors of failing to provide timely treatment. He said, “When I called the CMO, he said, ‘Ten people die here every day. What difference will it make if one more dies?’” See the pictures... Know the full story... Advocate Alok Asthana (45), a resident of Raptinagar in Gorakhpur, originally hailed from Santhu village in Kushinagar. He had been practising at the civil court for nearly 20 years. His family includes his wife, Shalini, son Aditya, daughter Siddhi, and younger brother. His son, Aditya, is pursuing a B.Tech degree at NIT Punjab, while his daughter, Siddhi, is in the first year of her graduation. His younger brother lives in Basti and works as a medical representative (MR). According to family members, at around 10 a.m. on Sunday, Alok went by motorcycle to the house of his associate, advocate Vinod Tiwari. Vinod's mother had passed away. After this, he reached Gorakhnath Ghat on the Rapti River to attend the funeral. During the funeral, Alok Asthana was sitting with advocate Sanjay Singh, a resident of Shaktinagar, under the dome-shaped awning built over the platform at the ghat. Meanwhile, the awning suddenly collapsed onto both of them. The two advocates were buried under the debris. People present nearby removed the debris and pulled them out. People said that an ambulance was called immediately after the accident, but it did not arrive at the scene for nearly half an hour. After that, both injured men were placed on a sheet and taken to the district hospital in an e-rickshaw. Wife accuses doctors of negligence in treatment Shalini Asthana, wife of advocate Alok Asthana, submitted a complaint at the Kotwali police station. In it, she alleged that her husband Alok and advocate Sanjay Singh were brought to the district hospital in critical condition, but the doctors did not treat them and referred them directly to the medical college. Alok died while being taken to the medical college. After Alok's death, his family members reached the district hospital with his body. A large number of his fellow advocates also gathered there. As soon as they learnt of the death, the enraged advocates began protesting and vandalised an ambulance. Shalini Asthana alleged that her husband died due to lack of treatment. She also claimed to have contacted the CMO several times. According to the wife, the CMO allegedly said, "Ten people die here every day; what difference would it make if one more died?" She alleged that the CMO and doctors at the district hospital deliberately failed to provide treatment, resulting in her husband's death. Protest continues for 2 hours Meanwhile, the protest by advocates at the district hospital has continued for nearly two hours. The protesters remain firm on their demand for action against the CMO and doctors. The city SP, CO, and police from several police stations are present at the scene. DM Says Lightning Strike Suspected DM Deepak Meena said that a family had arrived at Rajghat for a cremation. During this time, advocates Alok Asthana and Sanjay Singh were sitting at a dome-shaped seating area. According to local residents, a strong jolt occurred there due to a lightning strike, causing the slab to collapse and injuring both advocates. The DM said that Alok Asthana was seriously injured, while Sanjay Singh also sustained injuries. Alok Asthana died during treatment. Sanjay Singh is still undergoing treatment. He said that local residents and family members had complained about a delay in the ambulance's arrival. The ambulance's response time is being investigated. If any negligence is found at any level during the investigation, action will be taken against those responsible. The Chief Minister inaugurated the ghat in 2021 The dome that collapsed and caused the accident was constructed by the Irrigation Department. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated Guru Gorakhnath Ghat on February 16, 2021. Questions have also been raised in the past about the quality of the ghat's construction. This is reportedly why the Municipal Corporation has not yet taken over the ghat. However, the Municipal Corporation carries out cleaning work here. The ghat was beautified at a cost of ₹27.85 crore The proposal for the beautification of Guru Gorakhnath Ghat was prepared in 2019. The ghat was beautified at a cost of approximately ₹27 crore 85 lakh 71 thousand. Ram Ghat was also constructed on the other side of the Rapti River at a cost of approximately ₹21 crore. At Guru Gorakhnath Ghat, domed-roof platforms had been built at various places for people attending cremation ceremonies to sit. On Sunday, one of these domes collapsed, trapping two advocates beneath it. Films have also been shot at the ghat Several films have been shot at Guru Gorakhnath Ghat. The shooting of MP Ravi Kishan's film 'Mahadev Ka Gorakhpur' also took place at this ghat. In addition, the ghat has been used for shooting other films as well.

stories.title: House collapses in Kanpur, killing father and 3 daughters:One daughter injured, only family member left; her wedding is in 2 months
stories.summary: Four members of the same family were killed and one person was seriously injured after a mud house collapsed in Kanpur on Sunday amid heavy rain. The house suddenly collapsed at around 9:30 am, trapping the father, Mukesh (45), and his four daughters under the debris. After hearing an explosion-like sound, nearby residents rushed out, began clearing the debris and informed the police and administration. After about two hours, all five were rescued and taken to a Community Health Centre, where doctors declared Mukesh and his daughters Maya (16), Neetu (12) and Pallavi (7) dead. The eldest daughter, Kajal (19), remains in critical condition and is undergoing treatment. She is now the only surviving member of the family. She is due to get married in two months. Her mother had died of an illness long ago. The incident took place in Hirni village under the Saadh police station area, 40 km from the district headquarters. Father lived with his four daughters in a two-storey mud house According to the police, Mukesh, who lived in Hirni village, supported his family by working as a labourer. His wife had passed away. He lived with his four daughters in a two-storey mud house. Everyone was at home on Sunday morning when the house suddenly collapsed. Villagers, together with the police, rescued all five people and took them to the nearest community health centre. However, by then, four of them had died. The eldest daughter, Kajal, was referred to Kanpur District Hospital because of her critical condition. She is currently undergoing treatment there. Called the police, but they did not arrive on time Villagers said, ‘The accident occurred due to continuous rain’ The villagers said that it had been raining continuously for the past several days. As a result, the walls and roof of the mud house had weakened. The accident occurred during the rain on Sunday. The police and administration teams also reached the spot and gathered information about the incident.

stories.title: BRICS chief justices visit Taj Mahal:Delegation also visits Agra Fort; 65-member team arrives in Agra
stories.summary: Amid rain on Sunday, a 65-member judicial delegation from more than 10 countries, including the Chief Justices of the BRICS nations, visited the Taj Mahal in Agra. The foreign guests arrived carrying umbrellas and admired the monument’s architectural design and intricate carvings despite the rain, later visiting Agra Fort and taking photographs with the Taj Mahal; the cool weather also allowed them to enjoy Agra’s climate. The delegation came to India to attend the BRICS Chief Justices Forum. The forum was held in New Delhi from September 4 to 6 under India's chairmanship. Chief justices and senior judicial officials from BRICS and participating countries took part in it. The forum was hosted by the Supreme Court of India. Discussion Held on the Justice System and Judicial Cooperation Meetings held in New Delhi included discussions on the justice systems of different countries, the rule of law, judicial cooperation, and the use of modern technology. Representatives shared judicial experiences from their respective countries. The meeting also focused on strengthening legal and judicial cooperation at the international level. Representatives from Russia, China and these countries The 65-member delegation that arrived in Agra included chief justices and senior judicial officials from more than 10 countries, including Russia, China, the United Arab Emirates, Egypt, South Africa and Indonesia. After meetings in Delhi, the delegation arrived in Agra on Sunday. Despite the rain, they visited the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort. Security arrangements were made at both monuments in view of the foreign guests' visit.

stories.title: Moving AC bus catches fire in Lucknow:Tyre bursts on Shaheed Path; carrying 30 passengers from Gorakhpur to Delhi
stories.summary: A double-decker AC bus caught fire while travelling on Shaheed Path in Lucknow, with the flames engulfing the entire bus within minutes and triggering panic among passengers. The bus was travelling from Gorakhpur to Surat with 30 passengers on board, all of whom hurriedly got off and ran to safety. The incident occurred at around 12:30 a.m. in front of Medanta Hospital. A police investigation revealed that the bus's rear tire had burst. Sparks then flew out, causing the fire to flare up. Upon receiving the information, three fire brigade vehicles reached the spot. At that time, the entire bus was ablaze. Flames rising about 20 feet high could be seen. The firefighters brought the fire under control in 30 minutes. See pictures of the fire- Driver said-He heard a breaking sound from the back of the bus, then it caught fire Driver Rahul Patel, a resident of Orai, said, "I left Gorakhpur with the bus at 5 p.m. on Saturday. As soon as I reached in front of Medanta Hospital, I heard something breaking from the rear section of the bus. Shortly afterward, it caught fire. I stopped the bus and asked all the passengers to get off. All the passengers got out safely. The police were then informed." Upon receiving the information, ADCP Rallapalli Vasanth Kumar arrived with his force. The police stopped traffic in both directions. Fire engines brought the blaze under control, but by then the bus had been completely burnt. SFO Mabad Chand Gujjar said that the fire was extinguished in time. No passenger was injured in the incident. The driver's quick thinking prevented a major accident. Traffic jam on highway after accident The accident caused a traffic jam on the highway. Traffic police diverted the vehicles and sent them via an alternative route. After the fire was extinguished, the police called a crane and had the bus removed from Shaheed Path. The traffic jam was cleared afterward. A passenger on the bus said, We were sleeping when the fire broke out. We woke up only after the driver shouted. After that, we got off the bus. All the passengers are safe.

stories.title: Crorepati medicine trader murdered in Kanpur:2 suspects seen entering flat; wife is marriage counsellor, son and daughter-in-law were at party
stories.summary: In Kanpur, a millionaire pharma businessman was allegedly killed by his employee and an accomplice. Police arrested both after an encounter in which they sustained bullet injuries to their legs. The arrested accused have been identified as Vishal Gautam and Raj Kishori. Vishal worked as the businessman’s employee. During questioning, he allegedly told police that they had killed the businessman at the behest of his daughter-in-law, who had promised them money. Earlier, the businessman’s body was found lying in a pool of blood on the floor of his flat. Blood was splattered across the room. According to police, his throat had been slit with a sharp weapon and he had suffered multiple injuries from a pointed object. The incident took place at Ratan Orbit Apartment in Kalyanpur, an upscale area of the city. The murder occurred between 10.30pm on Saturday and 3am. At the time, the businessman’s son, daughter-in-law and grandson had gone to a party. When the family returned at around 3am, they found the main door of the flat open. They went inside and found the 63-year-old businessman’s body. The family informed police, who reached the spot. Police examined CCTV footage from inside the flat, which showed two suspects entering the premises. Based on the footage, the two were detained for questioning. Investigators also examined CCTV footage from the apartment’s main entrance and surrounding areas and seized the apartment’s entry register. See 2 pictures related to the incident… Know the full case... The medicine trader, 63-year-old Vineet Vinocha, lived with his family in flat C-104 on the first floor of Ratan Orbit Apartment in the city. He was a wholesale medicine dealer. He ran a medicine firm named 'Pharma Traders' on Birhana Road in the city and managed the business along with his son, Subrat. His family includes his wife Punita, son Subrat, daughter-in-law Shalu and six-year-old grandson Shrijay. Vineet's wife Punita is a marriage counsellor and had travelled to Ghaziabad around a week earlier. His daughter Subhani and son-in-law live in Gurugram. Both are engineers. Returned from party to find father's body lying on the floor Vineet's samdhi, Naresh Arora, a resident of Thakurganj in Lucknow, said, "At around 10:30pm on Saturday, my daughter Shalu, Subrat and their son Shrijay went to a party. When the three of them returned home at around 3am, they found Vineet's blood-soaked body lying on the floor inside." There were marks of knife attacks on Vineet's body. Subrat then informed the police. As soon as they received the information, Kalyanpur police reached the spot. A forensic team also examined the crime scene and collected evidence. Vineet was a wholesale medicine distributor, ran business with son The deceased businessman, Vineet Vinocha, lived with his family in flat C-104 on the first floor of Ratan Orbit Apartment. The four-bedroom flat, which also has a dining room, is reportedly worth more than ₹1 crore. Vineet ran a pharmaceutical firm called ‘Pharma Traders’ on Birhana Road and managed the business with his son, Subrat. His family includes his wife Puneeta, son Subrat, daughter-in-law Shalu and six-year-old grandson Shrijay. Puneeta is a marriage counsellor and had been in Ghaziabad for a week. Their daughter Subhani and son-in-law, who are both engineers, live in Gurugram. Neighbours had no idea the murder had taken place Naresh Arora, the father-in-law of Lucknow resident Vineet, said his daughter called him early on Sunday to inform him about the incident. She told him that she had left home with her husband and son at around 10.30pm. When the three returned at 3am, they found Vineet’s body lying inside the flat. Her husband then called neighbour Pankaj Tiwari and others. When the neighbours arrived and saw the body, they were shocked. Pankaj said they had no idea the incident had taken place, even though his house was right next to Vineet’s. Signs of struggle found inside room The forensic team collected evidence from the scene. Vineet’s body was found in the room where he slept. The bedsheet was stained with blood, while blood was also found on the floor. Signs of a struggle were found inside the room. During the initial investigation, police suspect that Vineet was attacked suddenly. After being attacked, he may have tried to escape, leading to a struggle inside the room. The attacker then allegedly killed him. No other belongings in the room appeared to have been disturbed, leading police to suspect that the attacker’s sole motive was murder. Police suspect businessman opened door for someone he knew Police suspect that Vineet may have opened the door himself for someone he knew. This is because when his family returned from the party at around 3am, they found the main door of the flat open. Police are now trying to determine who had come to meet Vineet and whether the same person was responsible for the murder. Two suspects seen on CCTV ACP Dileep Singh said police had found several important leads during the investigation. CCTV footage showed two people entering the house, and both have been detained. Police are also questioning domestic staff. The accused allegedly slit the victim’s throat and stabbed him multiple times across his body. This indicates that the murder was not committed with the intention of robbery. Police suspect the killing may have been carried out due to an old enmity. The DVR has been seized and the footage is being examined. A case has been registered based on the victim’s son’s complaint. Police said the case would be solved soon. Pharma business spans three generations Rajendra Saini, president of the Kanpur Drug Traders Association and state general secretary of the UP Retail Chemists and Distributors Association (RCDA), said businessman Vineet was among Kanpur’s top five pharmaceutical traders. He said Vineet’s family had been in the pharmaceutical business for three generations. His father ran the business first, followed by Vineet, and his son Subrat now manages it. The family has operated a shop under the name Pharma Traders in the Birhana Road medicine market since 1968. Saini condemned Vineet’s brutal murder and said the incident had sparked anger among pharmaceutical traders over their safety. He urged police to solve the murder soon and send the accused to jail. Employees says, ‘Boss never deducted even a rupee from our salaries’ Twenty-two employees work at Vineet’s firm. As soon as they learned about his murder, several employees, including Aditya and Anurag, reached the post-mortem house. “Our boss Vineet never deducted even a single rupee from our salaries. He was very cheerful by nature. Even when he scolded us, there was always warmth and affection in his words,” the employees said. Businessman’s mother cries, ‘Bring my Vineet back’ The businessman’s body was taken to Bhairav Ghat for the last rites. Seeing her son’s body, his elderly mother, Chanchal, broke down in tears. “Bring my Vineet back. Why is my son sleeping? Wake him up. Why is my Vineet sleeping?” she cried. Vineet is survived by his younger brother, Puneet, who lives in Nawabganj’s Signature City and runs a laptop shop on Mall Road.

stories.title: 6 killed including siblings in Sambhal:Youth decapitated in head-on collision between dumper and tempo on highway
stories.summary: A sand-laden dumper collided with a tempo in Sambhal, Uttar Pradesh, on Sunday. Six people, including two young siblings, were killed in the accident, while four others were injured. The collision was so severe that the front portion of the tempo was badly damaged and the driver became trapped inside. The dumper also went out of control, hit a roadside tree and overturned. According to eyewitnesses, the tempo was travelling in its lane. An e-rickshaw travelling ahead suddenly took a U-turn. As the dumper driver tried to avoid it, he lost control and collided with the tempo. The tempo was thrown around 10 feet away by the impact. Bodies were scattered across the road. One young man's head was severed from his body. Hearing the screams, local residents rushed to the spot. They pulled the injured to the side of the road. Police reached the spot and sent the injured to Bahjoi CHC by ambulance, where doctors declared four more people dead. The deceased were identified as siblings Aaradhya, 3 months, and Dhruv, 6, their maternal aunt Rohini, 20, tempo driver Saudaan Pal, 40, Ruvaid, 30, and Rampal, 35. The accident took place at around 9am on the Agra-Moradabad National Highway in the Bahjoi police station area, around 2 km from the district headquarters. See the pictures of the accident- Now, understand the full case step by step- SP Vikas Chandra Tripathi said, The accident took place on the Bahjoi-Chandausi road. Police reached the spot immediately. The deaths of six people have been confirmed. The other four injured people are undergoing treatment. An investigation into the matter has been launched. stories.title: Technical education service exam begins in Varanasi:Over 16,000 candidates appear; entry allowed after three-layer security check
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) Technical Education (Teaching) Service Examination-2025 has begun in Varanasi. A total of 16,129 candidates are appearing for the examination. For this, 36 examination centres have been set up across the city. The examination is being conducted in two shifts. First shift examination underway The first shift is being held from 9am to 11am. Candidates were required to reach their centres by 7:30am. Before being allowed to enter through the centre gates, candidates underwent security checks and biometric verification. Thousands of candidates to appear in the second shift The second shift will be held from 2:30pm to 5pm. Candidates are required to reach their centres by 1pm. A total of 16,129 candidates are appearing across both shifts. Entry only after three-level security checks Special security arrangements have been made at the examination centres. Candidates are being checked at three levels. They are being allowed inside only after biometric verification and approval from the police and examination inspectors. 36 sector magistrates and 36 static magistrates deployed To monitor the examination, 36 sector magistrates and 36 static magistrates have been deployed. Surveillance is also being maintained around the examination centres. Photocopy shops closed within 200-metre radius To maintain the confidentiality of the examination, photocopy shops within a 200-metre radius of the centres have been ordered to remain closed.

stories.title: Technical education teaching exam today at 44 centres in Gorakhpur:19,496 candidates to appear in two shifts; CCTV surveillance
stories.summary: The Gorakhpur district administration has completed preparations for the Technical Education Teaching Examination-2026, with 19,496 candidates set to appear for the exam at 44 centres across the district on Sunday, September 6. The examination will be conducted in two shifts, with arrangements made for security, monitoring, traffic management and essential facilities to ensure it is held peacefully, fairly and transparently. In view of the large number of candidates appearing, separate sector magistrates have been appointed for both shifts. The sector magistrates will continuously inspect the examination centres in their respective areas. Officials will also visit the centres before the examination begins to check the arrangements. If any problem arises during the examination, the concerned officials will take immediate action. Monitoring to Be Conducted Through CCTV Cameras To maintain transparency in the examination, surveillance through CCTV cameras has been arranged at all examination centres. Activities taking place inside the centres during the examination will be monitored. A centre superintendent, room invigilators, and other staff have been deployed at each centre. Officials have been instructed to ensure that there is no negligence in maintaining the confidentiality of the examination and enforcing the prescribed rules. Gajendra Kumar, Nodal Examination Officer and ADM City, said that all necessary arrangements have been made to conduct the examination with complete transparency and integrity. The responsibilities of the officials and staff associated with the examination have been explained to them. Adequate Police Force Will Be Deployed at the Centers Considering that more than 19,000 candidates will take part, adequate police personnel will be deployed at all examination centres. Police officers will also manage security arrangements around the centres. Instructions have been issued to control crowds and monitor any suspicious activity. Security arrangements have also been strengthened to prevent cheating or any other improper activity. Police and administrative teams will also monitor the areas outside the examination centres. Special arrangements have been made to prevent unnecessary crowds from gathering around the centres due to people accompanying the candidates. The administration has appealed to people not to gather around the examination centres and to cooperate in maintaining order. Traffic arrangements also under watch to avoid congestion The arrival of thousands of candidates at examination centres at the same time and their return after the examination could increase traffic pressure on the city's major roads. In view of this, the traffic police have also made special arrangements. Police personnel will be deployed at major examination centres and on nearby routes to prevent traffic jams as candidates arrive and depart. The administration has appealed to candidates to reach the examination centre well in advance so that last-minute crowds and traffic problems can be avoided. Arrangements for Electricity, Water, and Cleanliness Also Made Arrangements for electricity, drinking water, and cleanliness have been ensured at all examination centres. The concerned officials have also been instructed to monitor these arrangements on the day of the examination. If any problem arises at a centre, it will be resolved immediately. Candidates have been advised to reach the examination centre well before the scheduled time. They must carry valid identification and all prescribed documents related to the examination. They should not bring any prohibited items to the centre and must follow all rules from entry until the examination concludes. ADM City Gajendra Kumar said that conducting the examination peacefully, fairly, and transparently is the district administration's priority. All departments have been instructed to work in coordination with one another. There must be no negligence at any level in security, traffic management, or examination arrangements. If any irregularity or inappropriate activity comes to light, action will be taken in accordance with the rules.

stories.title: 400-metre bypass submerged in UP’s Shravasti:Funeral pyres burn on road in Prayagraj; rain in Meerut-Ghaziabad; alert in all 75 districts
stories.summary: Monsoon rainfall continues across Uttar Pradesh. Intermittent rain has been reported in 10 cities, including Ghaziabad, Meerut, Agra and Bareilly, since Sunday morning. In Shravasti, so much rain fell that a 400-metre stretch of the bypass was submerged. In Bijnor, roads and lanes have turned into ponds, with water entering homes to a depth of 2-3 feet. Rivers are in spate due to the continuous rainfall. As many as 26 districts, including Varanasi, Prayagraj, Kanpur and Ayodhya, are affected by floods. In Prayagraj, people are having to wait to perform last rites at the Daraganj crematorium because it is flooded. They are being forced to cremate bodies at elevated spots along the roadside. In Varanasi and Kanpur, rising water levels in the Ganga have caused floodwater to enter people's homes. Residents are being forced to stay on rooftops. Yogi had conducted an aerial survey of the affected areas of Kashi on Saturday. A rain alert has been issued across all 75 districts of the state today. Bijnor has been witnessing intermittent heavy rain for the past three days, disrupting normal life. The rising water levels of the Ganga and Malan rivers have increased concerns among residents, while several roads across the district have been waterlogged by one to two feet, causing inconvenience to commuters. Power supply was also affected in several areas. On Saturday, a teenager drowned in a drain in Kiratpur, while two livestock died after being struck by lightning in Chandpur. See pictures of the rain and flooding... Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said, The monsoon system formed near Rajasthan, close to eastern Uttar Pradesh, will turn eastward after 24 hours. As a result, some areas of eastern Uttar Pradesh will receive heavy rain between September 6 and 8. After September 8, this system responsible for the rain will weaken. Consequently, heavy rain will stop across the state. However, light rain or showers may continue in some places.

stories.title: Power minister says ‘Enjoy when electricity goes out':Smiles and walks away when asked about wire theft in UP's Mau
stories.summary: Energy Minister A.K. Sharma arrived in Mau on Saturday (5 Sept). When asked a question related to electricity, he said, “If the power goes out, enjoy it.” After saying this, the minister moved on. He was asked about the theft of wires from a 33,000-volt high-tension line in the Gontha substation and Dargah area. However, the minister did not answer the question. A.K. Sharma had attended an educational seminar and teacher felicitation ceremony organized at the Gontha Primary School. Read what A.K. Sharma said in response to questions related to electricity... Reporter: Minister, the wire on the poles has gone missing for up to 3 kilometers in the district. A.K. Sharma: Where is your home? Reporter: Right here in Mau. A.K. Sharma: Does the electricity go out? Reporter: Yes, sir, it does. A.K. Sharma: Enjoy the electricity. Wires from a 33-kilovolt high-tension line had been stolen. After this, he moved on. In fact, wires from the 33-kilovolt high-tension line were stolen from the Gotha substation on August 20. The Energy Minister was questioned at 5 p.m. on Saturday (5 Sept) as he was leaving the event. Villagers Anurag, Surendra, and Ramesh say that when electricity department officials themselves claim to be unaware of such a major incident, it is right to question the Energy Minister. Since the matter concerns the minister's home district, it is necessary to demand an explanation from him about the system.

stories.title: Former UP Dy-CM Dinesh Sharma appointed Andaman Nicobar LG:BJP Rajya Sabha MP replaces Admiral D.K. Joshi
stories.summary: Former Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister and current Rajya Sabha MP Dr Dinesh Sharma has been appointed Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. He will replace Admiral D.K. Joshi (Retd.). Sharma’s current Rajya Sabha term has around two months remaining and is due to end in November 2026. Sharma thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah for appointing him to the post. Tenure as Lucknow mayor and UP deputy CM Sharma served as Mayor of the Lucknow Municipal Corporation from 2007 to 2017. He was appointed Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh in 2017 and held the post until March 2022. He was elected to the Rajya Sabha in 2023. BJP’s prominent Brahmin face in Awadh Sharma has been actively involved in politics since 1998 and has held various organisational and political positions over the years. His appointment as Lieutenant Governor is also being viewed as an outreach to Uttar Pradesh’s Brahmin community. In the Awadh region, Sharma is considered one of the BJP’s prominent Brahmin leaders. BJP UP in-charge Vinod Tawde congratulates him Uttar Pradesh BJP in-charge Vinod Tawde congratulated Dr. Dinesh Sharma. Writing on social media platform X, he said: “Heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to Dr. Dinesh Sharma ji, former Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, current Rajya Sabha MP, and senior BJP leader, on being appointed Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. I am confident that your able leadership and experience will give new direction and momentum to the development of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.” Who is Dr. Dinesh Sharma? Dr. Dinesh Sharma was born on January 12, 1964, in Lucknow, the state capital. He comes from a traditional Brahmin family in Lucknow. His father, Kedar Nath Sharma (Padha Ji), was an RSS and Jan Sangh worker. Dr. Dinesh Sharma studied at Lucknow University and later served as a professor there. During his tenure as a professor, he supervised more than 20 students for their PhDs and authored six books. Dinesh Sharma Remained in Office Continuously for Three Decades Former Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister and Rajya Sabha member Dr. Dinesh Sharma has been actively involved in politics for the past three decades. Since then, he has held various positions in the government and the party organization. He served as the state president of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha from 1993 to 1998. He served as the chairman of the National Youth Commission. He also held various other positions, including vice-chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Tourism Corporation. He served as the mayor of Lucknow from 2007 to March 2017. In 2014, he was appointed national vice-president of the BJP. That same year, he was appointed national convener of the BJP's membership drive. He served as Uttar Pradesh's Deputy Chief Minister from 2017 to 2022. In 2023, he was elected to the Rajya Sabha again. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, he was appointed the BJP's election in-charge for Maharashtra.

stories.title: Muslim clerics to move HC over demolition in Saharanpur:100-year-old mosque razed; Maulana asks, 'Are only masjid, madrasas, or shrines illegal?'
stories.summary: A mosque built on the Saharanpur Collectorate premises was completely demolished after a bulldozer operation that lasted around 16 hours. The demolition began at around 4 am on Saturday and continued until about 9 pm. The administration said the mosque had been illegally built on government land and was removed after following due legal procedure. Muslim clerics and members of the mosque committee, however, have questioned the action. They claim the mosque was more than 100 years old and existed before the present Collectorate building was constructed. They also claim that the mosque and the Collectorate premises are recorded under the same khasra (land survey) number. The Muslim side has cited old revenue records and other documents to challenge the administration’s claim that the mosque was an illegal structure. They have also questioned the timing of the demolition and the legal process followed. They claim they were not given enough time to approach a higher court after the City Magistrate’s order. According to them, six bulldozers were brought in at night, and the mosque was demolished before the matter could be taken to the High Court. The mosque’s legal representatives have now said they will approach the High Court. Read the report on this entire action... Mosque committee claims it existed before 1911 Muslim clerics and the mosque committee claim the structure was more than 100 years old and existed before the present Collectorate building. The mosque side reportedly presented a power bill dated January 1, 1911, as an old record. It has also claimed that the mosque has been registered with the Sunni Waqf Board for around 70 years. Congress MP Imran Masood also claimed that the mosque existed before 1911. According to him, old records show the land ownership in the names of Waheed Khan and Yakub Khan. Administration questions authenticity of 1911 power bill The administration has questioned the claim regarding the 1911 electricity bill. Officials said electricity supply began in Saharanpur around 1922, raising questions about the authenticity of a bill dated 1911. The mosque side, however, says the bill was obtained from a government website and had been presented before the court as an old record. The mosque side has also raised questions over the khasra number of the land. Maulana Qari Ishaq Gora claims that the mosque and the entire Collectorate premises are recorded under the same khasra number. The mosque committee has questioned how only the mosque could be declared an illegal structure if both properties fall under the same land record. It has demanded that this aspect also be examined. Muslim side cites 1926 revenue record Advocate Babar Wasim, who represented the mosque side, said a 1926 Fasli Khewat revenue record was presented before the court. According to him, the document lists Yakub Khan as the owner of the land and the Collectorate as the occupant. Wasim said the land covered around 24 bighas at the time. The area included the present Collectorate premises. Around eight bighas were used for the Collectorate building and its premises, while the remaining 16 bighas included the kotyard and mosque area, he claimed. According to the mosque side, the record described the Collectorate as an occupant rather than the owner of the land. Rent receipts and 1995 agreement also cited According to advocate Babar Wasim, records show that the post office operating from the Collectorate premises had paid rent for the mosque. He said the post office initially paid Rs 500 per month, which was increased to Rs 1,500 per month after an agreement in 1995. However, rent receipts from before 1995 were not presented as part of the records, he said. The mosque side argues that if the structure was completely illegal, the existence of rent payments and other government records over such a long period should also have been examined. The mosque side further claims that municipal tax had been imposed on the mosque since the municipality was formed in 1962 and that the tax was regularly paid. It says municipal documents were also presented before the court, but alleges that they were not accepted as evidence. Another key claim relates to Waqf records. According to advocate Babar Wasim, the mosque property has been registered with the Waqf Board since 1955 and has a Waqf number. An affidavit was also submitted by Tanveer, the mosque’s mutawalli (caretaker), according to the mosque side. Five other witnesses also submitted affidavits. Wasim alleged that these witnesses were not formally examined by the court. Dispute began with Bajrang Dal complaint in February 2025 The mosque was spread across around 3,300 square feet within the Collectorate premises. The two-storey structure had five rooms and two large halls. The ground floor had a large hall and two rooms, while the first floor had a hall and a large room. The post office was operating from the room, according to the report. On February 10, 2025, former Bajrang Dal state coordinator Vikas Tyagi complained to the District Magistrate, alleging that the mosque was an illegal structure. The complaint also alleged that rent was being collected from rooms on the mosque premises and from the post office. Following the complaint, the District Magistrate ordered a probe by a magistrate. The investigation concluded that the mosque was illegal, according to the administration. City Magistrate declares mosque illegal on July 16 On March 24, 2025, the administration filed a petition before the City Magistrate’s Court. On July 16, 2026, the court declared the mosque illegal and ordered its removal. It also ordered recovery of Rs 6.41 crore as compensation. The occupants were given 30 days to comply. On July 20, the mosque side filed a petition in the District Court challenging the magistrate’s order. On July 24, the District Court stayed the magistrate’s order and continued with the hearing. On September 2, District Judge Satendra Kumar upheld the City Magistrate’s demolition order and dismissed the mosque side’s petition. The administration then began preparations for the demolition. Police personnel were deployed in large numbers around the Collectorate premises to prevent any possible protest or law-and-order situation. Six bulldozers brought in after night-time security operation Security was increased around the Collectorate at around 11 pm on September 4. Around 300 police and Provincial Armed Constabulary personnel were deployed around the mosque. The demolition began at around 4 am on Saturday, September 5, with around six bulldozers brought to the site. After around 16 hours of work, the mosque was completely demolished and the debris was removed from the premises. Around 200 security personnel were deployed during the operation, according to the report. The surrounding borders were also sealed to prevent opposition leaders from entering the area. Local opposition leaders were placed under house arrest during the night, the report said. Mosque side plans to approach High Court The demolition has ended the physical structure but not the legal dispute. Advocate Babar Wasim, who represented the mosque side, said a writ petition would be filed in the High Court. The petition will seek consideration of the documents and evidence that were presented before the lower court. The mosque side will also seek action in accordance with the law, he said. Maulana Qari Ishaq Gora asked: Are only mosques, madrasas, or shrines illegal? Maulana Qari Ishaq Gora: ‘Are only mosques, madrasas and shrines illegal?’ Question: What do you have to say about the mosque that was demolished? Answer: The City Magistrate’s Court declared it illegal. I do not know on what basis it did so or what evidence the committee was able to present. This is certainly a day of grief not only for Saharanpur but for the entire country. There could also be a political angle behind the demolition of a mosque that was around 100 years old. We should have been given time to present our case before the court, but we were not given enough time to follow the legal process. The bulldozers were brought in so quickly. The question is: are only mosques, madrasas and shrines illegal? Are Muslims being treated unfairly? Question: It is being claimed that the mosque and the entire Collectorate premises have the same khasra number. Does that mean the Collectorate is also illegal? Answer: Everyone knows that the entire Collectorate area has the same khasra number. According to the information available, the Collectorate was built later and the mosque was already there. Despite this, we were not given time to appeal before a higher court. The bulldozers were brought in immediately. This has given politicians an opportunity to turn the matter into a political issue, which is unfortunate. Question: Do you feel that the mosque or the Muslim community is being targeted? Answer: There are some politicians who, by taking action against one community or targeting its religious places, are trying to please certain extremist groups. I believe this is the wrong approach. People have become more aware and we need to move beyond such issues. We respect people of every religion. Question: What will you do next? Will you continue the legal battle? Answer: Does the government see only mosques, madrasas and shrines as illegal across the state and the country? What kind of justice is this? This is a major question, and who will answer it? For now, we have appealed to everyone to remain calm and not act emotionally. We should follow the law and decide what legal step the panel handling the matter will take next.

Did Akhilesh’s Saharanpur rally get postponed due to factionalism?:Why did SP chief visit on 2 September; met some leaders, and brought others along?
stories.summary: A major Samajwadi Party (SP) public meeting was scheduled to be held in Saharanpur on September 6, 2026. It was named the ‘Yuva Yoddha Sammelan’ (Young Warriors’ Conference). However, the event was suddenly postponed. The SP officially cited bad weather and the possibility of heavy rain as the reason. However, there was speculation that two factors were behind the decision. 1- Internal factionalism within the party. 2- Opposition to remarks made about the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD). Interestingly, shortly after the public meeting was postponed, Akhilesh Yadav arrived in Saharanpur. During his nearly five-hour visit on September 2, he had lunch at the Chaudhary family home and held a closed-door meeting. He also met leaders from different factions in an attempt to manage the political equations. Read the report… What was the factionalism and real reason behind postponing the rally? Party national general secretary Chaudhary Rudrasen and his brother Chaudhary Indrasen said the event had been postponed in view of the possibility of rain. A new date could be fixed in October-November. Meanwhile, the RLD linked the postponement of the rally to Akhilesh Yadav’s ‘from a 25-paise coin to a rupee’ remark about Jayant Chaudhary. The RLD claimed that 36 communities in western UP had decided to boycott the rally. The SP rejected the claim, saying the rally had not even been officially announced. The party said that whenever the rally was held, it would be historic. How did factionalism emerge during preparations for the rally? Rudrasen and Indrasen, sons of the late Chaudhary Yashpal Singh, were given responsibility for organising the rally in Saharanpur. Chaudhary Rudrasen is the SP’s national general secretary. The family began preparations for the event as an opportunity to demonstrate its strength. However, questions also arose over who would get credit for the rally’s success. Some hoardings put up during the preparations did not feature pictures of local leaders. Some leaders complained in Lucknow that not everyone was being involved in the preparations. In other words, differences within the party had begun to come out into the open even before the rally. Akhilesh personally took charge of damage control During his Saharanpur visit, Akhilesh Yadav met leaders from different factions instead of siding with any one group. In other words, during his nearly five-hour visit, Akhilesh tried to bring together different political factions in Saharanpur. Chaudhary brothers came to Lucknow in a special aircraft To understand the importance of the late Yashpal Chaudhary’s family in Akhilesh’s eyes, it is important to look at what happened before the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Rudrasen wanted a Lok Sabha ticket from Saharanpur or Kairana. However, the Saharanpur seat went to the Congress. In Kairana, the ticket went to Ikra Hasan, daughter of the late Munawwar Hasan. This left Rudrasen and Indrasen unhappy. At a panchayat of their supporters, the two had even spoken of leaving the party. When Akhilesh learnt about this, he called both of them. He described them as members of the family and persuaded them not to leave the party. The two leaders were then flown to Lucknow on a special aircraft. Rudrasen and Indrasen travelled to Lucknow with Ashu Malik. They met Akhilesh, who addressed their grievances and resolved their differences. Expert says RLD would have benefited if Akhilesh had not acted Senior journalist Naved Shikoh, speaking about the shifting political equations in Saharanpur, says, The electoral mood in western UP is determined by the direction of the political wind in Saharanpur. In such a situation, if factionalism had surfaced during the public meeting and voices of dissent had emerged within the party, it could have caused greater damage to Akhilesh Yadav. This is why he sensed the sensitivity of the situation in advance. He not only postponed his rally but also went there himself before Jayant’s rally and managed the situation. Had he not done so, the RLD would perhaps not have hesitated to use the issue to its advantage at its public meetings. Understand the political significance of the entire episode SP spokesperson Fakhrul Hasan Chand says, No rally had been proposed in Saharanpur. This was propaganda created by the RLD. Akhilesh Yadav was initially scheduled to visit someone’s home in Saharanpur on September 6, but the programme was rescheduled and brought forward. Everyone in the party is united; there is no factionalism here. In fact, the sudden visit by Akhilesh Yadav is now being discussed more than the postponement of the rally itself. On one hand, he sought to win over the Chaudhary family, while on the other, he sent a message of maintaining a balance among local leaders. At the same time, he also appeared to be trying to manage the resentment caused by the war of words with the RLD.

stories.title: Will Cockroach Party help SP?:CJP spokesperson on 1.5-hour meeting says, 'Akhilesh invited me'; party to protest over youth issues
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav and Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka met in Lucknow on 3 September (Thursday). The two held a closed-door meeting that lasted around one and a half hours. The SP said Ashutosh Ranka had come to meet Akhilesh to convey thanks on behalf of CJP’s Abhijit Dipke. The SP had supported CJP during its protest in Delhi. The question is that several Opposition parties had supported the protest, so why did the meeting take place only with Akhilesh Yadav? What does the meeting mean ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections? Read about it in today’s Sunday Big Story... 1. Full story behind the meeting CJP national spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka answered Dainik Bhaskar’s five questions. Question: Did you come to meet Akhilesh yourself, or did he invite you? Ashutosh: CJP’s protest was underway at Jantar Mantar. During the protest, Akhilesh Yadav and the SP had supported us. Akhilesh Yadav had also been inviting me to meet him, so I came to Lucknow. Question: What is your connection with Uttar Pradesh? Ashutosh: My in-laws are in Varanasi. I studied at IIT Kanpur. So I have always had a connection with Uttar Pradesh. Question: What role will CJP play in the UP elections? Ashutosh: The party will not contest the elections. We will not enter active politics. Question: Then what is the purpose of coming to UP? Ashutosh: Uttar Pradesh is the largest state in the country. We will expand our organisation here. Question: What will be the main issues? Ashutosh: Education and employment are our key issues. Young people should have access to good education and adequate employment opportunities. We will work on these issues in Uttar Pradesh as well. 2. Will CJP bring votes or just shape the narrative? CJP began on social media. It does not have a strong grassroots cadre, but it has a significant reach on social media. The party is claimed to have around 2.55 crore followers. Uttar Pradesh has around 2.07 crore Gen-Z youths aged between 18 and 29. During CJP’s protest in Delhi, large numbers of young people from several cities in UP travelled to the capital. Student protests were also held in Prayagraj, Agra and Kanpur. In such a scenario, CJP’s biggest utility for the SP may not be vote transfer but raising issues on social media and among young people. It is believed that if CJP becomes active in UP on issues such as education, employment and recruitment, it could have an impact among the youth. The social media battle between the SP and BJP is already underway. In such a situation, CJP’s support could help create a favourable atmosphere for the SP. How effective will CJP be in UP? Recruitment, unemployment and paper leaks are major issues among young people in Uttar Pradesh. There has been no basic teacher recruitment drive in the state for the past eight years. Candidates have been protesting continuously. CJP leaders have also repeatedly said they want to make development, education and employment the main issues in UP. Ashutosh Ranka has said that if a major youth movement emerges over paper leaks and unemployment, CJP will join it. 7.7% of young people unemployed in UP According to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2025, the unemployment rate among young people aged 15 to 29 in UP is 7.7%. In urban areas, it is 10.1%. The government claims to have provided 9 lakh jobs over nine years. Meanwhile, data has emerged showing that more than 55,000 posts in basic education and for lekhpals are vacant. In recent years, several recruitment examinations, including UPTET, RO/ARO, UP Police recruitment and the assistant professor examination, have been hit by paper leaks or other controversies. Millions of candidates have been affected by these examinations. Political ambitions of CJP leaders? Sonam Wangchuk had spoken about political ambitions among CJP’s leadership. He said political ambition was not wrong, but a student platform should not be turned into an individual political vehicle. He suggested that if CJP leaders wanted to enter politics in the future, they should form a separate political party. Alternatively, they could enter politics through an existing party. Responding to this, Ashutosh Ranka says CJP’s political ambition is not to gain power but to change the way politics in the country works. Met Opposition leaders at different times CJP currently has 12 prominent members. Six of them have been associated with the Aam Aadmi Party at some point in the past. Abhijit Dipke and Ashutosh Ranka are among them. After CJP came into existence and began its protest in Delhi, Aam Aadmi Party leaders were the first to support it. Senior party leader Manish Sisodia posted a video on social media expressing his support. During the protest, AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal also met CJP leaders. Apart from him, TMC MPs Mahua Moitra and Kirti Azad, Shiv Sena (Uddhav faction) leader Sanjay Raut, CPI(M)’s John Brittas, and SP leaders Priya Saroj, Iqra Hasan and Dimple Yadav, among others, met CJP leaders. However, Congress leaders stayed away from the protest. CJP leaders have also not met any Congress leader so far. CJP’s possible model in UP CJP says it will not contest the UP elections, but is preparing to expand its organisation and become active on issues concerning young people. In such a scenario, CJP’s strength could lie less in winning seats and more in shaping issues and the narrative among the youth. The question now is whether it will remain merely a partner of the SP in protests or also help create an anti-government mood among young voters ahead of the elections.

stories.title: Village chief's son dies of swine flu in Kanpur:Postmortem confirms cause; second patient on ventilator at Hallet Hospital
stories.summary: A 30-year-old man from Kannauj, identified as Shivam, has died of swine flu while undergoing treatment at a private hospital in Kanpur. His family had alleged negligence in his treatment and demanded a post-mortem. After the post-mortem and the investigation report, it became clear on Saturday that Shivam did not die due to medical negligence but because of swine flu. The officer in charge of the post-mortem house has sent a report to the Chief Medical Officer (CMO). Following the death of the swine flu patient, the health department has gone on alert. Meanwhile, another 55-year-old swine flu patient is undergoing treatment on a ventilator at the LLR Hospital (Hallet Hospital). His condition remains extremely critical. Post-mortem report reveals the cause of death, health department issues alert Village Chief Ram Raj, a resident of Tera Jaket village in Kannauj's Gursahaiganj area, said that on the afternoon of August 28, his son suddenly experienced severe stomach pain. When his condition worsened, he was taken to Dr. Tomar's clinic in Kannauj. After examining him, the doctor said that fluid had accumulated in his lungs and that he had an abdominal infection. As his condition was described as critical, he was admitted for better treatment to Anurag Hospital in Sharda Nagar, Kanpur. When his condition deteriorated, the hospital management admitted him to the ICU, where he remained under treatment for four days. He died on September 1. The family members created a disturbance, alleging negligence in treatment, and demanded that the body be post-mortem examined. After an investigation, police from Rawatpur police station sent the body for a post-mortem examination, which was conducted on September 2. During the post-mortem, samples were sent for testing after suspicions arose. The test report received on September 5 made it clear that the youth had not died due to incorrect treatment, but because of a swine flu infection. As soon as the information was received, the officer in charge of the postmortem house sent a report to the CMO. Along with this, an investigation report was sent to the CMO of Kannauj. Now, all family members will also be tested to determine whether any of them have contracted swine flu. Meanwhile, the health department was also put on alert as soon as it learned of the death of the first swine flu patient. CMO Dr. Haridutt Nemi took cognizance of the matter and issued an alert. The staff at the hospital where the patient died will be tested. In addition, the employees of the postmortem house will also be tested to determine whether anyone has been exposed to the infection.

stories.title: SP MLA’s uncle says offering namaz is matter of pride:'I'm not afraid of FIR'; had offered prayers at Moradabad Circuit House
stories.summary: Offering namaz is not a matter of shame, but of pride. I am not afraid of legal proceedings. Saraswati Vandana is performed in schools, and Bhoomi Pujan is conducted before government construction projects. In such a situation, filing an FIR or raising questions only about namaz is discrimination. This was said on Saturday by Haji Mohammad Usman, the uncle of Samajwadi Party MLA Mohammad Faheem Irfan, in Moradabad. A video of Mohammad Usman offering namaz at the Circuit House in Moradabad on Friday (September 4) had surfaced. An FIR was registered against Mohammad Usman in the matter that same Friday. After this, Usman said that he did not know when or where the video was recorded, or who had recorded it. SP leader says-I did not block anyone's way Mohammad Usman said, I can be seen offering prayers behind cars in the parking lot. I am not seen blocking anyone's way. If any law has been violated, there should be an impartial investigation. However, the case registered over offering prayers should be dismissed. The Constitution has given everyone the right to worship. People who believe in the Constitution will not be intimidated by such cases. Usman appealed to people not to respond to hatred with hatred and to raise their voices while staying within the framework of the Constitution and the law. FIR registered for offering namaz at circuit house An FIR was registered against Samajwadi Party district vice president Haji Mohammad Usman at the Majhola police station late Friday evening on the complaint of Anit Kumar, the junior engineer in charge of the Circuit House. City SP Ranvijay Singh said, Haji Usman parked his car on the Circuit House road and offered namaz illegally behind it. This obstructed the movement of vehicles and people. The police have registered a case and begun an investigation. Video posted on Facebook on September 3 A video of Haji Usman offering prayers was posted on September 3 by a Facebook user named Malik Sharif. The caption of the post read: ‘Mohammad Usman Pradhan ji offering the Asr prayer today.’ Photos and videos related to the programs and activities of SP MLA Mohammad Faheem have been regularly posted from this account. Several photos and videos of the MLA and his uncle, Haji Usman, together have also been posted on this account. After the matter came to light, the video of the prayer was deleted from the social media account. Bajrang Dal also demands an investigation from the administration The police are now investigating when and under what circumstances the video was made, and who posted it on social media. Meanwhile, Rohan Saxena, state president of the Rashtriya Bajrang Dal, has demanded that the administration conduct an impartial investigation into the matter. He said, The Circuit House is government premises. In such a situation, the administration should clarify whether religious activities of any religion are permitted on government premises. The administration should also investigate the intention behind offering namaz at the Circuit House on the day of Shri Krishna Janmashtami. High Court had said-No one has the right to offer namaz in public places In May 2026, the Allahabad High Court delivered a ruling regarding offering namaz on public land. A bench of Justice Saral Srivastava and Justice Garima Prasad had said: Everyone has equal rights over public land. Its one-sided use is not legally acceptable. Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi Barelvi had supported the High Court's decision. The Maulana had said, Islam clearly states that prayers should not be offered at a place where there is any dispute, where a spectacle is being created, or where someone has an objection or opposition. Mohammad Usman has been involved in controversies before Haji Mohammad Usman has also served as a former district panchayat member. He has previously been the head of his ancestral village, Ibrahimपुर. Haji Usman is the younger brother of former Bilari MLA Haji Mohammad Irfan and the uncle of the current Bilari MLA. Haji Mohammad Usman's name had earlier surfaced in a caste certificate controversy as well. Following a complaint, the district-level verification committee investigated the matter. The investigation found that the Other Backward Class (OBC) certificates belonging to MLA Mohammad Faheem and his uncle Mohammad Usman, identifying them as members of the Jhojha caste, did not comply with the rules. Following this, the administration cancelled the OBC caste certificates of MLA Mohammad Faheem, Haji Mohammad Usman, and his two daughters, Farheen Jahan and Samreen Jahan.

stories.title: 7 daughters carry mother’s bier:Youngest daughter performs last rites, says ‘She raised us like sons’
stories.summary: In Auraiya on Saturday, after their mother's death, seven daughters took turns carrying her bier on their shoulders. When they reached the cremation ground, preparations for the last rites began. Meanwhile, when the question of lighting the funeral pyre arose, everyone was left wondering who would perform the ritual. After a discussion, the youngest daughter decided that she would light her mother's funeral pyre. Why rely on a male relative? Her elder sisters also supported her decision. At around 3 p.m., the youngest daughter lit her mother's funeral pyre. The incident took place in the Dibiyapur area. Complete incident details Mother raised them alone after the father's death Krishna Devi (59), a resident of Durga Nagar, was married to Ramkishore Savita, who had served in the army. He died a few years after retiring. At the time, due to social customs, the family sought the help of a nephew for Ramkishore's last rites, as they had no son. After her husband's death, Krishna Devi raised her seven daughters all by herself. Their mother was their sole support and guide. Krishna Devi had been ill for quite some time. Her daughters jointly bore the expenses of her treatment and the household. Her youngest daughter, Soni Savita (25), was living at her maternal home to care for her mother. Her husband works in a private job in Agra. All seven daughters shouldered their mother's bier Krishna Devi passed away on Saturday morning. During preparations for the funeral, there was a discussion about who would perform the last rites. The villagers and family members discussed whether a male relative should take on this responsibility. Meanwhile, Krishna Devi's youngest daughter, Soni Savita, interrupted everyone. She said, "Our mother raised us like sons. She used to say that all of you daughters are sons to me. We also never let her feel the absence of sons. Now, we will not depend on anyone else for our mother's last rites." Daughter performed the last rites for her mother following all traditions Setting aside social customs, Krishna Devi's 7 daughters took turns carrying their mother's bier on their shoulders. The villagers and family members also helped them. Everyone reached the cremation ground in Dibiyapur with the deceased's body. There, Krishna Devi's youngest daughter, Soni, lit her mother's funeral pyre following all the traditional rituals. This decision conveyed a message about the role of daughters in society. According to the villagers, their mother made her daughters self-reliant throughout her life. She stood by them through every difficulty. The daughters, too, fulfilled their responsibility toward their mother at the end of her life.
