The accident occurred at around 3 p.m. at Pintu Singh Patel's crusher plant in the Ahraura area. As soon as they learned of the incident, nearby residents reached the site and informed the police and administration. Four workers from Chunar trapped After receiving the information, a police team reached the site and inspected the scene. According to Chunar Circle Officer Mohammad Faheem, Bargawan resident Lal Bahadur, son of Dulaare, Ashok, son of Basant, Rakesh, son of Ram Ji, and Duryodhan, son of Jhingai, all under Chunar police station limits, are feared to be trapped in the debris. No plant owner or employee was present at the site at the time of the accident. However, the police have begun gathering information by questioning people connected with the incident. SDM and SP reached the spot SDM, SP Rajkumar Meena and CO Gayatri Yadav reached the spot to investigate the incident. They inspected the site and gathered information. The officials have begun examining all the facts related to the accident. At present, it will become clear only after the administration's investigation under what circumstances the heavy part of the machine fell and how many workers were present at the plant at the time of the accident. The police have not confirmed the death of any worker or that anyone was trapped under the debris. The news is being updated continuously...

stories.title: Vinod Tawde on Akhilesh’s PDA:‘Someone else’s wealth is ours’; reaches Lucknow for first time as BJP’s UP in-charge to meet Yogi
stories.summary: BJP’s Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde on Saturday said the party would “thwart Akhilesh Yadav’s PDA”, interpreting the Samajwadi Party leader’s acronym as “Paraya Dhan Apna” (someone else’s wealth is one’s own). Addressing his first visit to Lucknow after being given charge of Uttar Pradesh, Tawde said the BJP had become the world’s largest party under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, while the pace of development in Uttar Pradesh had accelerated under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. He further said- Every worker of the BJP and NDA will contest and win the upcoming Assembly elections with full strength. After that, we will remain dedicated to serving the people of Uttar Pradesh for the next five years. Earlier, Vinod Tawde received a grand welcome at Lucknow airport. Uttar Pradesh BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary, state organization general secretary Dharampal Singh, state general secretary Sanjay Rai, and state office in-charge Govind Narayan Shukla were present on the occasion. BJP president Nitin Nabin appointed Vinod Tawde as the new state in-charge of Uttar Pradesh on December 18. Jagdish Ishwarbhai Patel was given the responsibility of co-in-charge. Tawde is the BJP's national general secretary and a Rajya Sabha MP. He has previously served as the in-charge of Haryana and Bihar. In 2025, under his charge, the BJP registered a landslide victory in Bihar. Will hold a review meeting behind closed doors, meet the CM and Deputy CM as well Vinod Tawde, who has arrived in Uttar Pradesh for a two-day visit, will begin a series of meetings to strengthen the organisation and sharpen the strategy for the upcoming elections. First, he will hold a closed-door review meeting with Pankaj Chaudhary and Organisation General Secretary Dharampal Singh. After this, he will meet with the BJP's state office-bearers to receive feedback on organisational activities, campaigns, and future action plans. He will then hold a core committee meeting with CM Yogi, Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya, and Brajesh Pathak. The meeting will deliberate on the current political climate, coordination between the government and the organisation, and the strategy for the upcoming elections. How important is Vinod Tawde's visit before the elections? Find out Vinod Tawde's visit to Lucknow before the assembly elections is considered highly significant. According to political analysts, the party will seek to infuse new enthusiasm among its organisation and workers through this visit so that preparations for the upcoming elections can be strengthened. The visit could also prove crucial in further consolidating the party's hold at the grassroots level. Elected as an MLA in 2014, became BJP's national secretary in 2020 Vinod Tawde is originally from Mumbai. He remained active in the party organisation in Maharashtra for a long time. He has also served as a minister in the Maharashtra government and as the leader of the opposition in the Legislative Council. In 2026, he was appointed in-charge of the Kerala Assembly elections. His political career began with the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP). In 2014, Tawde was elected as an MLA from Maharashtra's Borivali constituency for the first time. On September 26, 2020, the BJP appointed him as its National Secretary. With this, his role expanded beyond Maharashtra into the national organisation. Why did the BJP give Tawde the most crucial state? The reason... Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh next year In Uttar Pradesh, which has 403 assembly seats, elections are likely to be held in February-March next year. The BJP suffered a setback in the state in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The Samajwadi Party emerged as the largest party with 37 seats, while the BJP was reduced to 33 seats. In this context, the 2027 elections are being seen as a major test for the BJP – not only to retain power in the state but also to strengthen its position following its performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

Villages in the low-lying areas of Barabanki and Gonda have turned into islands. Water can be seen everywhere. People do not even have space to light their cooking stoves. In Unnao, water has entered homes to a depth of 4-5 feet. People are being forced to spend their lives on rooftops. In Hamirpur, 100 bighas of crops have been submerged due to riverbank erosion. stories.title: 81 teachers honoured on Teachers’ Day:CM Yogi felicitates them in Gorakhpur; retirement age raised by 2 years, 4,000 km free bus travel annually
stories.summary: During a Teachers' Day ceremony in Gorakhpur, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath broke with protocol and invited all 81 teachers to the stage to honour them. He said he had been told that only 10 teachers would come on stage, but he knew that all the teachers had travelled from faraway places. "Some have come from Meerut, while others have come from Hamirpur and Mahoba," he said. He further said, "It is fine. If they instil values in children, they are themselves well-cultured. They may not say anything, but they too have feelings. It may have taken up some of my time, but I called everyone to the stage and honoured them." Taking a dig at previous governments, CM Yogi said: "Before 2017, cheating was carried out on a contract basis. Children from other states used to come here and pay money to pass examinations. The education system was in a poor state and the youth were facing a crisis of identity. Questions were being raised about Uttar Pradesh, and the state with India's largest population was being put in the dock." The ceremony was held at the Yogiraj Baba Gambhirnath Auditorium. Of the 81 teachers honoured, 61 are from the Basic Education Department and 20 are from the Secondary Education Department. The group also includes 33 women teachers. At the ceremony, 76 teachers from the Basic and Secondary Education Departments were honoured with the 'State Teachers' Award 2025', while five teachers from self-financed secondary schools received the 'Chief Minister's Teachers' Award 2025'. See the pictures... CM Yogi Adityanath felicitating teachers. Also present on stage are Basic Education Minister Sandeep Singh, Secondary Education Minister Gulab Devi, Fisheries Minister Sanjay Nishad, MLC Dhruv Kumar Tripathi and others. Yogi says, 'We have stopped making cheating hubs examination centres' CM Yogi said that the ‘Nipun Abhiyan’ would now be implemented up to Class 5. He said that before 2017, children did not even have basic knowledge of letters. He said, "If a child does not know letters and numbers, how will they study mathematics and science, and how will they understand the meaning of a sentence?" He said the result was that schools had turned into hubs for cheating. “Cheating was carried out on a contract basis, and students from distant states used to come here to take examinations.” He added, "Contracts were run in the name of examinations, and another person would appear for an examination in place of a candidate. I instructed that such schools should not be made examination centres, and subsequently, such schools were stopped from being made centres." Yogi says, ‘For the first time, teachers have been guaranteed social security’ CM Yogi said, "For the first time, teachers have been guaranteed social security so that, in the event of any unfortunate incident, a teacher's family does not feel that it has been left alone. This is also a part of respecting teachers." He added, "The government has taken several steps in this direction so that students can receive quality education and a better environment can be created for it."

stories.title: Bulldozer action at mosque in Saharanpur Collectorate:Mayawati urges govt to stop action, Iqra placed under house arrest; MP Masood vows HC move
stories.summary: 70-year-old mosque in the collectorate complex in Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh, is being demolished. Six bulldozers have been carrying out the demolition since 4am on Saturday. As a precautionary measure, five companies of PAC and RAF personnel, along with 200 police officers, have been deployed. Police are not allowing anyone to approach the mosque. So far, around 70% of the mosque has been demolished. The action is being carried out on the orders of a magistrate after a court declared the mosque illegal. Before the demolition, rumours spread around 11pm on Friday that the administration was planning to demolish the mosque, drawing a large crowd. The administration team immediately reached the spot and dispersed the crowd. Kairana MP Ikra Hasan, who was travelling to Saharanpur to oppose the action, was placed under house arrest by police. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav said in Lucknow that a true Hindu can never insult another religion. He alleged that the action was being taken because people had been caught stealing from the Ram temple. AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi questioned whether Muslims still have their constitutional right to religious freedom. He asked why places of worship were repeatedly being demolished over what he called weak and fabricated reasons. BSP chief Mayawati appealed to the government to immediately stop the demolition. stories.title: SP launches PDA Pathshala in Lucknow:Free bags, books featuring Akhilesh Yadav distributed; spokesperson says 26,000 schools shut across UP
stories.summary: Today (5 Sept) on the occasion of Teachers’ Day, the Samajwadi Party organised a PDA Pathshala in Gomtinagar, Lucknow. SP leaders and workers taught children as part of a protest against the closure of primary schools across Uttar Pradesh. Notebooks and books were also distributed among the children. SP says 26,000 schools have been shut SP leader Fakhrul Hasan Chand said, “PDA Pathshalas were organised in all 75 districts of the state following a call by party national president Akhilesh Yadav. The campaign was launched in protest against the closure of around 26,000 primary schools.” According to Chand, “Children from PDA communities have been most affected by the closures, particularly those from backward, Dalit, minority, Muslim and farming families. The disruption was affecting their education.” Party vows to continue raising education issue Chand said, “The Samajwadi Party would continue to raise issues related to education through PDA Pathshalas and oppose measures that, according to the party, are disrupting access to schooling for children from disadvantaged communities.” SP workers to teach children daily and provide study materials SP workers said the PDA Pathshala will continue to operate, with a Samajwadi Party worker teaching the children for an hour every day. Study materials will also be provided to them. Facilities to be added soon At present, the children study while sitting on mats spread on the ground. SP workers said chairs, desks and other necessary facilities would soon be arranged for them. Promise to reopen closed schools The workers said that if the Samajwadi Party forms the government in Uttar Pradesh, all schools that were shut down will be reopened.

stories.title: Student’s father beats principal in Gorakhpur:Tears shirt, vandalises school; daughter was made to do squats for arriving late
stories.summary: The father of a Class 6 student allegedly assaulted a government school principal after the teacher punished his daughter for arriving late in Gorakhpur. The principal was reportedly beaten in front of the staff, and his shirt was torn. Other teachers intervened and defused the situation. According to reports, the teacher had made the student perform the ‘murga’ (rooster) punishment for coming late to school. After learning about it, her father became angry, reached the school and allegedly assaulted the principal. The principal has filed a complaint against the man, accusing him of assault and vandalising school property. The incident took place on 1st September at Purva Madhyamik Vidyalaya in Khirkita Dubey, under the Gola police station area. The complaint was filed on 3rd September. Student was made to perform the 'murga' pose for arriving late Jitendra Kumar (56), the principal of Purva Madhyamik Vidyalaya Khirkita Dubey in the Gola area, filed a complaint against a student's father, Dilip Kumar, on September 3. In his complaint, Jitendra Kumar stated that on the morning of September 1, a class 6 student arrived late to school. Students who arrive late to school are punished to maintain discipline. Under this policy, the student was made to perform the 'murga' (rooster) pose for a short time. When the student's father, Dilip Kumar, learned about this, he became angry. It is alleged that Dilip Kumar then reached the school and started a dispute. Jitendra Kumar stated that he tried to reason with Dilip, but he began to assault him. Beaten in front of staff, shirt torn Jitendra Kumar alleged that Dilip Kumar assaulted him in front of other school staff. Other teachers stepped in to save him and calmed the situation by reasoning with the accused. It is alleged that during the assault, Dilip Kumar also tore his shirt. Additionally, government property was damaged due to vandalism in the school. Accused works as a painter Dilip Kumar works as a painter. It is being reported that he had gone to the school earlier as well to secure a contract, which had also led to a dispute. The accused has been absconding since the incident, and the police are searching for him. Fear among staff after the incident After receiving information about the incident, the police reached the spot. The head teacher has demanded strict action against the accused from the police. He expressed apprehension that the accused might repeat such an incident with him in the future as well. After the incident, the school teachers and staff are also scared. The matter is a topic of discussion in the area. Gola Police Station In-charge Inspector Chandraprakash Pandey said that a case has been registered against the accused based on the complaint of the headmaster. The matter is being investigated. Further action will be taken based on the facts that emerge during the investigation.

stories.title: Floods hit 26 UP districts, 3.5 lakh affected:17,000 rescued so far; rainfall quota nearly met, alert in 71 districts
stories.summary: Due to continuous monsoon rains in UP, 26 districts, including Varanasi and Prayagraj, are affected by floods. This has impacted 3.53 lakh people. So far, 17,544 people have been moved to safe locations, while approximately 5,000 people are staying in relief camps. On Saturday morning, light rain occurred in 10 cities, including Lucknow, Barabanki, Hardoi, and Sitapur. The rest of the districts are experiencing mild sunshine. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an alert for rain with thunderstorms in 71 districts today. Heavy rain is expected in Western UP. The rainfall quota for this monsoon season in the state has almost been met. As of September 4, an average of 612 mm of rainfall has been recorded in the state, whereas 619.7 mm of rain was recorded by September 4 last year. This means that so far, there has been only 1% less rainfall compared to last year. See pictures of the flood... Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh stated- Due to the weather systems formed near Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, Western UP will experience heavy rainfall in the next 24 hours. After this, the system will move towards Eastern UP. This will cause heavy rainfall in some areas of Eastern UP between September 6 and September 8. After September 8, this rain-bearing system will weaken, leading to a cessation of heavy rainfall across the state. However, light rain or drizzles will continue in some places.

UP MLAs caught taking bribes:Bhaskar exposes BJP, SP MLAs insisting on 35% commission - Part I
stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, MLAs themselves are allegedly engaging in corruption in the name of development. They reportedly write recommendation letters for roads, drains and street lights only when they receive a 35% to 40% commission. A recommendation letter is a letter from an MLA based on which the CDO (Chief Development Officer) releases money from the MLA development fund. With 40% of the money allegedly going into the MLA's pocket, it can be imagined what the quality of the work would be. Dainik Bhaskar has made its biggest expose so far, catching two MLAs allegedly taking bribes on camera. A Bhaskar reporter posed as an NGO manager and negotiated with the MLAs for the release of funds. The MLAs were focused on just one question: how much commission would they get? The MLAs were caught taking commissions on a hidden camera and subsequently issued recommendation letters for the release of MLA funds. Of the two MLAs, one is from the BJP and the other from the Samajwadi Party (SP). Read the full investigation… First, we conducted a sting operation on BJP MLA Jai Mangal Kannaujiya. Kannaujiya has previously faced allegations of bribery. We registered an NGO and then underwent training related to solar lights because we intended to seek funds from the MLA specifically for installing solar lights. To build a rapport with the MLA, we travelled with him from village to village for 30 days. We held a total of eight rounds of negotiations with the MLA for funds for solar lights. In the fourth round, MLA Kannaujiya agreed to sanction work worth ₹10.50 lakh in return for a 35% commission. During the subsequent meetings, he took the bribe and signed the recommendation letter and handed it to us. Read our conversation with him word for word… "Others are giving me 40% commission. How much will you give me?" - Kannaujiya Kannaujiya: "The other solar people are giving 40% commission." Reporter: "We can give you up to 35%." Kannaujiya: "Fine. I want the money on the same day we write the letter." Reporter: "How much should we pay as an advance?" Kannaujiya: "Why pay an advance? Pay the full amount. Get the letter written by me and finish the matter." Reporter: "If you say so, we can pay 20% of the 35% commission now. Once the letter is issued, we will pay the remaining 80%." Kannaujiya: "Fine. Come tomorrow morning at 11am." Kannaujiya: "Is the proposal for ₹10.50 lakh?" Reporter: "The 35% commission will be ₹368,500. Twenty per cent of this will be ₹73,500." (While handing over the money) "We have brought ₹50,000 in cash for now. We will pay the rest later." Kannaujiya: "Fine. Bring it tomorrow." (Two days later, we reached the MLA's house and handed over the remaining amount.) "Give me some more money. We had agreed that you would give me 20% of the total payment," - Kannaujiya Kannaujiya: "How much is this?" Reporter: "₹23,500." Kannaujiya: "How much does it come to?" Reporter: "Thirty-five per cent of ₹10.50 lakh comes to ₹367,500, which we will give you. We had agreed to pay 20% of this amount upfront, which comes to ₹73,500. We had already given you ₹50,000." Kannaujiya: (surprised) "₹73,500. No, brother." (He took out the calculator on his mobile phone and spent some time adding up the figures.) "You are giving me 20%, aren't you? You had said you would give us 20% of the 35%." Reporter: "We are giving you 20% of the 35%. We have already given you ₹73,500. Now ₹294,000 remains." Kannaujiya: "Give me something more, brother. We had agreed that you would give me 20% of the total payment." Reporter: "You were upset, so we have come to give you something more." Kannaujiya: "I am not the kind of person who gets upset. If you want to give something more, then give it." Reporter: "Sir, this is ₹10,000." Kannaujiya: (while taking the money) "Go, enjoy yourself. Come tomorrow and collect the letter." In this way, MLA Kannaujiya took a total bribe of ₹83,500 from us. The following day, he handed over the recommendation letter. SP MLA Pooja Saroj from Mehnagar in Azamgarh district has also faced allegations of taking bribes. We developed a relationship with the MLA's relative and representative, Vikas Saroj. Posing as an NGO manager, we presented the MLA with a proposal to install solar lights and water coolers. When the MLA asked for a sample, we purchased and installed a solar light to demonstrate it. For 15 days, we went from village to village with her associates and selected the locations where the solar lights were to be installed. We held a total of 15 meetings with the MLA. During the 12th meeting, the MLA raised the issue of commission. ‘Our only rule on bribes is 50% in advance,’ - MLA Pooja Pooja: "What was discussed?" Reporter: "Please give us the work order. We will make some advance payment." Pooja: (laughing) "Not some. We have only one rule: 50% commission first and 50% later. Vikas can discuss the matter accordingly. How much commission are we getting?" Reporter: "We will be able to give up to 35%." Pooja: "How much will you give as an advance, 50% or…?" Reporter: "We will pay 10% of the 35% as an advance." Pooja: "Before the paper, the recommendation letter, is prepared; that is, when I sign it, 50% of the advance must have reached me." (At a rate of ₹13,500 per unit for 200 solar street lights and ₹20,000 per unit for 20 water coolers, the total budget came to ₹31 lakh.) Pooja: "The amount is very low. Around ₹10 lakh. Only ₹5 lakh has to be given as an advance." Reporter: "Take 10% of ₹10 lakh now. We will make the remaining 90% later." Pooja: "First, arrange the commission for the solar lights." Reporter: "Fine. The budget for 200 lights comes to ₹27 lakh. Thirty-five per cent of this is ₹9.45 lakh." Pooja: "How much is 50%?" Reporter: "It will be around ₹5 lakh. When you sign the letter, we will give you ₹1 lakh. As soon as the money is released, we will give you ₹8.45 lakh." Pooja: "No." (Showing ₹5 lakh on the calculator on her mobile phone) "Bring this amount and I will sign the letter and give it to you." Pooja: "Don't do this. Give the full amount after two days. It is not such a large amount." Reporter: "This is our NGO's policy." Pooja: "Who is it? Let me speak to them. Call them. They are following some nonsensical policy." Reporter: "We can arrange 25% for you tomorrow, which comes to ₹236,650. The rest will be paid after the letter is issued." Pooja: "No. You see how you want to do it." Reporter: "Ma'am, it is just a matter of two days." Pooja: "Their policy will not work with me. We are getting entangled for no reason. This is not right." A few days later, Vikas called. He said, "You haven't come." We said, "Madam, the MLA is insisting on 50% in advance. We can give 25%. If you get the MLA to sign the letter and send it to us on WhatsApp, we will come with ₹5 lakh." Seven days later, Vikas sent four recommendation letters. Vikas said, "Bring ₹14,17,500, which is half of the 35% commission, and take the hard copies of the letters." Since we had already exposed the MLA, we did not go to collect the hard copies. MLAs' close associates are also taking money MLA Pooja Saroj's representative Vikas took ₹10,000 from us three times: ₹10,000, then another ₹10,000, and then ₹5,000. That means these people are allegedly taking 1-2% of the MLA development fund. Similarly, Sanjeev Shukla, a close associate of Maharajganj Sadar MLA Jai Mangal Kannaujiya, took ₹5,000 from us on four occasions, totalling ₹20,000. Now know where MLAs can use the MLA fund In Uttar Pradesh, every MLA receives ₹5 crore every year under the MLA development fund. That means ₹25 crore over five years. The funds can be used for various works, including roads, drains, brick-paved roads, community buildings, drinking water and lighting. Taking commission from the MLA fund is a serious matter and can lead to a seven-year sentence Atul Singh, AGM-1 (Additional Government Advocate) at the Lucknow High Court, said, "If an MLA takes a commission or bribe, Section 7 of the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita will apply. It provides for a sentence of three to seven years. The accounts containing approved or remaining MLA funds in the name of the accused MLA can be frozen immediately. At the Assembly level, the Conduct Committee or Ethics Committee investigates the matter." The chain of bribery in the MLA fund does not end here. When an MLA's recommendation letter reaches the CDO office, a commission is allegedly fixed for everyone there, from employees to officers. Read Part 2 of Bhaskar's biggest expose tomorrow for the rate list of bribes allegedly demanded by officers and employees at the CDO office.

stories.title: Will Jayant Chaudhary field wife Charu in elections?:Just 2-minute speech in Saharanpur, but her reply to Akhilesh steals the show
stories.summary: At the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD)’s ‘Swabhiman Rally’ in Saharanpur, Charu Chaudhary, wife of Jayant Chaudhary, is drawing more attention for her speech than her husband. Charu directly hit back at Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav’s ‘chavanni’ (quarter-rupee coin) jibe at Jayant Chaudhary. Charu said, ‘No one has the right to insult you or lecture you.’ She added that such remarks reflect the other person’s mindset and arrogance. In a democracy, she said, it is the people who decide which government comes to power and who enters or leaves office. Following Charu’s assertive speech, speculation is growing in political circles that Jayant could field his wife in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. If that happens, Charu would become the second woman from the Chaudhary family to enter electoral politics. Jayant’s grandmother, Gayatri Devi, wife of former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh, was active in politics. She served as an MLA from Iglas in 1969 and Gokul in 1974, and was elected MP from Kairana in 1980. Will Jayant field Charu in 2027? Charu has three key advantages: a political family legacy, years of election campaign experience, and the ability to deliver political speeches openly and confidently. She has regularly addressed rural women at village gatherings in Mathura and Baghpat with ease. Charu’s association with politics is not new. She has been active in election campaigns and RLD activities since 2009 and has regularly appeared at her husband Jayant Chaudhary’s rallies. Her late father-in-law and former Union minister Ajit Singh also made her a star campaigner for the party, recognising her political involvement. During the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, Charu held a roadshow for Jayant Chaudhary in Chhaprauli, Baghpat. The event was scheduled to last around six hours, but the huge crowd and enthusiasm kept it going until around 1 am. In 2021, she also joined the farmers’ protest in Delhi and was seen supporting women farmers. She has a strong presence in rural areas of western Uttar Pradesh. During the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign, she also shared the stage with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath at rallies in Baghpat and Baraut. If the RLD fields her from a Jat-dominated constituency in 2027, it would not simply be a decision to field another candidate. It could be part of a strategy to simultaneously target women voters in western UP, Jat pride, and the political legacy of the Chaudhary family. Charu shows an aggressive side in Saharanpur The ‘Swabhiman Rally’ in Saharanpur on 3 September 2026 is being seen as significant in Charu’s political journey because this time, her speech directly targets the Opposition. Charu is invited to the stage before Jayant Chaudhary speaks. She is introduced in a distinctly political manner and then addresses the crowd directly without reading from a written speech. She says no one has the right to insult the people. Elections come and go, and it does not matter whether a party is in power or in Opposition. Commitment towards the people, she says, will always remain. She also links the regional identity and ‘chaudharahat’ (influence of the Chaudhary community) of western UP with electoral politics and appeals to voters to send RLD and its alliance candidates to Lucknow with overwhelming support. ‘Chavanni’ jibe heats up western UP politics The controversy in western UP politics begins with Akhilesh Yadav’s remark targeting Jayant Chaudhary. He says, ‘You turned a chavanni into a rupee, and still left us.’ The RLD turns the remark into an issue of political and social respect in western UP. Reactions emerge in Jat-dominated areas, amid which the ‘Swabhiman Rally’ is organised in Saharanpur. Charu and their two daughters also join Jayant on the stage at the rally. Jayant also hits back at Akhilesh Amid the political confrontation, Jayant Chaudhary also responds to Akhilesh Yadav. He says he generally tries to ensure that nobody becomes his enemy. Jayant says he has not even provoked Akhilesh, yet the SP chief keeps making remarks against him. Jayant plays videos of SP leaders at the rally and takes a political swipe, saying, Forget ABCD politics. We will trap you in G for sugarcane and J for Jat, and then SP will not come to power. Charu and Jayant’s love marriage Charu Chaudhary comes from a business family and is originally from a Punjabi family in Delhi. Her family has been associated with a fashion and jewellery business called ‘Juki’ in South Extension, south Delhi. Charu and Jayant are classmates at Delhi University’s Sri Venkateswara College. Their friendship develops into a relationship, and they marry on 14 August 2003. After marriage, Charu continues her professional career and works in the corporate sector for around two-and-a-half years. She later leaves her job to pursue her interests in fashion designing and jewellery. She studies at the Jewellery Product Development Centre (JPDC) in Delhi and also attends the Gemological Institute of America. From fashion designer to entrepreneur Charu runs a multi-brand, multi-product store called ‘Zuki’, featuring jewellery, clothing and other design-related products. According to Charu, the idea for a multi-brand store came to her several years earlier, but family responsibilities delayed the plan. She eventually turns the idea into a business. In October 2019, she also showcased her designer fashion collection at Toronto Fashion Week. Charu is conscious of fitness and regularly goes to the gym. She enjoys watching detective shows and has also appeared on the covers of several magazines. Charu and Jayant have two daughters, Sahira and Elisha.

stories.title: Mirzapur’s damaged school now rivals convent schools:Fewer than 50 students earlier, now AI-computer classes; principal says, ‘We won parents’ trust’
stories.summary: In the smart classroom, children are learning how artificial intelligence (AI) works through a digital screen. The children are sitting in front of computers, wearing headphones and speaking into microphones. Paintings explaining the syllabus adorn the classroom walls. Outside, the campus is surrounded by greenery. This is not a scene from a high-end private school. We are talking about the PM Shri Composite School in Mirzapur. More than 200 children come to the school to study every day. The learning environment seen at the school today was not the same before 2016. Back then, the building was in ruins, and there was not even enough space for children to sit in the classrooms. With no boundary wall, the premises would become a hangout for drunkards after sunset. Gradually, parents also became afraid to send their children to school. That was when Madhurima Tiwari became the school's principal. She sought help from officials to turn the school into a smart school. She went door to door, assuring parents that their children would get a good education and a better learning environment. She then delivered on those promises. The school is now giving convent schools in Mirzapur a run for their money. Madhurima received the President's Award in 2025. Only two teachers from Uttar Pradesh received the award, Madhurima and Ramlal Yadav from Bhadohi. On Teachers' Day, read the story of how this school changed, step by step Broken ground, no boundary wall, children sat on mats Principal Madhurima Tiwari recounts the school's transformation: It was 2009. I got a job as an assistant teacher. My first posting was at a primary school in the Madihan area of Mirzapur. Two years later, I was transferred to this school in the city. What was the condition of the school at the time? Madhurima says, School operated from two separate campuses. The primary school was on one side and the upper primary school on the other. There was no boundary wall. Inside the school, children sat on the ground on mats. The school premises were also in poor condition.Within two to three years, I realised that children were not coming to school to study. Parents were also not coming for new admissions. By then, fewer than 50 children were left in the school.When we visited the homes of children who were not attending school, we found that parents were unhappy with the lack of facilities. Many parents told us, ‘Why should we send our children to your school when it gets flooded during the rains and there is no proper seating arrangement? What will you people teach them?’ Met MPs and MLAs, secured grants from officials, then repaired the building Madhurima says, In 2016, we met MPs and MLAs and showed officials photographs of the dilapidated building. After the grant was sanctioned, we got the building repaired. First, we brought the primary and upper primary schools together on the same campus. A year later, I became the principal here.We then started visiting parents with photographs of the new building and classrooms. We requested them to send their children back to our school. The impact was visible in the very first year. The number of children increased from 56 to 132. This felt like a major achievement for us. We continued our efforts, installing projectors in every classroom and increasing greenery across the school. First recognition in 2018, then experiments with teaching methods In 2018, Mirzapur BSA Praveen Tiwari visited the school. He praised the classrooms and campus and also presented a certificate of appreciation. This was the first recognition for the school and its principal. Madhurima says, After this recognition, I felt that we needed to make the school even better. My fellow teachers began working on new ways of teaching children. We started trying to explain every topic in an interesting way and make greater use of screens to display and explain the syllabus. Children receive ID cards arranged at their own expense Children at the school can now be seen in clean uniforms, shoes, ties and ID cards. Madhurima explains, There are several private schools around our school. Government schools do not charge fees, and we do not want children to develop an inferiority complex about studying in a government school rather than a private one, so we ask them to follow a dress code. Several things are not provided by the government, so my staff and I arrange them and provide them to the children.I learnt computers from my son and daughter and now teach them here.The school has a computer lab, a modern library, smart classrooms and computer systems. How are children being taught about these facilities? Madhurima says, We studied for a BSc, followed by BEd and BTC. Indeed, we did not get the opportunity to study computers. But I have a son and a daughter at home, and I learnt many things through them. Apart from that, the department provides us with training from time to time, and we use that training to teach the children here. ‘Parents withdrawing children from private schools and bringing them here’ There are currently 221 children enrolled at Madhurima's school. We asked whether parents were now withdrawing their children from private schools and bringing them here. Madhurima says, A parent came and asked us to enrol his child. We registered the name, but later found out that he had admitted the child to UKG at a private school just two months earlier. We told him to get the child's name removed from that school before it could be registered here on U-DISE. When he went there, the school refused to remove the child's name. We sought the help of officials, after which the school charged the poor parent ₹1,600. When I found out about this, I felt very sad. Now, hear from the students We asked a student named Khushi, who was studying in the computer lab, whether people in the neighbourhood ever asked her why she studied at a government school. Khushi says, When people ask us that, we tell them that our school provides much better education than theirs. Our school is even better than private schools. We have everything here that they have in expensive private schools. During the conversation, we learnt that Khushi's father is a carpenter and his financial situation does not allow him to afford private schooling for his daughter. ‘The facilities here are no less than those in private schools’ Samya, a Class 8 student sitting in the computer lab, says, I have been studying here since Class 1. My father is a carpenter, and my mother stays at home. We do not have to pay any fees here. Our school is very good. We have digital classes and a digital library. Whenever we do not understand something, we ask our teachers, and they explain everything to us. Tamanna, a Class 8 student attending an online class, says, My father is a tailor. Our family's financial situation is not good enough for us to study at a private school, so I study here. The facilities here are no less than those at any private school. Everything is very good. We keep telling our teacher to develop the school further, otherwise we will have to go to Arya Kanya Vidya Mandir for Class 9. After speaking to the students and staff at the school, it becomes clear that the school has now developed into something resembling a model school. It has almost every facility required for teaching. The only major problem is a shortage of staff. Apart from Madhurima, there is one assistant teacher and one Shiksha Mitra. In other words, just three people are managing the school. More staff are needed so that the children can be taught and guided even better.

stories.title: Youth attacked over old rivalry in Kanpur:Beaten with sticks and sharp-edged weapons; skull and nasal bones fractured
stories.summary: 27-year-old man was allegedly attacked by around six people over an old dispute in Kanpur’s Om Purwa area on Monday night. Mohammad Sufiyan had gone out to buy milk when the attackers allegedly surrounded him near Shiva Park and assaulted him with sticks, clubs and sharp-edged weapons, leaving him seriously injured. Sufiyan’s brother, Farhan, said the attack left him with serious injuries to his head and nasal bone. He also suffered two broken teeth and a severe injury to his left leg. The attackers allegedly took away his two mobile phones and the cash in his pocket. Police initially took Sufiyan to Kanshi Ram Hospital, where doctors referred him to Halet Hospital considering his condition. He was shifted there for further treatment around 10 pm. Farhan alleged that the accused had been roaming around the area and threatening people for several days. He claimed they had attacked others in the past as well, but continued their activities due to a lack of concrete action. Local residents also alleged that the group assaulted people to establish its dominance in the area. Jajmau police station in-charge Sanjay Pandey said Sufiyan had been sent to hospital for treatment. Police are examining CCTV footage from cameras installed around the scene and will take legal action after receiving a written complaint.

stories.title: Fake notes worth ₹7.40 crore found in PNB:CCTV shows housekeeper taking out cash; 3 officials suspended in Saharanpur
stories.summary: Fake currency notes worth approximately ₹7.40 crore were found in the currency chest of Punjab National Bank (PNB) in Saharanpur during a bank audit. The matter came to light after auditors detected the suspected fake notes. Around 3 pm on Monday, the bank suspended three officials in connection with the case. During the investigation, CCTV footage reportedly showed a part-time housekeeper removing cash from bundles of notes. An FIR has been registered against four people at Sadar Bazaar police station on the complaint of PNB Meerut Chief Manager and Investigating Officer Arun Kumar Choubey. The FIR names Senior Divisional Manager Ravi Kumar Kans, Currency Chest Manager Sushil Kumar, Currency Chest Manager Amit Kumar, who is posted in Yamunanagar-Jagadhri, and housekeeper Vishal Kumar. The bank has suspended three officials and launched an internal investigation into the alleged irregularities. ₹4.30 lakh found missing from amount sent to Jaipur The case came to light after a shortage was detected in the cash sent from PNB’s currency chest in Saharanpur to Jaipur. A few days earlier, part-time housekeeper Vishal Kumar had been assigned to arrange currency bundles worth around ₹11.50 crore at the PNB branch near Ghantaghar. The cash included soiled, mutilated and other types of notes. The bank was required to send the amount to the RBI’s Jaipur Currency Chest. As per the prescribed procedure, the cash was sent to Jaipur on August 5. During counting, officials found ₹4,30,900 missing and informed the PNB officials in Meerut. Housekeeper seen taking notes on CCTV Following this, the bank sent Chief Manager Arun Kumar Chaubey to Saharanpur to investigate the matter. Along with other bank officials, he examined CCTV footage from cameras installed inside the currency chest. The footage reportedly showed part-time housekeeper Vishal Kumar taking cash from bundles of notes. After reviewing the footage, the bank terminated Vishal’s services and lodged a theft case against him for allegedly misappropriating the money. Currency chest audit began on 9 August After the alleged irregularities involving the housekeeper came to light, the bank launched an audit of its currency chest on 9 August. The audit team matched the cash physically present in the chest with the corresponding records. During the audit, a major irregularity was detected. The team found counterfeit currency notes worth approximately ₹7.40 crore among the cash stored in the currency chest. The discovery of such a large quantity of counterfeit notes raised serious concerns among bank officials. 3 bank officials questioned The investigating officer subsequently questioned officials associated with the currency chest Senior Divisional Manager Ravi Kumar Kans, Currency Chest Manager Sushil Kumar and Currency Chest Manager Amit Kumar, who is posted in Yamunanagar-Jagadhri. They were questioned about how the counterfeit notes entered the currency chest and remained there. According to the investigating officer, none of the three officials could provide a satisfactory explanation. The matter was subsequently brought to the attention of senior bank officials. Departmental inquiry initiated against bank officials Senior Manager Nisha Singh, posted at PNB’s divisional office on Delhi Road, said the bank suspended all three officials after the irregularities came to light. She added that a departmental inquiry is also underway. Police are investigating how such a large quantity of counterfeit notes entered the bank’s currency chest, when and through whom they were placed there, and whether others were involved. DIG says, ‘Case registered against four in currency chest matter’ DIG Abhishek Singh said, Based on a complaint filed by the bank’s chief manager, a case has been registered against three managers. A separate case of theft has also been registered against the part-time housekeeper. The bank is conducting an internal inquiry, while the police are also investigating the matter.

stories.title: Youth sleeping on the roof stabbed to death:Body found 400 meters away in Lucknow, brother said-villagers had threatened him
stories.summary: 25-year-old man was stabbed to death while sleeping on the rooftop of an under-construction house in Lucknow late Sunday night. The incident took place in Ganeshpur village under the Mahingwan police station area. The attackers allegedly stabbed Satish Yadav, causing him to fall from the roof into a field below. Around 2 am, a villager spotted Satish lying unconscious and seriously injured near a field about 400 metres from the house and alerted his family. His father, Shivbalak Yadav, and other relatives rushed to the spot and took him to hospital. With police assistance, Satish was later shifted to the trauma centre, where doctors declared him dead. Satish had left home around 8 pm on Sunday after dinner to sleep at the under-construction house. His brother alleged that some villagers had threatened Satish with serious consequences two days before the murder. Had started working as a watchman just 5 days earlier According to the family, Satish had started working as a watchman at an under-construction house just five days before the incident. The house was located about 1 km from the village, and Satish had been hired by a contractor named Ashok. The house reportedly belongs to a woman who lives in Lucknow. Satish would stay at the site and sleep on the rooftop at night. Threatened after being chased 2 days ago The deceased’s younger brother, Shivam Yadav, said, "Satish had been involved in a long-standing dispute with fellow villagers Sunil and Dheeraj. According to Shivam, the two men chased Satish two days ago and threatened him with dire consequences. The family suspects that the old dispute may have led to Satish’s murder. However, the exact motive has not yet been established. Shivam said the family received information at around 1 am that Satish had been attacked. They rushed to the spot and found him injured. He said Satish had gone to sleep at the under-construction site, where he was allegedly attacked. 2 suspects detained As soon as the incident was reported, Mahingwan Police reached the spot and launched an investigation. Two suspects have been detained and are being questioned. Police are also speaking to people living near the crime scene and examining the old dispute along with other possible angles. DCP North Amit Kumar Anand said, Satish, who sustained knife injuries, died during treatment. His body has been sent for a post-mortem examination, and a case has been registered based on a complaint filed by his family.

stories.title: Cop pulls pistol from youth’s jeans in middle of road:Poses film-style in Agra; 2 cops hold his hands
stories.summary: Agra Police arrested a young man for allegedly possessing an illegal country-made pistol and then staged his arrest in the middle of a busy market. In front of onlookers, two policemen held the man while a sub-inspector dramatically pulled the pistol from his jeans. The sub-inspector then posed for the cameras with the seized weapon in his hand. The incident took place on 29 August. On Monday, Etmadpur Police released a video of the arrest, apparently to highlight the action and receive appreciation for the recovery. However, instead of drawing praise on social media, the video sparked criticism and trolling over the “filmi-style” manner in which the suspect was apprehended and the weapon recovered. First, take a look at these 2 pictures... Now, read the full story Two days ago, Etmadpur Police in Agra received information that a young man was carrying an illegal country-made pistol. During a checking operation, police arrested Deepu alias Devesh near the primary school in Vasawala village. Deepu, a resident of Satta Mohalla in Etmadpur, was allegedly found carrying a .315-bore country-made pistol and two cartridges. Police registered a case against him and sent him to jail. 26-second video goes viral On Monday, a 26-second video showing the entire police action went viral on social media and was widely shared within a short time. The video shows Sub-Inspector Parth Sarathi and constable Vinod Kumar holding a young man in the middle of the village. Moments later, Sub-Inspector Rampoot Gautam arrives in a cinematic manner. He lifts the man’s T-shirt, pulls out the country-made pistol tucked into his waistband and then poses with the weapon while looking at the camera. The person recording the video can then be heard saying, “It’s a .315-bore country-made pistol. Look, sir, make sure it isn’t loaded.” The policemen subsequently search the man and recover two cartridges from the back pocket of his jeans. A crowd of villagers can be seen gathered at the spot throughout the incident. Video draws mixed reactions on social media The video was shared by several users who described the police action as commendable. However, many others criticised the way the arrest and weapon recovery were staged. One user commented, “The script is good, but the acting isn’t.” Another wrote, “Now even the police have caught the reel-making bug.” Meanwhile, ACP Etmadpur Devesh Kumar said police had gone to the village after receiving information about a fight. The accused tried to flee after seeing the police, but two policemen caught him. As the police were taking him away, a villager informed them that he was carrying a country-made pistol. The sub-inspector then recovered the weapon. ACP Kumar said the video was recorded as evidence and confirmed that it was genuine.

Yogi flags off 4 new trains in Bahraich:Nepalgunj linked with Varanasi and Gorakhpur; Vaishnaw says bullet train will run in UP
stories.summary: Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath flagged off four new trains from Nepalgunj Road railway station in Bahraich on Monday. Ashwini Vaishnaw joined virtually. He also inaugurated the approximately 56-kilometre-long Nepalgunj Road-Bahraich broad-gauge line, built at a cost of around ₹730 crore, using a remote. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that railway projects worth ₹1.29 lakh crore are currently underway in Uttar Pradesh. The state has 32 Vande Bharat and 46 Amrit Bharat trains in operation. He said that bullet trains will bring major changes to Uttar Pradesh in the coming years. In fact, there are plans to operate bullet trains under the Delhi-Varanasi high-speed rail corridor, with a maximum speed of 300 kilometres per hour. Yogi said that previous governments had made Bahraich synonymous with backwardness. Today, it has been converted from metre gauge to broad gauge. For us, this region has served as the gateway to India. Launch of these 4 trains Trains extended up to Nepalgunj railway station Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that four trains have been launched. With gauge conversion, Nepalgunj, Babaganj, Nanpara, Matera, Risia, and Bahraich will now be connected to the wider railway network. In a way, this program is fulfilling everyone's long-standing demand. I would like to thank the Chief Minister and, especially, Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the excellent planning undertaken for the development of the railway network in Purvanchal and Uttar Pradesh. Find out train schedule 1- Varanasi-Bahraich Express 2- Varanasi-Gorakhpur Express The route of the Varanasi City-Gorakhpur-Varanasi City Express (15132/15131) has been extended to nepalgunj Road. The train will now run from Varanasi to nepalgunj Road and, on its return journey, from nepalgunj Road to Varanasi. The train will have a total of 18 coaches, including General, Sleeper, AC Third, AC Third Economy, and AC Second Class coaches. The train will be operated with an LHB rake. 3- Gonda-Bahraich DEMU The route of the Gonda-Bahraich-Gonda DEMU (75111/75112) has been extended to Nepalgunj Road. Passengers will now have a direct train service from Gonda to Nepalgunj Road. This route extension will provide a direct rail connection for passengers traveling between Gonda, Bahraich, and Nepalgunj Road. 4- Gonda-Bahraich DEMU key points from the CM's speech 1. Mafias were sheltered earlier; now medical colleges are being built In the previous government, people sheltered mafias, but today medical colleges are being built in every district. Did anyone ever imagine that there would be a medical college in Bahraich? Today, Bahraich has a medical college named after Maharaja Suheldev. There are medical colleges in Balrampur and Gonda, an airport has been constructed in Shravasti, and there are also medical colleges in Ayodhya, Sultanpur, and Ambedkar Nagar. 2. Encephalitis, like the mafia, has also been eradicated This region was once affected by diseases such as encephalitis. When children died, the previous government described it as an unknown disease. When the double-engine government came to power in Uttar Pradesh, it said that the disease could not remain unknown; it would be identified and eradicated. Just as the mafia was eliminated from Uttar Pradesh, diseases such as encephalitis have also been permanently eradicated. Now, no father worries that his child might succumb to the disease. 3. Women and traders need not feel afraid Today, no woman, trader, or ordinary citizen needs to fear any mafia member or criminal. These are the achievements of the double-engine government, which are now visible on the ground. 4. Six-lane Lucknow-Bahraich road approved Recently, under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister, the Union Cabinet approved connecting Lucknow to Bahraich by upgrading the road connectivity from four lanes. Road and railway connectivity in every direction is helping realize the vision of development in the new India. Today, almost all railway lines in India have been converted to broad gauge. 5. Grand memorial built for Maharaja Suheldev Maharaja Suheldev freed this land by killing the foreign invader. Under previous governments, fairs and Urs gatherings were held here in the name of Salar Masud, but today a grand memorial dedicated to Maharaja Suheldev has been built on this very land, so that people can learn about their heritage and pride. 6. When railway tracks are broader, roads and markets become larger When the railway tracks are broader, the roads also become wider; when the roads become wider, the markets also expand; and when the markets grow, trade flourishes. This is the path of development under the double-engine government, which is becoming visible through better railway connectivity to nepalgunj Road. 7. We stand with Nepal in this hour of grief Before the program, everyone paid tribute to those who lost their lives in the devastating disaster in Nepal. The Chief Minister said that recently, hundreds of people in Nepal, India, and several other countries around the world had fallen victim to natural disasters. CM expressed condolences to the families who lost their loved ones and assured the people of Nepal that we would stand together through happiness and sorrow. Under the leadership of PM Modi, the Government of India has taken swift decisions and stepped forward to assist the friendly nation of Nepal. Our relationship is not merely political; we also share a cultural heritage. stories.title: Wife found dead in room, husband flees:Man locked sister-in-law in room in Jhansi; couple had a love marriage 18 months ago
stories.summary: Woman was found dead inside her home in Jhansi on Monday, hours after she allegedly had an argument with her husband. According to her family, the couple went to sleep late on Sunday night, while the woman’s younger sister slept in another room. During the night, the husband allegedly latched both rooms from outside and fled. At around 9 am, the woman’s brother arrived at the house and opened the latch. He found his sister, Shivani, unconscious inside the room, while her younger sister Muskan was asleep in the adjacent room. The family rushed Shivani to the Medical College, where doctors declared her dead. The woman’s brother accused his brother-in-law of strangling Shivani and fleeing the scene. Police are searching for the husband. The incident took place in the Sipri Bazar police station area. Became friends on social media Sudha, also known as Shivani, was a resident of Indergarh in Datia, Madhya Pradesh. Her father, Santram Vanshkar, sells fruit from a cart, while her mother works as a domestic help in Delhi. Shivani was the eldest of four sisters. Her younger sisters, Preeti and Neha, are married. She also had a younger sister, Muskan (18), and two brothers, Aniket (17) and Kapil (14). Muskan said, “Around two years ago, my elder sister Shivani became friends with Yash Thakur (28), a resident of Gwalior, on social media. They eventually fell in love. Yash worked at a clothing store. After some time, they told their families about their relationship, and our family agreed to the marriage. Shivani married Yash around one-and-a-half years ago.” Shivani had been living in Jhansi for three months Muskan said, “After their marriage, Shivani lived with Yash in Gwalior. However, he later started assaulting her over petty issues. Troubled by this, my sister rented a room near Awas Vikas Fauji Tiraha in Jhansi.” Muskan and her brother Aniket also lived with Shivani, while their father and younger brother Kapil stayed in their village. Yash would occasionally visit Shivani in Jhansi. A day before Raksha Bandhan, Shivani went to Gwalior with Kapil. After staying there for two days, she returned to Jhansi with her husband, while Kapil went back to the village. She argued with her husband before her death Muskan said, “On Sunday night, my sister had an argument with her husband. He was hurling abusive remarks at our family. He told her, ‘I have slept with your sister, and I will beat your father with a slipper.’ This led to a heated argument between them. “Our maternal uncle, Santosh, lives nearby. He intervened and calmed my brother-in-law down. After that, Aniket went to our uncle’s house. Things then appeared to return to normal. I went to sleep in my room, while my sister and brother-in-law slept in the other room.” Husband allegedly latched the room from outside Muskan said, “Around 1:30–2 am, my brother-in-law asked for his bag, saying he needed to take some things. We gave it to him, after which he latched the door from outside. “At around 5 am, I tried to open the door to go to the bathroom, but it would not open. I called out to my sister and brother-in-law for around half an hour, but there was no response. I eventually went back to sleep. At around 9 am, my brother returned home and opened the door. I then went into my sister’s room and found her body lying there.”, she added Brother says, ‘Doors of both rooms were latched from outside’ Shivani’s brother Aniket said, “When I reached home at around 9 am, I found the latch of my sister’s room locked from outside. I opened it and entered the room, where I found my sister lying on the floor. Blood was coming from her ear, and there were marks on her neck. The door of the other room was also latched from outside. I opened it and woke my sister Muskan.” Neighbours and family members gathered at the house after the incident. The family rushed Shivani to the Medical College, where doctors declared her dead. Aniket and Muskan alleged that their brother-in-law killed Shivani, latched the room from outside and fled. They demanded his arrest. CO Ramveer Singh said an injury mark was visible on the woman’s neck, while no other injuries were found. The body was sent for a post-mortem examination, and the exact cause of death will be established after the report is received. He said Shivani had been having a dispute with her husband and police teams were searching for him. Post-mortem confirms murder Shivani’s body was examined at night by a two-doctor panel. According to the doctors, she was strangled to death. Five injuries were found on her neck and face. Police suspect that she was strangled with a rope or piece of clothing.

stories.summary: Divya Mittal IAS Resignation: उत्तर प्रदेश कैडर की चर्चित IAS अधिकारी दिव्या मित्तल के इस्तीफे के बाद उनकी प्रशासनिक यात्रा एक बार फिर चर्चा में है। अपने कार्यकाल के दौरान उन्होंने कई जिलों और महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक पदों पर जिम्मेदारी संभाली। हालांकि, इस्तीफे के साथ साझा किए गए अपने भावुक संदेश में उन्होंने खास तौर पर मिर्जापुर और देवरिया का जिक्र किया। दिव्या मित्तल ने मिर्जापुर को लेकर लिखा कि इस जिले ने उन्हें सिखाया कि ‘असंभव’ कोई तथ्य नहीं, बल्कि एक राय है। वहीं देवरिया के लिए उन्होंने कहा कि इस जिले ने उन्हें सिखाया कि सही के साथ खड़ा होना कोई विकल्प नहीं, बल्कि कर्तव्य है। यही वजह है कि उनके इस्तीफे के बाद इन दोनों जिलों से जुड़ी उनकी यादें और अनुभव लोगों के बीच चर्चा का विषय बने हुए हैं।

stories.title: Yogi says opposition spreading misinformation, BJP workers silent:Smriti says speeches won’t work, make videos on govt schemes
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday alerted BJP workers in Lucknow ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. He said the opposition was spreading confusion among the public over issues concerning Gen Z, Gen Alpha and the Ram Temple. “But you are silent. Those who are asleep should wake up. Do not sit back complacently, relying only on the government’s work,” he said. Yogi cited a remark by Hindutva ideologue Vinayak Damodar Savarkar: “We are not as concerned by the insolence of the wicked as we are troubled by the excessive goodness of the virtuous.” The Chief Minister was speaking at a meeting of the BJP’s Seva Sankalp campaign at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Lucknow. BJP national general secretary Smriti Irani said party workers must counter the opposition’s narrative through videos. “Speeches alone will not work,” she said. Yogi also agreed with Irani’s remarks. Chief Minister Yogi mentions ‘Gen Z’ and ‘Gen Alpha’ Yogi referred to ‘Gen Z’ and ‘Gen Alpha’ in his speech. He said the opposition claims that the current government has done nothing for children’s future or education. “But no one is unaware of the condition of schools run by the Uttar Pradesh Basic Education Council before 2017,” he said. He highlighted the differences between the work done by the Samajwadi Party and BJP governments: Claim of 9.30 lakh government jobs Chief Minister alleged that before 2017, recruitment examinations conducted by the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) were marred by open corruption, with merit being sidelined in favour of candidates from “one particular caste”. He claimed that at one point, 56 of the 86 sub-divisional magistrates (SDMs) selected were from the same caste. Yogi claimed that over the past seven to eight years, the state government has provided government jobs to 930,000 young people through a transparent process, without recommendations, financial transactions or discrimination. He said that of the 29,000 Shakti Kendras (groups of polling booths) across the state, there would hardly be one where two to four young people had not secured government jobs. However, he said the organisation had failed to bring the “success stories” of these youths before the public. Yogi targets SP over Ram Temple and encephalitis (brain fever) Chief Minister said efforts were now underway to discredit the Ram Temple project and the arrangements surrounding it, despite the temple’s construction after decades of legal and political hurdles. He accused opposition parties of putting all their strength into the campaign, while BJP workers remained silent instead of responding aggressively. Yogi also targeted the opposition over encephalitis in eastern Uttar Pradesh. He said, “Thousands of poor children used to die of encephalitis every year in Purvanchal, but no opposition leader shed a tear. They remained silent about the safety of daughters. But when our government took action against the mafia, they turned up to mourn them.” Smriti Irani lays out plan for BJP workers BJP national general secretary Smriti Irani laid out a plan for party workers during the meeting. She said speeches alone would not be enough to counter the opposition’s digital narrative. Irani directed the organisation to identify at least 10 “success stories” from each of Uttar Pradesh’s 29,000 Shakti Kendras involving people who have directly benefited from government schemes. These could include a beneficiary who received a house under PM Awas Yojana, an artisan associated with the One District One Product (ODOP) scheme, an entrepreneur who benefited from the MUDRA scheme, or a child studying in a school renovated under Operation Kayakalp. The Chief Minister endorsed the idea and highlighted several major figures related to Uttar Pradesh’s economy and development: ‘Seva Pakhwada’ to begin on PM Modi’s birthday till 1 month During the final phase of the meeting, the BJP finalised the programme for ‘Seva Pakhwada’, which will begin on 17 September till one month, Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday.

stories.title: Varanasi woman lies on railway track:Attempts suicide after being stopped from using Instagram; woman cop saves her life
stories.summary: Young woman allegedly attempted suicide at the Ashapur railway crossing in Varanasi’s Sarnath police station area after her family stopped her from using Instagram. Upset after being scolded, she lay down on the railway tracks. An alert woman police officer reached the spot in time and pulled her to safety, moments before a train passed. Sarnath SHO Pankaj Kumar Tripathi said police received information at around 11:45 pm that a young woman was lying on the tracks near the Ashapur railway crossing. Ashapur outpost in-charge Diksha Pandey immediately rushed to the spot and found the woman lying on the tracks as a train approached from the opposite direction. Showing quick presence of mind, Pandey pulled the woman off the tracks just moments before the train passed through the spot. Police took the woman to the Ashapur outpost and counselled her. After she had calmed down, she identified herself as Pinky (18). Originally from Patna, she currently lives in a rented accommodation in the Ashapur area, where she is reportedly working or studying. Pinky told police that her brother had stopped her from using social media and had severely scolded her the previous night. Upset over the incident, she said she decided to take the extreme step. Following counselling, Pinky acknowledged her mistake and assured police that she would not repeat such an act. Later that night, police contacted her colleagues and handed her over to them to ensure she reached home safely.

stories.title: Property dealer drugged and shot in car:Lucknow driver threw mobile on train, messaged wife 'Don’t look for me'
stories.summary: Property dealer Dhirendra Pratap Singh, 35, was allegedly kidnapped and murdered by his own driver in Lucknow. Police said the driver, Ravi Tiwari, first made Dhirendra unconscious by making him smell a handkerchief inside the car before shooting him. He then threw Dhirendra’s mobile phone into a moving train to mislead the police, causing its location to shift and eventually showing up in Chandauli, around 350 km away. In an attempt to cover up the crime, Ravi later went to the police station himself and filed a missing person report for Dhirendra. Before throwing the phone onto the train, he also sent a message to Dhirendra’s wife: “I am leaving. Do not look for me and do not tell anyone my location.” After Dhirendra’s body was recovered, Ravi allegedly confessed to the murder during police interrogation and revealed that he was in contact with a man named Monu Singh. Police said he had been promised a house, a shop and ₹12 lakh in cash in Lucknow in exchange for killing Dhirendra. Ravi had worked with Dhirendra for nearly 10 years and had earned his complete trust. Dhirendra would even leave lakhs of rupees in cash with him and share almost all his business-related details. Police said Ravi betrayed that trust for greed. First, know the full case Thirty five year old property dealer Dhirendra Pratap Singh was shot dead in Lucknow. His body was recovered from a small canal in Dubagga, around 22 km from the district headquarters, at 5 pm on Sunday. Bullet wounds were found on his forehead and chest. Dhirendra, a resident of Unnao, was the president of the Maharana Pratap Charitable Foundation and was involved in the property and transport businesses. He lived in Lucknow’s PGI area. On Saturday, his wife lodged a complaint alleging that Dhirendra had been kidnapped by his driver and his associates. The initial investigation suggests that the murder may have been linked to a dispute over a piece of land in Unnao worth around ₹50 crore. Dhirendra had reportedly written a letter to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath raising a complaint over the land dispute. Police have taken Dhirendra’s driver, Ravi Tiwari, and his associate, Omkar, into custody. During questioning, Ravi reportedly confessed to the murder. 4 people suspected of involvement; police searching for 2 According to ADCP South Rallapalli Vasanth Kumar, the names of four people have emerged in the investigation so far. They include Ravi Tiwari, a driver from Nilmatha, and his acquaintance Omkar, a resident of Khargapur. Ravi and Omkar are currently in police custody, while a search is underway for the other two suspects based on information obtained during their interrogation. Police said Ravi had been working as Dhirendra Pratap Singh’s driver for around 10 years and had earned his complete trust. Investigators allege that the conspirators exploited this trust and lured Ravi into the murder plot by promising him a house, a shop and ₹12 lakh in cash in Lucknow. Body dumped 25 km away after murder During police interrogation, the driver allegedly revealed that he first made Dhirendra unconscious by making him smell a handkerchief. He then shot him in the right side of the chest. As Dhirendra collapsed, the driver allegedly fired another shot into the back of his head. The murder took place near Utarethia. He then allegedly carried Dhirendra’s body in a Fortuner to an isolated spot along Kisan Path in Dubagga, around 25 km away. The body was dumped in the Sharda Sahayak Canal, about 50 metres from the road. The driver later abandoned Dhirendra’s Fortuner near Medanta Hospital and allegedly fled with Omkar. Location traced from Lucknow to Amethi within hours Dhirendra had two mobile phones. To mislead the police, the accused allegedly threw one of them onto a moving train, causing its location to keep changing and diverting the investigation. When police tracked the phone, its location was first recorded in Gosainganj, Haidergarh and Jagdishpur in Amethi. Later, its last location was traced to Chandauli, around 350 km from Lucknow. This raised suspicion that the phone had been deliberately moved to another location to mislead investigators. Wife filed kidnapping complaint DCP South Mushtaq said Dhirendra’s wife, Mamta Singh, had lodged a complaint alleging that her husband had been kidnapped by his driver and his associates. Based on the complaint and initial suspicion, police detained driver Ravi Tiwari for questioning. He initially attempted to mislead investigators. During sustained questioning, Ravi allegedly confessed to the murder. Based on information provided by him, police recovered Dhirendra’s body from Dubagga. The investigation indicated that a land dispute in Unnao was allegedly behind the conspiracy and murder. Two accused, including Ravi, are currently in custody. Dhirendra was considered a close aide of former MLA Sengar Dhirendra Pratap Singh was considered a close aide of former MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar from the Bangarmau assembly seat of Unnao. It has been reported that while Kuldeep Singh Sengar was lodged in Lucknow District Jail, Dhirendra Pratap Singh often visited him in jail. He also used to advocate for his legal cases. Pictures of Dhirendra Pratap Singh with several prominent BJP leaders are also going viral on social media. Rumors of the murder of a Hindu Yuva Vahini leader spread After the murder of Dhirendra Pratap Singh, the president of Maharana Pratap Charitable Trust, rumors of the murder of his namesake, Hindu Yuva Vahini leader Dhirendra Pratap Singh, spread on social media. Following this, hundreds of people started calling the Hindu Yuva Vahini leader. He informed everyone that he was safe. After this, he made a video of himself being alive and safe and posted it on social media.

stories.title: VIDEO| Drunk Lucknow cop assaults man, damages car:Abuses in uniform caught on camera; DCP attaches him to police lines
stories.summary: Sub-inspector Gopesh Sharma, posted at Naka police station, assaulted a young man while under the influence of alcohol, abused him, and broke his car window. The young man recorded a video of this incident. After the video surfaced, the DCP suspended the sub-inspector to police lines. The incident and the subsequent action took place on Sunday. Rahul Geetam, a resident of Barawan Kala in Dubagga, runs a tiffin service. According to Rahul, he had a prior acquaintance with Sub-Inspector Gopesh Sharma. On Sunday morning, the sub-inspector allegedly arrived at his house in an intoxicated state and asked him to accompany him. After getting into the car, the sub-inspector started assaulting and abusing Rahul. After breaking the car window, he snatched ₹15,000 Rahul alleges that he got out of the car on the way to urinate. During this time, the sub-inspector broke the car's window with a brick. Rahul also accused the sub-inspector of snatching ₹15,000. After this, Rahul took the sub-inspector to the Dubagga police station and filed a complaint regarding the matter. Dubagga Inspector Shrikant Rai stated that a compromise had been reached between both parties. However, after the video of the incident went viral, police officials took it seriously. Western DCP Kamlesh Dixit stated that cognizance of the viral video has been taken. Sub-Inspector Gopesh Sharma has been sent to police lines, and the investigation of the case has been handed over to the ACP of Chowk. Further action will be taken based on the investigation report.

stories.title: Blast at firecracker factory near Prayagraj Air Force Station:11 killed, including 8 children; DM orders bulldozer at warehouse
stories.summary: Massive explosion at a firecracker factory on the Prayagraj-Kaushambi border in Uttar Pradesh on Monday killed 11 people, including eight children, and left five others with burn injuries. Police said the blast was so powerful that the entire factory collapsed. Eight houses within a 100-metre radius were damaged, three of them completely destroyed. The explosion occurred around 12:30 pm in Mohammadpur village in Kaushambi, located on the Prayagraj border and about 2 km from the Air Force station in Manauri. Around 200 personnel from the police, Air Force, NDRF and SDRF are involved in the rescue operation, while 10 bulldozers are being used to clear the debris. Police suspect that more people may be trapped underneath, raising the possibility of a further increase in the death toll. Seven workers were inside the factory when the blast occurred, three of whom were killed. The remaining eight victims were residents of nearby houses. Police are investigating the cause of the explosion. However, Rani, who reached Swaroop Rani Hospital in Prayagraj, said the blast occurred after an electricity pole fell and triggered a powerful explosion in the gunpowder stored inside the factory. Explosion was heard up to 2 km away, and within minutes, a thick cloud of smoke engulfed the area. Villagers were seen carrying injured people on charpoys to get them to safety. The intensity of the blast can be gauged from the fact that it blew an 8-foot-wide hole through the third floor of a nearby house. Single-storey illegal factory was spread across 600 sq ft and was owned by a man identified as Adil. According to police, a new residential settlement was coming up next to the factory. A case has been registered against Adil, his father Naushad, his uncle Shakeel and three women. Four teams have been formed to arrest the accused. District Magistrate Amit Pal Sharma said strict action would be taken against those responsible and their properties would also be attached. Within eight hours of the blast, the DM and SP ordered a bulldozer action against a warehouse located 400 metres from the factory. The warehouse was demolished. See pictures- Deputy CM Keshav meets injured victims Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced compensation for the victims. The families of those killed will receive ₹2 lakh each, while the injured will be given ₹50,000 each. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya visited the injured at SRN Hospital in Prayagraj. He described the deaths of several members of the same family as deeply tragic and heartbreaking. He said the government’s top priority was to save the lives of the injured and ensure they received the best possible treatment. The DM and SSP have been directed to investigate the incident, and strict action will be taken against anyone found responsible. See where the explosion occurred in this graphic...
