stories.title: Jewellery shop robbed in 6 minutes in Lucknow, CCTV:2 masked thieves flee with ₹2.5 lakh goods
stories.summary: A jewellery shop in Hanuman Market, Shankarpuri Colony, in Lucknow’s Kamta area was allegedly robbed after two unidentified thieves broke its shutter and entered the premises. According to police, the thieves stole artificial yellow-metal jewellery and around 200 grams of white-metal jewellery worth approximately ₹2.20 lakh, with CCTV footage showing them inside the shop for nearly six minutes. The thieves arrived wearing caps and masks In the CCTV footage, a thief wearing a cap is first seen entering the shop. He gathers goods inside the shop. After this, another masked thief enters carrying a bag. The two fill the bag with the goods and flee. One of the thieves is also seen looking toward the CCTV camera. The owner learned about the theft when he arrived to open the shop in the morning and found the shutter broken. He then informed the police. Based on the CCTV footage, the police are working to identify and search for the two accused. Traders demand increased patrolling Following the incident, nearby shopkeepers are angry. The traders have demanded increased police patrolling in the area at night. The police have asked the shop owner to submit a written complaint. After receiving the complaint, a case will be registered based on the evidence, and further action will be taken.

stories.title: Youth found dead in hotel near Mahakal Temple:Drank with friend for 2 days; friend paid bill and fled; both came from UP
stories.summary: A 38-year-old man from Ghaziabad who had come to Ujjain in Madhya Pradesh for Mahakal's darshan was found dead under suspicious circumstances in a hotel room. The man's friend stayed with him for two days, drank alcohol, and then suddenly disappeared after paying the hotel bill in full. The police are now searching for him and investigating the case from a murder angle. The deceased has been identified as Mukesh Kumar, a resident of New Kotgaon (Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh). He had come to Ujjain on September 1 with his friend Vineet Goyal to seek darshan of Baba Mahakal. The two had taken a room at Hotel Temple View, located opposite the Neelkanth Gate of Mahakal Lok. Friend disappeared after paying the full bill without informing anyone According to the hotel staff, the two men stayed together for two days and would come and go from the hotel after drinking alcohol. On September 3, Vineet suddenly paid the entire hotel bill and left without informing anyone. He did not return afterwards. Body found in room after foul smell On Friday morning, the hotel management became suspicious after a strong foul smell emanated from the room. Upon receiving the information, Mahakal police reached the spot. When the door was opened, Mukesh's body was found inside. Considering the condition of the body, an FSL team was also called to investigate. Police teams engaged in searching for the accused Mahakal Police Station in-charge Gagan Badal said that the cause of death will become clear after the post-mortem report. However, the companion's sudden disappearance after paying the bill makes the case suspicious. The police are examining the hotel's CCTV footage and teams have been dispatched to search for Vineet Goyal.

stories.title: Ex-MLA Guddu Pandit drags wife by hair:Entered home in Bulandshahr; she screamed and fled to save her life
stories.summary: In Bulandshahr, former MLA and Samajwadi Party leader Guddu Pandit assaulted his third wife, Archana Pandit. A video of the incident has surfaced. It shows Guddu pulling his wife's hair and dragging her across the floor. His wife is seen screaming and hitting him with a broom. After this, the former MLA dragged his wife along with the broom. Calling Guddu Pandit a goon and a criminal, his wife ran out of the house. The video is from September 2 but surfaced today. The incident took place at Archana's house, located 1 km from the district magistrate's office. Archana, the state vice president of the Congress Mahila Sabha, filed a complaint at the police station on Thursday against Shribhagwan Sharma, alias Guddu Pandit. Archana Panda is also the state vice-president of the Congress Mahila Sabha. On Thursday, she filed a complaint against Guddu Pandit at the police station. She alleged, “Shribhagwan Sharma, aka Guddu Pandit, entered my house and assaulted me.” Claiming that she faced a threat to her life from the former MLA, she demanded that female police personnel be deployed at her residence round the clock. See the pictures – Congress leader says – pushed to the ground and assaulted In the complaint filed at Shikarpur police station, the Congress leader wrote, ‘On Thursday, she was at home with her son Samar Pandit when her husband, former MLA Guddu Pandit, suddenly arrived at the house and began banging loudly on the door.’ He started shouting and calling for her. As soon as she opened the door, Guddu Pandit pushed her forcefully, causing her to fall to the floor. Guddu Pandit assaulted her. Hearing her screams, the domestic help reached the spot and began recording the incident on a mobile phone. Seeing the video being recorded, Guddu Pandit backed away. She somehow ran toward the road to save her life and informed the police. 'The former MLA wants me to withdraw the divorce case' Archana alleged that she and her son have been continuously receiving death threats from the former MLA and his family. Her divorce case with the former MLA is pending in court. They want her to withdraw the divorce case, which is why they are harassing her. City CO Prakhar Pandey said: The Congress leader has filed a complaint against Guddu Pandit. A video has also surfaced. Her allegations and the video are being investigated. Strict action will be taken against the accused based on the facts that emerge during the investigation. Archana-Guddu dispute has been going on for 2 years Guddu Pandit Has Served as an MLA from Dibai Twice Archana Pandit has also been with the SP and recently joined the Congress Archana Panda has served as the national general secretary of the Samajwadi Party's women's wing. Recently, she joined the Congress in Lucknow. In 2023, she contested the Bulandshahr Municipal Council chairperson election under the Samajwadi Party banner. She finished second after losing to the wife of BJP candidate Himanshu Mittal.

stories.title: Drug network busted in Lucknow:9.6 lakh alprazolam tablets, 1.2 lakh tramadol capsules seized; 6 arrested
stories.summary: A joint team of the Lucknow unit of the Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) and the Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) has busted a major narcotics network in Lucknow’s Transport Nagar, recovering around 228 kg of medicines, including 9.6 lakh alprazolam tablets, 1.2 lakh tramadol capsules and 720 bottles of codeine-based cough syrup. Seven mobile phones and ₹11,140 in cash were also seized from the spot, while six accused have been arrested under the NDPS Act. They were hiding the medicines in cartons and sacks; caught under surveillance ANTF received information that a large consignment of narcotic drugs was due to arrive at Transport Nagar. On September 3, the team began surveillance in front of S-363/364. During this time, three people were seen hiding cartons inside sacks. A search led to the recovery of narcotic drugs from the possession of Kishan Vaswani, Sameer Ahmed, and Shad Irshad. Drug inspectors from the FSDA present at the scene collected samples of all three types of recovered drugs for testing. Billing connection found linked to Kanhaiya Pharma During questioning, Kishan Vaswani and Sameer Ahmed stated that the medicines had been obtained from Umesh Kumar, the operator of Kanhaiya Pharma. The team subsequently arrested Umesh Kumar and Satendra Singh as well. According to the ANTF's investigation, it emerged that Umesh Kumar allegedly used the documents of Satendra Singh's firm for billing narcotic medicines. In return, Satendra was paid a commission. The FSDA investigation found seven types of medicines stored at Kanhaiya Pharma, including 1,116 boxes of Proximek-SPAS capsules. According to the team, the firm's operator was unable to provide complete records related to the purchase and sale of the medicines. Kanhaiya Pharma was subsequently sealed. License revoked earlier, followed by allegations of conducting business through other firms After questioning Shad Irshad, the name of Vishal Chaurasia emerged. The team subsequently arrested him as well. According to the ANTF, Vishal admitted to supplying drugs to Shad. During questioning, he revealed that his drug licence had been revoked after an FIR was registered against him at the Aminabad police station in a codeine-related case. After that, he was conducting the drug trade through other firms. He also stated that he had purchased the recovered codeine-based cough syrup from Brijesh Verma. Case filed against six accused under the NDPS Act; further investigation into the network underway According to the ANTF, Kishan Vaswani, Sameer Ahmed, Shad Irshad, Umesh Kumar, Satendra Singh and Vishal Chaurasia were found to be part of an organised network involved in the illegal drug trade. Action has been taken against all six accused under Sections 8/21/22/29 of the NDPS Act.

stories.title: NEET student dies by suicide, blames fiancée’s family in note:FIR against 4, including fiancée in Lakhimpur
stories.summary: A 22-year-old NEET aspirant allegedly died by suicide by hanging himself in Lakhimpur-Kheri. Before his death, he left behind a note that read, “My fiancée’s family will be the reason for my death.” The incident took place around 4 pm on 2nd September in Shastri Nagar, under the Sadar Kotwali police station area, about 1 km from the district headquarters. The deceased, identified as Aman, was living in a rented room and preparing for the NEET examination. The day after the incident, on Thursday, when the youth's father went to the rented room to collect his son's belongings, he found a suicide note under a book. Following this, the student's father filed an FIR against 4 accused, including the fiancée, her brother-in-law, sister, and mother. The father stated that talks were underway for his son's marriage to a girl named Rupali. The families agreed, but the girl's sister and brother-in-law were not happy with this relationship. They used to pressure Aman to get a government job. The father alleges that his son committed suicide due to this pressure. See the pictures... Know the whole matter... Farmer Anil Gupta (55) lives in Danga village with his wife Seema (50), younger son Ashwani (20), and the rest of the family. His daughter Varsha (28) is married, while his elder son Aman (22) was living in their house located in Shastri Nagar, Lakhimpur, preparing for NEET. Talks of marriage between Aman and Rupali, daughter of the late Ramu Gupta from Naurangabad, Lakhimpur, had been ongoing for about three years. Ramu Gupta passed away about a year ago. His family consists of his wife Sunita (55), son Suraj (32), and daughter Shalu (24). Father Anil stated that he had discussed Aman's marriage to Rupali with her mother, Sunita Devi. Following the discussion about the alliance, Aman and Rupali also began communicating. According to Aman's father, Rupali's brother-in-law, Rishi Gupta, and her sister, Shalu, were not in favor of this marriage. The two would constantly pressure his son Aman to secure a government job. Aman was told that if he did not get a government job, they would refuse to go ahead with the marriage. Due to the constant pressure being exerted, Aman had started suffering from mental distress. He had been withdrawn for the past few days. It is alleged that he was provoked and threatened. Distressed by the pressure and provocation from these people, Aman hanged himself in his rented room in Shastrinagar at around 4 PM on 2nd September. Family grew suspicious when he did not answer his mother's call On Wednesday, when Aman's mother called him to talk, he did not pick up the phone. When there was no response even after calling multiple times, the family grew suspicious. Following this, Aman's father, Anil, called the landlord and asked him to check the room. When the landlord knocked on Aman's room door, there was no response from inside. After this, he peeked through the window and saw Aman hanging from the ceiling fan with a noose. The landlord informed Aman's family and the police about this. Upon receiving information about the incident, Aman's family reached the spot. Seeing her son's body, the mother fainted. The father was inconsolable. The police collected evidence from the crime scene and sent the body for a post-mortem. The police have also seized Aman's mobile phone. Suicide note found by father in the room on Thursday On Thursday, when Aman's father, Anil, went to his son's room to collect his belongings, he found a note under a book. It read, "Rupali's family will be the reason for my death." Following this, Aman's father filed an FIR against Rupali's brother-in-law Rishi Gupta, her sister Shalu, and her mother Sunita Devi for his son's death. On the day of the incident, Aman had called Rupali to meet him Police investigation revealed that shortly before the incident, Rupali had sent a WhatsApp message to her brother-in-law. She had informed her brother-in-law, a resident of Shahjahanpur, that Aman was calling her to meet. Rupali had refused to meet Aman because she did not have a scooter. Case filed against four people based on the father's complaint ASP East Pawan Gautam stated that a report has been filed against four people based on the complaint lodged by the deceased's family members. The matter is being investigated. Further action will be taken based on the facts and evidence that emerge during the investigation.

stories.title: Railway relief for Janmashtami travellers:Jhansi-Agra Cantt Express extended to Mathura; more trains added between Mathura-Gwalior
stories.summary: Railways has provided relief to passengers travelling from Agra to Mathura and Gwalior during the Shri Krishna Janmashtami celebrations. In view of the expected increase in passenger numbers during the festival, the Agra Railway Division has temporarily extended two important trains. The move will provide direct travel options for passengers heading from Agra towards Mathura and Gwalior. Jhansi-Agra Cantt Express extended to Mathura Train 11901 Veerangana Lakshmibai Jhansi-Agra Cantt Express, which was earlier extended to Mathura after September 3, will also operate up to Mathura on September 6. The train will depart Jhansi at 4 pm, reach Agra Cantt at 9:40 pm and then leave for Mathura at 11:25 pm, reaching there later that night. On the return journey, the train will depart Mathura at 4:30 am on September 4 and 7. Passengers travelling to Mathura for Janmashtami are expected to benefit from the temporary extension. Intercity Express to run up to Gwalior Similarly, 14212 New Delhi-Agra Cantt Intercity Express has been temporarily extended to Gwalior until September 7. The train will reach Agra Cantt at 10:05 pm and, after a 15-minute halt, depart for Gwalior at 10.20 pm. It will reach Gwalior at 1:10 am. According to Railways, the train operated up to Gwalior on Thursday under the temporary arrangement. On its return journey, it will operate from Gwalior from September 4 to 8. Hoshiarpur Express gets additional halt at Mohali Railways has also increased travel convenience for passengers heading towards Punjab. The Agra Cantt-Hoshiarpur Express has been given an additional halt at Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar (Mohali) station. Train 11905 departs Agra Cantt at 7:10 pm. The additional halt at Mohali will remain in place from September 9 to October 14. The railway arrangements are expected to ease travel not only for passengers heading to Mathura during Janmashtami, but also for those travelling towards Gwalior and Punjab.

stories.title: Rail traffic affected in Gorakhpur on Sept 6-7:Trains delayed by up to 150 minutes; passenger service suspended between Bhatni-Salempur
stories.summary: Rail passengers in Gorakhpur may face inconvenience on September 6 and 7 as railway work is expected to affect train services. Non-interlocking work is underway between Nunhkar, Bhatni and Bhatpar Rani stations on the Gorakhpur Cantt-Chhapra rural rail section to commission an automatic signalling system. As a result, several trains originating from, arriving at or passing through Gorakhpur will be affected. Some trains will run 50 to 150 minutes late. Passenger train services between Bhatni and Salempur will also be changed during the two-day period. Railways has advised passengers to check their train status before leaving for the station. Trains departing from Gorakhpur to run late The following trains departing from Gorakhpur will be delayed: Passengers who travel on these trains regularly may face disruption to their journeys. Trains arriving in Gorakhpur also affected The timings of several trains arriving at Gorakhpur will also be affected: These trains will also be affected The following trains are expected to face delays: Passenger trains suspended between Bhatni and Salempur Passenger services between Bhatni and Salempur will face the biggest change. 55124 Barhaj Bazar-Bhatni Passenger will operate only up to Salempur on September 6 and 7. Meanwhile, 55129 Bhatni-Barhaj Bazar Passenger will start from Salempur. This means these two passenger trains will not operate between Bhatni and Salempur on both days. Work underway to commission automatic signalling system The non-interlocking work is being carried out to commission an automatic signalling system on the rail section. Once operational, the system is expected to improve the efficiency and safety of train operations. Railways has advised passengers to check their train status before leaving for the station. This will help them avoid unnecessary waiting at the station because of delays.

stories.title: ‘Two more murders will happen’:Shooter accused in singer Ankit Balyan murder case posts threat video
stories.summary: A video of shooter Satyam, who carries a reward of ₹1 lakh, has surfaced in connection with the murder case of Haryanvi singer Ankit Balyan in Shamli. In the video, he is heard threatening: In the coming time, brother, there will be two murders, okay! And if anyone can save them, then save them, brother. We will kill them, we will definitely kill them, brother, we will not spare them. Following the emergence of the video, the police have increased security for Ankit's family. Additionally, an investigation has been initiated to verify the authenticity of the video and identify the person who posted it. Four days ago, the UP Police killed two shooters involved in the Ankit murder case, Sumit (24) and Mohit (22), in an encounter. Both had a reward of ₹50,000 each on their heads. Meanwhile, two accused, Satyam and Aryan, are still absconding. Both carry a reward of ₹1 lakh each. Ankit Balyan was shot dead while leaving a gym in Shamli on the evening of 26 August. Now know the whole matter On Wednesday, a 17-second video was posted on Instagram from an ID named 'kady.4nsatyam'. It features a photo of the murder accused shooter, Satyam. An audio clip in his voice is playing in the video. In it, he is heard saying, 'In the coming time, brother, there will be two murders, two, okay! And if anyone can save them, then save them, brother; we will kill them, we will kill them, brother, we will not spare them.' The police became alert after the video surfaced. During the investigation, more than 20 accounts in the names of Satyam, Aryan, and the Gogi gang were found on social media platforms including Instagram and Snapchat. Videos are being posted continuously from these accounts. The police are investigating the activities of all these accounts and are trying to identify those operating them. 12 friends who arrived from Haryana alerted the family On Tuesday, about 12 of Ankit's friends from Haryana reached Bantikheda village. They met Ankit's father, Satbir Singh, and other family members. The friends advised the family to remain alert and expressed apprehension that the gang might target the family as well. Satbir Singh told the friends that he had already lost his son. In such a situation, he asked everyone to take care of themselves and exercise caution. Preparations to take jailed accused on remand In the investigation of the murder case, the police will now also interrogate the accused who are currently in jail. The police will file an application in court on 7 September to take Rakesh alias Pumpu, who is lodged in Karnal jail, and Rohit, who is lodged in Delhi's Tihar jail, on remand. According to ASP Sumit, several important clues related to the murder case are expected to be found during the interrogation of the accused while on remand. Raids in Chandigarh and Punjab as well Police teams are continuously raiding potential hideouts in search of the wanted shooters. A police team also reached Chandigarh Airport and searched for the accused in the premises and surrounding areas, but did not find any success. Apart from this, police teams are also raiding potential hideouts in Karnal, Panipat, Sonipat, and Punjab. Aryan's passport expired, Satyam's contacts under investigation The investigation has revealed that Aryan's passport had expired and he was trying to get it renewed. The police reached Karnal and gathered information about both shooters. People associated with Satyam and his past activities are also being investigated. The police found locks on the houses of several suspects. Information about them is also being gathered. Ankit was murdered on 26 August On the evening of 26 August, 32-year-old singer Ankit Balyan left the gym in Shamli. During this time, the attackers surrounded him and fired 18 rounds. Ankit was seriously injured due to the gunshot wounds. Upon receiving the information, the police took him to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. SP said - Accused will be in custody soon SP Narendra Pratap Singh said- Four additional police personnel have been deployed for the security of the Baliyan family. Full vigilance is being maintained regarding security. Several important details about the accused have come to light. The accused will soon be in police custody. No accused will be spared.

stories.title: ‘Champat Rai is spotless; his innocence became a problem’:First interview with Govind Dev Giri after becoming general secretary
stories.summary: Champat Rai is spotless and beyond reproach. I say this based on my own experience. His naivety became a liability for him. He made the mistake of trusting everyone. He failed to judge people correctly…There have been some shortcomings in carrying out the trust’s responsibilities. If there had been no lapses, how could the theft have happened? Wherever there have been shortcomings, they will be addressed. Those responsible for the theft must be punished. These are the words of Govind Dev Giri Maharaj, the new General Secretary of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. After taking charge, he spoke to Dainik Bhaskar in his first interview, answering questions on the alleged theft of offerings, his new responsibilities and the future management of the Ram Temple. He said there appeared to be a conspiracy behind the alleged theft of offerings. “If an incident has occurred, responsibility must be fixed. But attention must also be paid to the way the entire incident was presented,” he said. Here are the key excerpts from the interview: Q: What will be your three priorities as General Secretary? Govind Dev Giri: First, I want this temple to become a centre of service to God. The Ram Temple should become a model for temples across the country. People should leave inspired by the way the temple is managed. Second, the system must be made completely transparent. Third, we need to strengthen communication between the people of Ayodhya and the temple. We need to understand their expectations and sentiments and create a better system of communication for this. Q: You were serving as the Trust’s Treasurer and are now its General Secretary. How do you see the change? Govind Dev Giri: Wherever the Lord places me in His service, it is all the same to me. I had to devote time as Treasurer as well, but I will now have to give more time as General Secretary. I will have to make some changes to my routine. I will give as much time as required to serve Lord Ram. For me, the position is not important; serving Ramlala is what matters. Q: Did you have any reservations before taking up the responsibility of General Secretary? Govind Dev Giri: There is no hesitation when it comes to serving Lord Ram. But I was certainly concerned. My programmes for the entire year are scheduled in advance. The responsibility of General Secretary is significant, so I will now have to make time to come to Ayodhya. The question was how I would find the time. But I decided that I had to make time for Lord Ram. Q: Nirmala Yadav has become the Trust’s first woman trustee. What was the thinking behind this decision? Govind Dev Giri: We should move forward by taking women along with us. That is my thinking. I have read Nirmala ji’s profile. Her experience and qualifications make her necessary here. She has MA degrees in Sanskrit and Hindi and has done a great deal of work in the field of education. The Trust will benefit from her qualifications and experience. Q: What new system will be introduced to monitor and ensure transparency in the crores of rupees offered at the temple? Govind Dev Giri: People from several banks have already come and given us suggestions. After discussions and deliberations, the system will be finalised. We will explain it in detail once that is done. Our effort will be to ensure that the process of handling offerings is secure and transparent. Q: The Trust has appointed former Air Marshal Jitendra Mishra as its first CEO. How will the responsibilities of the General Secretary and CEO be divided? Govind Dev Giri: The CEO will not be a system that works only for the General Secretary. The Trust will decide what needs to be done, while the CEO will be responsible for implementing those decisions. Therefore, there must be very good coordination between the two. Their responsibilities are different, but their goal is the same. Q: What happens if the General Secretary and CEO disagree on an issue? Who will have the final say? Govind Dev Giri: That situation should not arise because the General Secretary does not take decisions alone. The Trust will formulate the policies and take the decisions, while the CEO will be responsible for implementing them. When the entire system is structured this way, there is no question of a disagreement between the two. Q: Will there be a new system to make the Trust’s decisions, offering collections and expenditure public? Govind Dev Giri: Certainly. Our plan is to publish details of the number of devotees visiting the temple and the amount of offerings received every day on the website. Work on this is already under way. Gradually, all systems will be updated.

stories.title: Ganga, Varuna water levels rise in Varanasi:330 families leave homes; heavy rain expected after 72 hours
stories.summary: The flood situation in Varanasi has remained serious as water levels in the Ganga and its tributaries continue to rise. Although signs of a fall in the Ganga’s water level were seen on Friday morning, the river is still flowing above the warning level. Floodwater has reached low-lying areas of the city and neighbourhoods along the Varuna river, disrupting daily life. Several families have been forced to leave their homes and move to safer locations. The temperature in Varanasi was around 30°C on Friday morning, with winds blowing at around 6 kmph and cloudy skies. According to the weather department’s forecast, monsoon clouds are expected to remain limited over the region until September 6. Light to moderate rain, with heavy rain at some places, is likely between the night of September 6 and September 8. Ganga level falls, but flood threat remains According to the Central Water Commission, the Ganga’s water level was recorded at 70.67 metres at 8am on Friday. The level has now started falling, but the river remains above the warning mark. The gap between the river’s water level and the danger mark had been narrowing as the level continued to rise, increasing concern among the administration and residents of flood-affected areas. The rise in the Ganga has also affected its tributaries, including the Varuna, Gomti and Nad rivers. Water pressure remains high in areas along these rivers, with several settlements affected by flooding. Boats used to rescue people from Varuna area Pankaj Sahni said teams were using boats to rescue people trapped by flooding in the Varuna area. “We are currently using boats to evacuate people trapped in the floodwaters in the Varuna area. Those whose homes have been flooded or who are unable to leave are being taken to safer places.” He said around 100 to 150 people are transported by boat every day. The rescue and transport operation continues from morning until evening. Children who need to attend school are also taken there by boat and brought back. People who need to collect essential belongings from their homes are also taken there by boat and safely brought back. “Our effort is to ensure that no one in need faces problems during the flooding and that people can carry out essential tasks safely,” Sahni said. Drain breaks in Maruti Nagar, water enters homes The impact of the rising Ganga water has been reported from several parts of the city. A drain broke in Maruti Nagar, allowing water to enter several homes. Electricity supply in the area had to be suspended as a precaution. Residents are struggling to manage their daily needs amid the floodwater. The ground floor of Rameshwar Math in Nagwa has also been submerged. Batuks living there have been shifted to a safer location. Floodwater has also reached Lane No. 1 of Gangotri Vihar. Residents in low-lying areas are worried about further rises in water levels and damage to household belongings. Flood-affected neighbourhoods rise to 16 The number of neighbourhoods affected by flooding along the Varuna River has increased from 15 to 16. So far, 330 families have left their homes and moved to safer locations. Residents living along the river continue to face difficult conditions. Water has also entered houses near Piperhawa Ghat, making it difficult for people to move their belongings or reach safer locations. Health concerns are also emerging in flood-affected areas. Local reports suggest an increase in cases of coughs, colds and fever. Prolonged exposure to floodwater and damp conditions could increase the risk of illness among residents.

stories.title: 2 accused arrested for attacking woman in Maharashtra:Hid in Chauri Chaura, Gorakhpur; STF tracks them down
stories.summary: Two men wanted by authorities in Maharashtra’s Thane district were arrested from the Chauri Chaura area of Gorakhpur on Thursday (3 Sept). The accused had attacked a young woman with a sharp weapon in Thane with the intention of killing her and fled to Gorakhpur after the incident. Acting on their location, a joint team of the Uttar Pradesh STF and Maharashtra Police arrested them. The accused have been identified as Krishna Raj Gupta and Ankesh Gupta, both residents of Thane. Maharashtra Police to take accused into custody According to the STF, a case had been registered against the two at Manpada Police Station in Thane for allegedly attacking Kumari Dikshita with a sharp weapon. Both had been wanted in the case, following which Mumbai Police approached the Uttar Pradesh STF for assistance in their arrest. The Gorakhpur STF field unit began collecting intelligence to trace the accused. On Thursday (3 Sept), the team received information that both men were at Bal Khurd Dudi intersection in Chauri Chaura. Acting on the tip-off, the joint STF and Maharashtra Police team surrounded the area and arrested them at around 3.15pm. Accused allegedly admitted involvement Following their arrest, the two men were taken to Chauri Chaura police station. The STF said that during questioning, both allegedly admitted their involvement in the incident. Maharashtra Police will question them further about the weapon and other details related to the case. The process of obtaining transit remand and taking both accused to Maharashtra for further legal proceedings has been initiated.

stories.title: Devotees dance at Krishna Janmabhoomi, 10 lakh reach Mathura:Yogi says, ‘Those who tried to erase faith are now dust’
stories.summary: Mathura in Uttar Pradesh is celebrating Shri Krishna Janmashtami with great enthusiasm. CM Yogi Adityanath offered prayers at the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi temple and showered flowers on devotees and residents of Braj. Addressing devotees at the birthplace of Lord Krishna, CM Yogi said several attacks had been carried out on India, but none could erase the faith of Sanatan. He said those who dared to do so were eventually wiped out and today, there is no one left even to remember their names. Targeting the SP and Congress, Yogi said: “Your government’s faith is in Shri Krishna, Shri Ram, Baba Vishwanath and Maa Vindhyavasini. But those whose faith is in Babur and Aurangzeb, can they respect your faith? These followers of Babur and Aurangzeb are going to work to spread poison in society because some people are forced by their habits. They can threaten the safety of sisters and daughters. Our government will never allow their intentions to succeed.” Yogi said those who did not like the grand Ram Temple in Ayodhya were trying to defame the city. He said the government’s effort was to develop a grand complex in Mathura-Vrindavan on the lines of Ayodhya and Kashi. “Our effort is to develop Braj Bhoomi according to your sentiments. We will leave no stone unturned in this,” he said. Meanwhile, thousands of devotees queued up at the Banke Bihari Temple for Lord Krishna’s 5,253rd birth anniversary. Around 10,000 devotees attended the Mangala Aarti held early in the morning. Women danced to the beats of drums, manjiras and conch shells. According to the administration, around 50 lakh devotees from India and abroad are expected to visit Mathura on the occasion of Janmashtami. Devotees have also gathered at ISKCON temples in Varanasi and Noida, while the Ram Temple in Ayodhya has been decorated for the occasion. On Friday, on the occasion of Lord Krishna’s birth celebrations, Namami Gange performed an aarti for Lord Adi Keshav at Kashi’s ancient Vishnu Teerth, Adi Keshav Ghat. Makhana-mishri was offered to Lord Adi Keshav, who is revered as the deity who plays the flute of love and equality. During the ceremony, prayers were offered for public welfare, India’s progress, peace and prosperity, along with blessings for the protection of nature.

stories.title: Photographer remained ‘alive’ for 20 days after murder:Friend who killed him kept chatting with girlfriend in Prayagraj; broke body’s hands and legs
stories.summary: Several sensational revelations have emerged in the case of the photographer's murder in Dhoomanganj, Prayagraj. After committing the murder, the three friends of photographer Alok Gupta (27) did not just stop at disposing of the body. The trio also kept using his iPhone to hide his death. According to the police, the mastermind of the murder, Shubham Tiwari, kept chatting with Alok's girlfriend by posing as Alok, so that no one would suspect his death. However, he kept avoiding meeting the girlfriend. He would also not receive video and voice calls. Meanwhile, shortly after Alok's murder, the three friends left the flat after locking it from the outside. At that time, the body had not been disposed of. About 16 hours later, on the evening of August 11, the three friends returned to the flat. Here, they prepared to pack the body into a bag. For this, they even broke his limbs. After this, around 5 PM, the three left the flat carrying the bag containing the body. Now read the confession of the accused Shubham In police interrogation, Shubham revealed - After leaving the flat, the three of us drove around with the body in the car for about 5 hours. Our motive was to find a place where the body could be disposed of easily, without anyone getting suspicious. Around 10 PM, seeing a deserted area, we reached Sohagi Pahari. We threw Alok's body, which was packed in a bag, there and returned. On being asked about meeting his girlfriend, he used to say - I am busy right now Even after disposing of the body, I did not end the conspiracy. I kept Alok's iPhone with me. Then, using that same phone, I kept chatting with his girlfriend, pretending to be Alok. For about 20 days, the girlfriend kept thinking that she was chatting with Alok. Whenever she talked about meeting, I would put it off with some excuse or another. I would not even receive video calls or voice calls. When the girlfriend asked the reason for this, I kept reassuring her by saying I was busy with work. I did all this so that no one would immediately suspect Alok's disappearance or death. Mastermind is only 12th pass, father is a driver Police interrogation also revealed that the mastermind of the murder conspiracy, Shubham Tiwari, has only passed the 12th grade. He previously lived with Alok in a rented room in Shantipuram. Later, when his work improved, Alok bought a flat in Dhoomanganj. The second accused, Shubham Yadav, is also a 12th-grade graduate, while the third accused, Ankush, holds a polytechnic diploma. Shubham Tiwari's father is a driver. Shubham Yadav's father is a home guard, while Ankush's father is a farmer. Money was not the only reason for the murder According to the police, Shubham's resentment towards Alok was not just about money. Shubham was having an affair with the younger sister of the girl Alok was close to. Alok used to give expensive gifts to his girlfriend. When she mentioned this to her younger sister, she would also demand expensive gifts from Shubham. Due to financial constraints, Shubham was unable to fulfill her demands. His girlfriend would often taunt him about this. The police are also investigating this aspect as one of the motives for the murder. Incited after making him drink, shot and then strangled Shubham stated - The three of us had planned the murder in advance and reached Alok's flat on the night of August 10. As per the plan, he was deliberately made to drink excessive alcohol first. Around 1 am, after he was heavily intoxicated, Shubham Yadav started abusing Alok. Following this, an argument broke out between the two. When Alok got enraged and got up to hit him, I took out a pistol and fired. The bullet hit him below the shoulder, and Alok fell to the ground. After this, Shubham Yadav covered his mouth and nose from behind, while I strangled him. Property dealer from Phaphamau had provided the pistol and car Dhoomanganj Station House Officer Dhananjay Pandey stated that during interrogation, the accused revealed that the pistol and car used in the murder were provided by Vipin Shukla from Phaphamau. Vipin works in property dealing. The police are now searching for him. For what purpose did Vipin provide the pistol and car to the accused? Was he involved in the murder conspiracy? Or was help provided to the accused for some other reason? This is being investigated. Alok's body will undergo a second post-mortem The most crucial twist in the case emerged regarding the post-mortem report. According to the police, the accused have confessed to shooting Alok during interrogation. The forensic team has also recovered shell casings and bloodstain samples from the flat. Police officials state that the body was recovered in a highly damaged condition. Given this, it is possible that bullet marks were not clearly visible during the initial post-mortem. Now, through a second post-mortem and medico-legal examination, efforts will be made to clarify whether Alok was shot or not, and what the actual cause of his death was.

stories.title: Father says son was upset over wife’s infidelity:Attacked 5 people with sword in Fatehpur; mob beats him to death
stories.summary: 'My son came home panicked. He was muttering that everything is gone now. I folded my hands and asked him what happened, but he didn't tell me. He left after just 15 minutes. He was distressed about his wife and kept calling his children, but no one would talk to him. His only pain was that those he fed his entire life were running away from him today.' This is what the father of Pawan, who attacked 5 people with a sword in Fatehpur on Thursday, had to say. Later, a mob beat him to death. The father says that his son was troubled by his wife's infidelity. Meanwhile, the condition of the 4 people injured in the attack remains critical. The case is from the Aung police station area. The Dainik Bhaskar team spoke to the accused's father and the families of the injured to understand the entire matter. Read the report... First, understand the case... In Fatehpur, early Thursday (August 3) at 2 AM, Pawan attacked his brother-in-law, sister-in-law, and three nephews with a sword at his in-laws' house. First, he attacked the brother-in-law's three sons one by one while they were sleeping. Then, upon hearing the screams, he also attacked the brother-in-law and his wife on their heads and necks with the sword. Hearing the commotion, the villagers reached the spot. They surrounded Pawan and snatched the sword from him. After this, they beat him to death with sticks and rods. According to the family members, the second brother-in-law who went with the son-in-law Pawan is missing, and there is a fear of some untoward incident happening to him. Families of two brothers lived in the same house Mahavir's family lives in Bikampur village. The family includes his 2 sons, Raju and Rajesh. Raju's family consists of his wife Vimlesh, 3 sons Khatu alias Rajkaran (25), Pradeep (23), Gore (20), and a daughter Gudiya (18). The younger son is Rajesh and his wife is Buddha. All 9 people live in the same house. The dispute started just a few years after the marriage About 26 years ago, Mahavir married off his daughter Phoolkumari, alias Seema, to Pawan (55), a resident of Asapur. Pawan was a carpenter. They have 4 children-daughters Sheetal, alias Mansi (22), Komal (18), Radha (15), and son Satyam (12). A few years after the marriage, disputes began between Pawan and Phoolkumari. Wife living in Gujarat with the children Nine years ago, Phoolkumari left her in-laws' house and returned to her parents' home with the children. Four years ago, a panchayat was also held in the village to reconcile them. People mentioned that Pawan was greatly humiliated during the panchayat as well. Phoolkumari is currently living with her children and a relative in Gujarat, while Pawan lived in the village with his father. Held a grudge, but did not stop visiting Pawan suspected that Phoolkumari's maternal family was supporting her. It was with their encouragement that she was not returning home. Pawan held a grudge against his in-laws in his heart, but he had not stopped visiting them. On Wednesday (August 30) at 5 PM, Pawan reached his in-laws' house. Took his brother-in-law along on the pretext of showing him a girl Here, he told his brother-in-law Raju (55) that he had found a girl in a nearby village for his son Rajkaran. "Come with me now. Let's go see her, and then the rest of the family can see her later." Upon hearing this, Raju got ready and left with Pawan. At 9 PM, Pawan returned to his in-laws' house alone. Seeing him alone, the family members asked about Raju. Pawan replied that Raju had stayed back at the girl's house and that they would all go to see the girl in the morning. Niece fed him, slept near the nephews The in-laws trusted Raju's words. After this, Raju's daughter Gudiya fed Pawan. Then everyone went to sleep. Pawan and Raju's three sons were sleeping outside the house, while the rest of the people were inside. Around 2 AM, people ran out of the house after hearing loud noises. Outside, Pawan was attacking the three nephews relentlessly with a sword-like weapon in his hand. When Rajesh and his wife Buddha ran to save their nephews, Pawan attacked them multiple times as well. Villagers caught him and beat him with sticks Gudiya saved her life by hiding in a room, but she also sustained some injuries. Meanwhile, hearing the commotion, the neighbors arrived and surrounded Pawan. Pawan died due to the beating with sticks. The police took all the injured to the hospital, from where they were referred to Kanpur due to their critical condition. The condition of 4 people remains critical. Now read what the accused's father said... Pawan's father, Ramsajivan Vishwakarma, says - I have 4 sons. Everyone lives separately with their families. Pawan was married to Phoolkumari. After the marriage, they had 3 daughters and one son. Our daughter-in-law stayed with us for only a few years. Her character was not right from the beginning. She had relations with many people in the village. My son had caught her talking to other people many times. No solution found even after the Panchayat Once, she even went away with a man. She stayed there all night. After this, she filed a false report against my son. A panchayat was also held in the village, but no solution was found. Now, she is living with someone else in Gujarat, taking all the children with her. Pawan used to live alone with me. He was very sad deep down. Wife and children did not talk to him Pawan used to call his children and his wife many times. However, no one would talk to him. He was deeply saddened by the fact that those whom he had fed and cared for his entire life were now running away from him. Pawan left the house in the evening but did not say where he was going. He returned home at 8 PM. He did not seem to be in a good state; he was filled with deep sorrow and anger. Changed clothes at home and reached his in-laws' house again He was speaking in a panicked manner, saying that everything would be fine now. Seeing his condition, I felt scared. I folded my hands and asked, "Son, what happened?" But he did not tell me anything. He changed his clothes quickly and left again on his bike. At that time, there were no stains or blood marks on his clothes. Later in the morning, we found out that so much had happened. Daughter said - Papa never stayed out We spoke to Gudiya, the daughter of the missing Raju. Gudiya said that there is still no trace of my father. My uncle (phupha) had taken him to see a girl for marriage. When he returned, Papa was not with him. We asked where he left Papa, to which he replied that at the place where they went to see the girl, her mother has kept your father there. We did not believe him. My brother said that we are going to get it. My father never stays out. On this, my uncle (phupha) said that he would take everyone along in the morning. After this, he made some excuse and coaxed the brothers. If we hadn't hidden, no one in the family would have survived today. Raju's wife Vimlesh said that there is no trace of her husband. All three sons are fighting for their lives in the hospital. I have lost everything. SP Abhimanyu Manglik said Three teams have been deployed to search for the missing Raju. Help is being taken from the CCTV footage installed on the highway. He will be recovered soon.

stories.title: Why did Mayawati remove Akash Anand for the third time:Will it benefit or hurt BSP? Is his political career over?
stories.summary: On 2nd August, 2026, Mayawati expelled Ashok Siddharth, the father-in-law of her nephew Akash Anand, from the party. Mayawati wrote on 'X'- Despite repeated warnings, there was no improvement in Ashok Siddharth's attitude. Because of this, all responsibilities were taken away from him. Exactly 32 days later, Mayawati stripped his son-in-law and her nephew, Akash Anand, of the post of National Coordinator. She wrote, ‘Kanshiram ji allowed his family members to support party work, but he was against fielding them in elections. I am fully committed to that resolution. I gave Akash permission to work in the party, but he still needs to mature further.’ The question is, will this decision cast a shadow over Akash's political career? Know everything in 5 points... 1. First, know why Mayawati expelled Akash from the party? Senior journalist Anand Rai says Mayawati had similarly removed Akash Anand during the last Lok Sabha elections as well. There is a similarity in all three actions: She first removed his father-in-law, Ashok Siddharth. After that, she took action against Akash. After the successful rally in Sadabad, Akash Anand received immense praise from party workers, the general public, and the media. News also circulated in the media that Akash Anand would play a key role in the UP assembly elections and would also distribute tickets. Mayawati responded to this immediately. She posted on social media platform X, stating that she alone distributes all tickets in the BSP. The names of the candidates decided by her are only announced at party workers' conferences. Akash Anand had done the same in Sadabad. Following this, Mayawati made another post stating that from now on, permission must be taken from her before scheduling Akash Anand's programs. She had also said that Akash would take her permission before attending any program. Due to Akash's popularity and his father-in-law Ashok Siddharth's influence within the organization, Mayawati has always been apprehensive that the father-in-law and son-in-law might join forces to remove her from her position. This sense of insecurity in Mayawati is not new. Ever since her influence in the party grew, she has been making decisions based on such apprehensions. This was also the reason behind showing the door to many leaders, including RK Chaudhary and Lalji Verma. Only two leaders could muster the courage to rebel against Mayawati while remaining in the party. The first was Naseemuddin Siddiqui, who made an audio tape related to Mayawati public. The second was Swami Prasad Maurya, who called Mayawati the 'daughter of wealth' by holding a press conference at the party office. 2. Did Mayawati take the decision suddenly or were there signs of it? Senior journalist Syed Qasim says - This is not a decision taken suddenly. No one except her can guess what Mayawati is going to do. But, signs of clipping Akash's wings had started appearing. Akash's rally in Sadabad was broadcast live on the official social media pages of the BSP. Short clips of his speeches were created and made viral on social media. Following this, Akash made a post regarding Ankit Kumar, who is associated with Rapido. It stated: "When 4 railway employees sat in his cab and made casteist remarks against a Dalit senior officer, Ankit protested and made them get out of the vehicle. He asked the question: If there is a question about someone's capability, then name them. Why are you defaming the entire caste?" What did he get in return? Rapido suspended Ankit's account for 99 years and 11 months. Then, Akash wrote about RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, who holds views on ending reservation, stating that he should answer Dalit youths like Ankit. Later, Akash deleted this post. This had to be done under pressure from Mayawati. Then, when his meeting was held in Jewar on 25 August, there was no broadcast of it on the party's official page. Akash also did not say anything significant at this meeting. When a meeting of UP state office bearers was called on 31 August, Akash was not invited then either. Following this, before the national executive meeting on 3rd September, Akash changed his bio to just 'BSP worker'. 3. How much does BSP benefit or lose from this Senior journalist Syed Qasim says - Mayawati has already seen the results of her decision in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Back then, she had taken action against Akash in the middle of the elections. The SP-Congress were successful in spreading the message among her core Dalit voters that BSP chief Mayawati was being forced to make decisions under pressure from the BJP. The result was that the BSP could not even open its account in the Lok Sabha across the entire country. Its vote percentage also fell below 10 percent. This time too, Mayawati has removed Akash Anand from his post right in the middle of the election atmosphere. Party workers were enthusiastic after the rallies in Sadabad of Hathras and Jewar. Especially young Dalit voters were very happy with Akash being active. Dalit voters had started thinking of turning towards the BSP once again. Now, the action against Akash will send a message among Dalit supporters that Mayawati is taking decisions under the influence of the BJP. They believe she is not keen on leading the party to victory in the elections. In such a situation, Dalit voters will look towards a third option. The Congress has been the old home for Dalits. A large section of Dalits may go with the Congress in the assembly elections. 4. Is Akash Anand's political career in crisis? On one hand, Mayawati stripped Akash Anand of his position, while on the other, she attended a meeting with his younger brother, Yishan Anand. Yishan was seen at a public event for the first time since Mayawati's birthday in 2024. His father, Anand Kumar, was also with him. Anand Kumar is the Vice President of the party. In the party meeting, Mayawati also mentioned that Anand Kumar has not been keeping well. Yishan Anand will assist him in his duties. After this decision by Mayawati, speculations are rife about whether Akash Anand's political journey will come to a halt. Responding to this, Dalit thinker and JNU Professor Vivek Kumar says that Akash Anand is young. He still has a long time ahead of him politically. Mayawati has not even expelled him from the party. Even in the past, when Mayawati removed him from the party, she later reinstated him. She had once even declared him her political successor. This time too, she had created a new post of National Coordinator for him in the party. This means she could entrust Akash Anand with responsibilities again in the future. 5. How much difference is there between Akash Anand and Ishaan Both are Mayawati's nephews. Among the two sons of Mayawati's younger brother Anand Kumar, Akash is the elder and Ishan is the younger one. Mayawati herself had arranged Akash's marriage to Pragya, the daughter of Ashok Siddharth. Whereas, Ishan rebelled against the family and had a love marriage with Isha Khanna, the daughter of a Punjabi Khatri family, of his own choice. Upset with the family, Yishan was even living separately in South Ex, Delhi. Akash has a daughter, while Ishan has a son. There is a one-day age difference between their children. Senior journalist Syed Qasim says - There is also a big difference in their upbringing. While Akash appears gentle and cultured, Ishan carries an attitude. A glimpse of this was also seen during the national executive meeting. Whenever Akash used to come to such meetings, he never forgot to touch Mayawati's feet. While Ishan did stand tall with his hands tied behind his back for a short while near Mayawati. After this, he sat on the side chair with his father. Secondly, there is also a big difference in the oratory skills of both brothers. No one has heard Ishan give a speech from a public platform yet. Whereas, Akash's speeches have been quite popular.

stories.title: Mirzapur locals want ex-IAS Divya Mittal to contest polls:Say she deserves to be MP, not MLA; why political debut is being discussed?
stories.summary: IAS Divya Mittal resigned on 30th August. While in the bureaucracy, her inclination was always towards the welfare of the people. This sparked discussions that she might contest elections. Mirzapur was the first name mentioned as her political base. After talking to the people of Mirzapur, 3 reasons for this became clear- 1. Before quitting her job (in July), she visited Mirzapur. She went to areas including Kachhwan, where she had carried out development work. 2. While serving as District Magistrate, she visited hundreds of villages. Even after no longer holding the post, she maintains direct communication with about 200 village heads (Gram Pradhans) and local residents. 3. After resigning from the IAS post, Divya Mittal specifically mentioned Mirzapur in her message. She wrote that Mirzapur taught her that 'impossible' is not a fact, just an opinion. So, is Divya Mittal really preparing to contest elections? If she does, how strong is her hold among the people of Mirzapur? Read in this report... Lecturer said - She should enter politics; there is no shortage of supporters... In Mirzapur city, KB Lal Srivastava, a retired lecturer from the Government Polytechnic College, says, "If Divya Mittal comes here to contest elections, it will be Mirzapur's good fortune. She has my full support. The people here like her, so they will support her." When questioned, KB Lal why so? He said, "Divya Mittal has been an approachable officer who used to stay among the public." People said - Her stature is worthy of contesting the MP election Santosh Singh says, 'Her tenure as DM was excellent. She brought water to the Lahuriadah village, where water could never reach before. After she left, some people even stopped the water facility. The local politicians did not let her work freely. If she enters politics, she should contest the MP election.' He says, 'To my knowledge, there have been disputes between Divya and the current MP. These include the issue of bringing water to Lahuriadah village.' Divya did not work under the pressure of any politician or minister Former Vishwa Hindu Parishad provincial secretary Manoj Srivastava is preparing to contest the elections this year. He has often met Divya Mittal. Manoj says, "As far as contesting the election is concerned, it would be too early to say anything. The public liked her work here, which is why people are remembering her." On the question of the dispute with the MP, Manoj gives an example and says, “If the MP were to say that the color of milk is black, Divya Mittal was the kind of officer who would say that the color of milk is not black, but white. This is the root cause of the entire conflict.” 'One wouldn't even think she was the DM, very simple behaviour' Chhavinath Tiwari lives in the Drummondganj area, about 50 kilometers away from Mirzapur city. He says, "Right now, the public is only talking about Divya Mittal. When she used to visit the village, she would meet people in a very simple manner. Looking at her, one wouldn't even think she was the DM. She paid attention to every facility in the village." Chhavinath says, "If Divya Mittal comes to contest the Lok Sabha elections, her influence will grow even further because she is very popular here. She had a rift with Anupriya Patel. Talk of friction between the two over water-related issues also kept coming up." 'Divya will have no influence here' Manish Tripathi, who contested the election on a BSP ticket in 2024. Manish has now left the BSP and joined the BJP. He says, 'Divya Mittal is not going to have any significant influence here. She did a good job while being the DM. But whatever she did, she did it according to the instructions of the administration. She did not do any work outside of the administration's directives. I did not see any tension between her and the MP.'

stories.summary: Khedan Wattan Punjab Diyan-2026 has officially kicked off in Punjab, with a vision to showcase the state's talent on a global scale. Almost one million participants, ranging from ages fourteen to seventy plus, are set to compete in thirty-nine different sports. Concluding on November twenty-ninth, the event boasts a prize pool of Rs 12.

stories.title: The annual Delhi Yamuna flood threat- why September matters?
stories.summary: Delhi is under the shadow of recurrent flooding threats as the Yamuna River inches closer to its danger threshold. The catastrophic floods from the previous year resulted in the displacement of thousands and interrupted vital public services. Fortunately, this year has seen reduced upstream water releases, offering a brief respite; however, the risk of heavy rainfall above could still ignite a serious crisis.

Meanwhile, Singapore's minister has expressed condemnation over racist remarks aimed at Indians during discussions about the recent disaster in Nepal. 'Students paying price for neglect': CJP attacks govt as boys PG collapses in Delhi

The incident took place at around 1.30 pm in the densely populated neighbourhood near Delhi University's South Campus, where student hostels, paying guest accommodations and eateries operate along narrow lanes.

stories.title: What does the law say about inheritance? Know your rights
Wisconsin publisher and women’s-rights pioneer Lester’s remains return home 138 years after death
stories.summary: Lisle Lester, a journalist, publisher, actress and women’s-rights advocate from Fond du Lac, died penniless in New York in 1888 at age 50. Her cremated remains remained unclaimed for 138 years. After efforts by local women and the Fond du Lac Soroptimists, her remains have now returned home for burial.

stories.title: How Kentucky protected a vast elk landscape
stories.summary: Kentucky hunters faced uncertainty with temporary land access agreements. A new conservation partnership secured permanent public access to a large elk hunting area. This agreement provides 54,560 acres for public use in eastern Kentucky. The project involved state officials, conservation groups, and federal funding programs. This ensures continued hunting traditions and habitat restoration for future generations.

60 years on, Ken Kesey’s psychedelic Furthur bus returns to San Francisco for restoration
stories.summary: Ken Kesey’s psychedelic “Furthur” bus has returned to San Francisco after decades and is now the centrepiece of a new Grateful Dead exhibition. The bus was used by Kesey and his Merry Band of Pranksters during their 1964 cross-country journey, which helped spread the emerging psychedelic counterculture. The exhibition also features Jerry Garcia’s BMW and will launch an effort to restore the now-dilapidated bus.

stories.title: IIT Mandi orders inquiry after poster says Shudras should ‘serve higher classes’
stories.summary: For Shudras, however, the poster listed their role as "serve higher classes", which became the focus of the controversy. The poster also quoted a Bhagavad Gita verse stating that the four divisions of human society were created according to the "three modes of material nature and the work associated with them". Behera said he had been away from IIT Mandi and returned on Saturday.

19 lakh lives impacted as Ganga breaches flood mark in Patna
stories.summary: In Bihar, more than 19.57 lakh individuals are grappling with severe flooding across eleven districts. The Ganga has surpassed its former record flood level at Gandhi Ghat, leading authorities to raise alerts for downstream localities and boost relief activities. Several other rivers are similarly exceeding danger levels, and with rain predictions suggesting additional water rises, the outlook remains concerning.

93-year-old Cleveland bridge closes after analysis finds severe floor-beam deterioration
stories.summary: A Cleveland bridge that opened in 1933 has been closed until further notice after new analysis found more extensive deterioration in its floor beams. The closure comes as the Ohio Department of Transportation was preparing a major rehabilitation project, with construction tentatively planned for 2028. Officials said the decision was made for public safety.

stories.title: ‘Can no longer be stopped’: AfD races towards historic win in Germany state vote
stories.summary: Voting is currently taking place in Saxony-Anhalt's vital state election, representing an important benchmark for the far-right AfD party. Latest surveys indicate they are notably ahead, with a chance to obtain a full majority, possibly leading to their first state governance since WWII. The results will be crucial in assessing Chancellor Friedrich Merz's approach to migration and security, with weeks of coalition talks likely if no party secures a majority.

stories.title: 242 trapped by wildfire; pilots flew into flames to save them
stories.summary: California National Guard crews performed a historic nighttime helicopter rescue during the Creek Fire. They saved 242 people trapped by intense flames and thick smoke. This extraordinary mission utilized night-vision goggles and combat helicopters in a wildfire zone. The daring rescue demonstrated new possibilities for nighttime wildfire aviation response. California has since expanded its nighttime aviation capabilities and interagency training.

stories.title: ‘Bye-bye, papa’: What 21-year-old told father before jumping into Chenab
stories.summary: A 21-year-old woman reportedly leaped into the Chenab River on Saturday after a phone call with her father where she expressed, 'This is my life.' Despite the efforts of bystanders to change her mind, she proceeded with the drastic act. A combined rescue mission was initiated, but she has yet to be located, leaving her motives shrouded in uncertainty.

stories.title: Couple bought 101 acres in 2024; before the sale closed, they planned to preserve it forever
stories.summary: In 2024, Jeff and Betsy Yingling bought 101 acres in Freedom Township, Adams County, Pennsylvania, and soon began considering how to protect the land permanently. After living there and seeing its wildlife, cropland, wooded areas and changing scenery, they decided to place a preservation easement on the property. The easement was finalised in August 2026, permanently protecting all 101 acres for future generations.

stories.title: 'Less than what politicians spend on pet': Dipke slams Maha govt's Rs 2L payout to Adivasi students
In 1984, Lou Dobbs acquired a New Jersey farm and expanded it over four decades
stories.summary: Lou Dobbs is parting with his stunning 283-acre estate, Hickory Hollow, now available for $6 million. This sprawling property, crafted over 40 years, boasts an impressive 11-acre pond alongside equestrian amenities. The main colonial-style residence, complemented by guest accommodations, reflects the late television personality's vision. With vast expanses, this land holds promise for both residential development and agricultural endeavors.

Landslide hits Sikkim’s Mangan, partially blocks Teesta River flow
stories.summary: A landslide has impacted the Chyakoong River in Mangan district, Sikkim, resulting in a partial obstruction of the Teesta and Chyakoong rivers. Local authorities are actively assessing the situation. While the water levels are stable, the river's water has become muddied. Precautionary alerts have been issued to residents in vulnerable lower regions.

stories.title: A 2021 landslide cut Denali’s only road; five years later, a $230M bridge spans the slope
stories.summary: A new bridge now spans the Denali National Park road after a landslide. This $230 million project reconnects the eastern and western road sections. Engineers built a 475-foot steel truss bridge over the unstable moving ground. Hikers and cyclists can now cross the bridge, while bus service resumes in 2027. This marks a long-term solution for accessing remote park areas.

stories.title: Colorado ranch listed for $5.9M as development site, bought by conservationists instead
stories.summary: A 674-acre ranch on Colorado’s Pikes Peak was listed for $5.9 million as a potential development site, but Palmer Land Conservancy bought it for conservation instead. The Pinestone Ranch property connects Woodland Park with more than 100,000 acres of public land and could eventually support trails, wildlife habitat and public access as part of wider efforts to complete the Ring the Peak route.

How discarded Christmas trees are being used to build dunes on a UK beach
stories.summary: Discarded Christmas trees are being used to strengthen the sand dunes at St Annes beach on England’s Fylde Coast. Since the project began in 2013, the trees have helped trap wind-blown sand and expand the dunes. The wider dunes act as a natural sea defence, helping protect nearby homes and businesses from coastal flooding while also creating habitat for specialised plants and wildlife.

stories.title: Four private Michigan islands spanning 520 acres hit the market for $2.3 million
stories.summary: Now on the market for $2.3 million, this exclusive private group of four islands spans 520 acres. It features a beautifully renovated home, essential machinery, two boats, and a dock slip on the mainland. With about 2,000 feet of waterfront along Michigan's northern border, most of the property is safeguarded by a conservation easement, preserving the area’s native ecosystems and ensuring enjoyment for generations to come.

Scientists exposed a Wisconsin forest to extra CO₂ for 11 years; productivity rose 39%, but ozone cut gains
stories.summary: A Wisconsin experiment studied forest communities exposed to high carbon dioxide and ozone. Elevated carbon dioxide significantly increased forest productivity and carbon storage over eleven years. Conversely, increased ozone levels reduced forest productivity and ecosystem carbon content. The combined effects showed carbon dioxide stimulating growth and ozone limiting it. These findings highlight forests' complex responses to atmospheric changes.

Akademiks Mocks Travis Scott: DJ blasts rapper after Yeat’s ‘ON NOTHING’ diss; feud motive remains unclear

The diss followed Yeat’s removed verse from Young Thug’s “Eaters,” sparking fan speculation about tension between the rappers. Neither Travis nor Yeat has confirmed what triggered the clash.

stories.title: TikTok Dog Dies At 8: Internet star Tucker Budzyn dies after chemo complication; fans mourn online
stories.summary: Tucker Budzyn, the beloved golden retriever who became a TikTok and social media sensation, has died at eight after a sudden complication during lymphoma treatment. His owner, Courtney Budzyn, said Tucker initially responded well to chemotherapy and entered partial remission before an intestinal infection rapidly worsened his condition. Despite emergency treatment, veterinarians could not save him. Courtney shared an emotional tribute, saying Tucker was “part of my soul,” as fans mourned his loss.

Authorities seized substantial quantities of heroin, opium, and other narcotics during this period. Police connected thousands of individuals struggling with addiction to de-addiction and treatment centers. This initiative effectively combines enforcement actions with citizen-generated intelligence for drug control.

stories.summary: Santa Monica's last intact shotgun house, built in 1897, faced demolition and several moves. Community efforts and preservation groups saved the structure from disappearing entirely. This historic building now educates the public about local history and preservation principles.

stories.summary: The inquiry into the illness affecting tribal children in Balaghat revealed various clinical factors behind their conditions. Many people were injured as they attempted to escape the rapidly spreading flames. Narrow hallways caused congestion, hindering escape efforts for those trapped inside. The exact cause of the tragic fire remains unconfirmed by authorities.

stories.summary: Recent Nepal floods highlight Himalayan vulnerabilities and cascading disaster risks. China's Yarlung Tsangpo dam project faces scrutiny due to its geologically unstable location. stories.title: In 1844, a Mexican land grant covered an 80,000-acre ranch; access fight continues centuries later
stories.summary: The Cielo Vista Ranch in Colorado is at the centre of a land dispute dating to the 1844 Sangre de Cristo Land Grant. Governor Jared Polis has now appointed Ken Salazar as a special envoy to help the heirs, community and property owner find a way forward.

Sikkim aspires to establish itself as an educational hub by significantly enhancing its school system and plans to integrate a life skills curriculum focused on disaster readiness.

stories.summary: Michigan's latest eco-friendly endeavor involves transforming thousands of old tires into rubber-modified asphalt for road building. Over 7,000 scrap tires have been repurposed on Ellsworth Road in Pittsfield Township, with researchers evaluating how this new asphalt stacks up against conventional materials. The initiative has earned a prestigious national award for its commitment to sustainability and effective recycling of resources, aiming to tackle tire waste while boosting road durability.

Port officials stated that all traffic in and out of the port had been stopped. Videos showed several dozen men dressed in black, shouting "stop the boats". The incident appeared to be an anti-immigration protest, causing significant traffic jams.

stories.title: In the late 1920s, mule deer were brought to Catalina Island; now a judge has ordered for 2,000 of them to be culled
stories.summary: Catalina Island's mule deer, released in the late 1920s, now pose serious threats to local flora and contribute to increased wildfire risks. In response, conservation leaders have outlined a contentious strategy to significantly reduce the mule deer population. Following a legal challenge that was dismissed by a judge, the cull is set to commence, aimed at preserving the island's natural environment and lowering fire hazards.

DTC fought conductor for 32 years over Rs 67 fare and his wages, now fined Rs 1 lakh by Delhi HC
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has imposed a fine of one lakh rupees on the Delhi Transport Corporation for its relentless pursuit of a thirty-two-year-old legal battle involving a bus conductor. The court criticized the drawn-out litigation as an abuse of the legal system. The conductor had been seeking seventeen months of unpaid wages following his dismissal, while the court dismissed DTC's challenge to a tribunal ruling.

stories.summary: For Gen Z, a secure salary still matters, but so do personal time, flexibility and career growth. A survey of young workers shows a generation trying to build a career without handing over its life to it.

stories.title: Taiwan faces alarming Chinese presence around its territory
stories.summary: Taiwan reported significant Chinese military incursions around its territory on Saturday. Up to twenty Chinese aircraft and several naval vessels were detected by Taiwan's defense ministry. Many of these aircraft crossed the median line into Taiwan's air defense zone. This surge follows recent days of increased Chinese naval and air presence. Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration noted a substantial rise in Chinese vessels last month.

stories.title: Output overdrive: 30% productivity boost could power 35% of future manufacturing
stories.summary: According to a KPMG report, productivity is identified as the leading catalyst for growth within manufacturing. Firms that excel in boosting productivity tend to see notable increases in both profits and market valuation. For large manufacturers, meaningful productivity improvements require transformative approaches. Meanwhile, small factories are shown to have lower per-worker output. Leveraging digital solutions and cultivating a positive workplace culture will be essential for driving productivity forward.

In 2018, a Hawaii study found green roofs stayed cooler than white roofs in Honolulu
stories.summary: A University of Hawaii study found green roofs stayed cooler than white roofs. The green roof's average daytime surface temperature was 4.1°F lower. Peak temperatures on the green roof were 18.5°F lower than the white roof. Evapotranspiration from plants cooled the surrounding air significantly. This vegetation offers a method to combat urban heat island effects.

LeT terrorist killed in J&K: Yasir was behind 2024 attack on IAF convoy, civilians
stories.summary: Yasir was gunned down on Friday during Operation Ashdar, launched after security forces received intelligence about the movement of a group of terrorists through the Pir Panjal mountains. Jammu and Kashmir Police identified the slain terrorist as Yasir and said he was affiliated with the banned Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT). stories.title: Five EU countries move towards first ‘return hub’ for rejected asylum seekers
stories.summary: Five European Union nations are planning migrant return hubs outside the EU. These facilities aim to process rejected asylum seekers for repatriation. The countries hope to finalize agreements with a partner nation this year. Human rights groups have raised concerns about potential risks to migrants. The proposed centers are intended to operate within international legal frameworks.

stories.title: Census 2027: The 14 questions and why opposition fears an NPR 'backdoor'
stories.summary: Enumerators have begun the decennial headcount in Ladakh and snowbound regions. New questions in the Census questionnaire have raised opposition concerns about its purpose. Critics allege the Census is becoming a backdoor for the National Population Register. The Census Act legally protects personal information collected during the exercise. Experts debate the data's use and potential privacy implications.

No registration number, no attendance: NMC warns medical colleges
stories.summary: Medical colleges have one month to update faculty registration numbers on the attendance system. Failure to comply will result in blocked daily attendance for specified teaching staff. The National Medical Commission issued this warning after finding blank registration fields. Colleges must review and update all medical faculty and resident profiles accurately. Non-medical faculty will have 'NA' entered in the registration number field.

stories.title: In 2017, New York high-school students redesigned a downtown park; 9 years later, their idea has finally been built
stories.summary: A transformative student design from ten years ago has blossomed into an enriching downtown park. North Tonawanda proudly launched Smart Growth 2.0, a redevelopment venture worth millions. This initiative has introduced a charming clock tower and improved pedestrian facilities, which enhance the ongoing rejuvenation of the area and contribute to broader downtown revitalization efforts, signifying the city's commitment to public investment and community enhancement.
