A Texas teenager started building birdhouses after losing his pet cockatiel; now he has inspired a conservation movement across 20 states
stories.summary: After adopting a pet cockatiel, Aamir Tinwala initiated a bird conservation movement focused on building birdhouses to combat habitat loss. His project promotes awareness of local biodiversity while encouraging community members to take an active role in habitat stewardship. Tinwala has personally constructed over 750 shelters and inspired countless others, illustrating how individual efforts can lead to significant environmental benefits.

stories.title: Nigerian engineer built a bottle house with 14,800 plastic bottles; experiment grew to 15 homes, including a five-bedroom duplex
stories.summary: In an inspiring initiative, Nigerian engineer Yahaya Ahmed is turning discarded plastic bottles into sustainable building materials. To date, he has constructed around fifteen houses utilizing this creative technique. This process cuts down construction costs and offers superior insulation properties. By filling empty bottles with sand, Ahmed effectively combats plastic waste while providing cost-effective and durable housing alternatives.

stories.title: Gateway of Arch is going dark this September; the surprising reason has everything to do with millions of birds
stories.summary: This September, the Gateway Arch in St Louis plans to turn off its lights in a bid to protect migratory birds heading south along the Mississippi Flyway. This essential route is vital for various bird species. To assist, people can keep their cats indoors, reduce outdoor lighting, and regularly clean bird feeders to help curb the spread of diseases.

stories.title: In 2016, Florida’s living shorelines withstood Hurricane Matthew’s 90 mph winds intact
stories.summary: A living shoreline project in New Smyrna Beach largely survived Hurricane Matthew's severe winds. This natural approach used vegetation and sand to stabilize the coast effectively. Conventional hardened structures nearby experienced significant damage and erosion during the storm. The project demonstrated how natural defenses can withstand powerful hurricane conditions. This resilience offers a promising model for future coastal protection strategies.

stories.title: North Carolina father to spend $800,000 building housing community for disabled son and those like him
stories.summary: Dave Curro is spearheading the development of Forest Grove, an innovative community designed specifically for adults with special needs. This initiative will include 20 tiny homes and a supporting community center, providing essential resources. A recent festival raised significant funds, demonstrating strong community support. Curro's son, Bret, inspires this heartfelt project, addressing a crucial shortage in housing options for this underserved population.

stories.title: Michigan scientist buried seeds in 1879; some still grew 142 years later in an experiment lasting to 2100
stories.summary: In a remarkable exploration of seed dormancy, William James Beal's 1879 experiment revealed astonishing results when researchers discovered viable seeds in 2021, 142 years later. This included a surprising hybrid moth mullein detected through DNA analysis, enriching the study's findings. Insights gained will enhance land restoration efforts and help control invasive species for a sustainable future, demonstrating the enduring legacy of scientific inquiry.

Using fossilised wings, laser measurements, computer modelling and AI, researchers found that some insects made clear chirping sounds, while one species may have produced ultrasonic calls above the human hearing range.

stories.title: 33-year-old buys neglected 81-room hotel for $2.55M; is spending $1.1M to rebuild it while living there
stories.summary: From a modest beginning, Greg Clark has embarked on an impressive journey in the hospitality sector, currently breathing new life into an eighty-one-room hotel located in the picturesque Eureka Springs. His aim is to craft exceptional guest experiences, showcasing his renovation progress on TikTok. With a vision to build ten carefully curated hotels over seven years, Clark's journey is one of ambition and creativity.

President Trump has been appraised of various options amidst growing tensions from the Iran conflict, though White House and Pentagon sources have refuted rumors regarding a review of the Deputy Secretary of War role. Ongoing restrictions on fuel shipments from the US have intensified these power outages and sanitation issues. Both locals and visitors are advised to exercise caution regarding food safety and refrigeration practices. UN experts caution that these sanctions may exacerbate a larger public health emergency.

stories.title: Devil Flower Species Found: Fungi-fed Thai plant stuns botanists; fewer than 50 exist
stories.summary: In a remarkable botanical find, scientists have discovered Thismia daemona, a unique flowering plant in Thailand's Thong Pha Phum National Park. This intriguing species, devoid of leaves and green structures, primarily derives its nourishment from subterranean fungi. Its eerie, horn-like form has earned it the moniker 'devil flower' among researchers, marking a significant discovery in the study of this rare plant group.

The individual reportedly attacked another traveler and directed racial insults toward a flight attendant. Thanks to the quick actions of retired law enforcement officer Juan Mejia and a vigilant flight attendant, the passenger was subdued using zip ties and duct tape for safety.

stories.summary: Hundreds of tiny snails are journeying over 5,000 miles from Michigan to Tahiti. This release is part of a long-running international conservation program for endangered native snails. Invasive predators had caused severe population collapses for these unique mollusks in their native islands. The Detroit Zoo has been breeding and caring for these snails since 1989. This ongoing effort has successfully returned over 17,000 snails to their natural habitat.

stories.summary: Australia’s endangered eastern quolls are showing signs of recovery after conservationists successfully bred captive-raised animals in Tasmania. One released female has six joeys in her pouch, offering hope for the species’ future. Eastern quolls disappeared from mainland Australia by the 1960s, largely due to habitat loss, disease, road accidents and predation.

stories.summary: Harvard neuroscientists have kept human brain organoids alive for over five years. These organoids matured and followed molecular patterns of human brain development. This breakthrough offers new avenues for studying brain biology and disease progression.

Initially in Hiroshima on August 6, he found himself in Nagasaki on August 9. stories.summary: Saturn's south pole reveals a giant, evolving 10-sided atmospheric wave. Hubble telescope observations trace subtle signs of this pattern back to 2023. Scientists have searched for a southern counterpart to the northern hexagon for decades. This discovery offers a rare chance to observe a major atmospheric pattern developing in real time.

The once-abandoned classrooms now serve as cozy guest rooms and inviting lounges, offering visitors a unique stay. This renovation breathes new life into a campus that had been closed for more than ten years, blending its historic charm with contemporary residential design.

stories.summary: A significant eight million dollar grant has facilitated the acquisition of one thousand six hundred eighty-eight acres of land for public use. This area safeguards a crucial wildlife corridor and an undammed river, enhancing conservation efforts for native fish habitats and seasonal wildlife migration. The Park Ranch, located near Markleeville, transitioned to Alpine County's management in August, with public access planned following the development of a thorough management strategy.

stories.title: UK mortgage approvals fall to lowest level since January 2024 as housing demand weakens
stories.summary: In July, UK mortgage approvals for home purchases hit a new low, highlighting a weakened demand in the housing market amid rising borrowing costs. Additionally, net mortgage borrowing plummeted, falling below the six-month average. While house prices saw slight annual growth, they decreased when adjusted for inflation. Conversely, unsecured consumer borrowing rose, revealing an increasing dependence on credit for everyday spending.

A fungus turns beetles into zombies and makes them die on flowers to infect the next generation
stories.summary: A fungus infects goldenrod soldier beetles, causing them to grip flowers before dying. After death, the fungus alters their bodies, raising wings between midnight and 7 am. These changes occur approximately fifteen to twenty-two hours after the beetles have expired. Infected beetles were found on frost aster and common boneset plants in Arkansas. Fungal outbreaks primarily occurred during autumn when adult beetles are present.

After their brother died, two siblings inherited 20.66 acres beside Zion National Park
stories.summary: In a heartfelt tribute to their late brother, two siblings have secured twenty-point-six-six acres of pristine land bordering Zion National Park through a conservation easement with the Virgin River Land Conservancy. This commitment ensures that the land remains untouched by commercial development, serving as a refuge for wildlife and offering breathtaking views of the iconic red sandstone formations, reinforcing their dedication to environmental stewardship.

Scientists removed 285,000 fish from a Wisconsin lake to help walleye, but perch rose 788% instead
stories.summary: Scientists removed about 285,000 centrarchid fish from Wisconsin’s McDermott Lake between 2018 and 2021 to see if reducing competition and predation could help walleye recover. The experiment sharply reduced several fish species and saw yellow perch numbers rise by about 788%. However, researchers found no detectable natural walleye recruitment, showing that removing centrarchids alone did not restore the lake’s walleye population.

Implementing Forecast-Informed Reservoir Operations may yield an additional 315,000 acre-feet each year, providing substantial economic leverage for both farmers and city dwellers. This innovative approach improves flood management and opens up opportunities for environmental flow, all while promoting conservation and aiding in infrastructure advancements.

The nonprofit Arthouse Houston plans to transform the building into an arts and film center. This new center will combine historic preservation with new cultural uses. The completed center is targeted for a grand opening in 2028.

This new system will lead to license suspension and cancellation for offenders. A pilot program for driver medical diagnosis was also launched. This initiative aims to improve road safety and worker well-being.

Many homeowners argue that the board has neglected crucial repairs for far too long and are now taking legal action, as well as initiating recall measures against the board. To cover legal expenses and assist neighbors in need, a GoFundMe has been launched.

stories.title: China's Xi tells Middle East to be ‘masters of their own destiny’ amid Iran war
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping urged Middle Eastern nations to resist external interference. He called for reshaping the region's security order during talks with Egypt's President Sisi. Both leaders agreed to deepen security and economic cooperation between their nations. China seeks to expand its influence and safeguard vital shipping routes. Egypt is diversifying its international partnerships by strengthening ties with Beijing.

stories.title: Princess Diana's godson Prince Philippos and Princess Nina welcome first child via surrogate
stories.summary: Princess Diana’s godson, Prince Philippos of Greece, and Princess Nina have welcomed their first child, a son named Kimon Thomas Konstantinos. Born via surrogate in the United States on July 27, the baby’s arrival was announced weeks later. His middle names honour Nina’s father Thomas Flohr and Philippos’ late father, Constantine II, Greece’s last king.

stories.summary: Wayne Wood, 64, who last won a cabbage in a 1977 meat draw, has struck it big with a £4 million Georgian mansion in Bath. stories.title: ‘Reprehensible act of vandalism’: India condemns demolition of century-old Hindu temple in Pakistan, seeks probe
stories.summary: India voiced deep concern over the reported destruction of a historic Hindu temple. The Ministry of External Affairs condemned the vandalism against the century-old place of worship. India noted the apparent apathy of authorities and failure to protect the temple. The government called for a prompt and transparent investigation into the incident. Pakistan must take remedial measures to restore the temple and ensure minority safety.

These fish have severely disrupted the balance of aquatic habitats. Teams are utilizing rotenone to treat streams connected to the Grand Ditch, focusing on fostering the endangered greenback cutthroat trout's habitat.

Protests continued demanding a clear roadmap for updating the NRC.

This makes passport applications more accessible and efficient for locals.

stories.summary: Former UFC star Rampage Jackson found himself in a fiery confrontation with his cameraman. The disagreement intensified as they exchanged words about mutual friends and associates, leading Jackson to chase after his cameraman, proclaiming he was terminated. Fortunately, the cameraman evaded any physical altercation. This dramatic encounter was live-streamed, giving viewers an inside look at the unexpected fallout.

stories.summary: A wooden fishing boat built in 1929 is nearing restoration on Martha’s Vineyard, almost a century after it was built beside the home of a family raising 13 children. Little Lady, the sole remaining wooden fishing dragger in New England, is set to undergo major repairs. The $1.5 million project still needs $630,000, while supporters hope to preserve the boat’s history and connection to the island’s fishing community.

The couple seeks to return to Florida after enjoying their time in New York.

Scientists released 45,000 cfs from Glen Canyon Dam for 8 days in 1996 to rebuild Grand Canyon sandbars
stories.summary: In 1996, a controlled flood was executed in the Grand Canyon to rejuvenate its natural river dynamics. Leveraging the Glen Canyon Dam, scientists released substantial volumes of water to transport sediment downstream, with the goal of restoring sandbars that had diminished due to the dam's existence. This initiative highlighted the potential of dam operations to contribute positively to ecological restoration, paving the way for future river management experiments.

stories.title: US detonated nuclear bomb to unlock gas; 213M cubic feet were produced, but the gas was radioactive
stories.summary: In 1967, the US detonated a 29-kiloton nuclear device 4,227 feet underground in New Mexico to boost natural gas production. Five tests produced 213 million cubic feet of gas, but it contained measurable radioactivity. The experiment was later ended, the site cleaned up, and radioactive contamination remains underground in the blast zone.

America's Gulf allies are urging the White House to de-escalate the conflict.

This incident sheds light on the ongoing struggles faced by disabled children living in rural communities.

Nearly 2,000-year-old vessel with two snake heads found at Roman villa in Spain
stories.summary: A Roman villa in Spain yielded fragments of a unique two-headed serpent vessel. This artifact suggests the private worship of the god Sabazios spread widely. Laboratory tests indicate the vessel likely originated from Roman Africa. Evidence for this cult on the Iberian Peninsula is generally scarce. The find highlights the quiet reach of ancient religious practices into rural areas.

stories.summary: More than 6,100 Ebola cases and 3,000 deaths are recorded in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Weak surveillance and insecurity hinder efforts to contain the nation's worst-ever epidemic. Schools have reopened amid concerns about potential transmission within classrooms. No approved vaccine exists for the Bundibugyo species, though some are in development. Britain has pledged over fifty million pounds to support outbreak containment efforts.

Salian's father alleged murder and sought a thorough investigation into the matter. The CBI will record statements and register an FIR for further proceedings. This development follows years of the father pursuing justice for his daughter.

12 artificial reefs created in 1998 boosted local fish numbers and species richness off Miami Beach
stories.summary: A 2002 study examined 12 artificial reefs built off Miami Beach using limestone boulders, concrete-gravel aggregate and concrete mixed with waste tyre chips. Divers surveyed the reefs every two months from October 1998 to February 2001, recording fish species, numbers and sizes, along with spiny lobsters. They counted 97,826 fish from 146 species. The researchers found no significant difference in fish abundance, biomass or species richness between the three reef materials. However, comparisons before and after deployment showed that the artificial reefs increased local fish abundance and species richness.

stories.title: Carmel River Free Project: Eastwoods’ ranch anchors $57m restoration; homes face lower flood risks
stories.summary: Clint Eastwood's previous artichoke farm is now being transformed into a significant wetland restoration initiative. This remarkable project aims to bolster flood protection for the surrounding communities. With the Eastwoods' generous donation, the area will see restoration of essential riparian and wetland ecosystems, fostering wildlife and promoting a more resilient river system. This change converts agricultural land into vital open space, enhancing both safety and community health.

stories.title: An Iowa priest vowed to build a shrine if he survived pneumonia; after recovering, he spent 42 years using over 100 train carloads of stone to create it
stories.summary: The Grotto of the Redemption in West Bend, Iowa, owes its existence to a young seminarian's promise made during his illness. Initiated by Father Dobberstein, the monumental structure took an astonishing 42 years to complete. Utilizing a variety of geological elements, over 100 train carloads of stones were involved in its construction, making it a celebrated historic landmark and one of the largest man-made grottos globally.

stories.title: 'It’s not 19th century': Kerala CM Satheesan slams cleric over 'women should stay home' remark
stories.summary: Kerala chief minister VD Satheesan rejected cleric Kanthapuram AP Aboobacker Musliyar's call for restricting women's public participation. Satheesan asserted that women must join the mainstream, stating that such views are unsuitable for developing Kerala. Labour Minister Bindu Krishna also criticised the cleric's remarks, calling them regressive for women's rights. Aboobacker defended directives limiting women's presence at religious events, citing Quranic interpretations.

stories.title: Five Indiana engineering students built a 12-hour wearable that helps visually impaired users detect obstacles beyond a cane or guide dog
stories.summary: Rose-Hulman students have developed a remarkable wearable device tailored for visually impaired individuals. This innovative headgear employs advanced sensors to identify surrounding obstacles, providing users with haptic feedback. With a remarkable twelve-hour battery life on a single charge, this device empowers users with greater independence. The project's goal is to enhance the day-to-day experiences of those with vision impairments.

Himachal under monsoon fury: 259 dead, 150 roads cut off, losses cross Rs 1,200 crore in last 64 days
stories.summary: Over the past 64 days, relentless monsoon rains have devastated Himachal Pradesh, resulting in the tragic loss of 259 lives and economic damages exceeding Rs 1,200 crore. The aftermath includes 150 roads still blocked, significantly hindering connectivity. Essential services such as power and water are disrupted in various districts, but restoration efforts are actively being pursued to bring relief and reopen crucial routes.

In 1940, Nazis seized a painting from a Jewish collector in Vienna; 86 years later, Austria returned it to his heir in Minnesota
stories.summary: In a poignant gesture, an Austrian diplomat returned a stolen miniature painting to Jackie Sondell, heir to Eduard Epstein, a victim of Nazi persecution. Confiscated from Epstein's collection during his imprisonment, the artwork symbolizes Austria's acknowledgment of its historical obligations and a step towards healing. The Austrian government diligently traced Sondell and her brother to restore this cherished piece of family history.

stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has served a notice to the Delhi police regarding the appeal filed by Tahir Hussain, who was found guilty of the murder of IB officer Ankit Sharma during the riots of 2020. Hussain, along with four others, received a life sentence, but he disputes the conviction, claiming the investigation was flawed and biased against him. The appeal is scheduled for a hearing on December 2.

stories.summary: New England's creative solution to invasive green crabs involves incorporating them into the local diet and economy. Fishermen now target these soft-shelled crabs, which are gaining popularity and higher prices. Emerging markets for green crab products, including pet snacks and whiskey infusions, aim to counteract the harmful effects of this invasive species while boosting the economy.

stories.title: Former British diplomat to Pakistan is running a global marathon to help educate 25.2 million children in the country
stories.summary: Former diplomat Mike Nithavrianakis is undertaking marathons to raise funds for The Citizens Foundation in Pakistan, aiming to secure one million dollars to enhance educational opportunities. This crucial support is set to benefit around six thousand students for an entire academic year. Having already gathered more than $350,000, he has funded the establishment of a new campus. His drive originates from observing educational inequalities during his time in diplomacy.

A woman, convinced she was sending $30,000 for cookbooks, exhibited signs of distress that caught the staff's attention. Authorities were called in, revealing the cash and halting its shipment. The intervention not only saved her funds but also the shipping costs, allowing her to breathe a sigh of relief.

stories.summary: In Northeast India, urbanization and climate change are driving a rise in vector-borne illnesses. There has been a significant uptick in dengue infections, and chikungunya is also on the rise. While malaria's prevalence is lessening at a national level, Japanese encephalitis continues to pose risks. The recommendation is for implementing innovative surveillance methods and targeted intervention measures, particularly to fill information voids affecting diverse populations.

Known for his leadership in advocating a referendum on Hong Kong's sovereignty, Wong is currently incarcerated for a previous national security offence. The East Bay Regional Park District would manage the site after its acquisition. Remaining funds are being sought from public and philanthropic sources. Public planning and phased construction will occur after the land purchase.

stories.title: Heart ablation cuts irregular beats, but may not make patients feel better
stories.summary: A recent study revealed that catheter ablation effectively diminishes abnormal heart rhythms in patients. Nonetheless, there was no notable enhancement in quality of life compared to those undergoing a sham procedure. Participants from both groups experienced considerable improvements after a six-month follow-up, indicating that patient expectations may shape their perceived benefits. Researchers urge careful consideration when suggesting this procedure for improving overall quality of life.

Retired in 1953, the aircraft was bought by a Florida owner who dismantled and packed it into boxes, carrying the parts through three moves over 50 years. Rediscovered in 2002, it was later restored by RARE Aircraft and returned to airworthy condition before being displayed at the Historic Flight Foundation.

Reddy pointed out the considerable debt left by the prior government, alongside the excessive public spending on KCR's security measures. He urged KCR to participate in the next assembly session to address these pressing issues.

stories.title: 'Purification' row: Congress protests FIR against Rahul Gandhi, attacks BJP's 'casteist' behaviour
Vance says Trump’s dramatic Kharg Island post was meant as a signal to Iran
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance stated Donald Trump's social media post conveyed a message to Iran. American military officials confirmed no strikes occurred on Kharg Island overnight. An Iranian official dismissed Trump's post as laughable and not credible. US forces did attack two Iranian launchers on Larak Island recently. These developments renew security concerns in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Punjab groundwater crisis shows signs of reversal, AAP cites rise in canal-water use
A Kohl’s closed in 2016 and sat vacant for nearly a decade; $28 million later...
stories.summary: An abandoned Kohl's store in Roswell, Georgia, has been redeveloped into a large church. This $28 million project created an 80,000-square-foot multi-use event venue. Eagles Nest Church purchased the site and completed the extensive renovations. The new facility will host worship services and various community events starting September 2026. Future development plans include additional retail and family-focused businesses on the property.

stories.title: Laurene Powell Jobs went from Wall Street bond trader to major philanthropist
Social activist Anna Hazare admitted to hospital in Mumbai

'I wish him nothing but suffering': Nikitha Godishala's friend knew murder accused Arjun Sharma but didn't think he was capable of this crime
1,800 volunteers took turns pulling a 400-ton Japanese castle with ropes and...
stories.summary: In a remarkable achievement, thousands of volunteers in Japan successfully relocated a historic castle keep using age-old techniques. This monumental task represents a critical advancement in a decade-long restoration initiative. The keep has been repositioned closer to its original stone foundation, revealing archaeological treasures like ancient drainage systems and remnants of earlier walls. Visitors can anticipate the keep's full reopening by 2033.

stories.title: Auchtertool village of 200 homes faces huge data centre plan, sparking 1,600 objections
stories.summary: Residents of Auchtertool, Fife, are fighting plans for the world’s second-largest data centre, which would cover more than 100 football pitches beside their 200-home village. More than 1,600 objections have been lodged, while locals fear the vast development could transform their quiet rural community and bring concerns over noise, heat, flooding and wildlife.

stories.title: A New Jersey town agreed to spend $13.4 million to preserve 50 acres once eyed for dense housing
stories.summary: In an impactful move, Denville Township has acquired seventeen acres dedicated to an essential land preservation effort, shielding around fifty acres from encroaching residential developments. This initiative also includes a plan to add thirty-three more acres by October 2026, ultimately creating a welcoming public park and safeguarded natural area to maintain Denville's unique heritage and ecology for future generations to enjoy.

stories.title: Michigan's AQI hit 616 as Ontario wildfire smoke crossed into the US
‘Uncertainties’ rising: Xi calls for stronger cooperation in meeting with Putin
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping met at the SCO summit. They discussed strengthening bilateral ties and international regional issues. Cooperation in artificial intelligence and digital innovation was also a key topic. Russia proposed making the bilateral visa-free regime permanent for Chinese citizens. The leaders also touched upon the Ukraine conflict during their talks.

PM Modi-Putin hit the road together again, share car ride after bilateral talks in Bishkek

Built in 1928, this $5.8M Dallas castle is now going to auction
stories.summary: The Château des Grotteaux mansion is set for auction after nearly a year on the market, with bids starting at around two million dollars—significantly lower than its original asking price. This enchanting Dallas property features modern updates while maintaining its fairy-tale charm. The auction will conclude on September twenty-ninth, targeting buyers who cherish distinctiveness over mere historical value.

stories.title: New visa, Green Card rules coming into effect from September 2026: Is the 75-country ban lifted?
Nepal tragedy: Owners missing, dog refuses to leave flood-hit Trishuli home
stories.summary: A black-and-white dog remains at the site of four homes destroyed by a flood. He refuses to leave the muddy patch where his home once stood. Rescue workers and JCBs clear debris around the steadfast canine. Volunteers offer food and water, which he accepts quietly when alone. Displaced residents understand his loyalty to his former territory.

stories.title: Indian-origin taxi driver Gurmeet Singh stripped of US citizenship 15 years after rape conviction
'Swachh Bharat an endeavour to reduce untouchability': Shaina NC targets Rahul Gandhi
A Tennessee man left a late-1700s house and about $500,000 to local government for a park
stories.summary: A historic home in Tennessee, along with $500,000, has been returned to its rightful family after local officials failed to fulfill the promise of establishing a public park as per the will. After a decade of inactivity, the descendant will take charge of crucial repairs and preservation efforts for the old house, shedding light on the complexities of municipal management involving donated heritage properties.

stories.title: Manipur census deferred ahead of September 1 house-listing exercise

Afghan general who led last-ditch effort to stop Taliban takeover now drives Uber in Washington
Vanished Texas bird island is back, with 2,500 pairs of birds
stories.summary: After years of erosion and extreme weather, Dickinson Bay's lost islands have seen a remarkable revival. Spearheaded by the Galveston Bay Foundation and U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, habitat restoration efforts have successfully created new nesting habitats for over 2,500 pairs of waterbirds. This revitalization not only boosts local biodiversity but also creates job opportunities and enhances economic activity through recreational fishing and improved oyster reefs.

stories.title: Scientists reconstruct face of 'Conquest Man,' skeleton from 1079 burial
stories.summary: Buried around 1079, Conquest Man's identity has been revealed through scientific analysis. His ancestry offers insights into his journey across Europe, showcasing a unique blend of Scandinavian artifacts with those linked to a Norman church. This finding complicates the simplistic Saxon versus Norman narrative, emphasizing resilience and adaptability in the aftermath of the Norman Conquest.

stories.title: 'Vishwaguru, not a Mahashakti': RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat highlights India's legacy of refuge, global service in Toronto
Evening news wrap: India rejects court ruling on IWT; PM Modi meets Iran President & more
stories.summary: India rejected the Indus Water Treaty court ruling, stating the agreement remains in abeyance. Prime Minister Modi met Iran’s President Pezeshkian to discuss trade and West Asia peace. India’s GDP grew 7.8% in the first quarter of FY27, exceeding RBI estimates. A stranger’s warning helped over 370 Nepal schoolchildren escape a devastating flood. Tensions grew between Congress and TVK over the 2029 prime ministerial candidate.

stories.title: PM Modi's jackets, Rahul's shirts, Mamata's sarees: How leaders use fashion for political messaging

'No jurisdiction': India rejects 'illegal' Court of Arbitration's Indus Waters Treaty award
IISc sets up quantum computing hub under National Quantum Mission
stories.summary: IISc has launched a not-for-profit company to advance India's quantum computing potential. This new entity will serve as a thematic hub under the National Quantum Mission. It aims to unite researchers, industry, and startups for indigenous technology development. Shared facilities will support the creation and testing of quantum devices. The initiative seeks to build a skilled workforce and reduce foreign technology dependence.

stories.title: Delhi gangrape on moving bus: Women Commission chairperson says culprits ‘must get punishment’
'Will continue to support all efforts for lasting peace': PM Modi meets Iranian Prez
Navy chief Admiral Swaminathan flags evolving threats, rising maritime contestation
stories.summary: Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, the Navy chief, emphasized the growing contestation in the maritime domain, highlighting a critical phase of strategic evolution and emerging threats. His remarks followed the induction of INS Nipun, a deep-sea diving vessel capable of operating at depths of 300 meters. This advanced ship is designed not only for submarine rescues but also excels in humanitarian missions and disaster relief efforts.

stories.title: Rahul or Vijay for PM? Congress-TVK rift talk grows after MLA’s seat shift
First exam reforms, now 'school thik karo' campaign: How CJP is changing the discourse of politics
stories.summary: Student protests for improved school conditions have shifted from cities to villages across India. The Cockroach Janata Party's campaign exposed poor government school infrastructure in several states. State governments responded with new regulations and accelerated development projects. Political parties are now focusing on youth outreach and educational issues. This movement highlights youth as potential game-changers in electoral politics.

Hungry Bears Increasingly Enter Towns: Drought pushes them into homes; experts fear rising lethal encounters
stories.summary: Amidst a severe drought, bears are encroaching on human habitats across the American West, with Colorado reporting over 7,000 sightings this year alone—a new high. These foraging bears can be spotted rummaging through homes, stores, and neighborhoods for food. As conservation efforts intertwine with urban development, wildlife officials emphasize the need for residents to secure food sources and refrain from feeding these hungry animals.

stories.title: UAE, Egypt coordinate over Banque Misr bank after US Treasury notice on Iran links, dollar curbs
China’s solar panels reduced young sea cucumbers’ inactivity by 12 days
stories.summary: Solar panels placed over sea cucumber ponds in China have effectively lowered water temperatures, leading to a significant reduction in the summer dormancy period for young sea cucumbers by twelve days. Alongside this, the panels changed the distribution of plankton and minimized organic material in the pond sediments. These insights highlight the potential of aquavoltaics to enhance aquaculture practices while promoting sustainable energy solutions.

stories.title: Texas tested a highway built with 4.5 tons of recycled plastic in 2025
He worked as the green ranger in 'Power Rangers', then used the experience to rob 43 homes as the 'Spider-Man thief'
stories.summary: After suffering an injury, Yasutomo Ihara—a former Green Ranger stunt performer—found himself lured into a life of crime. He became notorious for orchestrating multiple burglaries across Japan, employing his unique skills. Authorities arrested Ihara in 2014, discovering he had stolen items worth around seventy-seven thousand dollars. Consequently, he was sentenced to five years in prison for these offenses.

stories.title: Muslim cleric's 'women should remain confined within their homes' draws Kerala minister's ire
Melinda Gates doubles Olivia Rodrigo's festival fund to $20M: Where will it go?
stories.summary: Olivia Rodrigo's first-ever Daisy Chain Fields Festival has come to a triumphant end, bringing in significant funding to aid women-focused initiatives. This remarkable event showcased a variety of female performers who united for a common purpose. Rodrigo revealed plans to donate a large sum to ten women-centered charities, with Melinda French Gates promising to match the total amount, reinforcing the festival's mission to empower women and girls around the globe.

stories.title: San Antonio storm cuts power and damages homes, but barber moves outside and keeps working
stories.summary: A powerful storm hit San Antonio’s West Side, knocking down trees, damaging homes and leaving more than 112,000 customers without power at its peak. As residents cleaned up and struggled with the heat, Misfit barbershop owner Juan Martinez moved his barber chair outside and continued serving customers despite the power outage.

stories.title: Osaka residents ate dozens of species in the 1600s, evidence stayed in teeth
stories.summary: Teeth unearthed in Osaka have unveiled a diverse dietary landscape of commoners, revealing that their dental calculus held traces of proteins from fish, mammals, and plants. This discovery suggests that they enjoyed access to a variety of foods, including terrestrial meats, thanks to Osaka's strategic position as a distribution center. This research provides a rare window into the food culture and accessibility of premodern Japan.

stories.title: 'Venezuela will be reborn': Maduro shares first photos from US prison since capture
Sadhguru pledges Rs 1 crore for Nepal flood relief, seeks joint Himalayan response
PM Modi pays floral tribute to Mahatma Gandhi in Bishkek, interacts with Indian diaspora
Did US military warn Hegseth over Iran war strain before latest escalation? What report claims
Chimpanzees keep throwing rocks at same trees for a decade, scientists probe why
stories.summary: In an intriguing study, scientists are examining the unusual habit of chimpanzees who consistently throw stones at designated trees. This behaviour, predominantly seen in adult males accompanied by their loud vocalisations, might indicate a method of communication or territorial assertion. The sustained use of these locations hints at a learned tradition being handed down over generations, shedding light on both primate culture and possible connections to human evolution.

stories.title: SC dismisses plea seeking mandatory ethanol content disclosure at petrol pumps, fuel bills
Meet Kim Ji-on, a 12-year-old South Korean student who invented a life-saving device that helps people escape deadly fires
stories.summary: In a remarkable feat of innovation, young inventor Kim Ji-on from South Korea has developed a groundbreaking fire-escape breathing phone grip. This exceptional device features filters designed to absorb toxic gases and trap harmful particles, granting users vital time to escape during a fire emergency. Kim's invention recently garnered a national award, and she intends to generously donate her prize money to aid those in developing nations.

Alaska eliminates invasive pike and restocks lake with 6,836 Arctic char
India ‘vishwaguru’ through service, not pursuit of superpower status: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat in Toronto
'Country Babur came from': Owaisi takes dig at PM Modi's Uzbek honour
Meet the Texas students transforming toxic Martian soil for future astronauts
No roofs, no toilets, no teachers: TOI check finds minuses in Rajasthan govt schools
stories.summary: TOI reporters visited govt schools in 6 Rajasthan districts after the CJP row. The findings show how basic govt schooling has collapsed in pockets of the state, from the coaching capital of Kota to desert villages and Jhalawar’s tragedy-hit Piplodi.

stories.title: Meet the students who built DiveGuard, a low-cost underwater messaging system
stories.summary: A group of Chinese students has created DiveGuard, an affordable system designed for underwater communication. By utilizing acoustic signals, this innovative technology allows divers to send concise text messages, thereby enhancing safety and teamwork in aquatic environments. DiveGuard was recognized as a finalist in the prestigious 2026 Conrad Challenge and offers a reliable communication alternative where traditional networks are unavailable.

stories.title: Nepal survivors return to ruins to salvage memories
Ahead of SCO, Uzbekistan joins India in condemning cross-border terrorism
stories.summary: Uzbekistan and India have elevated their relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership. Both nations unequivocally condemned terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, in a joint statement. This marks a significant diplomatic alignment on regional security dynamics and counter-terrorism efforts. Leaders called for concerted actions against terrorist entities and disrupting financing networks. They stressed holding perpetrators and their backers accountable for their actions.

stories.title: US breaks weeks-long Iran strike lull by targeting Larak island; Tehran hits American bases in Middle East
stories.summary: In a sudden escalation, US forces targeted Iranian rocket launchers near Larak Island, disturbing an ongoing quiet period. Iran retaliated, showcasing missiles aimed at Jordan, where Jordanian forces successfully intercepted eight threats early Monday. Meanwhile, the US military noted Iranian efforts to deploy sea mines in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, contributing to a rise in oil prices as crude values surged after the military action.

Modi lauds Bengali actor ahead of birth centenary
File FIR against those who did 'purification': Priyanka to PM Modi
stories.summary: Priyanka Gandhi Vadra has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to order an FIR. This appeal follows an alleged "purification" of a rally venue in Haldwani. Rahul Gandhi previously alleged BJP-RSS elements were responsible for the incident. The Congress leader stated the act violated the Constitution and SC/ST Act. She questioned the government's inaction over the alleged crime.

stories.title: Create social media content against drug menace: PM to youth
stories.summary: In a call to action, Prime Minister Modi urged young Indians to use social media in innovative ways to fight against drug addiction. He also celebrated the success of the PM SVANidhi scheme in promoting women's economic empowerment, with approximately 35 lakh women benefiting from it to strengthen their businesses.

stories.title: Constitutional norm for jurist as SC judge unmet: Justice Bhuyan
A Norwegian farmer uncovered a Viking ship buried with two women
CJP netas not saints ... nothing wrong in having political ambitions: Wangchuk
stories.summary: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk believes organizers of the Cockroach Janta Party movement have political ambitions. He stated that such aspirations are normal and not objectionable if the platform remains non-party. Wangchuk described the organizers as well-meaning and skilled individuals with no current indications of corruption. He advised them to maintain the CJP as a neutral pressure group for broader support.

stories.title: NEET-PG 2026 smooth; retest for 2.4k Jaipur kids hit by glitch
stories.summary: The NEET-PG 2026 examination faced disruption due to a power failure at two Jaipur centres. A retest is scheduled for September 5 for 2,445 affected candidates. A three-member committee will investigate the internal power supply problem. The nationwide examination was conducted with extensive security measures and real-time monitoring. NBEMS expressed regret for the inconvenience caused to the candidates.

stories.title: PM Modi likely to hold bilateral talks with Iranian president
Right to question not defiance, every dissent not a threat: SC judge
stories.summary: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan stressed that governments must listen to citizens and allow dissent. He stated that questioning is an essential expression of citizenship and liberty in democracies. Universities should foster free thinking and encourage students to ask difficult questions. Intolerance undermines the constitutional framework when disagreement is silenced or punished. A democracy's maturity is shown by its response to unpopular or inconvenient opinions.

stories.title: Modi in Tashkent: India, Uzbekistan target long-tern uranium pact, ramp up trade & defence ties
stories.summary: In a significant diplomatic move, India and Uzbekistan have enhanced their engagement to a comprehensive strategic partnership. They have ambitious plans for trade, aiming for a target of five billion dollars each year. The nations also formalized an agreement for uranium supply and created a foreign minister-level coordination council while signing eleven memorandums of understanding across diverse fields like mining and education.

stories.title: Sneako Claims Suspect Arrested: Alleges livestream attacker held; police confirmation pending
stories.summary: Streamer Sneako announced his attacker's arrest for aggravated assault. This news arrived shortly after he received a significant IRS refund. The original assault occurred during a livestream in April 2026. Police had been investigating the incident where Sneako was pepper-sprayed. Fellow streamer Ac7ionMann offered to assist the arrested individual with legal costs.

stories.title: For every Rs 100 laundered, only Re 1 recovered by authorities: CJI
Diabetes impacts men, women differently: Study
stories.summary: Type 2 diabetes affects men and women with different health risks. Women face greater mental health challenges after diagnosis, while men experience more heart and kidney issues. Hypertension is a common complication for both sexes following diabetes. People developing mental health conditions after diabetes tend to die earlier. The study suggests sex-specific diabetes care and monitoring are needed.

stories.title: Colorado has logged more than 7,000 bear sightings in 2026, topping its previous full-year record
stories.summary: In recent months, severe drought conditions in the American West have driven malnourished bears into urban areas in search of food. With natural vegetation dwindling, bears have turned to human settlements, often scavenging through trash cans. These encounters, which typically start with easily preventable issues like unsecured rubbish bins or unattended bird feeders, are becoming more frequent as the population grows in the region.

stories.title: NHAI mandates end-to-end AI-MC deployment for projects over 20 km in length
Manhunt underway in Switzerland after rave shooting; police say terrorism possible motive
Workers restoring a medieval English house found 800 years of hidden history, including...
stories.summary: A conservation project at Dunstable's Priory House has revealed eight centuries of hidden history. Nationally important wall paintings and sealed medieval doorways were discovered during the extensive restoration. Scientific tests confirm the building's early 13th-century origins as part of Dunstable Priory. Protective symbols, known as witch marks, were carved into old timber and stonework. The building is expected to reopen as a community heritage hub in early 2027.

stories.title: A Phoenix concert promoter spent 50 years collecting music history; he is now selling more than...
stories.summary: Danny Zelisko is auctioning his remarkable collection of music memorabilia online, boasting over two thousand treasures amassed from five decades of live performances. The revenue from these sales will benefit The Joy Bus charity, which provides nourishing meals to homebound cancer patients, ensuring they receive essential nutrition and care during their tough treatments.

He died at 23 after fighting in the Korean War; nearly 74 years later Estrada’s family is still...
stories.summary: Sergeant Willie Estrada's family is urging for the highest military accolade, the Medal of Honor, in remembrance of his courageous sacrifice during the Korean War. Strikingly, he lost his life defending his tank crew near Bongowol, North Korea, in 1952. Honored posthumously with the Distinguished Service Cross, his loved ones are diligently working with legislators to officially document his remarkable legacy and heroism.

Meet Marcus Klepacki, 19-year-old musician who learned to play an acoustic drum kit with one arm
stories.summary: Marcus Klepacki, a talented musician from Phoenix, is set to perform with Third Man Factor, captivating audiences with his remarkable drumming skills—even more impressive as he plays a traditional acoustic drum kit with one arm. Having battled severe health issues like scoliosis and leukemia in his youth, he found his passion for music at Alice Cooper's Solid Rock Teen Centers, crafting a sound reminiscent of 1990s alternative rock and grunge.

stories.title: IISc eco-friendly foam moves from lab to market; TOI story drew industry
"Lucknow has BrahMos, smart roads and clean Gomti river": CM Yogi highlights city's transformation
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday highlighted Lucknow's transformation into a city combining modern infrastructure and defence technologies with its cultural heritage, saying the state government is working to fully clean the Gomti River by the end of this year.

stories.title: Rare manatees spotted along Texas coast prompt warnings for boaters
"PM Modi's call will raise awareness among youth against drug abuse": Uttarakhand CM Dhami tunes into 137th edition of 'Mann Ki Baat'
stories.summary: The Chief Minister said that the Prime Minister, through 'Mann Ki Baat', had urged the youth to stay away from drugs and turn the resolve of a 'Drug-Free Youth, Developed India' into a mass movement.

stories.title: British woman fatally stabbed at railway station in southern Germany; one arrested
A Florida wife grew suspicious of her husband’s phone call; deputies found him in...
stories.summary: In a swift response, Nassau County deputies saved a resident from losing fourteen thousand dollars to a group of scammers who were pushing him to buy gift cards under a tight two-hour deadline. This event signals an alarming increase in reported fraud cases locally. Authorities remind the public that no reputable entity should ever request immediate payments via gift cards or cryptocurrency. Always verify suspicious calls by contacting official channels.

Maine students rebuild dunes washed away by 2024 storms, plant 20,000 grass stalks along the beach
stories.summary: After storms washed away dunes along Maine’s coast in 2024, University of New England students and local volunteers returned to Biddeford Pool in 2026 for a second restoration effort. They planted 20,000 dune-grass stalks across 20,000 square feet, while researchers studied how grass spacing, wind and waves affect dune recovery.

stories.title: Nepal floods: Stranger ran past school screaming ‘Run, water’. It saved 370 kids, teachers
stories.summary: An unidentified man's warning saved over 370 pupils and teachers from a massive flood. Students and staff scrambled to a forested hill as floodwaters surged rapidly. Communications were disrupted, making it difficult to account for all students after the event. One father tragically perished while attempting to reach the school for his son. The school continues efforts to trace pupils and reunite them with their families.

stories.title: 'BJP thinks it is bigger than RSS, it should listen to Mohan Bhagwat': CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke
‘Gift from Venezuela’: Trump says oil deal will help refill US strategic reserve
stories.summary: US President Trump announced a deal to secure Venezuelan oil for the US reserve. This oil will be used to refill the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The agreement involves developing untapped oil fields in Venezuela. Significant investment is needed before Venezuelan production can increase. The immediate impact on US fuel prices remains unclear.

West Texas rancher rejected wind turbines twice; royalties now help keep his family ranch running
stories.summary: A fifth-generation West Texas rancher twice rejected wind turbines on his family property before agreeing to host seven turbines from the Cactus Flats wind project. Since 2019, the regular wind income has helped cover ranching costs, from livestock feed and workers to fences and repairs. The project also helped him invest in a community site in Menard, showing how wind royalties can support traditional ranching and rural development.

stories.title: In 1966, Marlon Brando bought a private Polynesian atoll; it is now a wildlife sanctuary
stories.summary: Marlon Brando's private atoll now serves as a crucial marine conservation site. Thousands of green sea turtle hatchlings have been recorded after decades of protection efforts. Habitat restoration and invasive species removal significantly aided this environmental transformation. Eco-tourism at The Brando luxury resort helps fund ongoing scientific research and conservation initiatives. While nesting beaches are safe, turtles face dangers from fishing and plastic pollution at sea.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: India, Uzbekistan elevate ties to Comprehensive Strategic Partnership; Nasa's Roman Space Telescope launches to explore dark universe & more
stories.summary: India and Uzbekistan have elevated their relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. Seven unidentified bodies were recovered from the Gandak river following devastating floods in Nepal. Iran's Supreme Leader urged Gulf rulers to identify and confront their real enemy. Himachal Pradesh is developing early warning systems for four high-risk glacial lakes. Nasa's Roman Space Telescope has launched to study the dark universe.

stories.title: 'Gud khaye, gulgule se parhez': Tejashwi targets BJP-RSS amid Jitan Ram Manjhi-Chirag Paswan reservation spat
In 2021, Amazon shut US rooftop solar after six incidents at 47 sites; audit found 259 issues
stories.summary: Amazon shut down rooftop solar systems at all 47 of its North American sites in 2021 after six facilities reported fires or arc flash incidents. A later audit found one critical and 259 significant issues across its global solar portfolio, including mismatched connectors, improper installation, poor wire management and water intrusion in inverters.

stories.title: In 1967, Guy Savy bought a Seychelles island; after restoring nesting habitat, its sooty tern colony...
stories.summary: Once threatened by severe ecological decline, Bird Island has transformed into a remarkable conservation achievement. Over decades of exploitation and farming, the island's environment was heavily damaged. However, when Guy Savy and partners took over in 1967, they began restoration and promoted eco-tourism. This initiative has led to a major recovery in seabird numbers, proving that long-term conservation can revitalize damaged ecosystems.

stories.title: ‘Violation of High Court order won't be tolerated’: Agnimitra Paul reacts after FIR against Mamata Banerjee
stories.summary: An FIR was filed against Mamata Banerjee for allegedly violating a court order. The case stems from a Trinamool Chhatra Parishad program held on August 28. Police allege the program exceeded permitted timings and caused disruptions. Ministers criticized Banerjee for disrespecting constitutional institutions and the judiciary. The investigation will examine the roles of all individuals involved.

stories.title: US mother pleads guilty to killing 11-month-old son to keep him from his father, says it was 'worth it'
Iowa plant shreds Wind Turbine blades into fibres and powders for concrete, mortar and asphalt
stories.summary: Regen Fiber has opened a wind turbine blade recycling facility in Fairfax, Iowa, using an all-mechanical process that avoids heat and chemicals. The plant shreds old blades into fibres and additives for use in concrete, mortar and asphalt. It expects to process more than 30,000 tons of blades each year.

stories.title: In 2019, a YouTuber was challenged to plant millions of trees, today his campaign has planted 25 million worldwide
stories.summary: MrBeast, the popular YouTuber, launched an ambitious initiative known as #TeamTrees. This groundbreaking campaign garnered viral attention, resulting in the planting of millions of trees funded by generous online donations. Partnering with various influencers and environmental organizations, it has successfully restored vast tracts of land and sequestered significant amounts of carbon. His innovative use of social media demonstrates how digital platforms can drive meaningful charitable endeavors.

stories.title: 'Uzbekistan is at heart of Central Asia': PM Modi announces new roadmap, $5 billion trade target - top quotes
In 2013, Florida’s Tortuga Music Festival began restoring dunes with sea oats; 13 years later...
stories.summary: For over thirteen years, music enthusiasts and dedicated volunteers have joined forces to rejuvenate the dunes at Fort Lauderdale Beach, a tradition that began alongside the Tortuga Music Festival in 2013. By planting resilient sea oats, they bolster coastal defenses against storm surges and erosion, while also creating essential nesting grounds for sea turtles. This inspiring initiative exemplifies how large-scale public events can embrace sustainability.

stories.title: Astronomers hear a mysterious cosmic hum linked to strange dark stars from 13 billion years ago
stories.summary: Astronomers may have found a new way to investigate the Universe's first supermassive black holes. A faint gravitational-wave hum detected through pulsars could contain clues about ancient objects. Hypothetical Dark Stars, powered partly by dark matter, could have left black-hole descendants. These ancient black-hole seeds could grow and merge, producing part of the gravitational-wave background.

stories.title: Northern spotted owl once became a symbol of America’s logging wars; now scientists say it is already functionally extinct
stories.summary: The northern spotted owl, once a revered icon of environmental activism, faces dire circumstances as it becomes functionally extinct in numerous regions. A recent study indicates a severe decline in its populations throughout their historical habitat. Factors such as habitat destruction and rampant wildfires have severely impacted the species over the years, while the encroaching barred owl emerges as a formidable threat.

stories.title: 'We never thought they were Muslims': Mohan Bhagwat recalls 1996 Charkhi Dadri mid-air collision
stories.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat recalled the Charkhi Dadri air disaster while speaking in New York. He highlighted RSS volunteers' immediate humanitarian aid to victims of the 1996 mid-air collision. Bhagwat stated volunteers served injured and deceased without considering their religious identity. He emphasized RSS's philosophy of selfless service and not seeking publicity for its actions. The organization's work aims to foster unity and social change through local initiatives.

stories.title: India, Uzbekistan seal long-term uranium supply deal during PM Modi visit
‘Gang’s name similar to someone in UP’: Akhilesh Yadav’s swipe at Yogi Adityanath over Ankit Balyan murder
Salary deductions for Odisha government employees defaulting on alimony
stories.summary: Odisha government will now deduct alimony directly from employee salaries. This order ensures timely financial support for estranged wives and children. Repeated complaints prompted the chief minister to take this stern stance. Court orders will now be enforced through automated salary deductions. This initiative aims to uphold judicial authority and ease family distress.

stories.title: Indian-origin US politician Anand Shah pleads guilty in illegal gambling case; earned $900,000, used it to fund campaign
SC to hear plea tomorrow against anonymous cash donations to political parties
‘If PM Modi respects Constitution, ensure FIR’: Priyanka Gandhi on Kharge stage ‘shuddhikaran’ row
Chicago physicist’s 20-year-old quantum imaging theory gets experimental proof using superconductors
stories.summary: The University of Illinois Chicago’s Dirk Morr proposed a way to create high-resolution quantum images using superconductors two decades ago. A new experiment by researchers in Germany, supported by Morr’s theoretical model, has now produced quantum imaging similar to what he predicted, providing experimental confirmation of his earlier work.

stories.title: In the 1940s, Nevada’s six-week divorce law turned a 1,627-acre ranch into a refuge for women seeking quick divorces; now it is becoming the state’s 28th park
stories.summary: Transforming from a historic divorce haven into a state park, Nevada's Lower Carson Ranch now spans 1,627 acres alongside the Carson River, preserving crucial wildlife habitats. This transition marks the end of 155 years of private ownership, officially now under Nevada State Parks. While development for future public use is underway and access is limited, the community is actively participating in selecting a new name for the park.

stories.title: Nepal seeks to advance electricity import arrangement due to floods
stories.summary: Nepal has requested advance approvals to import electricity from India starting September 2026. This request stems from generation deficits caused by recent flash floods in Nepal. India will provide any additional electricity that Nepal may need during this period. Major cross-border transmission lines remain operational and unaffected by the local damage. India's national grid capacity can absorb the temporary shortfall without disruption.

stories.title: ‘Order of Oliy Darajali Dustlik’: Uzbekistan confers its highest state honour on PM Modi
stories.summary: During his two-day visit to Uzbekistan, Prime Minister Narendra Modi was awarded the prestigious Order of Oliy Darajali Dustlik, the highest state honor from Uzbekistan. Presented by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, this award highlighted Modi's role in enhancing the strategic partnership between India and Uzbekistan. The leaders engaged in discussions aimed at boosting bilateral cooperation and aligning their developmental goals.

stories.title: Nepal floods revive Bihar’s annual nightmare: Why the state faces flooding every year
PM Modi in Tashkent: India, Uzbekistan agree to strengthen trade, defence and energy ties
stories.summary: In a significant diplomatic move, India and Uzbekistan announced a commitment to enhance cooperation in essential arenas. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Shavkat Mirziyoyev engaged in meaningful talks focusing on shared development aspirations and a robust strategic partnership. Modi's participation in a yoga session underscored their cultural bonds, ahead of his journey to Kyrgyzstan for the upcoming SCO summit.

stories.title: Trump wants 'Lake America'. Canada puts up a 24-foot sign saying otherwise
Russia prepares for ‘massive strikes’ against Ukraine's energy facilities
stories.summary: Amid rising tensions, Russia announced plans for large-scale attacks aimed at Ukraine's energy infrastructure, following strikes on its own civilian areas. A recent attack in Bucha tragically resulted in thirty-seven fatalities. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy called out perceived negligence in ammunition storage practices. As these aerial campaigns escalate, the region faces a deepening crisis with infrastructure under relentless assault.

stories.title: ‘No question of bringing back Article 370’: BJP hits out at Mirwaiz Umar Farooq
stories.summary: BJP spokesperson Altaf Thakur dismissed Mirwaiz Umar Farooq's appeal for the restoration of Article 370, reinforcing that the Parliament's decision to abrogate it was conclusive and confirmed by the Supreme Court. He cautioned against comments that might threaten peace in the Valley, pointing out that Kashmiri youth are now pursuing educational and employment avenues. Thakur also mentioned that Jammu and Kashmir's statehood would be reinstated when the time is right.

stories.title: Texas WWII veteran’s remarkable century is being celebrated with a heartfelt tribute
stories.summary: Weldon Kenneth Bowen, a centenarian and World War II veteran from Texas, is commemorating his 100th birthday in style. The Texas Veterans Land Board has launched a campaign urging individuals to send 100 birthday cards to this distinguished Marine Corps veteran, who selflessly served during the war’s final months and earned the Good Conduct Medal. This effort not only recognizes his service but also celebrates his extraordinary life.

stories.title: NASA tests GPS-free navigation using other satellites and space debris as landmarks
stories.summary: NASA has tested FALCON, a system that lets satellites navigate without GPS by using other spacecraft and orbital debris as reference points. During a three-day test, the system autonomously improved the known orbits of more than 200 space objects while also calculating the position of NASA’s Starling spacecraft.

stories.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: 750 dead, 20,000 deployed as rising rivers hamper rescue ops
stories.summary: Nepal and Tibet floods have claimed 750 lives and left over 3,000 missing. Rescuers continue operations amid warnings of fresh flooding and difficult conditions. Hundreds are believed trapped in hydropower tunnels, requiring specialized international assistance. India and China are providing crucial support including forensic experts and relief supplies. Infrastructure damage has cut off communities, while aid efforts are ongoing.

stories.title: 1 in 5 food samples fails: Why so few cases end in conviction
NEET-PG 2026 exam at Jaipur centre rescheduled to September 5 over power outage
stories.summary: The NEET-PG 2026 examination at a Jaipur centre was rescheduled for September 5. This decision followed power outages and technical disruptions during the test on Sunday. Nearly 300 candidates were affected by the rescheduling at the Sitapura centre. Aspirants reported repeated computer shutdowns and system failures during the examination. Officials are investigating the technical arrangements and their impact on the exam's fairness.

stories.title: American startup raises $180 million to drill rock over 5km deep to build world's first superhot geothermal plant at 500 °C
stories.summary: Quaise Energy has successfully raised $180 million for its groundbreaking superhot geothermal plant initiative. Utilizing cutting-edge microwave technology, the project vaporizes rock instead of using conventional drill bits. Collaboration with Nabors Industries will provide essential drilling expertise and equipment. The Obsidian Project, located in Oregon, is set to generate 50 MW by 2030, paving the way for a sustainable energy future.

stories.title: A Colombian man struggling to build his own home created Lego-like bricks from recycled plastic
stories.summary: A Colombian architect helped develop Lego-like building blocks made from recycled plastic and rubber to create temporary and permanent homes. The system was used to build shelters for 42 displaced families in Guapi in 2015. Four people could assemble a 40-square-metre house in five days, without using glue, cement or water.

stories.title: USS Abraham Lincoln sails past Singapore on way home after gruelling Middle East deployment
stories.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln, an aircraft carrier, is heading back home after more than 250 days of supporting operations in the Middle East, recently passing by Singapore. Despite reports of declining crew morale and supply difficulties, US Navy representatives have rejected the idea of a widespread mental health crisis. The ship is expected to stop in Thailand before concluding its journey back to the US.

stories.title: ‘Identify your real enemy’: Khamenei urges Gulf rulers to unite, defend each other
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader urged Gulf rulers to identify their real enemy and confront it. He also called for Muslim unity and mutual defense against external threats. The message comes amid ongoing war and significant economic pressure on Iran. Iranian President dismissed speculation about the leader's health, stating he is healthy. Diplomacy and defense remain Iran's complementary approach to national interests.

stories.title: 'Drug-free India' to 'vocal for local': Key quotes from PM Modi’s 137th Mann Ki Baat
stories.summary: In the latest episode of Mann Ki Baat, Prime Minister Modi focused on grassroots movements and national initiatives, emphasizing the role of technology in preserving history alongside the importance of a drug-free India. The contributions of women street vendors and sanitation campaigns were also highlighted. The Prime Minister called for greater support for local products as the festive season approaches, encouraging individuals to transform environmental stewardship into thriving businesses.

stories.title: A 55-year-old Missouri official reached the 13,804-foot summit of Wyoming's highest mountain
stories.summary: In a remarkable tale of survival, a Missouri deputy attorney general was found alive after an arduous five-day ordeal on Gannett Peak. Despite achieving his goal of reaching the summit, he faced severe dehydration and confusion near Scott Lake. Fortunately, search teams successfully located him amidst the challenging terrain, and he is now in recovery, expressing heartfelt gratitude to his rescuers for their relentless efforts.

stories.title: Indian-origin teen accused of killing family allegedly used ChatGPT for ‘fantasy stories’
stories.summary: A tutor's alarming visit in Acton, Massachusetts, unveiled a grim double homicide involving a mother and her young son. The police later apprehended the grieving elder sibling in his mother's car nearby. Disturbingly, prosecutors disclosed that the teenager employed AI and ChatGPT to delve into hypothetical murder scenarios, prompting a critical examination of artificial intelligence's influence on harmful behaviors.

Kim Jong UN shakes up North Korea’s military, dismisses defence minister No Kwang Chol
stories.summary: North Korea has shaken up its military hierarchy by removing the defense minister, a move approved by Kim Jong Un in a recent leadership meeting. This change mirrors advancements at the nation's weapons research center, which has introduced new combat weapon systems. As tensions rise, trilateral military drills involving South Korea, the US, and Japan will carry on, designed to counter North Korea's ongoing nuclear and missile provocations.

Trump-Putin-Zelenskyy summit floated in secret Moscow talks: Report
stories.summary: John Ratcliffe, the CIA Director, is advocating for a trilateral summit involving the US, Russia, and Ukraine, with hopes of revitalizing diplomatic negotiations aimed at resolving the ongoing conflict. He recently conferred with Russian intelligence heads to discuss strategies for encouraging President Putin to engage in talks. US officials have updated President Zelenskyy about these ongoing discussions, yet skepticism amongst Ukrainian officials persists regarding Russia's motives amid potential escalations.

'Slippages reveal design flaw on Kanpur-Lucknow e-way'
stories.summary: Slippages on the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway suggest design issues, not construction defects. Affected stretches will require rebuilding from the ground up, officials stated. A preliminary investigation identified weak, plastic soil as a primary cause. Poor drainage also contributed to the expressway's structural problems. The government awaits a final report on the detailed investigation.

stories.title: BJP-SAD alliance revival gains ground ahead of Punjab polls
stories.summary: The BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal may revive their alliance for upcoming Punjab assembly elections. Both parties acknowledge this partnership as their strongest option despite seat-sharing disagreements. Talks have intensified since Prime Minister Narendra Modi met SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal recently. The BJP seeks a larger seat share and greater government role, reflecting its increased vote share.

stories.title: Congress & BJP clash over Haldwani ‘purification’ row, Rahul seeks FIR
stories.summary: BJP and Congress clashed over allegations of rally venue purification. Rahul Gandhi demanded an FIR, linking it to untouchability practices. BJP rebutted charges, showing organizers' videos and questioning the delay. Organizers stated a hawan followed cleaning for Ramlila, denying BJP links. Both parties exchanged accusations regarding caste divisions and past incidents.

stories.title: August rainfall fails to reduce India's monsoon deficit
stories.summary: India's cumulative monsoon rainfall deficit remains despite August's better-than-expected rains. This deficit has caused a significant acreage gap in kharif crop sowing. Paddy and maize acreage have both reported notable declines compared to last year. Erratic rainfall distribution prevented increased acreage for most kharif crops. Several states, including Bihar and Andhra Pradesh, face substantial rainfall deficits.

stories.title: FSSAI bans Everest, LG from selling hing
stories.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has issued prohibition orders against two spice companies. Everest Food Products and Laljee Godhoo and Company faced these orders for non-compliance issues. Samples of compounded asafoetida and hing powder did not meet alcohol-soluble extract requirements. Earlier reviews also found violations in other masala products from Everest. These actions highlight ongoing food safety scrutiny within the Indian market.

stories.title: Man on Phuket-B’luru flight tries to hide drugs in overhead panel, held
stories.summary: A passenger flying from Phuket to Bengaluru allegedly tried to hide narcotics. He attempted to conceal thirteen packets of contraband substance in an overhead panel. The passenger then discarded some of the substance into the lavatory bin. Upon landing in Bangalore, customs officials arrested the individual at the aerobridge. Air India Express is cooperating with authorities in the ongoing investigation.

stories.title: BJP president pulls up 3 Delhi MPs for visiting Sajjan Kumar’s house
stories.summary: Nitin Nabin, the BJP president, took disciplinary action against three Delhi MPs who visited the recently deceased Sajjan Kumar's home. Kumar, notorious for his conviction in the anti-Sikh riots, passed away at the age of eighty. This controversial visit comes at a crucial time for the party as they prepare for the Punjab assembly elections.

stories.title: Will work with SCO to free region from terror: PM Modi ahead of summit
stories.summary: On his diplomatic mission to Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, Prime Minister Modi aims to bolster India's regional aspirations and forge stronger ties. At the SCO summit, he will advocate for collective efforts against terrorism and initiate dialogue on trade and strategic collaboration. This trip underscores India’s dedication to nurturing historical connections and fostering prosperity for all involved nations.

stories.title: FBI lowers hiring bar: Getting services from prostitutes, stealing from employer, bestiality not automatic deal-breakers
An entrepreneur began melting discarded plastic; within three years his startup had built...
stories.summary: In a remarkable daily effort, workers in Mexico convert plastic waste into robust building panels, driving change for impoverished families. Spearheaded by the social enterprise EcoDom, this eco-friendly solution tackles pressing issues of pollution and inadequate housing. Informal waste collectors benefit significantly from improved purchasing deals, and this sustainable model aims to reach broader audiences worldwide, striving to alleviate waste and poverty challenges.

stories.title: Unfinished for nearly 30 years, Hollywood Video’s founder's Oregon mansion is up for $4.7 million
stories.summary: A nearly 52,000-square-foot mansion in West Linn, Oregon, has remained unfinished for almost 30 years and is now listed for $4.7 million. Hollywood Video founder Mark Wattles bought the 32-acre property for $1.25 million in 1994 and spent about $12 million on the project. Two later owners also had plans for the estate, but the mansion was never completed.

stories.title: In 2020, four engineers started Moment Energy in a British Columbia garage; 6 years later...
stories.summary: Moment Energy has launched its most extensive second-life battery manufacturing plant, transforming used electric vehicle batteries into essential energy storage systems. This innovative facility aims to deliver backup power for various crucial facilities across North America. The company has successfully obtained considerable funding and safety certifications, while also planning to broaden its manufacturing operations into Texas.

Haunted Drake’s Island with Grade-II listed house, 6.4-acre site, tunnels goes on sale for over £2M
stories.summary: Drake’s Island, a 6.4-acre historic island in Plymouth Sound, Devon, has gone on sale for offers above £2 million. The former military site features a Grade-II listed Governor’s House, underground tunnels, Tudor fortifications and planning consent for a 43-bed hotel. Fortified in the 16th century, the island also has a mysterious, reportedly haunted past.

No one calls UP 'Bimaru' state anymore: CM Yogi inaugurates Rs 305 cr projects in Deoria, says mafia crushed; encephalitis eradicated
stories.summary: Addressing a programme in Deoria, where he inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 80 development projects worth ₹305 crore, Adityanath said encephalitis was not merely a disease but reflected what he described as the "sick mindset" of previous Samajwadi Party and Congress governments.

stories.title: Americans don't always want to move to coastal cities for tech jobs, leaving families: Indian-origin founder Apoorva Govind explains why companies have to hire H-1Bs
‘No threat to UP from Nepal floods’: State Jal Shakti minister says authorities remain on alert
'We do not want to burden people': Auto, taxi unions oppose CNG hike in Delhi
Haiti gang frees 13 women and children days after raid that killed at least 47 people
stories.summary: A gang in Haiti has freed thirteen hostages, including women and children, following a brutal assault. UNICEF played a crucial role in securing their release from a farming community. This incident in Kenscoff underscores the rampant violence impacting children across Haiti. The region has faced numerous fatalities and displacement due to gang activities, although mass abductions are less frequent and often yield unpredictable results for those abducted.
